title.zh: 卷一 魏書一 武帝紀
title.en: Volume 1: Book of Wei 1 - Annals of Emperor Wu
title.raw: 卷一 魏書一 武帝紀 Volume 1: Book of Wei 1 - Annals of Emperor Wu

sentences.zh: 太祖武皇帝，沛國譙人也，姓曹，諱操，字孟德，漢相國參之後。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor Martial Emperor was a man of Qiao in the state of Pei; his surname was Cao, his taboo name was Cao, his style name was Mengde; he was a descendant of Cao Shen, who had served as Chancellor of State of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, canonically titled Grand Progenitor, came from Qiao in Pei commandery. His clan name was Cao; his given name Cao (taboo form); his courtesy name Mengde. His line traced back to Cao Shen, who had served the Han as Chancellor of State.

sentences.zh: 〈〔《曹瞞傳》曰：〕太祖一名吉利，小字阿瞞。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: The Grand Progenitor also had the name Jili, and his childhood name was A Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan adds that Cao Cao was also called Jili and was known in childhood as A Man.

sentences.zh: 王沈《魏書》曰：其先出於黃帝。

translations.literal: Wang Chen's Wei Shu says: His ancestors came from the Yellow Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen's Book of Wei traces his ancestry to the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 當高陽世，陸終之子曰安，是爲曹姓。

translations.literal: In the generation of Gaoyang, the son of Lu Zhong named An was the one who became the Cao surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the line of Gaoyang, Lu Zhong's son An founded what became the Cao clan.

sentences.zh: 周武王克殷，存先世之後，封曹俠於邾。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou conquered Yin, preserved the posterity of former ages, and enfeoffed Cao Xia at Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu of Zhou overthrew Shang, he preserved ancient noble lines and enfeoffed Cao Xia in Zhu.

sentences.zh: 春秋之世，與於盟會，逮至戰國，爲楚所滅。

translations.literal: In the age of Spring and Autumn, it participated in alliances and meetings; reaching the Warring States period, it was destroyed by Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Spring and Autumn era that state joined the great alliances; by the Warring States period Chu had swallowed it.

sentences.zh: 子孫分流，或家于沛。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons branched apart; some made their home in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The family scattered, and one branch settled in Pei.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖之起，曹參以功封平陽侯，世襲爵土，絕而復紹，至今適嗣國於容城。〉

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu rose, Cao Can was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyang for merit; generation after generation inherited the fief and territory; it was cut off and then restored; down to the present the legitimate heir holds a state at Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bang founded the Han, Cao Shen earned the marquisate of Pingyang; the title passed down through the generations, was once broken, then restored, and the rightful heir still holds an enfeoffment at Rongcheng today.

sentences.zh: 桓帝世，曹騰爲中常侍大長秋，封費亭侯。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Huan, Cao Teng served as palace attendant and grand chief steward for the empress, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Feiting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan, Cao Teng rose to senior eunuch and chief steward to the empress, and received the title of marquis of Feiting.

sentences.zh: 〈司馬彪《續漢書》曰：騰父節，字元偉，素以仁厚稱。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Xu Han Shu says: Teng's father Jie, style Yuanwei, was always called benevolent and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's Continuation of the Han History records that Cao Teng's father, Jie (courtesy Yuanwei), was widely known for kindness and generosity.

sentences.zh: 鄰人有亡豕者，與節豕相類，詣門認之，節不與爭；

translations.literal: A neighbor had lost a pig; it resembled Jie's pig; he came to the door to claim it; Jie did not contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor who had lost a pig insisted the one at Jie's door was his; Jie yielded without argument.

sentences.zh: 後所亡豕自還其家，豕主人大慙，送所認豕，并辭謝節，節笑而受之。

translations.literal: Later the lost pig returned of itself to its home; the pig's owner was greatly ashamed, sent the pig he had claimed, and apologized to Jie; Jie laughed and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The runaway pig soon wandered home. Mortified, the neighbor brought back Jie's animal and apologized; Jie accepted both with a smile.

sentences.zh: 由是鄉黨貴歎焉。

translations.literal: Thereby the village esteemed and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his community held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 長子伯興，次子仲興，次子叔興。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Boxing; the second son was Zhongxing; the second son was Shuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Boxing, Zhongxing, and Shuxing, in birth order.

sentences.zh: 騰字季興，少除黃門從官。

translations.literal: Teng's style name was Jixing; in youth he was appointed attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng, courtesy Jixing, entered service young as a Yellow Gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年，鄧太后詔黃門令選中黃門從官年少溫謹者，配皇太子書，騰應其選。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongning, Empress Dowager Deng issued an edict through the Yellow Gate minister to select among the young and mild and careful attendants of the Yellow Gate those to be paired with the Imperial Crown Prince for study; Teng answered that selection.
translations.idiomatic: In 120 CE, Empress Dowager Deng ordered the selection of steady young pages to tutor the crown prince; Cao Teng was chosen.

sentences.zh: 太子特親愛騰，飲食賞賜與衆有異。

translations.literal: The heir apparent especially loved Teng; in drink, food, and rewards he differed from the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince singled him out for meals and largesse.

sentences.zh: 順帝即位，爲小黃門，遷至中常侍大長秋。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, he became junior attendant at the Yellow Gate, and was promoted to palace attendant and grand chief steward for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun came to the throne, Cao Teng advanced from junior Yellow Gate attendant to senior eunuch and chief steward to the empress.

sentences.zh: 在省闥三十餘年，歷事四帝，未甞有過。

translations.literal: In the inner precincts more than thirty years, he served four emperors in succession, and never had fault.
translations.idiomatic: For more than thirty years inside the palace he served four sovereigns without a stain on his record.

sentences.zh: 好進達賢能，終無所毀傷。

translations.literal: He liked to advance the worthy and able; in the end he never harmed any.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in promoting talent and never used his influence to ruin anyone.

sentences.zh: 其所稱薦，若陳留虞放、邊韶、南陽延固、張溫、弘農張奐、潁川堂谿典等，皆致位公卿，而不伐其善。

translations.literal: Those whom he praised and recommended, such as Yu Fang and Bian Shao of Chenliu, Yan Gu and Zhang Wen of Nanyang, Zhang Huan of Hongnong, and Tangxi Dian of Yingchuan, all reached the ranks of duke and minister, yet he did not boast of their goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Men he backedYu Fang and Bian Shao of Chenliu, Yan Gu and Zhang Wen of Nanyang, Zhang Huan of Hongnong, Tangxi Dian of Yingchuan, and othersall rose to the highest offices, yet he never bragged about his part in their careers.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡太守因計吏修敬於騰，益州刺史种暠於函谷關搜得其牋，上太守，并奏騰內臣外交，所不當爲，請免官治罪。

translations.literal: The governor of Shu commandery, through the clerk on the annual accounting mission, sent a letter of respect to Teng; the inspector of Yizhou, Chong Hao, at Hangu Pass searched and obtained his letter, reported it to the governor, and together memorialized that Teng, an inner court minister, had foreign dealings, which was improper, requesting dismissal from office and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A Shu prefect tried to curry favor with Cao Teng through his clerk; Inspector Chong Hao intercepted the letter at Hangu Pass, informed the court, and charged the powerful eunuch with unauthorized external correspondence.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「牋自外來，騰書不出，非其罪也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The letter came from outside; Teng did not send a letter out; it is not his crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The letter came from outside the palace; Cao Teng sent nothing out, so he is blameless."

sentences.zh: 」乃寑暠奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set aside Hao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He shelved Chong Hao's accusation.

sentences.zh: 騰不以介意，常稱歎暠，以爲暠得事上之節。

translations.literal: Teng did not take it to heart, and constantly praised Hao, considering that Hao grasped the propriety of serving superiors.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng bore no grudge and instead praised Chong Hao for understanding how a loyal official should serve his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 暠後爲司徒，語人曰：「今日爲公，乃曹常侍恩也。

translations.literal: Later, when Hao became Minister of Education, he said to people: "Today I am a duke; it is owing to the grace of Palace Attendant Cao."
translations.idiomatic: Years later, as Minister of Education, Chong Hao told people that his exalted rank owed everything to Cao Teng's generosity.

sentences.zh: 」騰之行事，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Teng's conduct in affairs was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng's public life was marked by such magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 桓帝即位，以騰先帝舊臣，忠孝彰著，封費亭侯，加位特進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huan ascended the throne, because Teng was an old minister of the former emperor, loyal and filial and illustrious, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Feiting and his rank was raised to special advance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan honored him as a veteran of the previous reign, enfeoffed him at Feiting, and advanced him to the exalted rank of tejin.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，追尊騰曰高皇帝。〉

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe, posthumously he was honored as Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In 229 CE, the third year of Taihe, he was posthumously canonized as Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 養子嵩嗣，官至太尉，莫能審其生出本末。

translations.literal: His adopted son Song succeeded; he reached the rank of Grand Commandant; no one could ascertain the root and end of his birth.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Cao Song inherited the title and rose to grand commandant, though his true parentage remained obscure.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》曰：嵩字巨高。

translations.literal: The Xu Han Shu says: Song's style name was Jugao.
translations.idiomatic: The Continuation of the Han History gives Cao Song's courtesy name as Jugao.

sentences.zh: 質性敦慎，所在忠孝。

translations.literal: His nature was honest and careful; wherever he was, he was loyal and filial.
translations.idiomatic: He was steady and conscientious, and loyal wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 爲司隷校尉，靈帝擢拜大司農、大鴻臚，代崔烈爲太尉。

translations.literal: He served as Colonel Director of Retainers; Emperor Ling promoted him to Grand Minister of Agriculture and Grand Herald, and in place of Cui Lie he became Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was colonel director of retainers; Emperor Ling then promoted him to grand minister of agriculture and grand herald, and finally made him grand commandant in place of Cui Lie.

sentences.zh: 黃初元年，追尊嵩曰太皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangchu, posthumously Song was honored as Grand Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In 220 CE, the first year of Huangchu, Cao Song was posthumously honored as grand emperor.

sentences.zh: 吳人作《曹瞞傳》及郭頒《世語》並云：嵩，夏侯氏之子，夏侯惇之叔父。

translations.literal: The people of Wu composed the Cao Man Zhuan and Guo Ban's Shi Yu both say: Song was a son of the Xiahou clan, the uncle of Xiahou Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Wu lore and Guo Ban's Shi Yu both claim Cao Song was actually a Xiahouson of Xiahou Dun's uncle.

sentences.zh: 太祖於惇爲從父兄弟。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor to Dun was a cousin of the same generation from the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: That would make Cao Cao and Xiahou Dun cousins on the male side.

sentences.zh: 嵩生太祖。

translations.literal: Song begat the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song was Cao Cao's father.

sentences.zh: 太祖少機警，有權數，而任俠放蕩，不治行業，故世人未之奇也；

translations.literal: In youth the Grand Progenitor was alert and clever, had stratagems and schemes, yet indulged knight-errantry and was unrestrained, not ordering his conduct and occupation; therefore the world did not regard him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Young Cao Cao was sharp and resourceful but swaggered as a brawling rake, neglecting steady study, so contemporaries saw nothing remarkable in him.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》云：太祖少好飛鷹走狗，游蕩無度，其叔父數言之於嵩。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: In youth the Grand Progenitor liked flying hawks and running dogs, wandered without limit; his uncle repeatedly spoke of it to Song.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says he spent his youth hawking and hunting, roaming without restraint, until his uncle kept reporting him to Cao Song.

sentences.zh: 太祖患之，後逢叔父於路，乃陽敗面喎口；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor worried about this; later, meeting his uncle on the road, he feigned a twisted mouth and ruined face.
translations.idiomatic: Annoyed by the tattling, he once met his uncle on the road and pretended to have a stroke-twisted mouth, slack features, the whole performance.

sentences.zh: 叔父怪而問其故，太祖曰：「卒中惡風。

translations.literal: The uncle wondered and asked the reason; the Grand Progenitor said: "I suddenly suffered a malign wind."
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle asked what was wrong, he gasped that a sudden fit of palsy had seized him.

sentences.zh: 」叔父以告嵩。

translations.literal: The uncle told Song.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle hurried the news to Cao Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩驚愕，呼太祖，太祖口貌如故。

translations.literal: Song was startled, called the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor's mouth and appearance were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song rushed out in alarmonly to find his son looking perfectly healthy.

sentences.zh: 嵩問曰：「叔父言汝中風，已差乎？

translations.literal: Song asked: "Your uncle said you were struck by wind; is it already better?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song asked, "Your uncle said you had a stroke. Are you recovered?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「初不中風，但失愛於叔父，故見罔耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "I never had a wind stroke; I only lost my uncle's favor, therefore I was deceived."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, "I was never ill; I only lost my uncle's goodwill, so he slandered me."

sentences.zh: 」嵩乃疑焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song doubted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Cao Song doubted his brother's reports.

sentences.zh: 自後叔父有所告，嵩終不復信，太祖於是益得肆意矣。〉

translations.literal: After that, whenever the uncle had something to report, Song in the end no longer believed; the Grand Progenitor thereby was all the more able to act as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: After that his uncle's complaints fell on deaf ears, and Cao Cao could misbehave with impunity.

sentences.zh: 惟梁國橋玄、南陽何顒異焉。

translations.literal: Only Qiao Xuan of Liang and He Yong of Nanyang regarded him differently.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qiao Xuan of Liang and He Yong of Nanyang saw something exceptional in him.

sentences.zh: 玄謂太祖曰：「天下將亂，非命世之才不能濟也，能安之者，其在君乎！」

translations.literal: Xuan said to the Grand Progenitor: "The realm is about to be in chaos; without a man of the age's destiny one cannot save it; he who can bring peace to it—that one is perhaps you!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Xuan told him, "The empire is sliding toward chaos; only a genius of the age can save it, and that man may be you!"

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太尉橋玄，世名知人，覩太祖而異之，曰：「吾見天下名士多矣，未有若君者也！

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan, generation after generation famed for knowing men, looked upon the Grand Progenitor and regarded him differently, saying: "I have seen the famous scholars of the realm; none is like you, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records that Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan, famed for reading character, exclaimed on meeting Cao Cao, "I have known every luminary of our age, and none compares to you."

sentences.zh: 君善自持。

translations.literal: You, be good at holding yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Mind how you carry yourself.

sentences.zh: 吾老矣！

translations.literal: I am old!
translations.idiomatic: I am an old man now.

sentences.zh: 願以妻子爲託。

translations.literal: I wish to entrust wife and children to you.
translations.idiomatic: I charge you with my family's future.

sentences.zh: 」由是聲名益重。

translations.literal: Thereby his reputation and name grew weightier.
translations.idiomatic: From that moment his name carried real weight at court.

sentences.zh: 《續漢書》曰：玄字公祖，嚴明有才略，長於人物。

translations.literal: The Xu Han Shu says: Xuan's style name was Gongzu; he was strict and bright and had talent and strategy, and excelled at judging men.
translations.idiomatic: The Continuation of the Han History describes Qiao Xuan (courtesy Gongzu) as stern, capable, and gifted at sizing people up.

sentences.zh: 張璠《漢紀》曰：玄歷位中外，以剛斷稱，謙儉下士，不以王爵私親。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan's Han Ji says: Xuan held posts inside and outside the court, was famed for resolute judgment, was humble and courteous to gentlemen of lower rank, and did not use royal titles to favor kin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Han Annals adds that Qiao Xuan served in the provinces and capital, was known for firm decisions and modesty toward inferiors, and never traded on rank for his relatives.

sentences.zh: 光和中爲太尉，以久病策罷，拜太中大夫，卒，家貧乏產業，柩無所殯。

translations.literal: In the Guanghe era he became Grand Commandant; because of long illness he was dismissed by rescript, was appointed Grand Palace Grandee, died, and his household lacked property; the coffin had nowhere to be buried.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghe era he rose to grand commandant, then retired ill as a grand palace counselor; he died so poor that his kin could barely bury him.

sentences.zh: 當世以此稱爲名臣。

translations.literal: The age thereby praised him as a famous minister.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries hailed him as a model minister.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：玄謂太祖曰：「君未有名，可交許子將。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Xuan said to the Grand Progenitor: "You have not yet gained a name; you may associate with Xu Zijiang."
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu records Qiao Xuan advising Cao Cao to seek out Xu Shao (Zijiang) if he wanted a reputation.

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃造子將，子將納焉，由是知名。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon visited Zijiang; Zijiang accepted him; thereby he became known.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao called on Xu Shao, who took him in, and his fame spread from that introduction.

sentences.zh: 孫盛異同雜語云：太祖甞私入中常侍張讓室，讓覺之；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's Yitong Zayu says: The Grand Progenitor once secretly entered the chamber of palace attendant Zhang Rang; Rang noticed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's Miscellaneous Tales of Agreement and Disagreement claims Cao Cao once slipped into eunuch Zhang Rang's quarters and was spotted.

sentences.zh: 乃舞手戟於庭，踰垣而出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he brandished a hand halberd in the courtyard and leaped the wall to go out.
translations.idiomatic: He waved a short halberd in the courtyard, vaulted the wall, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 才武絕人，莫之能害。

translations.literal: His talent and martial skill surpassed others; none could harm him.
translations.idiomatic: His fighting skill was so extraordinary that no one could touch him.

sentences.zh: 博覽群書，特好兵法，抄集諸家兵法，名曰接要，又注孫武十三篇，皆傳於世。

translations.literal: He broadly read the classics and histories, especially loved military methods, copied and gathered the military writings of various houses, named it Jieyao, and also annotated Sun Wu's thirteen chapters; all were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, loved strategy, compiled excerpts from military treatises under the title Essentials Drawn Together, and annotated Sunzi's thirteen chaptersworks that circulated for generations.

sentences.zh: 甞問許子將：「我何如人？

translations.literal: He once asked Xu Zijiang: "What sort of man am I?"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Xu Shao, "What kind of man am I?"

sentences.zh: 」子將不荅。

translations.literal: Zijiang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 固問之，子將曰：「子治世之能臣，亂世之姦雄。

translations.literal: He pressed the question; Zijiang said: "You are a capable minister in an ordered age, a crafty hero in a chaotic age."
translations.idiomatic: Pressed again, Xu Shao replied, "In a well-ordered age you would be an outstanding minister; in disorder you would dominate as a formidable power."

sentences.zh: 」太祖大笑。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舉孝廉爲郎，除洛陽北部尉，遷頓丘令，

translations.literal: At age twenty, he was recommended for filial and incorrupt and became a gentleman; he was appointed Northern District Lieutenant of Luoyang, transferred to be magistrate of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered office on the Filial-and-Incorrupt list, became a gentleman cadet, served as captain of the northern district of Luoyang, then was named magistrate of Dunqiu county.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：太祖初入尉廨，繕治四門。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: When the Grand Progenitor first entered the lieutenant's office, he repaired and put in order the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says that on taking up his post in Luoyang he immediately set his yamen in order, including the four gates.

sentences.zh: 造五色棒，縣門左右各十餘枚，有犯禁者，不避豪彊，皆棒殺之。

translations.literal: He made five-colored clubs; at the county gates left and right he hung more than ten each; those who violated prohibitions, not avoiding the powerful, were all clubbed to death.
translations.idiomatic: He hung colored clubs by each gate and bludgeoned every curfew-breaker, powerful house or petty thief alike.

sentences.zh: 後數月，靈帝愛幸小黃門蹇碩叔父夜行，即殺之。

translations.literal: After several months, the uncle of petty yellow-gate attendant Jian Shuo, whom Emperor Ling favored, went out at night; immediately he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Months later a kinsman of the favored eunuch Jian Shuo violated the night curfew; Cao Cao had him beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 京師斂迹，莫敢犯者。

translations.literal: The capital drew in its footsteps; none dared violate.
translations.idiomatic: The capital went quiet; no one dared test him.

sentences.zh: 近習寵臣咸疾之，然不能傷，於是共稱薦之，故遷爲頓丘令。〉

translations.literal: The favored attendants and doted-on ministers all hated him, yet could not harm him; therefore together they praised and recommended him; therefore he was transferred to be magistrate of Dunqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Palace favorites seethed but could not strike him, so they conspired to praise him upward and bundle him off as magistrate of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 徵拜議郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖從妹夫㶏彊侯宋奇被誅，從坐免官。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: The Grand Progenitor's cousin-in-law, Marquis Qiang of Yin, Song Qi, was executed; by association he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes his dismissal when his wife's cousin Song Qi, marquis of Yinqiang, was executed.

sentences.zh: 後以能明古學，復徵拜議郎。

translations.literal: Later, because he could clarify ancient learning, he was again summoned and appointed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: His classical scholarship later won him a second appointment as gentleman consultant.

sentences.zh: 先是大將軍竇武、太傅陳蕃謀誅閹官，反爲所害。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand General Dou Wu and Grand Tutor Chen Fan plotted to execute the palace attendants, but on the contrary were harmed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand General Dou Wu and Grand Tutor Chen Fan had tried to purge the eunuchs and were themselves destroyed.

sentences.zh: 太祖上書陳武等正直而見陷害，姦邪盈朝，善人壅塞，其言甚切；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor submitted a memorial stating that Wu and the others were upright yet were framed; evil and wicked men filled the court; good men were blocked and stopped; his words were very cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao submitted a blunt memorial charging that honest men had been murdered while villains choked the court.

sentences.zh: 靈帝不能用。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling ignored it.

sentences.zh: 是後詔書勑三府：舉奏州縣政理無效，民爲作謠言者免罷之。

translations.literal: After this an edict ordered the three offices: those who reported that the provinces and counties had ineffective government and that the people made slanderous songs about them were to be dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered the three bureaus to dismiss local officials whose misrule had provoked popular lampoons.

sentences.zh: 三公傾邪，皆希世見用，貨賂並行，彊者爲怨，不見舉奏，弱者守道，多被陷毀。

translations.literal: The three dukes were crooked and evil, all seeking favor from the age and being employed; bribes went side by side; the strong became objects of resentment yet were not reported; the weak kept the Way and were mostly framed and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies were venal time-servers; bribery decided cases, the ruthless escaped impeachment, and principled minor officials were ruined.

sentences.zh: 太祖疾之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor detested this.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao despised the corruption.

sentences.zh: 是歲以災異博問得失，因此復上書切諫，說三公所舉奏專回避貴戚之意。

translations.literal: That year, because of disasters and prodigies, he broadly asked about gains and losses; thereby he again submitted a memorial sharply remonstrating, explaining that what the three dukes reported and impeached specialized in avoiding powerful relatives.
translations.idiomatic: When omens prompted a policy review, he fired off another memorial accusing the Three Excellencies of shielding well-connected wrongdoers.

sentences.zh: 奏上，天子感寤，以示三府責讓之，諸以謠言徵者皆拜議郎。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, the Son of Heaven was moved to understanding, showed it to the three offices and reproached them; all those summoned because of slanderous songs were appointed Gentlemen Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point, showed the memorial to the three bureaus, rebuked them, and appointed the lampooned officials as gentlemen consultants.

sentences.zh: 是後政教日亂，豪猾益熾，多所摧毀；

translations.literal: After this government and instruction daily grew chaotic; powerful knaves daily grew fiercer; many were smashed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet governance only worsened, predators grew bolder, and honest men were torn down faster than ever.

sentences.zh: 太祖知不可匡正，遂不復獻言。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor knew it could not be corrected and uprighted; therefore he no longer presented words.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no hope of reform, Cao Cao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 光和末，黃巾起。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Guanghe, the Yellow Turbans rose.
translations.idiomatic: Near the close of the Guanghe era the Yellow Turban rebellion broke out.

sentences.zh: 拜騎都尉，討潁川賊。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief of Cavalry and attacked the bandits of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was named chief of cavalry and sent to suppress the rebels in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 遷爲濟南相，國有十餘縣，長吏多阿附貴戚，贓污狼藉，於是奏免其八；

translations.literal: He was transferred to be chancellor of Jinan; the state had more than ten counties; the senior officials mostly fawned on noble relatives and were corrupt and filthy beyond reckoning; therefore he memorialized and dismissed eight of them.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor of Jinan he purged eight corrupt magistrates out of more than ten who had been currying favor with great houses.

sentences.zh: 禁斷淫祀，姦宄逃竄，郡界肅然。

translations.literal: He prohibited and cut off excessive sacrifices; the wicked fled and scattered; the commandery's borders were solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He banned illicit shrines, drove off criminals, and brought the commandery to order.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：長吏受取貪饕，依倚貴勢，歷前相不見舉；

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: Senior officials received bribes and were greedy, relied on noble power; through former chancellors they had not been impeached.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that magistrates had grown fat on bribes and noble protection while successive chancellors looked the other way.

sentences.zh: 聞太祖至，咸皆舉免，小大震怖，姦宄遁逃，竄入他郡。

translations.literal: When they heard the Grand Progenitor had arrived, all were impeached and dismissed; great and small trembled in fear; the wicked fled and scattered, fleeing into other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao arrived, officials were cashiered wholesale; high and low trembled, and wrongdoers bolted to neighboring jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 政教大行，一郡清平。

translations.literal: Government and instruction were greatly carried out; the whole commandery was clear and peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Sound administration took hold and the entire commandery grew calm.

sentences.zh: 初，城陽景王劉章以有功於漢，故其國爲立祠，青州諸郡轉相倣效，濟南尤盛，至六百餘祠。

translations.literal: At first, Prince Jing of Chengyang, Liu Zhang, because he had merit toward Han, therefore his state had a shrine established for him; the various commanderies of Qingzhou turned and imitated one another; Jinan was especially flourishing, reaching more than six hundred shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to Prince Liu Zhang of Chengyanghonored for aiding the Hanhad multiplied across Qingzhou until Jinan alone held over six hundred.

sentences.zh: 賈人或假二千石輿服導從作倡樂，奢侈日甚，民坐貧窮，歷世長吏無敢禁絕者。

translations.literal: Merchants or others borrowed the carriages and robes of two-thousand-dan officials, with outriders and attendants making music and revelry; extravagance daily grew worse; the people sat in poverty; generation after generation of long-term senior officials had none who dared forbid and cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants paraded in faux ministerial splendor with musicians and outriders while the people grew poorer, and no previous governor had dared stop them.

sentences.zh: 太祖到，皆毀壞祠屋，止絕官吏民不得祠祀。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor arrived, he destroyed all shrine houses and stopped officials and commoners from sacrificing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao tore down the shrines and forbade officials and commoners from offering sacrifice there.

sentences.zh: 及至秉政，遂除姦邪鬼神之事，世之淫祀由此遂絕。〉

translations.literal: When he reached holding power, then he eliminated wicked affairs of ghosts and spirits; the age's excessive sacrifices thereby were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held real authority he stamped out such superstitious abuses for good.

sentences.zh: 久之，徵還爲東郡太守；

translations.literal: After a long time, he was summoned back to be governor of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was recalled to serve as prefect of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 不就，稱疾歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He did not take up the post, claiming illness and returning to his village.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post, citing illness, and retired to his home district.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：於是權臣專朝，貴戚橫恣。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: At this time powerful ministers monopolized the court, and noble relatives ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records that, by then, dominant ministers controlled the government while imperial in-laws threw their weight about unchecked.

sentences.zh: 太祖不能違道取容。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor could not violate the Way to curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused to abandon principle just to stay in office.

sentences.zh: 數數干忤，恐爲家禍，遂乞留宿衞。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he offended them; fearing it would become a disaster for his family, he begged to remain in the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: He kept rubbing powerful men the wrong way and, fearing for his kin, asked to be kept on palace night duty instead.

sentences.zh: 拜議郎，常託疾病，輙告歸鄉里；

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman Consultant, constantly pleading illness, repeatedly requesting leave to return to his village;
translations.idiomatic: As a gentleman consultant he habitually cited illness and took repeated leaves to go home.

sentences.zh: 築室城外，春夏習讀書傳，秋冬弋獵，以自娛樂。〉

translations.literal: he built a house outside the walls; in spring and summer he practiced reading texts and histories, in autumn and winter he went shooting and hunting, to amuse himself.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the city walls he put up a retreat where he read through the warm months and hunted through the cold ones for his own diversion.

sentences.zh: 頃之，冀州刺史王芬、南陽許攸、沛國周旌等連結豪傑，謀廢靈帝，立合肥侯，以告太祖，太祖拒之。

translations.literal: Before long, Wang Fen, Inspector of Ji, Xu You of Nanyang, Zhou Jing of Pei, and others linked bold spirits, plotted to depose Emperor Ling and establish the Marquis of Hefei; they informed the Grand Progenitor, who refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Fen of Ji, Xu You of Nanyang, Zhou Jing of Pei, and other local notables conspired to depose Emperor Ling in favor of the prince of Hefei; they sounded out Cao Cao, who turned them down flat.

sentences.zh: 芬等遂敗。

translations.literal: Fen and the others thereupon failed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot collapsed and Wang Fen's party fell apart.

sentences.zh: 〈司馬彪《九州春秋》曰：於是陳蕃子逸與術士平原襄楷會於芬坐，楷曰：「天文不利宦者，黃門、常侍貴族滅矣。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Jiuzhou Chunqiu says: At this time Chen Fan's son Yi and the occultist Xiang Kai of Pingyuan met at Fen's seat, and Kai said: "The stars augur ill for the eunuchs; the Yellow Gate and regular attendants' noble houses will be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's Spring and Autumn of the Nine Provinces relates how Chen Yi, son of Chen Fan, met the prognosticator Xiang Kai of Pingyuan at Wang Fen's house. Xiang declared that heaven's signs foretold the ruin of the eunuch clans.

sentences.zh: 」逸喜。

translations.literal: Yi rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi was delighted.

sentences.zh: 芬曰：「若然者，芬願驅除。

translations.literal: Fen said: "If it is so, Fen is willing to drive them out."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fen replied, "If that is the omen, I will lead the purge."

sentences.zh: 」於是與攸等結謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon he joined in plotting with You and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He then sealed the conspiracy with Xu You and the rest.

sentences.zh: 靈帝欲北巡河間舊宅，芬等謀因此作難，上書言黑山賊攻劫郡縣，求得起兵。

translations.literal: Emperor Ling wished to tour north to his old residence in Hejian; Fen and the others planned thereby to raise trouble, memorializing that Black Mountain bandits were attacking and plundering commanderies and counties, requesting permission to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling planned a northern progress to his old Hejian estates; Wang Fen meant to use the journey as cover, filing false reports of Black Mountain raids so he could mobilize an army.

sentences.zh: 會北方有赤氣，東西竟天，太史上言「當有陰謀，不宜北行」，帝乃止。

translations.literal: It happened that in the north there was red vapor, east to west spanning the sky; the Grand Clerk memorialized, "There must be a plot; it is not appropriate to go north"; the emperor therefore stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A band of crimson mist then stretched from horizon to horizon in the north; the court astronomers warned of hidden treachery, and the emperor canceled the trip.

sentences.zh: 勑芬罷兵，俄而徵之。

translations.literal: He ordered Fen to dismiss the troops; soon after he summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wang Fen to disband his levies, then summoned him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 芬懼，自殺。

translations.literal: Fen was afraid and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Wang Fen took his own life.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》載太祖拒芬辭曰：「夫廢立之事，天下之至不祥也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the Grand Progenitor's words of refusal to Fen: "As for the affair of deposing and enthroning, it is the most inauspicious thing under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves Cao Cao's answer to Wang Fen: "Deposing one sovereign and raising another is the darkest business a subject can touch."

sentences.zh: 古人有權成敗計輕重而行之者，伊尹、霍光是也。

translations.literal: Among the ancients there were those who weighed success and failure and calculated the balance of weight, then acted; Yi Yin and Huo Guang were such.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients who dared it—Yi Yin and Huo Guang—weighed every risk before they moved.

sentences.zh: 伊尹懷至忠之誠，據宰臣之勢，處官司之上，故進退廢置，計從事立。

translations.literal: Yi Yin embraced the utmost sincerity of loyalty, occupied a chief minister's authority, stood above the officials; therefore advancing, withdrawing, deposing, and enthroning: plans followed and undertakings succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin commanded absolute trust, held the chief minister's leverage, and stood over the bureaucracy, so his every move to install or remove a ruler carried the weight of law.

sentences.zh: 及至霍光受託國之任，藉宗臣之位，內因太后秉政之重，外有羣卿同欲之勢，昌邑即位日淺，未有貴寵，朝乏讜臣，議出密近，故計行如轉圜，事成如摧朽。

translations.literal: By the time it reached Huo Guang, he received the charge of the state's trust, relied on the position of a clan minister, inwardly had the empress dowager's weight of holding power, outwardly had the momentum of many ministers sharing the same desire; the King of Changyi had ascended the throne for few days, had not yet received noble favor, the court lacked frank ministers, deliberation came from secret intimacy; therefore plans moved like turning a wheel, success came like splitting rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang inherited a mandate to steady the realm, spoke with the authority of an imperial clansman, had the empress dowager's backing inside the palace and a bloc of ministers outside, faced a boy king with no roots in power, and could act in closed session. His coup turned as smoothly as a wheel; the old regime crumbled like dry rot.

sentences.zh: 今諸君徒見曩者之易，未覩當今之難。

translations.literal: Now you gentlemen only see the ease of former times, and have not observed the difficulty of the present.
translations.idiomatic: You are dazzled by how easy it looked in the old stories and blind to how hard it would be today.

sentences.zh: 諸君自度，結衆連黨，何若七國？

translations.literal: You gentlemen measure yourselves: in tying multitudes and connecting factions, how do you compare to the Seven States?
translations.idiomatic: Honestly weigh your coalition against the rebel kingdoms of the Han civil warare you stronger?

sentences.zh: 合肥之貴，孰若吳、楚？

translations.literal: The nobility of Hefeihow does it compare to Wu and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: Is a minor prince of Hefei as formidable as the old kingdoms of Wu and Chu?

sentences.zh: 而造作非常，欲望必克，不亦危乎！」〉

translations.literal: Yet you manufacture the extraordinary and desire certain victory—is it not perilous!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you mean to stage a coup and expect a sure win—is that not courting ruin?"

sentences.zh: 金城邊章、韓遂殺刺史郡守以叛，衆十餘萬，天下騷動。

translations.literal: Bian Zhang and Han Sui of Jincheng killed the inspector and grand administrators and rebelled; their hosts were more than a hundred thousand; the realm was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Zhang and Han Sui in Jincheng murdered their provincial superiors and rose in revolt with well over a hundred thousand followers, throwing the empire into panic.

sentences.zh: 徵太祖爲典軍校尉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was summoned to be Colonel Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was called to the capital as colonel director of the army.

sentences.zh: 會靈帝崩，太子即位，太后臨朝。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Ling died; the crown prince ascended the throne; the empress dowager held court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling died just then; the heir came to the throne while the empress dowager ruled from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 大將軍何進與袁紹謀誅宦官，太后不聽。

translations.literal: Grand General He Jin plotted with Yuan Shao to execute the palace attendants; the empress dowager would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General He Jin and Yuan Shao planned to slaughter the eunuchs, but the empress dowager blocked them.

sentences.zh: 進乃召董卓，欲以脅太后，

translations.literal: Jin thereupon summoned Dong Zhuo, intending thereby to coerce the empress dowager,
translations.idiomatic: He Jin then summoned Dong Zhuo from the west, hoping to intimidate the empress dowager into yielding,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖聞而笑之曰：「閹豎之官，古今宜有，但世主不當假之權寵，使至於此。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: When the Grand Progenitor heard this he laughed and said: "The office of the castrates has existed in every age, but the ruler ought not to have fed them such power and favor until it came to this."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Cao Cao laughed when he heard the plan: "Eunuchs are an old evil, but no sovereign should have pampered them until they grew this dangerous."

sentences.zh: 旣治其罪，當誅元惡，一獄吏足矣，何必紛紛召外將乎？

translations.literal: Having already determined their crimes, one ought to execute the chief evildoers; a single jailer would suffice—why must you in confusion summon generals from outside?
translations.idiomatic: Once their guilt is fixed, behead the ringleaders; one stern warden could do it—why drag frontier armies into the capital?"

sentences.zh: 欲盡誅之，事必宣露，吾見其敗也。」〉

translations.literal: Desiring to kill them all, the affair must be exposed; I see their defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Try to wipe out every eunuch at once and the plot will leak; I already see He Jin's downfall."

sentences.zh: 卓未至而進見殺。

translations.literal: Before Zhuo arrived, Jin was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo had not reached Luoyang when He Jin was cut down.

sentences.zh: 卓到，廢帝爲弘農王而立獻帝，京都大亂。

translations.literal: When Zhuo arrived, he deposed the emperor as King of Hongnong and established Emperor Xian; the capital region was greatly in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo entered the city, demoted the young emperor to prince of Hongnong, set Liu Xie on the throne as Emperor Xian, and plunged the capital into chaos.

sentences.zh: 卓表太祖爲驍騎校尉，欲與計事。

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized the Grand Progenitor as Colonel of Valorous Cavalry, wishing to consult with him on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo recommended Cao Cao for the post of colonel of valorous cavalry and wanted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃變易姓名，間行東歸。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon changed name and surname and by stealth traveled east to return.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao assumed a false identity and slipped away eastward toward home.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖以卓終必覆敗，遂不就拜，逃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: The Grand Progenitor, considering Zhuo would in the end surely be overturned and defeated, therefore did not accept the appointment and fled to return to his village.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei adds that Cao Cao was sure Dong Zhuo would fall, so he never took the commission and fled homeward.

sentences.zh: 從數騎過故人成臯呂伯奢；

translations.literal: Accompanied by several horsemen he passed his old friend Lü Boshe of Chenggao;
translations.idiomatic: With a handful of riders he stopped to visit his old acquaintance Lü Boshe at Chenggao;

sentences.zh: 伯奢不在，其子與賔客共劫太祖，取馬及物，太祖手刃擊殺數人。

translations.literal: Boshe was not present; his son with guests together robbed the Grand Progenitor, taking horses and goods; the Grand Progenitor with his own hand bladed and struck several to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lü was away; his son and house guests tried to rob Cao Cao of his mounts and baggage, and Cao Cao cut several of them down with his own blade.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：太祖過伯奢。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: The Grand Progenitor passed Boshe.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu offers a different version of the same visit.

sentences.zh: 伯奢出行，五子皆在，備賔主禮。

translations.literal: Boshe went traveling; all five sons were present and prepared host-guest courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Boshe was out, but his five sons were home and laid out a full guest reception.

sentences.zh: 太祖自以背卓命，疑其圖己，手劔夜殺八人而去。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor himself considered he had defied Zhuo's orders; he suspected them of plotting against him; with sword in hand by night he killed eight people and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao knew he was a fugitive from Dong Zhuo; he imagined treachery, drew his sword in the dark, slaughtered eight people, and fled.

sentences.zh: 孫盛雜記曰：太祖聞其食器聲，以爲圖己，遂夜殺之。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's miscellaneous record says: The Grand Progenitor heard the sound of their eating utensils; thinking they plotted against him, therefore by night he killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's Miscellany says he mistook the clatter of kitchenware for an ambush and murdered the household in the night.

sentences.zh: 旣而悽愴曰：「寧我負人，毋人負我！

translations.literal: Afterward he said mournfully: "Better I betray others than let others betray me!"
translations.idiomatic: Walking away in anguish, he muttered, "I would rather wrong the world than let the world wrong me!"

sentences.zh: 」遂行。〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went on.
translations.idiomatic: Then he pressed on.

sentences.zh: 出關，過中牟，爲亭長所疑，執詣縣，邑中或竊識之，爲請得解。

translations.literal: Having left the pass, passing Zhongmou, he was suspected by a village headman, seized and taken to the county; some in the town secretly recognized him and pled for him so he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the pass, at Zhongmou, a suspicious post chief arrested him; locals who quietly knew who he was interceded until the magistrate let him go.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：中牟疑是亡人，見拘於縣。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Zhongmou suspected he was a fugitive and held him in the county.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu says the county took him for a runaway and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 時掾亦已被卓書；

translations.literal: At that time the clerk had also already received Zhuo's document;
translations.idiomatic: By then the yamen staff already held Dong Zhuo's wanted notices;

sentences.zh: 唯功曹心知是太祖，以世方亂，不宜拘天下雄儁，因白令釋之。〉

translations.literal: only the merit officer in his heart knew it was the Grand Progenitor; considering the age was in chaos, one ought not restrain an outstanding hero of the realm, therefore he reported to the magistrate and released him.
translations.idiomatic: but the merit officer privately recognized Cao Cao and, arguing that these times called for heroes rather than shackles, persuaded the magistrate to release him.

sentences.zh: 卓遂殺太后及弘農王。

translations.literal: Zhuo thereupon killed the empress dowager and the King of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo then murdered the empress dowager and the deposed boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 太祖至陳留，散家財，合義兵，將以誅卓。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor arrived at Chenliu, distributed family wealth, gathered righteous troops, intending thereby to execute Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao reached Chenliu, spent his family fortune, and began recruiting a loyal army to bring down Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，始起兵於己吾，

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, he first raised troops at Jiwu,
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the twelfth month, he first raised an army at Jiwu,

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：陳留孝廉衞茲以家財資太祖，使起兵，衆有五千人。〉

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Wei Zi, filial and incorrupt of Chenliu, with family wealth supplied the Grand Progenitor, enabling him to raise troops; the host had five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu records that Wei Zi, a filial-and-incorrupt graduate of Chenliu, bankrolled Cao Cao's first levy of five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是歲中平六年也。

translations.literal: That year was the sixth year of Zhongping.
translations.idiomatic: The year was 189 CE, the sixth year of the Zhongping era.

sentences.zh: 初平元年春正月，後將軍袁術、冀州牧韓馥、

translations.literal: In the first year of Chuping, spring, first month, Rear General Yuan Shu, Governor of Ji Han Fu,
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 190 CE, the first year of Chuping, Rear General Yuan Shu, Ji Inspector Han Fu,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：馥字文節，潁川人。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: Fu's style name was Wenjie; he was a man of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes gives Han Fu's courtesy name as Wenjie and his origin as Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 爲御史中丞。

translations.literal: He served as Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He had been assistant secretary in the censorate.

sentences.zh: 董卓舉爲冀州牧。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo promoted him to be Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo named him inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 于時冀州民人殷盛，兵糧優足。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Ji province were abundant and flourishing; soldiers and grain were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was populous and rich in men and supplies.

sentences.zh: 袁紹之在勃海，馥恐其興兵，遣數部從事守之，不得動搖。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao was at Bohai, Fu feared he would raise troops; he dispatched several department clerks to watch him, not allowing him to stir.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuan Shao held Bohai, Han Fu feared he would mobilize and posted several aides to hem him in.

sentences.zh: 東郡太守橋瑁詐作京師三公移書與州郡，陳卓罪惡，云「見逼迫，無以自救，企望義兵，解國患難。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Dongjun Qiao Mao forged a dispatch from the three dukes of the capital to the provinces and commanderies, stating Zhuo's crimes and wickedness, saying, "We are compelled and pressed, unable to save ourselves; we look to righteous troops to relieve the state's peril and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Mao, governor of Dongjun, forged a circular from the capital's three excellencies denouncing Dong Zhuo and begging the provinces to march: "We are helpless in Luoyang; only a loyal coalition can save the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」馥得移，請諸從事問曰：「今當助袁氏邪，助董卓邪？

translations.literal: " When Fu obtained the dispatch, he asked the various clerks, saying, "Now ought we to aid the Yuan clan, or aid Dong Zhuo?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu read the letter and polled his staff: "Do we back the Yuans or Dong Zhuo?"

sentences.zh: 」治中從事劉子惠曰：「今興兵爲國，何謂袁、董！

translations.literal: " Liu Zihui, the headquarters clerk, said, "Now we raise troops for the state; what is this talk of Yuan and Dong!"
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters clerk Liu Zihui snapped, "We mobilize for the Han, not to pick between Yuan and Dong!"

sentences.zh: 」馥自知言短而有慙色。

translations.literal: Fu himself knew his words were short and showed a shameful color.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu flushed, knowing he had misspoken.

sentences.zh: 子惠復言：「兵者凶事，不可爲首；

translations.literal: " Zihui again said, "Soldiers are an ill omen; one cannot be first;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zihui went on, "War is a curse; no province should fire the first shot;

sentences.zh: 今宜往視他州，有發動者，然後和之。

translations.literal: now it is appropriate to go observe the other provinces; when there is one that moves, then harmonize with it.
translations.idiomatic: wait until another region moves, then fall in with the coalition."

sentences.zh: 冀州於他州不爲弱也，他人功未有在冀州之右者也。

translations.literal: Ji province compared to other provinces is not weak; others' merit is not yet to the right of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Ji is no weaker than its neighbors, and no one else has a better claim to lead."

sentences.zh: 」馥然之。

translations.literal: " Fu approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fu agreed.

sentences.zh: 馥乃作書與紹，道卓之惡，聽其舉兵。〉

translations.literal: Fu thereupon wrote a letter to Shao, stating Zhuo's wickedness, and permitted him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Yuan Shao listing Dong Zhuo's crimes and authorized him to take the field.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史孔伷、

translations.literal: Inspector of Yu Kong Zhou,
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Kong Zhou of Yu province,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：伷字公緒，陳留人。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: Zhou's style name was Gongxu; he was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes identifies Kong Zhou (courtesy Gongxu) as a native of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 張璠《漢紀》，載鄭泰說卓云：「孔公緒能清談高論，噓枯吹生。」〉

translations.literal: Zhang Fan's Han Ji, recording Zheng Tai's persuasion of Zhuo, says: "Kong Gongxu can pure-talk and high discourse, breathe life into the withered and blow life into the dead."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Han Annals quotes Zheng Tai warning Dong Zhuo that Kong Zhou is a brilliant talker who "can make the dead seem alive" with rhetoric alone.

sentences.zh: 兖州刺史劉岱、

translations.literal: Inspector of Yan Liu Dai,
translations.idiomatic: Yan Inspector Liu Dai,

sentences.zh: 〈岱，劉繇之兄，事見《吳志》。〉

translations.literal: Dai was Liu Yao's elder brother; the affair is seen in the Wu zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai was the elder brother of Liu Yao; his career is noted in the Book of Wu.

sentences.zh: 河內太守王匡、

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Henei Wang Kuang,
translations.idiomatic: Henei Governor Wang Kuang,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：匡字公節，泰山人。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: Kuang's style name was Gongjie; he was a man of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes gives Wang Kuang (courtesy Gongjie) as a man of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，以任俠聞。

translations.literal: He lightly valued wealth and liked bestowing; he was famed for knight-errantry.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-handed and famed as a brawling man of honor.

sentences.zh: 辟大將軍何進府進符使，匡於徐州發彊弩五百西詣京師。

translations.literal: He was summoned to Grand General He Jin's office as credential envoy; Kuang at Xu province raised five hundred strong crossbowmen and went west to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin recruited him as an envoy; Wang Kuang shipped five hundred crack crossbowmen from Xu toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會進敗，匡還鄉里。

translations.literal: It happened that Jin was defeated; Kuang returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin fell before they arrived, and Wang Kuang marched home.

sentences.zh: 起家，拜河內太守。

translations.literal: Rising from commoner status, he was appointed Grand Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose from private life to governor of Henei.

sentences.zh: 謝承《後漢書》曰：匡少與蔡邕善。

translations.literal: Xie Cheng's Hou Han Shu says: Kuang in youth was on good terms with Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng's Later Han History notes that Wang Kuang and Cai Yong were close in youth.

sentences.zh: 其年爲卓軍所敗，走還泰山，收集勁勇得數千人，欲與張邈合。

translations.literal: That year he was defeated by Zhuo's army, fled back to Taishan, collected stalwart braves and obtained several thousand men, wishing to join with Zhang Miao.
translations.idiomatic: That year Dong Zhuo's troops routed him; he fled to Taishan, scraped together a few thousand fighters, and meant to link up with Zhang Miao.

sentences.zh: 匡先殺執金吾胡母班。

translations.literal: Kuang first killed Chief of the Metropolitan Guards Humu Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way he murdered Chief of the Metropolitan Guards Humu Ban.

sentences.zh: 班親屬不勝憤怒，與太祖并勢，共殺匡。〉

translations.literal: Ban's kin could not overcome rage; together with the Grand Progenitor they joined forces and together killed Kuang."
translations.idiomatic: Ban's relatives, beside themselves with fury, allied with Cao Cao and put Wang Kuang to the sword."

sentences.zh: 勃海太守袁紹、陳留太守張邈、東郡太守橋瑁、

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Bohai Yuan Shao, Grand Administrator of Chenliu Zhang Miao, Grand Administrator of Dongjun Qiao Mao,
translations.idiomatic: Bohai Governor Yuan Shao, Chenliu Governor Zhang Miao, Dongjun Governor Qiao Mao,

sentences.zh: 〈《英雄記》曰：瑁字元偉，玄族子。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: Mao's style name was Yuanwei; he was a clansman's son of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes calls Qiao Mao (courtesy Yuanwei) a kinsman of Qiao Xuan.

sentences.zh: 先爲兖州刺史，甚有威惠。〉

translations.literal: Earlier he had been Inspector of Yan; he had great awe and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He had previously governed Yan with a firm but fair hand.

sentences.zh: 山陽太守袁遺、

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Shanyang Yuan Yi,
translations.idiomatic: Shanyang Governor Yuan Yi,

sentences.zh: 〈遺字伯業，紹從兄。

translations.literal: Yi's style name was Boye; he was Shao's cousin elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi (courtesy Boye) was Yuan Shao's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 爲長安令。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He had been magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 河間張超甞薦遺于太尉朱儁，稱遺「有冠世之懿，幹時之量。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao of Hejian once recommended Yi to Grand Commandant Zhu Jun, praising Yi as "having excellence surpassing the age, capacity for the times.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao of Hejian once urged Grand Commandant Zhu Jun to notice Yuan Yi, praising his "virtue above his generation and judgment fit for the age."

sentences.zh: 其忠允亮直，固天所縱；

translations.literal: His loyalty, trustworthiness, uprightness, and straightness are indeed what Heaven releases;
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty and candor are plainly heaven-given;

sentences.zh: 若乃包羅載籍，管綜百氏，登高能賦，覩物知名，求之今日，邈焉靡儔。

translations.literal: as for embracing the classics and carrying the hundred schools, ascending high and being able to rhapsodize, seeing things and knowing their namesseek him today, remote indeed, without peer.
translations.idiomatic: as for mastering the canon, surveying every school, composing fu from a height, and naming whatever he sawyou will not find his like today."

sentences.zh: 」事在超集。

translations.literal: " The affair is in Chao's collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: The full text survives in Zhang Chao's literary collection.

sentences.zh: 《英雄記》曰：紹後用遺爲揚州刺史，爲袁術所敗。

translations.literal: The Yingxiong Ji says: Shao later employed Yi as Inspector of Yang; he was defeated by Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes adds that Yuan Shao later made Yuan Yi inspector of Yang, where Yuan Shu destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱「長大而能勤學者，惟吾與袁伯業耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said, "Among those who grew up yet were able to study diligently, only I and Yuan Boye."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once remarked, "Of all the men who kept studying after they came of age, only Yuan Yi and I really kept at it."

sentences.zh: 」語在文帝《典論》。〉

translations.literal: " The words are in Emperor Wen's Dianlun."
translations.idiomatic: The remark is quoted in Emperor Wen's Treatise on Literature."

sentences.zh: 濟北相鮑信

translations.literal: Chancellor of Jibei Bao Xin
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin, chancellor of Jibei,

sentences.zh: 〈信事見子《勛傳》。〉

translations.literal: Xin's affairs are seen in his son Xun's biography.
translations.idiomatic: his career is summarized under his son Bao Xun's biography.

sentences.zh: 同時俱起兵，衆各數萬，推紹爲盟主。

translations.literal: At the same time all raised troops; each had several tens of thousands; they pushed Shao to be covenant leader.
translations.idiomatic: All rose together, each with tens of thousands of men, and chose Yuan Shao as alliance chief.

sentences.zh: 太祖行奮武將軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor acted as General Who Inspires Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao served as acting general who inspires martial might.

sentences.zh: 二月，卓聞兵起，乃徙天子都長安。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhuo heard troops had risen, therefore moved the Son of Heaven to make the capital at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Dong Zhuo learned the coalition had risen and relocated the imperial court to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 卓留屯洛陽，遂焚宮室。

translations.literal: Zhuo remained garrisoned at Luoyang, then burned the palace buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed to hold Luoyang and burned the palace quarter.

sentences.zh: 是時紹屯河內，邈、岱、瑁、遺屯酸棗，術屯南陽，伷屯潁川，馥在鄴。

translations.literal: At this time Shao was garrisoned at Henei, Miao, Dai, Mao, and Yi were garrisoned at Suanzao, Shu was garrisoned at Nanyang, Zhou was garrisoned at Yingchuan, Fu was at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao held Henei; Zhang Miao, Liu Dai, Qiao Mao, and Yuan Yi camped at Suanzao; Yuan Shu at Nanyang; Kong Zhou at Yingchuan; Han Fu remained in Ye.

sentences.zh: 卓兵彊，紹等莫敢先進。

translations.literal: Zhuo's troops were strong; Shao and the others none dared advance first.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's army was too strong for any of them to move first.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「舉義兵以誅暴亂，大衆已合，諸君何疑？

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "We raised righteous troops to punish violence and chaos; the great host has already united; why do you gentlemen hesitate?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "We took up arms to crush a tyrant; the coalition is assembled—why do you shrink from striking?"

sentences.zh: 向使董卓聞山東兵起，倚王室之重，據二周之險，東向以臨天下；

translations.literal: Supposing Dong Zhuo had heard that east-of-the-mountains troops rose, relied on the weight of the royal house, occupied the peril of the two Zhous, faced east to oversee the realm;
translations.idiomatic: If Dong Zhuo had seized the two capitals, wrapped himself in the emperor's legitimacy, and menaced the east from those fortress passes,

sentences.zh: 雖以無道行之，猶足爲患。

translations.literal: though he conducted it without the Way, still would be enough to become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: even ruling viciously he would still have been a serious threat.

sentences.zh: 今焚燒宮室，劫遷天子，海內震動，不知所歸，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Now he burns the palace buildings, coerces and shifts the Son of Heaven; within the seas there is shock and movement, not knowing where to turn; this is the time when Heaven will destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he torches Luoyang, drags the sovereign west, and leaves the empire reeling with no rallying point—this is Heaven handing us our moment.

sentences.zh: 一戰而天下定矣，不可失也。

translations.literal: One battle and the realm will be settled; it cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: One hard blow could finish him; we must not miss it.

sentences.zh: 」遂引兵西，將據成臯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops west, intending to occupy Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west to seize Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 邈遣將衞茲分兵隨太祖。

translations.literal: Miao dispatched general Wei Zi to divide troops and follow the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao detached Wei Zi with a column to accompany Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 到熒陽汴水，遇卓將徐榮，與戰不利，士卒死傷甚多。

translations.literal: Arriving at Yingyang on the Bian River, they encountered Zhuo's general Xu Rong; they battled and it was unfavorable; soldiers died and were wounded in very great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingyang on the Bian River they ran into Xu Rong; the fight went badly and casualties were heavy.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲流矢所中，所乘馬被創，從弟洪以馬與太祖，得夜遁去。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was struck by a stray arrow; the horse he rode was wounded; his cousin Hong gave his horse to the Grand Progenitor, enabling him to flee by night.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took a stray arrow and his mount was cut down; his cousin Cao Hong gave him a horse and he escaped under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 榮見太祖所將兵少，力戰盡日，謂酸棗未易攻也，亦引兵還。

translations.literal: Rong saw the Grand Progenitor's led troops were few, yet they fought strenuously a whole day; he thought Suanzao not easy to attack; also led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rong saw how few men Cao Cao had yet how fiercely they fought all day and judged Suanzao too tough a nut; he withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 太祖到酸棗，諸軍兵十餘萬，日置酒高會，不圖進取。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor arrived at Suanzao; the various armies' soldiers were more than a hundred thousand; daily they set out wine and high feasts, not planning advance.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Suanzao the allies mustered over a hundred thousand men but spent their days feasting instead of advancing.

sentences.zh: 太祖責讓之，因爲謀曰：「諸君聽吾計，使勃海引河內之衆臨孟津，酸棗諸將守成臯，據敖倉，塞轘轅、太谷，全制其險；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor rebuked them and for them planned, saying: "If you gentlemen listen to my plan, let Bohai lead Henei's multitudes to press Mengjin, let the Suanzao generals guard Chenggao, occupy Aocang, block Huanyuan and Daigu, completely control their perilous points;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao rebuked them and laid out a plan: "Let Yuan Shao from Bohai drive the Henei host against Mengjin; hold Chenggao and Aocang, plug Huanyuan and Daigu, and seal every choke point;

sentences.zh: 使袁將軍率南陽之軍軍丹、析，入武關，以震三輔：皆高壘深壁，勿與戰，益爲疑兵，示天下形勢，以順誅逆，可立定也。

translations.literal: let General Yuan Shu lead Nanyang's army to encamp at Dan and Xi, enter Wuguan, to shake the three auxiliaries: all build high ramparts and deep walls, do not battle with them, increase suspicious troops, show the realm's configuration, with the compliant punish the rebellious, can be immediately settled."
translations.idiomatic: let Yuan Shu march the Nanyang troops to Dan and Xi, punch through Wuguan, and threaten the Guanzhong heartland. Raise high walls, refuse pitched battle, feint everywhere, and show the empire that legitimacy lies with us against the usurper—peace would follow quickly."

sentences.zh: 今兵以義動，持疑而不進，失天下之望，竊爲諸君耻之！

translations.literal: Now the troops for righteousness have moved, yet hold doubt and do not advance, losing the realm's hope; I privately feel shame for you gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet here we stand, righteous banners raised, paralyzed by doubt—the whole realm is watching, and I am ashamed for you!"

sentences.zh: 」邈等不能用。

translations.literal: Miao and the others could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao and the rest ignored him.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵少，乃與夏侯惇等詣揚州募兵，刺史陳溫、丹楊太守周昕與兵四千餘人。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor's troops were few; therefore he with Xiahou Dun and others went to Yang province to recruit soldiers; Inspector Chen Wen and Danyang Grand Administrator Zhou Xin gave more than four thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Short of men, Cao Cao went with Xiahou Dun to Yang province to recruit; Inspector Chen Wen and Danyang governor Zhou Xin furnished a little over four thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 還到龍亢，士卒多叛。

translations.literal: Returning, reaching Longkang, many soldiers rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back, near Longkang, most of the recruits mutinied.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：兵謀叛，夜燒太祖帳，太祖手劔殺數十人，餘皆披靡，乃得出營；

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: the soldiers plotted rebellion, by night burned the Grand Progenitor's tent; the Grand Progenitor with sword in hand killed several tens of men; the rest all scattered; then he was able to exit the camp;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says the mutineers torched his tent at night; he cut down dozens with his sword while the rest fled, and only then broke out of the camp;

sentences.zh: 其不叛者五百餘人。〉

translations.literal: those who did not rebel were more than five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: leaving barely five hundred loyal men.

sentences.zh: 至銍、建平，復收兵得千餘人，進屯河內。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhi and Jianping, again gathered troops and obtained more than a thousand men, advanced and encamped at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhi and Jianping he scraped together another thousand-odd troops and moved to camp in Henei.

sentences.zh: 劉岱與橋瑁相惡，岱殺瑁，以王肱領東郡太守。

translations.literal: Liu Dai and Qiao Mao mutually hated each other; Dai killed Mao, and made Wang Gong acting grand administrator of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai feuded with Qiao Mao, murdered him, and installed Wang Gong as acting governor of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 袁紹與韓馥謀立幽州牧劉虞爲帝，太祖拒之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao with Han Fu plotted to establish Inspector of You Liu Yu as emperor; the Grand Progenitor refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Han Fu wanted to enthrone Liu Yu, inspector of Youzhou; Cao Cao refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載太祖荅紹曰：「董卓之罪，暴於四海，吾等合大衆興義兵，遠近莫不響應，此以義動故也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the Grand Progenitor's answer to Shao: "Dong Zhuo's crimes are exposed across the four seas; we united the great host and raised righteous troops; far and near none did not respond; this is because we moved from righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves his reply: "Dong Zhuo's guilt is known everywhere; we raised a host in the name of righteousness and the realm answered—because the cause was just.

sentences.zh: 今幼主微弱，制於姦臣，未有昌邑亡國之釁，而一旦改易，天下其孰安之？

translations.literal: Now the young lord is weak and slight, controlled by treacherous ministers; he has not the blame of Changyi's state-losing; yet one morning to change and replace himhow in the realm would anyone be settled?
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor is frail and trapped by villains, but he is no deposed King of Changyi; to swap thrones overnight would unsettle everyone under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 諸君北面，我自西向。」〉

translations.literal: You gentlemen face north; I myself face west."
translations.idiomatic: You may press north toward Youzhou; I will keep facing west against Dong Zhuo."

sentences.zh: 紹又甞得一玉印，於太祖坐中舉向其肘，太祖由是笑而惡焉。

translations.literal: Shao also once obtained a jade seal; in the Grand Progenitor's sitting place he raised it toward his elbow; the Grand Progenitor thereupon laughed and disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao once flashed a jade imperial seal at Cao Cao during a banquet; Cao Cao laughed it off and marked him as dangerous.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖大笑曰：「吾不聽汝也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: The Grand Progenitor laughed greatly and said: "I do not heed you."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Cao Cao roared with laughter and answered, "I am not listening."

sentences.zh: 」紹復使人說太祖曰：「今袁公勢盛兵彊，二子已長，天下羣英，孰踰於此？

translations.literal: Shao again sent person to persuade the Grand Progenitor: "Now Lord Yuan's momentum flourishes and troops are strong; two sons have already grown; the realm's gathered heroeswho surpasses this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent another envoy: "Lord Yuan's power is unmatched, his sons are grown, and no hero in the land surpasses him—will you not follow him?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖不應。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 由是益不直紹，圖誅滅之。〉

translations.literal: Thereby he all the more did not consider Shao upright, and plotted to exterminate him.
translations.idiomatic: He thought even less of Yuan Shao's integrity after that and began plotting his destruction.

sentences.zh: 二年春，紹、馥遂立虞爲帝，虞終不敢當。

translations.literal: Second year spring, Shao, Fu thereupon established Yu as emperor; Yu in the end did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Yuan Shao and Han Fu proclaimed Liu Yu emperor anyway; Liu Yu never dared take the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，卓還長安。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, Zhuo returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Dong Zhuo withdrew to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，袁紹脅韓馥，取冀州。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, Yuan Shao coerced Han Fu and took Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Yuan Shao bullied Han Fu out of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 黑山賊于毒、白繞、眭固等

translations.literal: Black Mountain bandits Yu Du, Bai Rao, Sui Gu and others
translations.idiomatic: The Black Mountain chiefs Yu Du, Bai Rao, Sui Gu, and company

sentences.zh: 〈眭，申隨反。〉

translations.literal: (Sui: read shen-shui fan.)
translations.idiomatic: Commentarial gloss: the surname graph Sui is read sui (fanqie spelling shen-sui).

sentences.zh: 十餘萬衆略魏郡、東郡，王肱不能禦，太祖引兵入東郡，擊白繞於濮陽，破之。

translations.literal: more than a hundred thousand hosts ravaged Wei commandery and Dong commandery; Wang Gong could not resist; the Grand Progenitor led troops into Dong commandery, attacked Bai Rao at Puyang, defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: They led over a hundred thousand men in plundering Wei and Dong commanderies. Wang Gong could not stop them, so Cao Cao entered Dong commandery, struck Bai Rao at Puyang, and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 袁紹因表太祖爲東郡太守，治東武陽。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao thereupon memorialized the Grand Progenitor as grand administrator of Dong commandery, administering from Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao then had him appointed governor of Dong commandery with his seat at Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 三年春，太祖軍頓丘，毒等攻東武陽。

translations.literal: Third year spring, the Grand Progenitor's army was at Dunqiu; Du and others attacked Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year's spring Cao Cao was at Dunqiu while Yu Du besieged Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃引兵西入山，攻毒等本屯。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon led troops west into the mountains, attacked Du and others' original encampment.
translations.idiomatic: He swung west into the hills to storm the bandits' home base instead.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：諸將皆以爲當還自救。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: the generals all thought one ought to return to save oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says every general wanted to march back to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「孫臏救趙而攻魏，耿弇欲走西安攻臨菑。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Sun Bin saved Zhao by attacking Wei; Geng Yan wished to flee Xi'an and attack Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Sun Bin relieved Zhao by striking Wei; Geng Yan saved himself by threatening Linzi while the enemy held Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 使賊聞我西而還，武陽自解也；

translations.literal: If we make the bandits hear we go west and they return, Wuyang will of itself be relieved;
translations.idiomatic: If Yu Du hears we are in the mountains and pulls back, Dongwuyang lifts the siege by itself;

sentences.zh: 不還，我能敗其本屯，虜不能拔武陽必矣。

translations.literal: if they do not return, I can defeat their original encampment; the bandits cannot capture Wuyang for certain."
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses to turn, I crush his base and he still cannot take Dongwuyang."

sentences.zh: 」遂乃行。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he went.
translations.idiomatic: He marched as planned.

sentences.zh: 毒聞之，棄武陽還。

translations.literal: Du heard it, abandoned Wuyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Du heard and abandoned the siege to race home.

sentences.zh: 太祖要擊眭固，又擊匈奴於夫羅於內黃，皆大破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor intercepted and attacked Sui Gu, again attacked the Xiongnu Yufuluo at Neihuang, both greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ambushed Sui Gu, then smashed the Xiongnu chieftain Yufuluo at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：於夫羅者，南單于子也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: Yufuluo was the Southern Shanyu's son.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei identifies Yufuluo as a son of the southern Xiongnu shanyu.

sentences.zh: 中平中，發匈奴兵，於夫羅率以助漢。

translations.literal: In the Zhongping era, they mobilized Xiongnu troops; Yufuluo led them to assist Han.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhongping era the court called out Xiongnu auxiliaries, and Yufuluo led his contingent to aid the Han.

sentences.zh: 會本國反，殺南單于，於夫羅遂將其衆留中國。

translations.literal: It happened that his native state rebelled and killed the Southern Shanyu; Yufuluo thereupon led his host to remain in the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion at home killed the shanyu, Yufuluo kept his warriors in China instead of returning.

sentences.zh: 因天下撓亂，與西河白波賊合，破太原、河內，抄略諸郡爲寇。〉

translations.literal: Because the realm was in turmoil and chaos, he joined with the Xihe White Wave bandits, broke Taiyuan and Henei, raided and plundered the various commanderies and acted as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire unraveled he merged with the White Wave rebels of Xihe, ravaged Taiyuan and Henei, and raided commanderies across the north.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，司徒王允與呂布共殺卓。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, Minister of Education Wang Yun together with Lü Bu jointly killed Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Minister Wang Yun and Lü Bu assassinated Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓將李傕、郭汜等殺允攻布，布敗，東出武關。

translations.literal: Zhuo's generals Li Jue, Guo Si, and others killed Yun and attacked Bu; Bu was defeated, went out east through Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's generals Li Jue and Guo Si struck back, killed Wang Yun, and drove Lü Bu east through Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 傕等擅朝政。

translations.literal: Jue and the others monopolized court government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue and his clique seized control of the government.

sentences.zh: 青州黃巾衆百萬入兖州，殺任城相鄭遂，轉入東平。

translations.literal: Qingzhou Yellow Turbans, a host of a million, entered Yan province, killed Rencheng Chancellor Zheng Sui, turned and entered Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: A Qingzhou Yellow Turban horde said to number a million poured into Yan, killed Rencheng's chancellor Zheng Sui, and rolled on toward Dongping.

sentences.zh: 劉岱欲擊之，鮑信諫曰：「今賊衆百萬，百姓皆震恐，士卒無鬬志，不可敵也。

translations.literal: Liu Dai wished to strike them; Bao Xin remonstrated, saying: "Now the bandits' host is a million; the hundred surnames all are shaken in fear; the soldiers have no fighting will; they cannot be opposed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai wanted to attack at once. Bao Xin warned, "They number a million, the people are terrified, and our men have no stomach for a stand-up fight."

sentences.zh: 觀賊衆羣輩相隨，軍無輜重，唯以鈔略爲資，今不若畜士衆之力，先爲固守。

translations.literal: Observe the bandits' multitudes following one another in groups; the army has no baggage train; they rely only on raiding for supplies; now it is not as good as storing the strength of gentlemen and troops, first making firm defense.
translations.idiomatic: Look at how they swarm without wagons or grain trains, living entirely on plunder. Better husband our strength and dig in behind solid walls.

sentences.zh: 彼欲戰不得，攻又不能，其勢必離散，後選精銳，據其要害，擊之可破也。

translations.literal: They will desire battle yet not obtain it, attack yet not be able; their momentum must scatter and separate; afterward select crack troops, occupy their vital points, strike them and can defeat them."
translations.idiomatic: Denied battle, unable to storm us, they will fall apart; then we can sortie with picked troops at the decisive point and break them."

sentences.zh: 」岱不從，遂與戰，果爲所殺。

translations.literal: " Dai did not follow; thereupon battled with them; indeed was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai refused, gave battle, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：岱旣死，陳宮謂太祖曰：「州今無主，而王命斷絕，宮請說州中，明府尋往牧之，資之以收天下，此霸王之業也。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: After Dai had died, Gong Chen said to the Grand Progenitor: "The province now has no lord, while royal commands are cut off; Gong requests to persuade those within the province; your enlightened office may then go and shepherd it, relying on it to gather the realm; this is hegemon-king enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu says that after Liu Dai fell, Chen Gong told Cao Cao, "Yan has no governor and the court cannot speak; let me rally the province behind you as its shepherd and you can use it to reunify the empire."

sentences.zh: 」宮說別駕、治中曰：「今天下分裂而州無主；

translations.literal: " Gong persuaded the chief clerk and headquarters clerk, saying: "Now the realm is split apart yet the province has no lord;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong urged the staff: "The empire is shattered and Yan has no leader;

sentences.zh: 曹東郡，命世之才也，若迎以牧州，必寧生民。

translations.literal: Cao of Dong commandery is a man of the age's destiny; if you welcome him to shepherd the province, he is sure to bring peace to the living people."
