translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao of Dong commandery is the man for this hour; make him inspector and he will bring the people peace."

sentences.zh: 」鮑信等亦謂之然。〉

translations.literal: Bao Xin and others also said it was so.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin and the others agreed.

sentences.zh: 信乃與州吏萬潛等至東郡迎太祖領兖州牧。

translations.literal: Xin thereupon with provincial clerk Wan Qian and others arrived at Dongjun to welcome the Grand Progenitor to act as shepherd of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin went with Wan Qian and other officials to Dongjun and invited Cao Cao to become inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 遂進兵擊黃巾於壽張東。

translations.literal: Thereupon advanced troops and attacked the Yellow Turbans east of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched against the Yellow Turbans east of Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 信力戰鬬死，僅而破之。

translations.literal: Xin fought strenuously and died in battle; barely thereby defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin died fighting hard; Cao Cao only barely won.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖將步騎千餘人，行視戰地，卒抵賊營，戰不利，死者數百人，引還。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: The Grand Progenitor led infantry and cavalry more than a thousand men, went to inspect the battleground, suddenly reached the bandits' camp; battle was unfavorable; several hundred died; drew back.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says he reconnoitered with a thousand-odd horse and foot, blundered into the enemy camp, lost several hundred men in a sharp skirmish, and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 賊尋前進。

translations.literal: The bandits soon advanced forward.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 黃巾爲賊久，數乘勝，兵皆精悍。

translations.literal: The Yellow Turbans had long been bandits; repeatedly they rode victory; the soldiers were all crack and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran rebels, they had won so often that every man fought like a picked warrior.

sentences.zh: 太祖舊兵少，新兵不習練，舉軍皆懼。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor's old troops were few; new troops were not practiced and drilled; the whole army was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's core troops were few, his recruits green, and the whole army was rattled.

sentences.zh: 太祖被甲嬰冑，親巡將士，明勸賞罰，衆乃復奮，承間討擊，賊稍折退。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor donned armor and put on helmet, personally inspected the generals and soldiers, clearly encouraging rewards and punishments; the host then again roused; taking advantage of intervals he attacked and struck; the bandits little by little bent and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: He donned armor, toured the lines in person, spelled out rewards and penalties, and steadied the men until they rallied; probing attacks gradually forced the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 賊乃移書太祖曰：「昔在濟南，毀壞神壇，其道乃與中黃太一同，似若知道，今更迷惑。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon sent a letter to the Grand Progenitor saying: "In the past at Jinan you destroyed spirit altars; your Way then was the same as the Central Yellow Grand Unity; it seemed as if you knew the Way; now again you are deluded.
translations.idiomatic: They sent him a letter: "At Jinan you smashed our shrines; your teaching then matched the Central Yellow Unity sectyou seemed to understand the Way, yet now you oppose Heaven."

sentences.zh: 漢行已盡，黃家當立。

translations.literal: Han's line has already ended; the Yellow House ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: The Han mandate is spent; the Yellow Heaven must rise."

sentences.zh: 天之大運，非君才力所能存也。

translations.literal: Heaven's great turning fortune is not something your lord's talent and strength can preserve.
translations.idiomatic: The great wheel of fate is not something your talents can hold back."

sentences.zh: 」太祖見檄書，呵之罪，數開示降路；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor saw the proclamation letter, shouted at their crimes, repeatedly opened and showed the road of surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ridiculed the manifesto, denounced their crimes, and kept offering terms of surrender;

sentences.zh: 遂設奇伏，晝夜會戰，戰輙禽獲，賊乃退走。〉

translations.literal: thereupon set strange ambushes, day and night joined battle; each battle then captured; the bandits thereupon retreated and fled."
translations.idiomatic: then laid ambushes, fought round the clock, took prisoners in every clash, and drove the rebels into full retreat."

sentences.zh: 購求信喪不得，衆乃刻木如信形狀，祭而哭焉。

translations.literal: They sought Xin's corpse but could not obtain it; the host thereupon carved wood in the shape of Xin's body, sacrificed and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xin's body was never found, so the army carved a wooden effigy, offered sacrifice, and mourned him.

sentences.zh: 追黃巾至濟北。

translations.literal: They pursued the Yellow Turbans to Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: They chased the Yellow Turbans into Jibei.

sentences.zh: 乞降。

translations.literal: They begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels asked to capitulate.

sentences.zh: 冬，受降卒三十餘萬，男女百餘萬口，收其精銳者，號爲青州兵。

translations.literal: In winter, received surrendering soldiers more than three hundred thousand, male and female more than a million mouths, gathered their crack and picked, titled them Qingzhou Troops.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he accepted over three hundred thousand soldiers and more than a million civilians, enrolled the best fighters, and organized them as the famed Qingzhou Army.

sentences.zh: 袁術與紹有隙，術求援於公孫瓚，瓚使劉備屯高唐，單經屯平原，陶謙屯發干，以逼紹。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu had a rift with Shao; Shu sought aid from Gongsun Zan; Zan made Liu Bei encamp at Gaotang, Shan Jing encamp at Pingyuan, Tao Qian encamp at Fagan, to press Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu quarreled with Yuan Shao and begged Gongsun Zan for help; Zan posted Liu Bei at Gaotang, Shan Jing at Pingyuan, and Tao Qian at Fagan to squeeze Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 太祖與紹會擊，皆破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor with Shao joined in striking; all defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao and Yuan Shao attacked together and broke every thrust.

sentences.zh: 四年春，軍鄄城。

translations.literal: Fourth year spring, the army was at Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year his headquarters lay at Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 荊州牧劉表斷術糧道，術引軍入陳留，屯封丘，黑山餘賊及於夫羅等佐之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Liu Biao cut Shu's grain road; Shu led the army into Chenliu, encamped at Fengqiu; Black Mountain remnant bandits and Yufuluo and others assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao, inspector of Jingzhou, severed Yuan Shu's supply lines, so Yuan Shu drove into Chenliu and camped at Fengqiu with Black Mountain remnants and Yufuluo in support.

sentences.zh: 術使將劉詳屯匡亭。

translations.literal: Shu made general Liu Xiang encamp at Kuangting.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed Liu Xiang at Kuangting.

sentences.zh: 太祖擊詳，術救之，與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor attacked Xiang; Shu rescued him; they battled; greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao struck Liu Xiang; when Yuan Shu tried to relieve him, Cao Cao routed him badly.

sentences.zh: 術退保封丘，遂圍之，未合，術走襄邑，追到太壽，決渠水灌城。

translations.literal: Shu retreated to defend Fengqiu; thereupon besieged him; before the encirclement closed, Shu fled to Xiangyi; pursued to Taishou, opened a canal and poured water to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu fell back to Fengqiu; Cao Cao besieged him, but before the ring closed Yuan fled to Xiangyi; Cao Cao chased him to Taishou and broke a dyke to flood the town.

sentences.zh: 走寧陵，又追之，走九江。

translations.literal: He fled to Ningling; again pursued him; he fled to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan ran to Ningling, then to Jiujiang under pursuit.

sentences.zh: 夏，太祖還軍定陶。

translations.literal: Summer, the Grand Progenitor returned the army to Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Cao Cao withdrew his army to Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 下邳闕宣聚衆數千人，自稱天子；

translations.literal: Que Xuan of Xiapi gathered a multitude of several thousand men, called himself Son of Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Que Xuan of Xiapi raised a few thousand followers and declared himself emperor;

sentences.zh: 徐州牧陶謙與共舉兵，取泰山華、費，略任城。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Shepherd Tao Qian together with him jointly raised troops, took Mount Tai's Hua and Fei, ravaged Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou governor Tao Qian joined him, seized Hua and Fei in Taishan, and raided Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，太祖征陶謙，下十餘城，謙守城不敢出。

translations.literal: Autumn, the Grand Progenitor campaigned against Tao Qian, took more than ten cities; Qian guarded the city and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Cao Cao invaded Tao Qian, captured over ten towns, and penned him up behind his walls.

sentences.zh: 是歲，孫策受袁術使渡江，數年閒遂有江東。

translations.literal: That year, Sun Ce received Yuan Shu's orders to cross the Yangzi; within several years then possessed Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Sun Ce crossed the Yangzi on Yuan Shu's orders and within a few years held the lands south of the river.

sentences.zh: 興平元年春，太祖自徐州還，初，太祖父嵩去官後還譙，董卓之亂，避難琅邪，爲陶謙所害，故太祖志在復讎東伐。

translations.literal: First year of Xingping, spring, the Grand Progenitor returned from Xuzhou; earlier, the Grand Progenitor's father Song, after leaving office, returned to Qiao; in Dong Zhuo's turmoil, he took refuge in Langye and was harmed by Tao Qian; therefore the Grand Progenitor's intent was to revenge eastward campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xingping 194 Cao Cao marched back from Xuzhou. His father Cao Song had retired to Qiao, fled the Dong Zhuo turmoil to Langye, and died at Tao Qian's hands, so Cao Cao's eastern campaigns were driven by vengeance.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：嵩在泰山華縣。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Song was in Taishan county Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu places Cao Song at Hua county in Taishan.

sentences.zh: 太祖令泰山太守應劭送家詣兖州，劭兵未至，陶謙密遣數千騎掩捕。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered Taishan Grand Administrator Ying Shao to escort the family to Yan province; Shao's troops had not yet arrived; Tao Qian secretly dispatched several thousand riders to seize them by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao told Taishan governor Ying Shao to escort the family into Yan, but before Ying Shao arrived Tao Qian sent several thousand horsemen on a secret raid.

sentences.zh: 嵩家以爲劭迎，不設備。

translations.literal: Song's household thought Shao was welcoming them; they did not set preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao household mistook them for Ying Shao's escort and let their guard down.

sentences.zh: 謙兵至，殺太祖弟德於門中。

translations.literal: Qian's troops arrived and killed the Grand Progenitor's younger brother De inside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian's men arrived and cut down Cao Cao's brother Cao De in the doorway.

sentences.zh: 嵩懼，穿後垣，先出其妾，妾肥，不時得出；

translations.literal: Song was afraid, bored through the rear wall, first sent out his concubine; the concubine was fat and could not in time get out;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song panicked, broke through the back wall, and tried to push his plump concubine out first; she stuck in the breach;

sentences.zh: 嵩逃于厠，與妾俱被害，闔門皆死。

translations.literal: Song fled to the privy; together with the concubine both were killed; the whole household died.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song hid in the latrine with her and both were butchered; the entire household perished.

sentences.zh: 劭懼，棄官赴袁紹。

translations.literal: Shao was afraid, abandoned office and went to Yuan Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao fled his post and threw in with Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 後太祖定冀州，劭時已死。

translations.literal: Later when the Grand Progenitor settled Ji province, Shao had already died.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Cao Cao conquered Ji, Ying Shao was already dead.

sentences.zh: 韋曜《吳書》曰：太祖迎嵩，輜重百餘兩。

translations.literal: Wei Yao's Wu Shu says: The Grand Progenitor welcomed Song with more than a hundred baggage carts.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao's Book of Wu records that Cao Song traveled with over a hundred wagonloads of luggage.

sentences.zh: 陶謙遣都尉張闓將騎二百衞送，闓於泰山華、費間殺嵩，取財物，因奔淮南。

translations.literal: Tao Qian dispatched commandant Zhang Kai leading two hundred riders to escort and guard; Kai between Taishan's Hua and Fei killed Song, took goods and wealth, then fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian sent Commandant Zhang Kai with two hundred horsemen as escort; between Hua and Fei in Taishan, Zhang Kai murdered Cao Song for his treasure and bolted to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 太祖歸咎於陶謙，故伐之。〉

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor blamed Tao Qian; therefore he campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao blamed Tao Qian anyway and used it as the pretext for war.

sentences.zh: 夏，使荀彧、程昱守鄄城，復征陶謙，拔五城，遂略地至東海。

translations.literal: In summer he ordered Xun Yu and Cheng Yu to guard Juancheng, again campaigned against Tao Qian, took five cities, then ravaged the land reaching Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he left Xun Yu and Cheng Yu to hold Juancheng while he struck Tao Qian again, seized five towns, and swept eastward into Donghai.

sentences.zh: 還過郯，謙將曹豹與劉備屯郯東，要太祖。

translations.literal: Returning, passing Tan, Qian's general Cao Bao with Liu Bei encamped east of Tan, intercepted the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: On the way back past Tan, Tao Qian's general Cao Bao and Liu Bei blocked the road east of the city.

sentences.zh: 太祖擊破之，遂攻拔襄賁，所過多所殘戮。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor broke them, then attacked and took Xiangben; wherever he passed there was much slaughter and massacre.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao smashed their line, stormed Xiangben, and left a trail of atrocities across the countryside.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫伐罪弔民，古之令軌；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: As for punishing crimes and comforting the people, that is the ancient good norm;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observes that punishing the guilty while sparing the innocent is the classical standard of conquest;

sentences.zh: 罪謙之由，而殘其屬部，過矣。〉

translations.literal: the crime was Qian's cause, yet to mutilate his subordinate departments is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian was the culprit, yet massacring his people was going too far.

sentences.zh: 會張邈與陳宮叛迎呂布，郡縣皆應。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Miao with Chen Gong rebelled and welcomed Lü Bu; commanderies and counties all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhang Miao and Chen Gong mutinied, opened Yan to Lü Bu, and the whole province flipped.

sentences.zh: 荀彧、程昱保鄄城，范、東阿二縣固守，太祖乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Xun Yu and Cheng Yu protected Juancheng; Fan and Dong'e two counties firmly defended; the Grand Progenitor thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu and Cheng Yu held Juancheng while Fan and Dong'e counties stood fast, allowing Cao Cao to wheel his army homeward.

sentences.zh: 布到，攻鄄城不能下，西屯濮陽。

translations.literal: When Bu arrived, he attacked Juancheng but could not take it, then encamped west at Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu besieged Juancheng without success, then shifted west to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「布一旦得一州，不能據東平，斷亢父、泰山之道，乘險要我，而乃屯濮陽，吾知其無能爲也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "Bu in one morning obtained one province; he could not occupy Dongping, cut the roads of Kangfu and Taishan, exploit the peril to intercept me, but instead encamps at Puyang; I know he is incapable of achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Lü Bu seized a province overnight yet failed to seal Dongping, block Kangfu and Taishan, and ambush me in the defiles; instead he sits in Puyang. That tells me he is no strategist."

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍攻之。

translations.literal: Thereupon advanced the army and attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 布出兵戰，先以騎犯青州兵。

translations.literal: Bu sent out troops to battle, first using cavalry to strike the Qingzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu sortied and led his horse first against the Qingzhou Army.

sentences.zh: 青州兵奔，太祖陳亂馳突火出，墜馬，燒左手掌。

translations.literal: The Qingzhou troops fled; the Grand Progenitor's formation was in chaos; he charged through fire, fell from a horse, burned the palm of the left hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Qingzhou men broke; Cao Cao's line collapsed; he charged through flames, was thrown, and scorched his left palm.

sentences.zh: 司馬樓異扶太祖上馬，遂引去。

translations.literal: Marshal Lou Yi helped the Grand Progenitor mount a horse; thereupon led away.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Lou Yi hoisted him onto a horse and they rode clear.

sentences.zh: 〈袁暐《獻帝春秋》曰：太祖圍濮陽，濮陽大姓田氏爲反閒，太祖得入城。

translations.literal: Yuan Wei's Annals of Emperor Xian says: The Grand Progenitor besieged Puyang; a great clan of Puyang, the Tian family, acted as double agents; the Grand Progenitor was able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei's chronicle says the Tian clan of Puyang feigned defection and lured Cao Cao inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 燒其東門，示無反意。

translations.literal: They burned its east gate, showing no intent to turn back.
translations.idiomatic: They torched the east gate to signal there would be no turning back.

sentences.zh: 及戰，軍敗。

translations.literal: When battle came, the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the trap sprang, Cao Cao's force was routed.

sentences.zh: 布騎得太祖而不知是，問曰：「曹操何在？

translations.literal: Bu's riders seized the Grand Progenitor but did not know it was he; they asked, "Where is Cao Cao?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu's horsemen seized Cao Cao without recognizing him and demanded, "Where is Cao Cao?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「乘黃馬走者是也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "The one who rides the yellow horse fleeing is he."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao pointed at another rider: "The man on the dun horse—that is Cao Cao."

sentences.zh: 」布騎乃釋太祖而追黃馬者。

translations.literal: Bu's riders thereupon released the Grand Progenitor and pursued the yellow horse rider.
translations.idiomatic: They let him go and galloped after the decoy.

sentences.zh: 門火猶盛，太祖突火而出。〉

translations.literal: The gate fire was still fierce; the Grand Progenitor burst through fire and went out.
translations.idiomatic: With the gate still blazing, he punched back through the flames and escaped.

sentences.zh: 未至營止，諸將未與太祖相見，皆怖。

translations.literal: Before reaching camp to stop, the generals had not yet seen the Grand Progenitor; all were frightened.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached headquarters his officers, not having seen him return, were terrified.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃自力勞軍，令軍中促爲攻具，進復攻之，與布相守百餘日。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon by his own effort encouraged the army, ordered the army to hurry making siege equipment, advanced again to attack him, and with Bu held each other more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the men in person, ordered siege gear rushed forward, and settled into a hundred-day standoff with Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 蝗蟲起，百姓大餓，布糧食亦盡，各引去。

translations.literal: Locusts arose; the hundred surnames were greatly hungry; Bu's grain and food also were exhausted; each led away.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts devoured the crops, the people starved, Lü Bu ran out of grain, and both sides drew apart.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，太祖還鄄城。

translations.literal: Autumn ninth month, the Grand Progenitor returned to Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn he withdrew to Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 布到乘氏，爲其縣人李進所破，東屯山陽。

translations.literal: Bu arrived at Chengshi, was broken by his townsman Li Jin of that county, encamped east at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu pulled into Chengshi, where local magnate Li Jin defeated him, so he fell back east to Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 於是紹使人說太祖，欲連和。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shao sent person to persuade the Grand Progenitor, desiring to join in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao then sent envoys seeking an alliance.

sentences.zh: 太祖新失兖州，軍食盡，將許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had newly lost Yan province; army food was exhausted; he was about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from losing Yan and out of supplies, Cao Cao was ready to agree.

sentences.zh: 程昱止太祖，太祖從之。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu stopped the Grand Progenitor; the Grand Progenitor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu talked him out of it, and he listened.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，太祖至東阿。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the Grand Progenitor arrived at Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he reached Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 是歲穀一斛五十餘萬錢，人相食，乃罷吏兵新募者。

translations.literal: That year grain one hu was more than five hundred thousand cash; people ate each other; therefore dismissed clerks and soldiers newly recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Grain hit five hundred thousand cash a hu; cannibalism appeared; he had to disband newly raised units.

sentences.zh: 陶謙死，劉備代之。

translations.literal: Tao Qian died; Liu Bei replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao Qian died, Liu Bei took Xuzhou in his place.

sentences.zh: 二年春，襲定陶。

translations.literal: Second year spring, raided Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he struck Dingtao by surprise.

sentences.zh: 濟陰太守吳資保南城，未拔。

translations.literal: Jiyin Grand Administrator Wu Zi protected the south city; it was not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin governor Wu Zi held the southern citadel and Cao Cao could not crack it.

sentences.zh: 會呂布至，又擊破之。

translations.literal: It happened that Lü Bu arrived; again broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lü Bu arrived and Cao Cao defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 夏，布將薛蘭、李封屯鉅野，太祖攻之，布救蘭，蘭敗，布走，遂斬蘭等。

translations.literal: In summer Bu's generals Xue Lan and Li Feng encamped at Juye; the Grand Progenitor attacked them; Bu rescued Lan; Lan was defeated; Bu fled; thereupon beheaded Lan and others.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Lü Bu's generals Xue Lan and Li Feng camped at Juye; Cao Cao attacked, Lü Bu tried to relieve them, Xue Lan fell, Lü Bu ran, and Cao Cao beheaded Lan and his officers.

sentences.zh: 布復從東緍與陳宮將萬餘人來戰，時太祖兵少，設伏，縱奇兵擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Bu again from Dongmin with Chen Gong led more than ten thousand men to come battle; at that time the Grand Progenitor's troops were few; he set ambushes, released strange troops to strike, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu returned from Dongmin with Chen Gong and ten thousand men; outnumbered, Cao Cao laid ambushes and routed them with a sudden strike.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：於是兵皆出取麥，在者不能千人，屯營不固。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: At this time the soldiers all went out to take wheat; those who remained could not reach a thousand men; the encampment was not firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that most men were out harvesting wheat, fewer than a thousand remained in camp, and the palisade was weak.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃令婦人守陴，悉兵拒之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon ordered women to guard the parapet, used all troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: He put women on the walls with every able fighter left in line.

sentences.zh: 屯西有大隄，其南樹木幽深。

translations.literal: West of the encampment there was a great dyke; south of it the trees were deep and dark.
translations.idiomatic: West of camp ran a long embankment with a dark wood to the south.

sentences.zh: 布疑有伏，乃相謂曰：「曹操多譎，勿入伏中。

translations.literal: Bu suspected there were ambushes; therefore they said to each other: "Cao Cao is full of stratagems; do not enter among ambushes."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu smelled a trap and warned his men, "Cao Cao is a trickster; do not march into an ambush."

sentences.zh: 」引軍屯南十餘里。

translations.literal: He led the army and encamped more than ten li south.
translations.idiomatic: He halted his host more than ten li to the south.

sentences.zh: 明日復來，太祖隱兵隄裏，出半兵隄外。

translations.literal: The next day they came again; the Grand Progenitor hid troops inside the dyke, sent out half the troops outside the dyke.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Cao Cao hid the bulk of his force behind the dyke and showed only half beyond it.

sentences.zh: 布益進，乃令輕兵挑戰，旣合，伏兵乃悉乘隄，步騎並進，大破之，獲其龍車，追至其營而還。〉

translations.literal: Bu advanced further; thereupon he ordered light troops to challenge; when they had joined, the ambush troops then all rode the dyke; infantry and cavalry advanced together; greatly defeated them, captured his dragon cart, pursued to his camp and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu pushed closer; Cao Cao sent skirmishers to draw him in, then unleashed the men hidden on the dyke in a combined arms rush, captured Lü Bu's command chariot, and chased him to his camp before pulling back.

sentences.zh: 布夜走，太祖復攻，拔定陶，分兵平諸縣。

translations.literal: Bu fled by night; the Grand Progenitor again attacked, took Dingtao, divided troops and pacified the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu fled by night; Cao Cao retook Dingtao, then detached columns to secure the county seats.

sentences.zh: 布東奔劉備，張邈從布，使其弟超將家屬保雍丘。

translations.literal: Bu fled east to Liu Bei; Zhang Miao followed Bu, made his younger brother Chao lead family dependents to defend Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu ran east to Liu Bei; Zhang Miao went with him and posted his brother Zhang Chao to defend Yongqiu with the families.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，圍雍丘。

translations.literal: Autumn eighth month, besieged Yongqiu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he invested Yongqiu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，天子拜太祖兖州牧。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the Son of Heaven appointed the Grand Progenitor shepherd of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the emperor formally named him inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，雍丘潰，超自殺。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Yongqiu collapsed; Chao killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Yongqiu fell; Zhang Chao committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 夷邈三族。

translations.literal: Exterminated Miao's three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao's three degrees of kin were extirpated.

sentences.zh: 邈詣袁術請救，爲其衆所殺，兖州平，遂東略陳地。

translations.literal: Miao went to Yuan Shu to beg rescue, was killed by his host; Yan province was pacified; thereupon raided east and took Chen territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Miao begged Yuan Shu for aid and was murdered by Shu's men; with Yan pacified, Cao Cao swept east into Chen.

sentences.zh: 是歲，長安亂，天子東遷，敗于曹陽，渡河幸安邑。

translations.literal: That year Chang'an was in chaos; the Son of Heaven moved east, was defeated at Caoyang, crossed the river and favored Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Luoyang-Chang'an convulsed; the emperor fled east, was beaten at Caoyang, crossed the Yellow River, and found refuge at Anyi.

sentences.zh: 太祖將迎天子，諸將或疑，荀彧、程昱勸之，乃遣曹洪將兵西迎，衞將軍董承與袁術將萇奴拒險，洪不得進。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was about to welcome the Son of Heaven; some generals doubted; Xun Yu and Cheng Yu urged him; therefore he dispatched Cao Hong leading troops west to welcome; Guards General Dong Cheng with Yuan Shu's general Chang Nu blocked the perilous passes; Hong could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao meant to escort the emperor west; some generals hesitated until Xun Yu and Cheng Yu pressed the case. He sent Cao Hong west, but Guards General Dong Cheng and Yuan Shu's general Chang Nu held the defiles and blocked him.

sentences.zh: 汝南、潁川黃巾何儀、劉辟、黃邵、何曼等，衆各數萬，初應袁術，又附孫堅。

translations.literal: Runan and Yingchuan Yellow Turbans He Yi, Liu Pi, Huang Shao, He Man and others, each host several tens of thousands, at first responded to Yuan Shu, again attached to Sun Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Bands under He Yi, Liu Pi, Huang Shao, He Man, and others mustered tens of thousands each in Runan and Yingchuan, having first answered Yuan Shu and then thrown in with Sun Jian's camp in the south.

sentences.zh: 二月，太祖進軍討破之，斬辟、邵等，儀及其衆皆降。

translations.literal: Second month, the Grand Progenitor advanced the army, campaigned against and defeated them, beheaded Pi, Shao, and others; Yi and his host all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Cao Cao marched against them, killed Liu Pi and Huang Shao, and accepted He Yi's surrender.

sentences.zh: 天子拜太祖建德將軍，夏六月，遷鎮東將軍，封費亭侯。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven appointed the Grand Progenitor General Who Establishes Virtue; summer sixth month, promoted to General Who Guards the East, enfeoffed as Marquis of Feiting.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him General Who Establishes Virtue, then in the sixth month of summer promoted him to general who guards the east and enfeoffed him at Feiting.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，楊奉、韓暹以天子還洛陽，

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, Yang Feng and Han Xian brought the Son of Heaven back to Luoyang,
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Yang Feng and Han Xian escorted the emperor back toward Luoyang,

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：天子初至洛陽，幸城西故中常侍趙忠宅。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: When the Son of Heaven first arrived at Luoyang, he favored the west city's former regular attendant Zhao Zhong's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicle says the emperor first lodged in the old mansion of the eunuch Zhao Zhong in Luoyang's west ward.

sentences.zh: 使張楊繕治宮室，名殿曰揚安殿，八月，帝乃遷居。〉

translations.literal: He made Zhang Yang repair the palace buildings, named a hall Yang'an Hall; eighth month, the emperor then moved residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang was told to patch up the halls, naming one the Hall of Yang'an; in the eighth month the court moved in.

sentences.zh: 奉別屯梁。

translations.literal: Feng separately encamped at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Feng camped separately at Liang.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂至洛陽，衞京都，暹遁走。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon arrived at Luoyang, guarded the capital region; Xian fled and ran.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao entered Luoyang to secure the capital while Han Xian bolted.

sentences.zh: 天子假太祖節鉞，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven lent the Grand Progenitor the tally and axe, recorded Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor invested him with the ceremonial axe and authority over the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝紀》曰：又領司隷校尉。〉

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: Also led Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial diary adds that he also took the colonel director of retainers post.

sentences.zh: 洛陽殘破，董昭等勸太祖都許。

translations.literal: Luoyang was ruined and broken; Dong Zhao and others urged the Grand Progenitor to make the capital at Xu.
translations.idiomatic: With Luoyang in ruins, Dong Zhao and others urged him to move the seat to Xu.

sentences.zh: 九月，車駕出轘轅而東，以太祖爲大將軍，封武平侯。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the imperial carriage exited Huanyuan and went east; appointed the Grand Progenitor Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the court passed east through Huanyuan, named Cao Cao grand commandant, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Wuping.

sentences.zh: 自天子西遷，朝廷日亂，至是宗廟社稷制度始立。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven's west shift, the court daily grew chaotic; down to this the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain system began to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's flight west the government had unraveled; only now were rites for the state shrines properly restored.

sentences.zh: 〈張璠《漢紀》曰：初，天子敗於曹陽，欲浮河東下。

translations.literal: Zhang Fan's Han Ji says: At first, when the Son of Heaven was defeated at Caoyang, he wished to float the Yellow River east downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fan's Han Annals says that after Caoyang the emperor first meant to ride the Yellow River downstream toward the east.

sentences.zh: 侍中太史令王立曰：「自去春太白犯鎮星於牛斗，過天津，熒惑又逆行守北河，不可犯也。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Grand Clerk Wang Li said: "From last spring the Grand White encroached on the Station Star in Ox and Dipper, passed the Ford of Heaven; the Sparkling Deluder again retrograded and guarded the North River; it cannot be violated."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant and grand astrologer Wang Li warned that Venus had overtaken Saturn in the Dipper, crossed the Celestial Ford, and Mars was retrograde at the North Riverall signs that a northern crossing was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」由是天子遂不北渡河，將自軹關東出。

translations.literal: " Thereby the Son of Heaven then did not cross north the Yellow River, was about to exit east from Zhiguan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore gave up crossing the river north and prepared to leave east through Zhiguan.

sentences.zh: 立又謂宗正劉艾曰：「前太白守天關，與熒惑會；

translations.literal: Li again said to Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ai: "Earlier the Grand White guarded the Celestial Pass and met the Sparkling Deluder;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Li also told Liu Ai, director of the imperial clan, "Venus had already lingered at the Celestial Gate and conjoined Mars;

sentences.zh: 金火交會，革命之象也。

translations.literal: metal and fire meeting is the image of dynastic change.
translations.idiomatic: a conjunction of metal and fire portends revolution."

sentences.zh: 漢祚終矣，晉、魏必有興者。

translations.literal: Han's fortune is ended; Jin and Wei must have those who will rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Han mandate is spent; Jin or Wei will produce the next power."

sentences.zh: 」立後數言於帝曰：「天命有去就，五行不常盛，代火者土也，承漢者魏也，能安天下者，曹姓也，唯委任曹氏而已。

translations.literal: " Li afterward repeatedly spoke to the emperor, saying: "Heaven's mandate has going and staying; the five phases do not constantly flourish; what replaces fire is earth; what succeeds Han is Wei; he who can settle the realm is of the Cao surname; only entrust affairs to the Cao clan."
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang Li kept telling the throne that the five phases cycled, earth would follow fire, Wei would follow Han, and only the house of Cao could pacify All under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」公聞之，使人語立曰：「知公忠於朝廷，然天道深遠，幸勿多言。」〉

translations.literal: " The duke heard it, sent person to tell Li, saying: "I know you are loyal to the court, yet Heaven's Way is deep and far; fortunately do not speak much."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao heard of it and sent word: "I know you are loyal, but Heaven's secrets are not for public chatter."

sentences.zh: 天子之東也，奉自梁欲要之，不及。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven moved east, Feng from Liang wished to intercept him, but did not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: As the court moved east, Yang Feng tried to cut it off from Liang but arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，公征奉，奉南奔袁術，遂攻其梁屯，拔之。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the duke campaigned against Feng; Feng fled south to Yuan Shu; thereupon attacked his Liang encampment and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Cao Cao struck Yang Feng, who fled south to Yuan Shu; Cao Cao then stormed his camp at Liang.

sentences.zh: 於是以袁紹爲太尉，紹恥班在公下，不肯受。

translations.literal: Thereupon appointed Yuan Shao Grand Commandant; Shao was ashamed to rank below the duke and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Yuan Shao grand commandant, but Yuan Shao refused the post because it ranked below Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 公乃固辭，以大將軍讓紹。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon firmly declined, yielding the grand commandant to Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao insisted on stepping aside and gave Yuan Shao the grand commandant title instead.

sentences.zh: 天子拜公司空，行車騎將軍。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven appointed the duke Minister of Works, acting chariot and cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed him minister of works with acting authority as chariot-and-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 是歲用棗祗、韓浩等議，始興屯田。

translations.literal: That year, following the proposals of Zao Zhi, Han Hao, and others, he first began military-agricultural colonies.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the advice of Zao Zhi, Han Hao, and others, he inaugurated the military colony system.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：自遭荒亂，率乏糧穀。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: From suffering famine and chaos, generally grain was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes that years of famine had emptied every granary.

sentences.zh: 諸軍並起，無終歲之計，饑則寇略，飽則棄餘，瓦解流離，無敵自破者不可勝數。

translations.literal: The various armies all rose, without a year-long plan; when hungry they raided and plundered, when full they cast aside surplus; disintegrated and drifted apart; those without an enemy who broke themselves cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Armies sprang up everywhere with no long-term logistics: they looted when hungry, wasted surplus when fed, and collapsed of their own disorder beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 袁紹之在河北，軍人仰食桑椹。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao was north of the Yellow River, soldiers relied on eating mulberries.
translations.idiomatic: North of the river Yuan Shao's men lived on mulberries.

sentences.zh: 袁術在江、淮，取給蒲蠃。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu was between the Yangzi and Huai, taking supply from mussels and snails.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Yangzi and the Huai, Yuan Shu's troops scraped by on shellfish.

sentences.zh: 民人相食，州里蕭條。

translations.literal: The people ate each other; prefectures and villages were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Cannibalism spread and the countryside went bare.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「夫定國之術，在於彊兵足食，秦人以急農兼天下，孝武以屯田定西域，此先代之良式也。

translations.literal: The duke said: "The art of settling the state lies in strong troops and ample food; the Qin people by urgent farming annexed the realm; Emperor Wu by military colonies settled the Western Regions; these are good models of former ages."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao declared, "To stabilize a state you need strong armies and full granaries: Qin unified China by pushing agriculture, Han Wudi held the west with tuntian farms; we should follow their example."

sentences.zh: 」是歲乃募民屯田許下，得穀百萬斛。

translations.literal: That year then recruited people to military-colony farm at Xu border, obtaining grain a million hu.
translations.idiomatic: That year he recruited settlers for colonies around Xu and harvested a million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 於是州郡例置田官，所在積穀。

translations.literal: Thereupon provinces and commanderies by precedent set field officials; wherever they were, grain accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies followed suit with colony overseers, and grain piled up in every district.

sentences.zh: 征伐四方，無運糧之勞，遂兼滅羣賊，克平天下。〉

translations.literal: Campaigning and punishing the four quarters, without the toil of transporting grain, thereupon annexed and destroyed the mass of bandits, was able to pacify the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Free of long supply trains, he could campaign in every direction, wipe out the rebels, and bring the realm to heel."

sentences.zh: 呂布襲劉備，取下邳。

translations.literal: Lü Bu raided Liu Bei and took Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu surprised Liu Bei and seized Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 備來奔。

translations.literal: Bei came fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei fled to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 程昱說公曰：「觀劉備有雄才而甚得衆心，終不爲人下，不如早圖之。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu persuaded the duke, saying: "Observe that Liu Bei has heroic talent and greatly wins the people's hearts; in the end he will not serve under others; it is better to plan against him early."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu urged, "Liu Bei is a hero who owns men's hearts; he will never serve under you—deal with him now."

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「方今收英雄時也，殺一人而失天下之心，不可。」

translations.literal: The duke said: "Now is the time to gather heroes; to kill one man and lose the realm's hearts cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "This is the hour to win allies; murdering him would cost me the world's trust."

sentences.zh: 張濟自關中走南陽。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji fled from Guanzhong toward Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji quit the Guanzhong war zone and marched into Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 濟死，從子繡領其衆。

translations.literal: When Ji died, his nephew's son Xiu led his host.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Ji died, his nephew Zhang Xiu inherited the command.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，公到宛。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, first month, the duke arrived at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 197 CE, he reached Wan.

sentences.zh: 張繡降，旣而悔之，復反。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiu surrendered; afterward he regretted it and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu capitulated, had second thoughts, and rose again.

sentences.zh: 公與戰，軍敗，爲流矢所中，長子昂、弟子安民遇害。

translations.literal: The duke battled with him; the army was defeated; he was struck by a stray arrow; the eldest son Ang and the younger brother's son Anmin met harm.
translations.idiomatic: The fight went badly: Cao Cao was wounded by a stray bolt, and his eldest son Cao Ang and nephew Cao Anmin were killed.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：公所乘馬名絕影，爲流矢所中，傷頰及足，并中公右臂。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: The horse the duke rode was named Shadowless; it was struck by a stray arrow, wounded cheek and foot, and also hit the duke's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says his mount Jueying took bolts in the jaw and leg and a hit on Cao Cao's right arm as well.

sentences.zh: 《世語》曰：昂不能騎，進馬於公，公故免，而昂遇害。〉

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Ang could not ride; he advanced a horse to the duke; the duke thereby escaped, but Ang met harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu adds that Cao Ang, unable to ride, gave his father a horse and died so Cao Cao could escape.

sentences.zh: 公乃引兵還舞陰，繡將騎來鈔，公擊破之。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon led troops back to Wuyin; Xiu led riders to come raiding; the duke broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao fell back to Wuyin, turned on Zhang Xiu's pursuing cavalry, and beat them off.

sentences.zh: 繡奔穰，與劉表合。

translations.literal: Xiu fled to Rang and united with Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu fled to Rang and linked up with Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 公謂諸將曰：「吾降張繡等，失不便取其質，以至于此。

translations.literal: The duke said to the generals: "When I accepted Zhang Xiu and others' surrender, I missed the convenience of not taking hostages, leading to this."
translations.idiomatic: He told his officers, "I accepted Zhang Xiu's surrender without taking hostages when I had the chance; that is how we came to this."

sentences.zh: 吾知所以敗。

translations.literal: I know the reason for defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Now I know why we lost.

sentences.zh: 諸卿觀之，自今已後不復敗矣。

translations.literal: You gentlemen observe; from now onward there will not again be defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mark this lesson: it will not happen again on my watch."

sentences.zh: 」遂還許。

translations.literal: Thereupon returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Then he withdrew to Xu.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：舊制，三公領兵入見，皆交戟叉頸而前。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: By old regulation, when the three dukes led troops in to audience, all crossed halberds at the neck to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu notes an old rule that commanders entering audience crossed halberds at their throats as a security ritual.

sentences.zh: 初，公將討張繡，入覲天子，時始復此制。

translations.literal: At first, when the duke was about to campaign against Zhang Xiu, he entered to audience the Son of Heaven; at that time this regulation had just been restored.
translations.idiomatic: That ritual had just been revived when Cao Cao went to court before the Wan campaign.

sentences.zh: 公自此不復朝見。〉

translations.literal: From this the duke no longer attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Cao Cao stopped appearing for formal audiences.

sentences.zh: 袁術欲稱帝於淮南，使人告呂布。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu wished to declare himself emperor in Huainan; he sent person to inform Lü Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu planned to declare an empire south of the Huai and sent word to Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 布收其使，上其書。

translations.literal: Bu arrested his envoy and submitted his letter.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu seized the messenger and forwarded Yuan Shu's letter to the capital.

sentences.zh: 術怒，攻布，爲布所破。

translations.literal: Shu was angry, attacked Bu, and was broken by Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu attacked in fury and Lü Bu smashed him.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，術侵陳，公東征之。

translations.literal: Autumn ninth month, Shu invaded Chen; the duke east campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn Yuan Shu struck Chen; Cao Cao marched east against him.

sentences.zh: 術聞公自來，棄軍走，留其將橋蕤、李豐、梁綱、樂就；

translations.literal: Shu heard the duke personally came, abandoned the army and fled, leaving his generals Qiao Rui, Li Feng, Liang Gang, and Yue Jiu;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu ran at the news, leaving Qiao Rui, Li Feng, Liang Gang, and Yue Jiu to cover his retreat;

sentences.zh: 公到，擊破蕤等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: when the duke arrived, he broke Rui and the others and beheaded them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao crushed that rear guard and executed every officer.

sentences.zh: 術走渡淮。

translations.literal: Shu fled crossing the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu escaped across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 公還許。

translations.literal: The duke returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao returned to Xu.

sentences.zh: 公之自舞陰還也，南陽、章陵諸縣復叛爲繡，公遣曹洪擊之，不利，還屯葉，數爲繡、表所侵。

translations.literal: When the duke returned from Wuyin, Nanyang and Zhangling various counties again rebelled for Xiu; the duke sent Cao Hong to strike them; it was unfavorable; he returned encamped at Ye and was repeatedly invaded by Xiu and Biao.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuyin, Nanyang and Zhangling counties went over to Zhang Xiu again; Cao Hong was beaten back to Ye and harried by Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，公自南征，至宛。

translations.literal: Winter eleventh month, the duke personally south campaigned and reached Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he led a southern drive to Wan.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：臨淯水，祠亡將士，歔欷流涕，衆皆感慟。〉

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: Approaching the Yu River, he sacrificed to the dead generals and soldiers, sobbed and wept; the host was all moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says he sacrificed by the Yu River for the fallen of Wan and wept until the whole army wept with him.

sentences.zh: 表將鄧濟據湖陽。

translations.literal: Biao's general Deng Ji held Huyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao's officer Deng Ji held Huyang.

sentences.zh: 攻拔之，生禽濟，湖陽降。

translations.literal: He attacked and took it, captured Ji alive; Huyang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the town, took Deng Ji alive, and Huyang submitted.

sentences.zh: 攻舞陰，下之。

translations.literal: He attacked Wuyin and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，公還許，初置軍師祭酒。

translations.literal: Third year spring, first month, the duke returned to Xu and first established the office of military counsellor libationer.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 198 CE, he returned to Xu and created the post of military counsellor (jijiu).

sentences.zh: 三月，公圍張繡於穰。

translations.literal: Third month, the duke besieged Zhang Xiu at Rang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he invested Zhang Xiu at Rang.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，劉表遣兵救繡，以絕軍後。

translations.literal: Summer fifth month, Liu Biao sent troops to rescue Xiu in order to cut off the army's rear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer Liu Biao sent a column to relieve Zhang Xiu and threaten Cao Cao's rear.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：袁紹叛卒詣公云：「田豐使紹早襲許，若挾天子以令諸侯，四海可指麾而定。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: A Yuan Shao deserter told the duke: "Tian Feng urged Shao to strike Xu early; if he seized the Son of Heaven to command the lords, the four seas could be settled at a gesture."
translations.idiomatic: A defector from Yuan Shao reported that Tian Feng had urged an early strike on Xu to seize the emperor and cow the provinces.

sentences.zh: 」公乃解繡圍。〉

translations.literal: The duke thereupon lifted the siege of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao broke off the siege of Rang.

sentences.zh: 公將引還，繡兵來，公軍不得進，連營稍前。

translations.literal: The duke was about to lead a withdrawal when Xiu's troops came; the duke's army could not advance; he connected camps and edged forward.
translations.idiomatic: As he withdrew, Zhang Xiu pressed so hard that he could only creep forward in a linked-camp formation.

sentences.zh: 公與荀彧書曰：「賊來追吾，雖日行數里，吾策之，到安衆，破繡必矣。

translations.literal: The duke wrote to Xun Yu: "Though the bandits pursue me and I march only a few li a day, I calculate that when I reach Anzhong I will certainly break Xiu."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Xun Yu, "The enemy is on my tail and we crawl along, but I know I will crush Zhang Xiu once we reach Anzhong."

sentences.zh: 」到安衆，繡與表兵合守險，公軍前後受敵。

translations.literal: When he reached Anzhong, Xiu and Biao's troops united to guard the peril; the duke's army received enemies front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: At Anzhong, Zhang Xiu and Liu Biao sealed the defiles and pinned him front and rear.

sentences.zh: 公乃夜鑿險爲地道，悉過輜重，設奇兵。

translations.literal: The duke then by night chiseled the perilous ground into a tunnel, entirely passed the baggage train through, and set ambush troops.
translations.idiomatic: By night he dug a covered way through the rough ground, slipped his baggage through, and planted an ambush.

sentences.zh: 會明，賊謂公爲遁也，悉軍來追。

translations.literal: When it became light, the bandits thought the duke had fled and sent their whole army in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels thought he had bolted and threw their whole force forward.

sentences.zh: 乃縱奇兵步騎夾攻，大破之。

translations.literal: Then he released the ambush infantry and cavalry in a pincer attack and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He sprang the trap with horse and foot and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，公還許。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, the duke returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he was back in Xu.

sentences.zh: 荀彧問公：「前以策賊必破，何也？

translations.literal: Xun Yu asked the duke: "Earlier by plan you knew the bandits must be broken; why?"
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu asked how he had known the enemy would break.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「虜遏吾歸師，而與吾死地戰，吾是以知勝矣。」

translations.literal: The duke said: "The captives blocked my returning army yet fought me on dead ground; I thereby knew victory."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "They barred my retreat yet forced a battle where I had nothing to lose—that is how I knew I would win."

sentences.zh: 呂布復爲袁術使高順攻劉備，公遣夏侯惇救之，不利。

translations.literal: Lü Bu again for Yuan Shu sent Gao Shun to attack Liu Bei; the duke sent Xiahou Dun to rescue him; it was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Bu again sent Gao Shun against Liu Bei for Yuan Shu; Xiahou Dun's relief column failed.

sentences.zh: 備爲順所敗。

translations.literal: Bei was defeated by Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei was routed by Gao Shun.

sentences.zh: 九月，公東征布。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the duke east campaigned Bu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Cao Cao marched east against Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，屠彭城，獲其相侯諧。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, he slaughtered Pengcheng and captured its chancellor Hou Xie.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he sacked Pengcheng and took its chancellor Hou Xie.

sentences.zh: 進至下邳，布自將騎逆擊。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xiapi, Bu personally led cavalry to intercept and strike.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi, Lü Bu led cavalry out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 大破之，獲其驍將成廉。

translations.literal: He greatly defeated them and captured his fierce general Cheng Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao crushed the sortie and captured Lü Bu's champion Cheng Lian.

sentences.zh: 追至城下，布恐，欲降。

translations.literal: Pursuing to below the walls, Bu was afraid and wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao drove him under the walls of Xiapi until Lü Bu panicked and offered to yield.

sentences.zh: 陳宮等沮其計，求救於術，勸布出戰，戰又敗，乃還固守，攻之不下。

translations.literal: Chen Gong and others thwarted his plan, begged rescue from Shu, urged Bu to go out to battle; again defeated in battle, then returned to firm defense; attacking could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gong blocked surrender, begged Yuan Shu for help, and talked Lü Bu into another sortie; after another defeat Lü Bu sealed himself inside, and the siege held.

sentences.zh: 時公連戰，士卒罷，欲還，用荀攸、郭嘉計，遂決泗、沂水以灌城。

translations.literal: At that time the duke had battled in succession; soldiers were weary and wished to return; using Xun You and Guo Jia's plan, thereupon opened the Si and Yi rivers to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: His men were exhausted and wanted to quit until Xun You and Guo Jia persuaded him to break the Si and Yi rivers and flood Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 月餘，布將宋憲、魏續等執陳宮，舉城降，生禽布、宮，皆殺之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Bu's generals Song Xian, Wei Xu and others seized Chen Gong, raised the city in surrender, captured Bu and Gong alive, and all killed them.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Song Xian and Wei Xu bound Chen Gong, opened the gates, and surrendered; Lü Bu and Chen Gong were executed.

sentences.zh: 太山臧霸、孫觀、吳敦、尹禮、昌狶各聚衆。

translations.literal: Mount Tai Zang Ba, Sun Guan, Wu Dun, Yin Li, and Chang Xi each gathered multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Ba of Taishan, Sun Guan, Wu Dun, Yin Li, and Chang Xi each led bandit hosts.

sentences.zh: 布之破劉備也，霸等悉從布。

translations.literal: When Bu broke Liu Bei, Ba and the rest all followed Bu.
translations.idiomatic: They had all followed Lü Bu after he defeated Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 布敗，獲霸等，公厚納待，遂割青、徐二州附于海以委焉，分琅邪、東海、北海爲城陽、利城、昌慮郡。

translations.literal: When Bu was defeated, he captured Ba and others; the duke generously received and treated them; thereupon carved out Qing and Xu two provinces attached to the sea and entrusted them, dividing Langye and Donghai and Beihai into Chengyang, Licheng, and Changlu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After Lü Bu fell, Cao Cao enrolled them with lavish favor, carved out the coastal tracts of Qing and Xu for their fiefs, and split Langye, Donghai, and Beihai into new commanderies.

sentences.zh: 初，公爲兖州，以東平畢諶爲別駕。

translations.literal: At first, when the duke was shepherd of Yan, he took Dongping's Bi Chen as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as inspector of Yan, he had named Bi Chen of Dongping as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 張邈之叛也，邈劫諶母弟妻子；

translations.literal: When Zhang Miao rebelled, Miao seized Chen's mother, younger brothers, wife, and children;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Miao mutinied he took Bi Chen's family hostage;

sentences.zh: 公謝遣之，曰：「卿老母在彼，可去。

translations.literal: the duke apologized and sent him off, saying: "Your old mother is there; you may go."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao dismissed him with regrets: "Your mother is in enemy hands; you should go."

sentences.zh: 」諶頓首無二心，公嘉之，爲之流涕。

translations.literal: " Chen kowtowed, showing no second heart; the duke praised him and for him shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Chen swore he would not waver; Cao Cao praised him and wept.

sentences.zh: 旣出，遂亡歸。

translations.literal: After he went out, then he fled and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Once outside the lines he bolted to the rebels anyway.

sentences.zh: 及布破，諶生得，衆爲諶懼，公曰：「夫人孝於其親者，豈不亦忠於君乎！

translations.literal: When Bu was broken, Chen was captured alive; the host feared for Chen; the duke said: "For a man to be filial to kin, would he not also be loyal to his lord!
translations.idiomatic: When Bi Chen was taken alive, everyone expected execution; Cao Cao said, "A man that filial to his parents must be loyal to his lord as well.

sentences.zh: 吾所求也。

translations.literal: That is what I seek.
translations.idiomatic: That is exactly the man I want."

sentences.zh: 」以爲魯相。

translations.literal: " He made him chancellor of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed him chancellor of Lu.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：袁紹宿與故太尉楊彪、大長秋梁紹、少府孔融有隙，欲使公以他過誅之。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: Yuan Shao long had a rift with former Grand Commandant Yang Biao, grand chief steward for the empress Liang Shao, and Minister of the Lesser Treasury Kong Rong; he wished to make the duke execute them on other faults.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Yuan Shao wanted Cao Cao to trump up charges against Yang Biao, Liang Shao, and Kong Rong.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「當今天下土崩瓦解，雄豪並起，輔相君長，人懷怏怏，各有自爲之心，此上下相疑之秋也，雖以無嫌待之，猶懼未信；

translations.literal: The duke said: "Now the realm is earth-broken and tile-shattered; bold heroes rise together; assisting and ministering lords and elders, each man harbors resentment and has a mind each for himself; this is the autumn of mutual suspicion above and below; though one treats them without suspicion, still one fears they will not trust;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao refused: "The realm is shattered; every warlord minds his own ambition; trust is already thin; even if I treat men openly they may still doubt me;

sentences.zh: 如有所除，則誰不自危？

translations.literal: if there is execution, then who would not fear for himself?
translations.idiomatic: if I start killing notables, who will feel safe?"

sentences.zh: 且夫起布衣，在塵垢之間，爲庸人之所陵陷，可勝怨乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, rising from common cloth, among dust and filth, being overwhelmed by mediocre menhow can resentment be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: Besides, we all rose from common ranks and petty slights in the mudwho is free of old grudges?"

sentences.zh: 高祖赦雍齒之讎而羣情以安，如何忘之？

translations.literal: Gaozu pardoned Yong Chi's enmity and the host of feelings thereby was settled; how can one forget this?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu forgave Yong Chi and won every heart; should I forget that lesson?"

sentences.zh: 」紹以爲公外託公義，內實離異，深懷怨望。

translations.literal: Shao thought the duke outwardly relied on public righteousness but inwardly truly estranged, and deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao decided Cao Cao was only mouthing principle while secretly dividing the coalition, and nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲楊彪亦曾爲魏武所困，幾至於死，孔融竟不免於誅滅，豈所謂先行其言而後從之哉！

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Yang Biao also was once trapped by Wei Wu and nearly reached death; Kong Rong in the end did not avoid execution and exterminationis this what is called first practicing one's words and afterward following them!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Yang Biao was later cornered by Cao Cao almost to death and Kong Rong was executed anywayhardly proof that fine words were followed by fine deeds.

sentences.zh: 非知之難，其在行之，信矣。〉

translations.literal: It is not hard to know it; the difficulty lies in carrying it outindeed true."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing is easy; doing is hard. That much is certain."

sentences.zh: 四年春二月，公還至昌邑。

translations.literal: Fourth year spring second month, the duke returned reaching Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, 199 CE, he reached Changyi.

sentences.zh: 張楊將楊醜殺楊，眭固又殺醜，以其衆屬袁紹，屯射犬。

translations.literal: Zhang Yang's general Yang Chou killed Yang; Sui Gu again killed Chou and attached his host to Yuan Shao, encamping at Shequan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yang's officer Yang Chou murdered him; Sui Gu killed Yang Chou and led the troops to Yuan Shao, camping at Shequan.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，進軍臨河，使史渙、曹仁渡河擊之。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, advanced the army to the river bank, ordered Shi Huan and Cao Ren to cross the river and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he moved to the Yellow River and sent Shi Huan and Cao Ren across to attack.

sentences.zh: 固使楊故長史薛洪、河內太守繆尚留守，自將兵北迎紹求救，與渙、仁相遇犬城。

translations.literal: Gu made Yang's former chief clerk Xue Hong and Henei grand administrator Miao Shang remain to guard; he himself led troops north to meet Shao and beg rescue, met Huan and Ren at Quancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sui Gu left Xue Hong and Miao Shang to hold the base while he rode north to beg Yuan Shao for aid; he ran into Shi Huan and Cao Ren at Quancheng.

sentences.zh: 交戰，大破之，斬固。

translations.literal: They battled, greatly defeated them, and beheaded Gu.
translations.idiomatic: They fought, routed him, and beheaded Sui Gu.

sentences.zh: 公遂濟河，圍射犬。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon crossed the river and besieged Shequan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao crossed the river and invested Shequan.

sentences.zh: 洪、尚率衆降，封爲列侯，還軍敖倉。

translations.literal: Hong and Shang led the host to surrender; they were enfeoffed as full marquises; returned the army to Aocang.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Hong and Miao Shang surrendered with their men and received full marquisates; Cao Cao withdrew to Aocang.

sentences.zh: 以魏种爲河內太守，屬以河北事。

translations.literal: He made Wei Chong grand administrator of Henei and entrusted him with Hebei affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wei Chong governor of Henei to handle the north bank.

sentences.zh: 初，公舉种孝廉。

translations.literal: At first, the duke recommended Chong for filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had once nominated Wei Chong on the Filial-and-Incorrupt list.

sentences.zh: 兖州叛，公曰：「唯魏种且不棄孤也。

translations.literal: When Yan province rebelled, the duke said: "Only Wei Chong will not abandon me in isolation."
translations.idiomatic: When Yan mutinied he said, "Only Wei Chong will never desert me."

sentences.zh: 」及聞种走，公怒曰：「种不南走越、北走胡，不置汝也！

translations.literal: " When he heard Chong had fled, the duke angrily said: "Unless Chong flees south to Yue or north to the Hu, I will not let you off!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wei Chong had bolted, he swore, "Unless he flees to the southern tribes or the steppe, I will have his head!"

sentences.zh: 」旣下射犬，生禽种，公曰：「唯其才也！

translations.literal: " After taking Shequan, he captured Chong alive; the duke said: "Only his talent!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shequan fell and Wei Chong was taken alive, Cao Cao exclaimed, "What a man!"

sentences.zh: 」釋其縛而用之。

translations.literal: " He released his bonds and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: He cut his bonds and put him back to work.

sentences.zh: 是時袁紹旣并公孫瓚，兼四州之地，衆十餘萬，將進軍攻許，諸將以爲不可敵，公曰：「吾知紹之爲人，志大而智小，色厲而膽薄，忌克而少威，兵多而分畫不明，將驕而政令不一，土地雖廣，糧食雖豐，適足以爲吾奉也。

translations.literal: At this time Yuan Shao had already annexed Gongsun Zan, combined the lands of four provinces, a host of more than a hundred thousand, and was about to advance the army to attack Xu; the generals thought him unbeatable; the duke said: "I know Shao's person: great ambition yet small wisdom, fierce appearance yet thin courage, jealous and stingy of merit yet little awe-inspiring power, many troops yet unclear division of commands, arrogant generals yet government orders not unified; though lands are broad and grain ample, they are just enough to be my provision."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had swallowed Gongsun Zan and held four provinces with a hundred thousand men, poised to strike Xu. His officers were daunted, but Cao Cao said, "I know Yuan Shao: big schemes and small wit, fierce looks and a timid heart, jealous of subordinates, confused command, arrogant generals, and no unified policy. His wide lands and rich grain will only end up supplying me."

sentences.zh: 」秋八月，公進軍黎陽，使臧霸等入青州破齊、北海、東安，留于禁屯河上。

translations.literal: Autumn eighth month, the duke advanced the army to Liyang, made Zang Ba and others enter Qingzhou and break Qi, Beihai, and Dong'an, left Yu Jin encamped on the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he moved to Liyang, sent Zang Ba into Qingzhou against Qi, Beihai, and Dong'an, and posted Yu Jin along the river.

sentences.zh: 九月，公還許，分兵守官渡。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the duke returned to Xu, divided troops to guard Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was back in Xu, detaching a force to hold Guandu.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，張繡率衆降，封列侯。

translations.literal: Winter eleventh month, Zhang Xiu led the host to surrender and was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhang Xiu capitulated with his army and received a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 十二月，公軍官渡。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the duke's army was at Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month his headquarters shifted to Guandu.

sentences.zh: 袁術自敗於陳，稍困，袁譚自青州遣迎之。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu, since being defeated at Chen, gradually was pressed; Yuan Tan from Qingzhou sent to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Chen, Yuan Shu grew desperate; Yuan Tan sent from Qingzhou to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 術欲從下邳北過，公遣劉備、朱靈要之。

translations.literal: Shu wished to pass north from Xiapi; the duke sent Liu Bei and Zhu Ling to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu meant to cross north near Xiapi; Cao Cao sent Liu Bei and Zhu Ling to block him.

sentences.zh: 會術病死。

translations.literal: It happened that Shu died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu died of illness on the way.

sentences.zh: 程昱、郭嘉聞公遣備，言於公曰：「劉備不可縱。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu and Guo Jia heard the duke had dispatched Bei and spoke to the duke, saying: "Liu Bei cannot be let loose."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu and Guo Jia warned, "You must not let Liu Bei go."

sentences.zh: 」公悔，追之不及。

translations.literal: The duke regretted it, pursued him but did not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao regretted the order but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 備之未東也，陰與董承等謀反，至下邳，遂殺徐州刺史車冑，舉兵屯沛。

translations.literal: Before Bei had gone east, secretly with Dong Cheng and others plotted rebellion; reaching Xiapi, then killed Xuzhou Inspector Che Zhou, raised troops and encamped at Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Before marching east Liu Bei had secretly joined Dong Cheng's plot; at Xiapi he murdered Inspector Che Zhou of Xuzhou and raised an army at Pei.

sentences.zh: 遣劉岱、王忠擊之，不克。

translations.literal: He dispatched Liu Dai and Wang Zhong to strike them; could not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Liu Dai and Wang Zhong; they failed.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝春秋》曰：備謂岱等曰：「使汝百人來，其無如我何；

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: Bei said to Dai and others: "Were you a hundred men to come, they could not do anything to me;
translations.idiomatic: The chronicle quotes Liu Bei taunting Liu Dai: "Send a hundred men and you still cannot touch me;

sentences.zh: 曹公自來，未可知耳！

translations.literal: if Lord Cao himself comes, it is not yet knowable!"
translations.idiomatic: we will see what happens if Cao Cao comes in person!"

sentences.zh: 」《魏武故事》曰：岱字公山，沛國人。

translations.literal: The Wei Wu gushi says: Dai's style name was Gongshan; he was a man of the state of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Wu anecdotes identify Liu Dai (courtesy Gongshan) as a native of Pei.

sentences.zh: 以司空長史從征伐有功，封列侯。

translations.literal: As chief clerk of the minister of works he followed the punitive expeditions and had merit; he was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as chief clerk under the minister of works on campaign and earned a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》曰：王忠，扶風人，少爲亭長。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Wang Zhong, a man of Fufeng, in youth was a village headman.
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei describes Wang Zhong of Fufeng as a former village chief.

sentences.zh: 三輔亂，忠饑乏噉人，隨輩南向武關。

translations.literal: When the three auxiliaries were in chaos, Zhong from hunger lacked food and ate people; he followed companions south toward Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong collapsed he starved to the point of cannibalism and drifted south with refugees toward Wuguan.

sentences.zh: 值婁子伯爲荊州遣迎北方客人；

translations.literal: It happened that Lou Zibo for Jingzhou dispatched to welcome northern guests;
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zibo, acting for Jingzhou, had sent men to escort northern refugees south;

sentences.zh: 忠不欲去，因率等仵逆擊之，奪其兵，聚衆千餘人以歸公。

translations.literal: Zhong did not wish to go; therefore he led his companions to strike them contrarywise, seized their weapons, gathered more than a thousand men and returned to the duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhong refused to disarm, ambushed the escort, seized their arms, rallied a thousand followers, and brought them to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 拜忠中郎將，從征討。

translations.literal: He was appointed Zhong as general of the gentlemen of the household, to follow campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao named Wang Zhong a general of the household and took him on campaign.

sentences.zh: 五官將知忠甞噉人，因從駕出行，令俳取冢間髑髏繫著忠馬鞍，以爲歡笑。〉

translations.literal: The heir apparent of the five offices knew Zhong had once eaten people; therefore when following the carriage on an outing, he ordered jesters to take skulls from among tombs and tie them on Zhong's saddle, for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent knew Wang Zhong's grim past and once, on a ride, had clowns tie graveyard skulls to his saddle for a cruel joke.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守劉勳率衆降，封爲列侯。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Lujiang Liu Xun led the host to surrender and was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Lujiang governor Liu Xun capitulated with his army and received a full marquisate.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，董承等謀泄，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Fifth year spring first month, Dong Cheng and others' plot leaked; all were executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 200 CE, the belt edict conspiracy was exposed and its members executed.

sentences.zh: 公將自東征備，諸將皆曰：「與公爭天下者，袁紹也。

translations.literal: The duke was about personally to east campaign against Bei; the generals all said: "The one who contends with you for the realm is Yuan Shao."
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao prepared to march east against Liu Bei, his generals warned, "Yuan Shao is your real rival for the empire."

sentences.zh: 今紹方來而棄之東，紹乘人後，若何？

translations.literal: Now Shao is just coming yet you abandon him east; Shao will seize men from behindwhat then?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is closing in; if you turn east he will stab you in the rearwhat then?"

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「夫劉備，人傑也，今不擊，必爲後患。

translations.literal: The duke said: "As for Liu Bei, he is an outstanding man of the age; if now we do not strike, he is sure to become a later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, "Liu Bei is a hero; if I do not crush him now he will haunt us later."

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛《魏氏春秋》云：荅諸將曰：「劉備，人傑也，將生憂寡人。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's Wei shi chunqiu says: he answered the generals: "Liu Bei is an outstanding man of the age; he will bring worry to me, the lonely one."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's Wei Annals quotes him telling the generals that Liu Bei was a rival fit to trouble even a king.

sentences.zh: 」臣松之以爲史之記言，旣多潤色，故前載所述有非實者矣，後之作者又生意改之，於失實也，不亦彌遠乎！

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that when histories record speech, they already much embellish; therefore what is narrated earlier sometimes is not factual; later authors again add ideas and alter itas for losing truth, is it not ever farther!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks that historians polish dialogue, earlier accounts may be false, and later compilers invent still moreso truth drifts further away.

sentences.zh: 凡孫盛製書，多用左氏以易舊文，如此者非一。

translations.literal: Whenever Sun Sheng composed books, he much used the Zuo tradition to replace old text; cases like this are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng habitually rewrote old passages in the style of the Zuo Commentary, and not only here.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎，後之學者將何取信哉？

translations.literal: Alas, later studentswhat shall they trust?
translations.idiomatic: How, then, is a later reader to know what to believe?

sentences.zh: 且魏武方以天下勵志，而用夫差分死之言，尤非其類。〉

translations.literal: Moreover Wei Wu was just then taking the realm as his ambition, yet to use Fuchai's "divide death" words is especially not of his kind."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Cao Cao was rallying the empire under himself; putting in his mouth a line borrowed from King Fuchai of Wu rings false."

sentences.zh: 袁紹雖有大志，而見事遟，必不動也。

translations.literal: Though Yuan Shao has great ambition, he sees affairs slowly; he is sure not to move.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao may dream big, but he is slow to act; he will not move in time."

sentences.zh: 」郭嘉亦勸公，遂東擊備，破之，生禽其將夏侯博。

translations.literal: Guo Jia also urged the duke; thereupon he east struck Bei, broke him, and captured alive his general Xia Hou Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jia seconded the plan; Cao Cao struck east, defeated Liu Bei, and took his general Xia Hou Bo alive.

sentences.zh: 備走奔紹，獲其妻子。

translations.literal: Bei fled running to Shao and captured his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei fled to Yuan Shao while Cao Cao seized his family.

sentences.zh: 備將關羽屯下邳，復進攻之，羽降。

translations.literal: Bei's general Guan Yu was encamped at Xiapi; he again advanced to attack him; Yu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu held Xiapi for Liu Bei; Cao Cao attacked again and won his surrender.

sentences.zh: 昌狶叛爲備，又攻破之。

translations.literal: Chang Xi rebelled for Bei; again he broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Xi rose for Liu Bei and was crushed in turn.

sentences.zh: 公還官渡，紹卒不出。

translations.literal: The duke returned to Guandu; Shao in the end did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was back at Guandu before Yuan Shao stirred.

sentences.zh: 二月，紹遣郭圖、淳于瓊、顏良攻東郡太守劉延於白馬，紹引兵至黎陽，將渡河。

translations.literal: Second month, Shao dispatched Guo Tu, Chunyu Qiong, and Yan Liang to attack Grand Administrator of Dongjun Liu Yan at Baima; Shao led troops to Liyang, about to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yuan Shao sent Guo Tu, Chunyu Qiong, and Yan Liang against Liu Yan at Baima while he massed at Liyang to ford the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，公北救延。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, the duke north rescued Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Cao Cao marched north to relieve Liu Yan.

sentences.zh: 荀攸說公曰：「今兵少不敵，分其勢乃可。

translations.literal: Xun You persuaded the duke: "Now troops are few and cannot match the enemy; dividing their momentum then is possible."
translations.idiomatic: Xun You said, "We are outnumbered; we must split their forces."

sentences.zh: 公到延津，若將渡兵向其後者，紹必西應之，然後輕兵襲白馬，掩其不備，顏良可禽也。

translations.literal: When the duke reaches Yan Ford, if he appears about to ferry troops against their rear, Shao is sure to respond west; then light troops raid Baima, catch them unprepared, and Yan Liang can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: Feign a crossing at Yanjin to draw Yuan Shao west, then hit Baima with a flying column and bag Yan Liang before he can react."

sentences.zh: 」公從之。

translations.literal: The duke followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took the advice.

sentences.zh: 紹聞兵渡，即分兵西應之。

translations.literal: Shao heard troops were crossing and immediately divided troops to respond west.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao heard of the feint and peeled off a wing to face west.

sentences.zh: 公乃引軍兼行趣白馬，未至十餘里，良大驚，來逆戰。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon led the army by double march hastening to Baima; not yet ten-odd li, Liang was greatly startled and came to oppose battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao raced to Baima; within ten li Yan Liang woke to the danger and hurried out to fight.

sentences.zh: 使張遼、關羽前登，擊破，斬良。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhang Liao and Guan Yu to lead the van, broke them, and beheaded Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Liao and Guan Yu forward and they broke the line, taking Yan Liang's head.

sentences.zh: 遂解白馬圍，徙其民，循河而西。

translations.literal: Thereupon lifted the siege of Baima, moved its people, and followed the river west.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the siege, evacuated the people of Baima, and withdrew along the river's west bank.

sentences.zh: 紹於是渡河追公軍，至延津南。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon crossed the river pursuing the duke's army, reaching south of Yan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao crossed in pursuit and caught Cao Cao south of Yanjin.

sentences.zh: 公勒兵駐營南阪下，使登壘望之，曰：「可五六百騎。

translations.literal: The duke reined troops and halted the camp south of the slope; he made them ascend the rampart and look, saying: "Perhaps five or six hundred riders."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao drew up south of a ridge and had scouts report: "Only five or six hundred horsemen."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，復白：「騎稍多，步兵不可勝數。

translations.literal: After a while, again reported: "Riders gradually increased; infantry cannot be counted."
translations.idiomatic: Soon they revised the count: "More cavalry arriving, foot soldiers beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「勿復白。

translations.literal: The duke said: "Do not report again."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Say no more."

sentences.zh: 」乃令騎解鞍放馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered riders to loosen saddle and loose horses.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to slip saddles and let the horses graze.

sentences.zh: 是時，白馬輜重就道。

translations.literal: At this time Baima baggage was on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The baggage train from Baima was strung out on the road.

sentences.zh: 諸將以爲敵騎多，不如還保營。

translations.literal: The generals thought enemy cavalry were many; it was better to return and protect the camp.
translations.idiomatic: His officers wanted to pull back to the fortified camp.

sentences.zh: 荀攸曰：「此所以餌敵，如何去之！

translations.literal: Xun You said: "This is the means to bait the enemy; how can we leave it!"
translations.idiomatic: Xun You snapped, "That train is bait; we must not abandon it!"

sentences.zh: 」紹騎將文醜與劉備將五六千騎前後至。

translations.literal: Shao's cavalry general Wen Chou and Liu Bei's five or six thousand riders arrived front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Chou and Liu Bei arrived with five or six thousand horse from two directions.

sentences.zh: 諸將復白：「可上馬。

translations.literal: The generals again reported: "It is possible to mount horses."
translations.idiomatic: The staff urged, "Time to saddle up."

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「未也。

translations.literal: The duke said: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，騎至稍多，或分趣輜重。

translations.literal: After a while, riders arrived gradually more; some divided to hasten toward the baggage.
translations.idiomatic: More enemy horse poured in; detachments peeled off toward the wagons.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「可矣。

translations.literal: The duke said: "It is possible."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "Now."

sentences.zh: 」乃皆上馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon all mounted horses.
translations.idiomatic: Every man mounted.

sentences.zh: 時騎不滿六百，遂縱兵擊，大破之，斬醜、良。

translations.literal: At that time riders were not yet six hundred; thereupon he released troops to strike, greatly defeated them, and beheaded Chou.
translations.idiomatic: With fewer than six hundred horsemen he charged, shattered the Yuan vanguard, and took Wen Chou's head.

sentences.zh: 醜、良皆紹名將也，再戰，悉禽，紹軍大震。

translations.literal: Chou and Liang were both Shao's famed generals; in two battles all were taken; Shao's army was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had now lost two of his champion generals in succession; his army reeled.

sentences.zh: 公還軍官渡。

translations.literal: The duke returned the army to Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao withdrew to Guandu.

sentences.zh: 紹進保陽武。

translations.literal: Shao advanced to defend Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao fell back to fortify Yangwu.
