sentences.zh: 關羽亡歸劉備。

translations.literal: Guan Yu fled and returned to Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu deserted and rejoined Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 八月，紹連營稍前，依沙塠爲屯，東西數十里。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Shao connected camps gradually forward, relying on sand mounds for encampments, east to west several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yuan Shao linked his camps along sand ridges for dozens of li east and west.

sentences.zh: 公亦分營與相當，合戰不利。

translations.literal: The duke also divided camps to match them; joined battle unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao matched him camp for camp but lost the pitched clash.

sentences.zh: 〈習鑿齒《漢晉春秋》曰：許攸說紹曰：「公無與操相攻也。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi's Han Jin chunqiu says: Xu You urged Shao: "You must not mutually attack with Cao."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi's Han–Jin Annals records Xu You telling Yuan Shao not to waste strength hammering Cao Cao head-on.

sentences.zh: 急分諸軍持之，而徑從他道迎天子，則事立濟矣。

translations.literal: Hastily divide the various armies to pin him, but go straight by another road to welcome the Son of Heaven; then the affair will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: Split your host to hold him while you seize another route to the emperor; victory will follow."

sentences.zh: 」紹不從，曰：「吾要當先圍取之。

translations.literal: Shao did not follow, saying: "I insist on first besieging and taking him."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao refused: "I mean to crush him here first."

sentences.zh: 」攸怒。〉

translations.literal: You was angry."
translations.idiomatic: Xu You stalked off in fury."

sentences.zh: 時公兵不滿萬，傷者十二三。

translations.literal: At that time the duke's troops were not yet ten thousand; wounded were two or three in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The text claims Cao Cao had fewer than ten thousand men and twenty or thirty percent casualties.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲魏武初起兵，已有衆五千，自後百戰百勝，敗者十二三而已矣。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that when Wei Wu first raised troops, he already had a host of five thousand; afterward a hundred battles a hundred victories; defeats were two or three in ten only.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Cao Cao began with five thousand men, won far more than he lost, and rarely suffered shattering defeats.

sentences.zh: 但一破黃巾，受降卒三十餘萬，餘所吞并，不可悉紀；

translations.literal: Only one smashing of the Yellow Turbans, accepting surrendering soldiers more than three hundred thousand; the rest swallowed and annexed cannot all be recorded;
translations.idiomatic: One victory alone added three hundred thousand surrendered Yellow Turbans, to say nothing of other annexations;

sentences.zh: 雖征戰損傷，未應如此之少也。

translations.literal: though there was damage in campaigning and fighting, it ought not to be this few.
translations.idiomatic: so even with attrition his army at Guandu could hardly have been that small.

sentences.zh: 夫結營相守，異於摧鋒決戰。

translations.literal: For tying camps and mutually guarding differs from crushing the vanguard in decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: A long siege differs from a single shock battle.

sentences.zh: 本紀云：「紹衆十餘萬，屯營東西數十里。

translations.literal: The basic annals says: "Shao's host was more than a hundred thousand; encampments east to west several tens of li."
translations.idiomatic: The main biography says Yuan Shao had over a hundred thousand men in camps dozens of li long.

sentences.zh: 」魏太祖雖機變無方，略不世出，安有以數千之兵，而得逾時相抗者哉？

translations.literal: Though Wei Taizu was endlessly resourceful, a strategist unequalled in a generation, how could there be with several thousand troops the ability to resist for a prolonged time?
translations.idiomatic: However brilliant Cao Cao was, he could not have held Yuan Shao for months with only a few thousand men.

sentences.zh: 以理而言，竊謂不然。

translations.literal: Judged by reason, I privately deem it not so.
translations.idiomatic: On the merits, I do not believe the figure.

sentences.zh: 紹爲屯數十里，公能分營與相當，此兵不得甚少，一也。

translations.literal: Shao made encampments several tens of li; the duke could divide camps to match him; these troops could not have been very fewfirst point.
translations.idiomatic: First, Yuan Shao's line stretched for dozens of li; Cao Cao matched him camp for camp, so he must have had substantial numbers.

sentences.zh: 紹若有十倍之衆，理應當悉力圍守，使出入斷絕，而公使徐晃等擊其運車，公又自出擊淳于瓊等，揚旌往還，曾無抵閡，明紹力不能制，是不得甚少，二也。

translations.literal: If Shao had tenfold the host, by reason he ought to have used full strength to besiege and guard, making exit and entry cut off; yet the duke made Xu Huang and others strike his transport wagons, and the duke again personally went out to strike Chunyu Qiong and others, raising banners back and forth without obstruction; this shows Shao's strength could not control him; therefore the troops could not have been very fewsecond point.
translations.idiomatic: Second, if Yuan Shao had truly outnumbered him ten to one he could have sealed every road, yet Cao Cao sent Xu Huang against his supply trains, rode out against Chunyu Qiong, and rode the lines freelyYuan Shao plainly could not pin him with a tiny force.

sentences.zh: 諸書皆云公坑紹衆八萬，或云七萬。

translations.literal: The various books all say the duke buried Shao's host eighty thousand, or some say seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sources agree Cao Cao executed seventy or eighty thousand of Yuan Shao's surrendered men.

sentences.zh: 夫八萬人奔散，非八千人所能縛，而紹之大衆皆拱手就戮，何緣力能制之？

translations.literal: For eighty thousand men scattering in flight, it is not what eight thousand men can bind; yet Shao's great host all folded hands and met executionwhat reason could there be for strength able to control them?
translations.idiomatic: You cannot round up eighty thousand fugitives with eight hundred guards; that they submitted meekly to massacre shows Cao Cao's army was not a token handful.

sentences.zh: 是不得甚少，三也。

translations.literal: Therefore the troops could not have been very fewthird point.
translations.idiomatic: Third, his force at Guandu could not have been negligible.

sentences.zh: 將記述者欲以少見奇，非其實錄也。

translations.literal: The generals who record narratives wish by fewness to show marvel; it is not their true record.
translations.idiomatic: Historians shrink the numbers for drama, not accuracy.

sentences.zh: 按《鍾繇傳》云：「公與紹相持，繇爲司隷，送馬二千餘匹以給軍。

translations.literal: According to the Zhong Yao biography: "When the duke and Shao held each other, Yao was colonel director of retainers and sent more than two thousand horses to supply the army."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao's biography says that during the standoff he sent over two thousand horses to Cao Cao's army.

sentences.zh: 」本紀及《世語》並云公時有騎六百餘匹，繇馬爲安在哉？〉

translations.literal: The basic annals and the Shi Yu together say the duke at that time had more than six hundred riders; where then were Yao's horses?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet the annals and Shi Yu speak of only six hundred cavalry on handwhere did Zhong Yao's remounts go?"

sentences.zh: 紹復進臨官渡，起土山地道。

translations.literal: Shao again advanced pressing Guandu, raised earth mountains and dug tunnels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao pushed up to Guandu again, building mounds and mining toward Cao Cao's lines.

sentences.zh: 公亦於內作之，以相應。

translations.literal: The duke also made them within to correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao countered with his own mounds and countermines.

sentences.zh: 紹射營中，矢如雨下，行者皆蒙楯，衆大懼。

translations.literal: Shao shot into the camp; arrows fell like rain; those who walked all covered with shields; the host was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan archers filled the sky; men had to crawl under shields and morale sagged.

sentences.zh: 時公糧少，與荀彧書，議欲還許。

translations.literal: At that time the duke's grain was little; he wrote to Xun Yu, discussing wishing to return to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Short of grain, Cao Cao wrote Xun Yu about pulling back to Xu.

sentences.zh: 彧以爲「紹悉衆聚官渡，欲與公決勝敗。

translations.literal: Yu considered that "Shao has gathered all his host at Guandu, desiring with the duke to decide victory and defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu answered that Yuan Shao had staked everything on Guandu to settle the war in one throw.

sentences.zh: 公以至弱當至彊，若不能制，必爲所乘，是天下之大機也。

translations.literal: The duke uses the utmost weak to meet the utmost strong; if he cannot control them, he is sure to be ridden by them; this is the realm's great turning point."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's weakest moment faces Yuan Shao's strongest; if he yields now Yuan Shao will own the empire."

sentences.zh: 且紹，布衣之雄耳，能聚人而不能用。

translations.literal: Moreover Shao is only a hero of common cloth; he can gather men but cannot use them."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao is a bully from the ranks who can recruit talent but cannot wield it."

sentences.zh: 夫以公之神武明哲而輔以大順，何向而不濟！

translations.literal: Now with the duke's divine martial brilliance and clear wisdom, assisted by great compliance, what direction would not succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: You combine military genius with the legitimacy of serving the Han; no campaign can fail you."

sentences.zh: 」公從之。

translations.literal: The duke followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao held his ground.

sentences.zh: 孫策聞公與紹相持，乃謀襲許，未發，爲刺客所殺。

translations.literal: Sun Ce heard the duke and Shao held each other; then he plotted to raid Xu; before he set out, he was killed by assassins.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce planned to strike Xu while Cao Cao was pinned at Guandu but was cut down by assassins before he moved.

sentences.zh: 汝南降賊劉辟等叛應紹，略許下。

translations.literal: Runan surrendering bandits Liu Pi and others rebelled answering Shao, ravaging the vicinity of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Runan bandits such as Liu Pi who had surrendered rose for Yuan Shao and raided the approaches to Xu.

sentences.zh: 紹使劉備助辟，公使曹仁擊破之。

translations.literal: Shao sent Liu Bei to assist Pi; the duke sent Cao Ren to break them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent Liu Bei to help Liu Pi; Cao Ren crushed them.

sentences.zh: 備走，遂破辟屯。

translations.literal: Bei fled; thereupon broke Pi's encampment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei ran; Cao Ren stormed Liu Pi's camp.

sentences.zh: 袁紹運穀車數千乘至，公用荀攸計，遣徐晃、史渙邀擊，大破之，盡燒其車。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao's grain carts several thousand vehicles arrived; the duke used Xun You's plan, dispatched Xu Huang and Shi Huan to intercept and strike, greatly defeated them, and burned all the carts.
translations.idiomatic: When a train of several thousand grain wagons arrived, Cao Cao used Xun You's plan: Xu Huang and Shi Huan intercepted it, routed the escort, and burned every cart.

sentences.zh: 公與紹相拒連月，雖比戰斬將，然衆少糧盡，士卒疲乏。

translations.literal: The duke and Shao resisted each other for successive months; though in repeated battles he beheaded generals, yet the host was few, grain exhausted, soldiers weary.
translations.idiomatic: Months of stalemate brought Cao Cao some tactical wins but left him short of men, out of grain, and with exhausted troops.

sentences.zh: 公謂運者曰：「却十五日爲汝破紹，不復勞汝矣。

translations.literal: The duke said to those transporting grain: "Withdraw fifteen days and I will break Shao for you; I will not again trouble you."
translations.idiomatic: He told his quartermasters, "Give me fifteen more days and I will finish Yuan Shaothen you can rest."

sentences.zh: 」冬十月，紹遣車運穀，使淳于瓊等五人將兵萬餘人送之，宿紹營北四十里。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, Shao dispatched carts transporting grain; he made Chunyu Qiong and five others lead more than ten thousand troops to escort them, lodging north of Shao's camp forty li.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Yuan Shao sent Chunyu Qiong with five officers and ten thousand men to convoy supply wagons, camping forty li north of the main Yuan lines.

sentences.zh: 紹謀臣許攸貪財，紹不能足，來奔，因說公擊瓊等。

translations.literal: Shao's planning minister Xu You was greedy for wealth; Shao could not satisfy him; he came fleeing and therefore persuaded the duke to strike Qiong and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xu You, angry that Yuan Shao would not line his pockets, defected and urged a night strike on Chunyu Qiong.

sentences.zh: 左右疑之，荀攸、賈詡勸公。

translations.literal: Those at his side doubted him; Xun You and Jia Xu urged the duke.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers were wary until Xun You and Jia Xu backed the gamble.

sentences.zh: 公乃留曹洪守，自將步騎五千人夜往，會明至。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon left Cao Hong to guard, personally led five thousand infantry and cavalry by night, reached at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao left Cao Hong to hold Guandu and took five thousand picked horse and foot on a night march, arriving at dawn.

sentences.zh: 瓊等望見公兵少，出陳門外。

translations.literal: Qiong and others saw the duke's troops were few and came out to array outside the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Qiong saw how small the column was and drew up outside his palisade.

sentences.zh: 公急擊之，瓊退保營，遂攻之。

translations.literal: The duke urgently struck them; Qiong retreated to defend the camp; thereupon attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao hit him hard, drove him inside, and stormed the camp.

sentences.zh: 紹遣騎救瓊。

translations.literal: Shao dispatched cavalry to rescue Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao sent cavalry to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 左右或言「賊騎稍近，請分兵拒之」。

translations.literal: Those at his left and right some said: "Enemy cavalry are gradually near; please divide troops to resist them."
translations.idiomatic: Aides warned, "Enemy horse is closing in behind us; detach a screen."

sentences.zh: 公怒曰：「賊在背後，乃白！

translations.literal: The duke angrily said: "The bandits are behind your backs, and only now you report!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao roared, "The enemy is on our rear and you tell me now!"

sentences.zh: 」士卒皆殊死戰，大破瓊等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: The soldiers all fought to the death, greatly broke Qiong and others, and all beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought to the last breath, shattered Chunyu Qiong, and executed the whole command group.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：公聞攸來，跣出迎之，撫掌笑曰：「子卿遠來，吾事濟矣！

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: when the duke heard You had come, barefoot he went out to welcome him, clapped his hands and laughed, saying: "Ziqing, you have come from afar; my affairs are saved!"
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says Cao Cao ran out barefoot to greet Xu You, clapping his hands: "Your coming from afar means my cause is won!"

sentences.zh: 」旣入坐，謂公曰：「袁氏軍盛，何以待之？

translations.literal: After they sat, he said to the duke: "The Yuan army is strong; how will you cope?"
translations.idiomatic: Once seated Xu You asked how he meant to face Yuan Shao's massed host.

sentences.zh: 今有幾糧乎？

translations.literal: "How much grain do you have now?"
translations.idiomatic: "How many days of grain do you have left?"

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「尚可支一歲。

translations.literal: The duke said: "Still enough to last one year."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "About a year's worth."

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「無是，更言之！

translations.literal: You said: "It is not so; speak again!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu You snapped, "Nonsense. Try again."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「可支半歲。

translations.literal: Again he said: "Enough to last half a year."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao revised it to six months.

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「足下不欲破袁氏邪，何言之不實也！

translations.literal: You said: "Sir, do you not wish to defeat the Yuans? Why speak so untruthfully!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you will not be straight with me," Xu You pressed, "how can we break Yuan Shao?"

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「向言戲之耳。

translations.literal: The duke said: "Earlier words were jest."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed, "The first answers were a joke."

sentences.zh: 其實可一月，爲之柰何？

translations.literal: In truth it can last one month; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: "In truth I have perhaps a month. What now?"

sentences.zh: 」攸曰：「公孤軍獨守，外無救援而糧穀已盡，此危急之日也。

translations.literal: You said: "You hold a lone army with no relief outside and grain already gone; this is a day of extremity."
translations.idiomatic: "You are isolated, out of supplies, and out of time," Xu You said flatly.

sentences.zh: 今袁氏輜重有萬餘乘，在故市、烏巢，屯軍無嚴備；

translations.literal: Now the Yuan baggage train numbers more than ten thousand carts at Gushi and Wuchao; the garrison is not on full alert;
translations.idiomatic: "More than ten thousand supply wagons sit at Gushi and Wuchao with slack guard duty;

sentences.zh: 今以輕兵襲之，不意而至，燔其積聚，不過三日，袁氏自敗也。

translations.literal: now strike with light troops, arrive unlooked-for, burn their stores; within three days the Yuan clan will defeat itself."
translations.idiomatic: hit them with a flying column, burn the depots, and Yuan Shao will collapse within three days."

sentences.zh: 」公大喜，乃選精銳步騎，皆用袁軍旗幟，銜枚縛馬口，夜從間道出，人抱束薪，所歷道有問者，語之曰：「袁公恐曹操鈔略後軍，遣兵以益備。

translations.literal: The duke greatly rejoiced, then selected crack foot and cavalry, all using Yuan army banners, mouth bits and bound horse mouths, by night went out bypaths, each man carrying a bundle of firewood; those on the road who asked were told: "Lord Yuan fears Cao Cao raiding the rear train and has sent us to reinforce the guard."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Cao Cao picked crack troops, dressed them in Yuan colors, gagged the horses, marched by night carrying faggots, and answered every challenge with a story about Yuan Shao reinforcing his rear.

sentences.zh: 」聞者信以爲然，皆自若。

translations.literal: Those who heard believed it was so; all were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The sentries swallowed the tale and stood down.

sentences.zh: 旣至，圍屯，大放火，營中驚亂。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they surrounded the encampment, greatly set fire; the camp was alarmed and chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: They ringed Wuchao, torched the stacks, and threw the depot into panic.

sentences.zh: 大破之，盡燔其糧穀寶貨，斬督將眭元進、騎督韓莒子、呂威璜、趙叡等首，割得將軍淳于仲簡鼻，未死，殺士卒千餘人，皆取鼻，牛馬割脣舌，以示紹軍。

translations.literal: They greatly defeated them, burned all grain stores and treasures, beheaded the heads of supervising general Sui Yuanjin, cavalry supervisor Han Juzi, Lü Weihuang, Zhao Rui, and others, cut off General Chunyu Zhongjian's nose while he was not yet dead, killed more than a thousand soldiers all taking noses, oxen and horses had lips and tongues cut, to display to Shao's army.
translations.idiomatic: They annihilated the garrison, incinerated grain and treasure, took the heads of Sui Yuanjin, Han Juzi, Lü Weihuang, Zhao Rui, and others, sliced the nose from the still-living Chunyu Qiong (courtesy Zhongjian), mutilated over a thousand prisoners, and hacked the lips and tongues off draft animals to horrify Yuan Shao's host.

sentences.zh: 將士皆怛懼。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were all fearful and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's men shook with terror.

sentences.zh: 時有夜得仲簡，將以詣麾下，公謂曰：「何爲如是？

translations.literal: At that time someone by night captured Zhongjian and was about to bring him to headquarters; the duke said to him: "Why do thus?"
translations.idiomatic: When night raiders dragged in the mutilated Chunyu Qiong, Cao Cao asked him, "Why did you let it come to this?"

sentences.zh: 」仲簡曰：「勝負自天，何用爲問乎！

translations.literal: Zhongjian said: "Victory and defeat are from Heaven; what use to ask!"
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Qiong snarled, "Win or lose is heaven's business—why ask me?"

sentences.zh: 」公意欲不殺。

translations.literal: The duke's intent was not to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao was inclined to spare him.

sentences.zh: 許攸曰：「明且鑒於鏡，此益不忘人。

translations.literal: Xu You said: "Tomorrow he will look in a mirror; this all the more will not forget men."
translations.idiomatic: Xu You warned, "Tomorrow he will glare at you from every mirror—he will never forget this humiliation."

sentences.zh: 」乃殺之。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon killed him."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao had him executed."

sentences.zh: 紹初聞公之擊瓊，謂長子譚曰：「就彼攻瓊等，吾攻拔其營，彼固無所歸矣！

translations.literal: When Shao first heard the duke was striking Qiong, he said to his eldest son Tan: "Let him attack Qiong and the rest; I will attack and take his camp; he will surely have nowhere to return!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao first learned of the raid on Wuchao, he told Yuan Tan, "Let Cao Cao waste strength on Qiong while I storm his main camp; he will have nowhere to run!"

sentences.zh: 」乃使張郃、高覽攻曹洪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Zhang He and Gao Lan attack Cao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zhang He and Gao Lan to storm Cao Hong.

sentences.zh: 郃等聞瓊破，遂來降。

translations.literal: He and the others heard Qiong was broken; thereupon came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wuchao had fallen, Zhang He and Gao Lan defected.

sentences.zh: 紹衆大潰，紹及譚棄軍走，渡河。

translations.literal: Shao's host greatly collapsed; Shao and Tan abandoned the army and fled, crossing the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao's army dissolved; he and Yuan Tan abandoned the field and fled north across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 追之不及，盡收其輜重圖書珎寶，虜其衆。

translations.literal: Pursuing did not catch up; he fully collected their baggage, maps, books, and precious treasures, and captured their host.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao could not overtake them but seized every wagon, archive, and trophy and rounded up the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：公上言「大將軍鄴侯袁紹前與冀州牧韓馥立故大司馬劉虞，刻作金璽，遣故任長畢瑜詣虞，爲說命錄之數。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xian's Daily Notes record the duke's memorial: "Grand General and Ye marquis Yuan Shao earlier with Ji Governor Han Fu established the former grand minister of works Liu Yu, carved a gold seal, and sent former magistrate of Ren Bi Yu to Yu to expound the numerology of the mandate."
translations.idiomatic: The court diary preserves Cao Cao's bill of indictment: Yuan Shao conspired with Han Fu to enthrone Liu Yu, cast a golden seal, and sent Bi Yu to lecture Liu Yu on omens of rule.

sentences.zh: 又紹與臣書云：『可都鄄城，當有所立。

translations.literal: Further Shao wrote me a letter saying: "We may make the capital at Juancheng; there will be something to establish."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao also wrote proposing Juancheng as a new capital "when the time comes to act."

sentences.zh: 』擅鑄金銀印，孝廉計吏，皆往詣紹。

translations.literal: He arrogantly cast gold and silver seals; filial-and-incorrupt graduates and accounting clerks all went to call on Shao.
translations.idiomatic: He minted private gold and silver seals while graduates and clerks flocked to his camp.

sentences.zh: 從弟濟陰太守敘與紹書云：『今海內喪敗，天意實在我家，神應有徵，當在尊兄。

translations.literal: His cousin Jiyin grand administrator Xu wrote Shao a letter saying: "Now within the seas there is ruin and defeat; Heaven's intent is truly with our house; divine response has its sign; it ought to be with your honored elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xu, governor of Jiyin, wrote that heaven favored the Yuans and the elder brother should take the throne.

sentences.zh: 南兄臣下欲使即位，南兄言，以年則北兄長，以位則北兄重。

translations.literal: The southern brother's ministers wished to make him ascend the throne; the southern brother said that by age the northern brother is elder, by position the northern brother is weightier.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu's followers wanted him crowned, but Yuan Shu argued that Yuan Shao was senior in years and rank.

sentences.zh: 便欲送璽，會曹操斷道。

translations.literal: They were about to deliver the seal when it happened that Cao Cao cut the roads.
translations.idiomatic: They were ready to hand over the seal when Cao Cao blocked the roads.

sentences.zh: 』紹宗族累世受國重恩，而凶逆無道，乃至於此。

translations.literal: Shao's clan for accumulated generations received the state's heavy grace, yet was fierce and rebellious without the Way, even reaching this.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan clan had enjoyed generations of imperial favor yet turned traitor to this degree.

sentences.zh: 輙勒兵馬，與戰官渡，乘聖朝之威，得斬紹大將淳于瓊等八人首，遂大破潰。

translations.literal: I thereupon led horse and foot and battled at Guandu, riding the sage court's majesty, was able to behead eight of Shao's great generals including Chunyu Qiong, and thereupon greatly broke and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore fought them at Guandu in the emperor's name, beheaded eight of their senior generals including Chunyu Qiong, and shattered their army.

sentences.zh: 紹與子譚輕身迸走。

translations.literal: Shao with his son Tan in light body bolted and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao and Yuan Tan fled with only their persons.

sentences.zh: 凡斬首七萬餘級，輜重財物巨億。」〉

translations.literal: In all beheaded more than seventy thousand heads; baggage and wealth exceeded a hundred million."
translations.idiomatic: The tally ran to more than seventy thousand heads taken, with booty beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 公收紹書中，得許下及軍中人書，皆焚之。

translations.literal: Among Shao's captured letters he obtained letters from within Xu and from men in the army; all he burned.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan Shao's correspondence he found letters from his own capital and even his officers; he burned them all unread.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：公云：「當紹之彊，孤猶不能自保，而況衆人乎！」〉

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu says: the duke said: "When Shao was strong, I alone still could not protect myself, how much more the multitude of men!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Annals quotes his explanation: "At Yuan Shao's height I could barely save myself; who could blame others for wavering?"

sentences.zh: 冀州諸郡多舉城邑降者。

translations.literal: The various commanderies of Ji mostly raised cities and towns to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ji province's towns opened their gates in droves.

sentences.zh: 初，桓帝時有黃星見於楚、宋之分，遼東殷馗

translations.literal: At first, in Emperor Huan's time there was a yellow star seen in the division between Chu and Song; Liaodong Yin Kui
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Huan's reign a yellow star appeared over the Chu–Song sky sector; Yin Kui of Liaodong

sentences.zh: 〈馗，古逵字，見三蒼。〉

translations.literal: (Kui is the ancient character for kui, seen in the San Cang.)
translations.idiomatic: The commentary treats Kui as an archaic spelling of the homophone kui, citing the San Cang lexicon.

sentences.zh: 善天文，言後五十歲當有真人起於梁、沛之閒，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: was skilled in astronomy and said that after fifty years a true man would rise between Liang and Pei; his edge could not be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: He was an astronomer who predicted that within fifty years a "true man" would rise between Liang and Pei with irresistible force.

sentences.zh: 至是凡五十年，而公破紹，天下莫敵矣。

translations.literal: Down to this it was in all fifty years, and the duke broke Shao; none under Heaven could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years later Cao Cao broke Yuan Shao and stood unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 六年夏四月，揚兵河上，擊紹倉亭軍，破之。

translations.literal: Sixth year summer fourth month, he displayed arms on the river and struck Shao's Cangting army, breaking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, 201 CE, he paraded along the Yellow River and crushed Yuan Shao's remnant force at Cangting.

sentences.zh: 紹歸，復收散卒，攻定諸叛郡縣。

translations.literal: Shao returned, again gathered scattered soldiers, and attacked and settled the various rebel commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao rallied stragglers and reconquered wavering counties in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 九月，公還許。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the duke returned to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Cao Cao was back in Xu.

sentences.zh: 紹之未破也，使劉備略汝南，汝南賊共都等應之。

translations.literal: Before Shao was broken, he had Liu Bei ravage Runan; Runan bandits such as Gong Du answered him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Guandu Yuan Shao had sent Liu Bei to plunder Runan, where bandits like Gong Du rose in support.

sentences.zh: 遣蔡揚擊都，不利，爲都所破。

translations.literal: He dispatched Cai Yang to strike Du; it was unfavorable; he was broken by Du.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yang was sent against Gong Du and was routed.

sentences.zh: 公南征備。

translations.literal: The duke south campaigned against Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched south against Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 備聞公自行，走奔劉表，都等皆散。

translations.literal: Bei heard the duke personally came, fled running to Liu Biao; Du and the rest all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Cao Cao was leading in person, Liu Bei bolted to Liu Biao and Gong Du's bands melted away.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月，公軍譙，令曰：「吾起義兵，爲天下除暴亂。

translations.literal: Seventh year spring first month, the duke's army was at Qiao; he issued an order, saying: "I raised righteous troops to remove violence and chaos for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 202 CE, he camped at Qiao and proclaimed, "I took up arms to purge the realm of tyranny."

sentences.zh: 舊土人民，死喪略盡，國中終日行，不見所識，使吾悽愴傷懷。

translations.literal: The old land's people, death and loss almost complete, in the state all day walking, not seeing anyone I knew, makes me mournful and wounded in the breast."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet in my home country the dead are so many that I walk all day without recognizing a face, and it breaks my heart."

sentences.zh: 其舉義兵已來，將士絕無後者，求其親戚以後之，授上田，官給耕牛，置學師以教之。

translations.literal: Since raising righteous troops, for generals and soldiers who have no posterity, seek their kin to continue them, grant superior fields, the office supplies plough oxen, establish study masters to teach them."
translations.idiomatic: "For every officer and man who died childless, I will find kin to carry his line, grant them good land, oxen from the government, and teachers for their children."

sentences.zh: 爲存者立廟，使祀其先人，魂而有靈，吾百年之後何恨哉！

translations.literal: For the living establish temples, make them sacrifice to their forebears; if souls have spirit, after my hundred years what regret shall I have!"
translations.idiomatic: "For the living I will raise shrines to their ancestors; if the dead can know, I shall go to my grave without regret."

sentences.zh: 」遂至浚儀，治睢陽渠，遣使以太牢祀橋玄。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reached Junyi, repaired the Suiyang canal, dispatched envoys with grand sacrifice to sacrifice to Qiao Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Junyi, repaired the Suiyang waterway, and sent a grand sacrifice to Qiao Xuan's spirit."

sentences.zh: 〈襃賞令載公祀文曰：「故太尉橋公，誕敷明德，汎愛博容。

translations.literal: The Baoshang ling records the duke's sacrificial text: "The former grand commandant Lord Qiao spread bright virtue, broadly loved and broadly contained."
translations.idiomatic: The reward edict preserves his elegy: "Grand Commandant Qiao spread bright virtue and embraced all the world."

sentences.zh: 國念明訓，士思令謨。

translations.literal: The state remembers clear instruction; gentlemen ponder wise plans.
translations.idiomatic: The state recalls his teaching; scholars cherish his counsel.

sentences.zh: 靈幽體翳，邈哉晞矣！

translations.literal: The numinous is dark, the body hidden; far away, alas, the dawn!"
translations.idiomatic: "The spirit is veiled in darkness; the body lies far away in the long night."

sentences.zh: 吾以幼年，逮并堂室，特以頑鄙之姿，爲大君子所納。

translations.literal: I in young years, reaching your hall, by special favor with dull and coarse manner was taken in by a great gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: "In my youth I came to your door, a rough boy whom a great man nonetheless welcomed."

sentences.zh: 增榮益觀，皆由獎助，猶仲尼稱不如顏淵，李生之厚歎賈復。

translations.literal: Added glory and increased repute all came from encouragement and aid, still as Zhongni said he was not equal to Yan Yuan, as Li Sheng deeply sighed over Jia Fu."
translations.idiomatic: "Whatever honor I gained came from your praiseas Confucius ranked below Yan Hui, as Li Sheng marveled at Jia Fu."

sentences.zh: 士死知己，懷此無忘。

translations.literal: A gentleman dies for one who knows him; I hold this and do not forget.
translations.idiomatic: "A knight dies for his patron; I have never forgotten."

sentences.zh: 又承從容約誓之言：『殂逝之後，路有經由，不以斗酒隻雞過相沃酹，車過三步，腹痛勿怪！

translations.literal: Further I received your relaxed covenant words: "After I am gone, if you pass my road, if you do not pour a libation with a peck of wine and a single chicken, do not blame stomachache after the carriage has passed three steps!"
translations.idiomatic: "You once joked that if I passed your tomb without a peck of wine and a chicken for a toast, I should not wonder at a bellyache three paces past your hearse."

sentences.zh: 』雖臨時戲笑之言，非至親之篤好，胡肯爲此辭乎？

translations.literal: Though temporary jesting words, were it not utmost kinship and deep friendship, how would one consent to such phrases?"
translations.idiomatic: "Only the closest friends banter like that."

sentences.zh: 匪謂靈忿，能詒己疾，懷舊惟顧，念之悽愴。

translations.literal: Not that I say the spirit is angry and can send illness upon oneself; cherishing the old, looking back, my thoughts are mournful."
translations.idiomatic: "I do not claim your ghost would punish me; only memory of you fills me with grief."

sentences.zh: 奉命東征，屯次鄉里，北望貴土，乃心陵墓。

translations.literal: Ordered east on campaign, halting at my village, gazing north toward your noble earth, my heart is toward the tomb mound."
translations.idiomatic: "Ordered east, I halt in my home district and turn my heart toward your grave northward."

sentences.zh: 裁致薄奠，公其尚饗！」〉

translations.literal: I send this meager offering; may you partake!"
translations.idiomatic: "Accept this poor offering; may you feast, noble sir!"

sentences.zh: 進軍官渡。

translations.literal: Advanced the army to Guandu.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his headquarters to Guandu.

sentences.zh: 紹自軍破後，發病歐血，夏五月死。

translations.literal: After Shao's army was broken, he fell ill vomiting blood; summer fifth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: Broken by defeat, Yuan Shao began vomiting blood and died in the fifth month of summer.

sentences.zh: 小子尚代，譚自號車騎將軍，屯黎陽。

translations.literal: The younger son Shang succeeded; Tan styled himself chariot-and-cavalry general and encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang succeeded him while Yuan Tan proclaimed himself chariot-and-cavalry general and camped at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，公征之，連戰。

translations.literal: Autumn ninth month, the duke campaigned against them, battling in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn Cao Cao attacked them in a series of fights.

sentences.zh: 譚、尚數敗退，固守。

translations.literal: Tan and Shang were defeated several times and retreated, firmly defending.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan brothers lost ground and dug in.

sentences.zh: 八年春三月，攻其郭，乃出戰，擊，大破之，譚、尚夜遁。

translations.literal: Eighth year spring third month, attacked their outer wall; then they came out to battle; struck, greatly defeated them; Tan and Shang fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, 203 CE, he stormed their outer rampart, drew them out, routed them, and the brothers fled by night.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，進軍鄴。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, advanced the army to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he advanced on Ye.

sentences.zh: 五月還許，留賈信屯黎陽。

translations.literal: Fifth month returned to Xu, left Jia Xin encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In May he withdrew to Xu, leaving Jia Xin at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 己酉，令曰：「《司馬法》『將軍死綏』，

translations.literal: On the day jiyou he issued an order: "The Sima fa says, 'The general dies for the cord'
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day he promulgated: "The Sima fa says the general dies rather than retreat,"

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》云：綏，却也。

translations.literal: the Wei Shu says: sui means withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: the Book of Wei glossing sui as "yield ground,"

sentences.zh: 有前一尺，無却一寸。〉

translations.literal: there is advance one foot, no retreat one inch."
translations.idiomatic: "advance a foot, never yield an inch."

sentences.zh: 故趙括之母，乞不坐括。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhao Kuo's mother begged not to situate Kuo under punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Zhao Kuo's mother begged exemption from his punishment.

sentences.zh: 是古之將者，軍破於外，而家受罪於內也。

translations.literal: This is how generals of old: the army was broken outside while the household received punishment within.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient law held generals accountable: defeat abroad meant punishment for the family at home.

sentences.zh: 自命將征行，但賞功而不罰罪，非國典也。

translations.literal: From appointing generals on campaign, only rewarding merit and not punishing crime is not the state's norm."
translations.idiomatic: Yet we have rewarded victory without punishing failure; that cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 其令諸將出征，敗軍者抵罪，失利者免官爵。」

translations.literal: Let it be ordered that generals who go on campaign, those whose armies are defeated shall answer with crime, those who lose advantage shall be stripped of office and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth any general who suffers rout shall face criminal charges, and any who loses ground shall lose title and rank."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載庚申令曰：「議者或以軍吏雖有功能，德行不足堪任郡國之選，所謂『可與適道，未可與權』。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the gengshen order: "Some debaters think military clerks, though they have merit and ability, lack virtue enough to be selected for commandery and state postswhat is called 'may travel the Way with them, not yet wield power with them.'"
translations.idiomatic: A further edict (gengshen) rejects the argument that fighting men lack virtue for civil office.

sentences.zh: 管仲曰：『使賢者食於能則上尊，鬬士食於功則卒輕於死，二者設於國則天下治。

translations.literal: Guan Zhong said: "If the worthy feed on ability then superiors are honored; if fighting men feed on merit then soldiers lightly face death; if both are set up in the state then the realm is ordered."
translations.idiomatic: Guan Zhong said talent must be paid for rank and fighters for deeds if the state is to thrive.

sentences.zh: 』未聞無能之人，不鬬之士，並受祿賞，而可以立功興國者也。

translations.literal: I have not heard that incapable men and men who do not fight, together receiving salary and reward, can thereby establish merit and raise the state."
translations.idiomatic: Paying drones who never fight cannot build an empire.

sentences.zh: 故明君不官無功之臣，不賞不戰之士；

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened lord does not office ministers without merit, does not reward soldiers who do not fight;
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler gives no office without merit and no pay without battle;

sentences.zh: 治平尚德行，有事賞功能。

translations.literal: in ordered times one esteems virtue; in times of trouble one rewards merit and ability."
translations.idiomatic: peace calls for virtue, crisis calls for results."

sentences.zh: 論者之言，一似管窺虎歟！」〉

translations.literal: The debaters' words seem like viewing a tiger through a bamboo tube!"
translations.idiomatic: Critics who dismiss soldiers are peering at a tiger through a reed!"

sentences.zh: 秋七月，令曰：「喪亂已來，十有五年，後生者不見仁義禮讓之風，吾甚傷之。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, he issued an order: "Since mourning and chaos, it has been fifteen years; those born later have not seen the wind of benevolence, righteousness, courtesy, and yielding; I am greatly pained by it."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he mourned that fifteen years of war had raised a generation ignorant of ritual.

sentences.zh: 其令郡國各修文學，縣滿五百戶置校官，選其鄉之俊造而教學之，庶幾先王之道不廢，而有以益於天下。」

translations.literal: Let commanderies and states each cultivate letters and learning; counties of five hundred households and up shall establish school officials, select their villages' outstanding talents and teach them, so that perhaps the former kings' Way will not be abandoned and there will be benefit to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every county above five hundred households to appoint schoolmasters, train local talent, and keep the classical Way alive for the empire.

sentences.zh: 八月，公征劉表，軍西平。

translations.literal: Eighth month, the duke campaigned against Liu Biao, army at Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he marched against Liu Biao and camped at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 公之去鄴而南也，譚、尚爭冀州，譚爲尚所敗，走保平原。

translations.literal: When the duke left Ye and went south, Tan and Shang contended for Ji province; Tan was defeated by Shang and fled to protect Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao turned south from Ye, Yuan Tan and Yuan Shang fought for Hebei; Shang drove Tan into Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 尚攻之急，譚遣辛毗乞降請救。

translations.literal: Shang attacked him urgently; Tan dispatched Xin Pi to beg surrender and request rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang pressed the siege until Yuan Tan sent Xin Pi to offer submission and beg aid.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆疑，荀攸勸公許之，

translations.literal: The generals all doubted; Xun You urged the duke to consent,
translations.idiomatic: The staff hesitated, but Xun You urged Cao Cao to accept.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：公云：「我攻呂布，表不爲寇，官渡之役，不救袁紹，此自守之賊也，宜爲後圖。

translations.literal: the Wei Shu says: the duke said: "When I attacked Lü Bu, Biao did not raid; at the Guandu battle he did not rescue Yuan Shao; he is a thief who only guards himself and ought to be dealt with later."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei quotes him calling Liu Biao a passive "self-guarding thief" who never helped Lü Bu or Yuan Shao.

sentences.zh: 譚、尚狡猾，當乘其亂。

translations.literal: Tan and Shang are crafty; one ought to ride their chaos."
translations.idiomatic: "The Yuan brothers are treacherous; we should exploit their civil war."

sentences.zh: 縱譚挾詐，不終束手，使我破尚，徧收其地，利自多矣。

translations.literal: Even if Tan harbors deceit and in the end will not fold hands, letting me break Shang and fully gather his lands brings profit of itself in great measure."
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yuan Tan is lying, crushing Yuan Shang for him still wins us most of Hebei."

sentences.zh: 」乃許之。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon he consented."
translations.idiomatic: He agreed to the alliance."

sentences.zh: 公乃引軍還。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: He wheeled his army north again.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，到黎陽，爲子整與譚結婚。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, he reached Liyang and for his son Zheng made marriage alliance with Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he reached Liyang and betrothed his son Cao Zheng to Yuan Tan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：紹死至此，過周五月耳。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: from Shao's death to here, more than five months have passed.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that fewer than six months had passed since Yuan Shao's death.

sentences.zh: 譚雖出後其伯，不爲紹服三年，而於再朞之內以行吉禮，悖矣。

translations.literal: Though Tan was given out posthumously to his uncle, he did not observe three years' mourning for Shao, yet within the second anniversary period performed auspicious rites; it was contrary.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan had been posthumously adopted to an uncle's line yet held a wedding while still in mourning for Yuan Shaoa breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 魏武或以權宜與之約言；

translations.literal: Wei Wu perhaps by expediency made agreement in words with him;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao may have treated the match as a political expedient;

sentences.zh: 今云結婚，未必便以此年成禮。〉

translations.literal: now it says marriage alliance; not necessarily did the rites complete in that year."
translations.idiomatic: so the betrothal need not have been consummated that same year."

sentences.zh: 尚聞公北，乃釋平原還鄴。

translations.literal: Shang heard the duke had gone north, then released Pingyuan and returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang abandoned the siege of Pingyuan and rushed back to Ye when he heard Cao Cao was marching north.

sentences.zh: 東平呂曠、呂翔叛尚，屯陽平，率其衆降，封爲列侯。

translations.literal: Dongping Lü Kuang and Lü Xiang rebelled against Shang, encamped at Yangping, led their host to surrender, and were enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kuang and Lü Xiang of Dongping mutinied against Yuan Shang, camped at Yangping, came over with their troops, and received full marquisates.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：譚之圍解，陰以將軍印綬假曠。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: after Tan's siege was lifted, he secretly lent the general's seal and ribbon to Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says Yuan Tan secretly handed his general's credentials to Lü Kuang after the siege lifted.

sentences.zh: 曠受印送之，公曰：「我固知譚之有小計也。

translations.literal: Kuang received the seal and sent it in; the duke said: "I solidly knew Tan had petty stratagems."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Kuang delivered the seal to Cao Cao, who said, "I knew Yuan Tan was playing games."

sentences.zh: 欲使我攻尚，得以其閒略民聚衆，比尚之破，可得自彊以乘我弊也。

translations.literal: He wished to make me attack Shang, thereby in the interval ravage the people and gather multitudes; by the time Shang was broken, he could strengthen himself to ride my exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: "He wanted me to wear down Yuan Shang while he plundered and recruited; once Shang fell he meant to grow strong on my fatigue."

sentences.zh: 尚破我盛，何弊之乘乎？」〉

translations.literal: When Shang is broken I am at full flourishwhat weakness is there to ride?"
translations.idiomatic: "Once Yuan Shang is gone I will be at peak strengthwhat opening would he find?"

sentences.zh: 九年春正月，濟河，遏淇水入白溝以通糧道。

translations.literal: Ninth year spring first month, crossed the Yellow River, dammed the Qi River into the Baigou canal to open a grain route.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 204 CE, he bridged the Yellow River, diverted the Qi into Baigou, and opened a supply line.

sentences.zh: 二月，尚復攻譚，留蘇由、審配守鄴。

translations.literal: Second month, Shang again attacked Tan, leaving Su You and Shen Pei to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yuan Shang struck Yuan Tan again, leaving Su You and Shen Pei to hold Ye.

sentences.zh: 公進軍到洹水，由降。

translations.literal: The duke advanced to the Huan River; You surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao reached the Huan River and Su You capitulated.

sentences.zh: 旣至，攻鄴，爲土山、地道。

translations.literal: Having arrived, he attacked Ye, making earth mounds and tunnels.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Ye with siege mounds and saps.

sentences.zh: 武安長尹楷屯毛城，通上黨糧道。

translations.literal: Wu'an magistrate Yin Kai encamped at Maocheng, connecting the Shangdang grain road.
translations.idiomatic: Wu'an magistrate Yin Kai held Maocheng, keeping the Shangdang supply line open for Ye.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，留曹洪攻鄴，公自將擊楷，破之而還。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, he left Cao Hong to attack Ye; the duke personally led a strike against Kai, broke him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he left Cao Hong before Ye while he personally routed Yin Kai.

sentences.zh: 尚將沮鵠守邯鄲，

translations.literal: Shang's general Ju Hu guarded Handan,
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang's officer Ju Hu defended Handan,

sentences.zh: 〈沮音菹，河朔閒今猶有此姓。

translations.literal: (Ju is read like zu; in Hebei this surname still exists today.)
translations.idiomatic: (The surname Ju is still heard in Hebei, pronounced like the pickle character zu.)

sentences.zh: 鵠，沮授子也。〉

translations.literal: Hu was Ju Shou's son."
translations.idiomatic: Ju Hu was the son of Yuan Shao's adviser Ju Shou."

sentences.zh: 又擊拔之。

translations.literal: Again he struck and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao took Handan as well.

sentences.zh: 易陽令韓範、涉長梁岐舉縣降，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: Yiyang magistrate Han Fan and She magistrate Liang Qi raised their counties in surrender; they were granted rank as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Han Fan of Yiyang and Liang Qi of She surrendered whole counties and received guannei marquis rank.

sentences.zh: 五月，毀土山、地道，作圍壍，決漳水灌城；

translations.literal: Fifth month, he destroyed the earth mounds and tunnels, made a circumvallation, and opened the Zhang River to flood the city;
translations.idiomatic: In May he tore down the mounds, ringed Ye with a wall, and broke the Zhang River banks to flood it;

sentences.zh: 城中餓死者過半。

translations.literal: Within the city those who starved to death exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: more than half the population inside starved.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，尚還救鄴，諸將皆以爲「此歸師，人自爲戰，不如避之」。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, Shang returned to rescue Ye; the generals all said, "This is a returning army; each man fights for himself; better to avoid them."
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shang marched to relieve Ye in the seventh month, his officers warned that a desperate relief column fights like devils and should be avoided.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「尚從大道來，當避之；

translations.literal: The duke said: "If Shang comes by the great road, we ought to avoid him;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "If he comes by the main road, sidestep him;

sentences.zh: 若循西山來者，此成禽耳。

translations.literal: if he follows the western mountains to come, this is game already in the net."
translations.idiomatic: if he threads the western hills, we have him."

sentences.zh: 」尚果循西山來，臨滏水爲營。

translations.literal: Shang indeed followed the western mountains and camped along the Fushui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang took the mountain track and camped on the Fushui as predicted.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：遣候者數部前後參之，皆曰「定從西道，已在邯鄲」。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: he sent several groups of scouts ahead and behind to check; all said, "They are surely taking the western road; they are already at Handan."
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says scouts reported Yuan Shang's column on the western road near Handan.

sentences.zh: 公大喜，會諸將曰：「孤已得冀州，諸君知之乎？

translations.literal: The duke greatly rejoiced, met the generals, and said: "I have already obtained Ji province; do you gentlemen know it?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao gathered his generals and announced, "Ji province is already mine; did you know?"

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「不知。

translations.literal: All said: "We do not know."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "No, my lord."

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「諸君方見不久也。」〉

translations.literal: The duke said: "You gentlemen will see it before long."
translations.idiomatic: "You will see for yourselves soon enough."

sentences.zh: 夜遣兵犯圍，公逆擊破走之，遂圍其營。

translations.literal: By night he sent troops to raid the siege lines; the duke counter-struck, routed them, and thereupon besieged his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang probed the siege by night; Cao Cao counterattacked, drove him off, and bottled his camp.

sentences.zh: 未合，尚懼。

translations.literal: Before the encirclement closed, Shang was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Before the ring closed Yuan Shang panicked.

sentences.zh: 故豫州刺史陰夔及陳琳乞降，公不許，爲圍益急。

translations.literal: The former Inspector Yin Kui and Chen Lin begged to surrender; the duke did not permit it and pressed the siege harder.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kui and Chen Lin offered to yield, but Cao Cao refused and tightened the noose.

sentences.zh: 尚夜遁，保祁山，追擊之。

translations.literal: Shang fled by night, guarded Qishan; he pursued and struck him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang bolted to Qishan; Cao Cao pursued.

sentences.zh: 其將馬延、張顗等臨陣降，衆大潰，尚走中山。

translations.literal: His generals Ma Yan, Zhang Yi, and others surrendered at the battle line; the host greatly collapsed; Shang fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yan, Zhang Yi, and other officers defected in the field; the army collapsed and Yuan Shang fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 盡獲其輜重，得尚印綬節鉞，使尚降人示其家，城中崩沮。

translations.literal: He fully captured their baggage, obtained Shang's seals, tally, and axe, and had Shang's surrendered men show them to his household; within the city morale collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao seized the baggage train, Yuan Shang's imperial regalia, and paraded captives before Ye until the defenders broke.

sentences.zh: 八月，審配兄子榮夜開所守城東門內兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shen Pei's nephew Rong by night opened the eastern gate he guarded to the inner troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shen Rong, Shen Pei's nephew, opened the east gate he commanded to Cao Cao's men.

sentences.zh: 配逆戰，敗，生禽配，斬之，鄴定。

translations.literal: Pei counterattacked, was defeated, was captured alive, and was beheaded; Ye was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei sortied, was taken alive, executed, and Ye fell.

sentences.zh: 公臨祀紹墓，哭之流涕；

translations.literal: The duke personally sacrificed at Shao's tomb and wept with flowing tears;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao visited Yuan Shao's grave and wept openly;

sentences.zh: 慰勞紹妻，還其家人寶物，賜雜繒絮，廩食之。

translations.literal: he comforted Shao's wife, returned her family treasures, granted mixed silks and wadding, and supplied food from the granary.
translations.idiomatic: he comforted the Yuan widow, restored her household goods, gave her silks and staples from the state granary.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛云：昔者先王之爲誅賞也，將以懲惡勸善，永彰鑒戒。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: When former kings applied punishments and rewards, they intended to punish evil and encourage good, to display forever mirror and warning.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng argues that ancient kings used reward and punishment to teach the realm,

sentences.zh: 紹因世艱危，遂懷逆謀，上議神器，下干國紀。

translations.literal: Shao by the world's peril and danger harbored a treasonous plot, above deliberated the divine vessel, below interfered with the state's norms.
translations.idiomatic: while Yuan Shao exploited chaos to grasp at the throne and trample law.

sentences.zh: 荐社汙宅，古之制也。

translations.literal: Defiling shrine and house is the ancient regulation.
translations.idiomatic: His line deserved extirpation by classical standards.

sentences.zh: 而乃盡哀於逆臣之冢，加恩於饕餮之室，爲政之道，於斯躓矣。

translations.literal: Yet to pour full mourning on a treacherous minister's tomb and heap favor on a devouring householdin the way of government, here he stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cao Cao wept at the tomb of a rebel and pampered his kinthat is a stumble in statecraft.

sentences.zh: 夫匿怨友人，前哲所恥，稅驂舊館，義無虛涕，苟道乖好絕，何哭之有！

translations.literal: To hide resentment while calling someone friend, former sages were ashamed of it; unharnessing at an old inn, righteousness allows no empty tears; if the Way parts and friendship ends, what is there to weep for!
translations.idiomatic: The sages despised feigned friendship; duty does not demand hollow tears once bonds are broken.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高失之於項氏，魏武遵謬於此舉，豈非百慮之一失也。〉

translations.literal: Former Han Gao mis-stepped with the Xiang clan; Wei Wu followed error in this actis it not one lapse among a hundred reflections."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu erred with Xiang Yu's burial; Cao Cao repeats the mistake."

sentences.zh: 初，紹與公共起兵，紹問公曰：「若事不輯，則方面何所可據？

translations.literal: At first, when Shao with the duke jointly raised troops, Shao asked the duke: "If affairs do not come together, on what quarter can one rely?"
translations.idiomatic: When they first raised armies together, Yuan Shao asked Cao Cao which territory he would fall back on if they failed.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「足下意以爲何如？

translations.literal: The duke said: "What does your foot think?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao returned the question: "What would you choose?"

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「吾南據河，北阻燕、代，兼戎狄之衆，南向以爭天下，庶可以濟乎？

translations.literal: Shao said: "I south hold the Yellow River, north block Yan and Dai, combine the hosts of Rong and Di, and southward contend for the realmperhaps that can succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao said he would hold the river, seal the northern passes, rally steppe auxiliaries, and push south for the empire.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「吾任天下之智力，以道御之，無所不可。」

translations.literal: The duke said: "I employ the realm's wisdom and strength and govern them by the Way; nothing is impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "I will use every talent the realm offers and lead them by principle; then no direction is closed to me."

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖又云：「湯、武之王，豈同上哉？

translations.literal: The Fu zi says: Taizu also said: "The kings Tang and Wu, could they be the same as high lords?"
translations.idiomatic: The Master Fu records Cao Cao adding, "The founders Tang and Wu were not mere regional lords."

sentences.zh: 若以險固爲資，則不能應機而變化也。」〉

translations.literal: If one relies on perilous fortifications as capital, then one cannot respond to opportunity and change."
translations.idiomatic: "Lean only on terrain and you cannot adapt when fortune shifts."

sentences.zh: 九月，令曰：「河北罹袁氏之難，其令無出今年租賦！

translations.literal: Ninth month, he issued an order: "Hebei has suffered the Yuans' calamity; let there be no rent or tax this year!"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he remitted the year's taxes for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 」重豪彊兼并之法，百姓喜恱。

translations.literal: He emphasized the law against powerful houses' annexations; the hundred surnames rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He tightened laws against great-clan land-grabs, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載公令曰：「有國有家者，不患寡而患不均，不患貧而患不安。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the duke's order: "Those who have a state or a family do not worry about scarcity but worry about inequality; do not worry about poverty but worry about insecurity."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei quotes his edict: rulers should fear inequality and unrest, not mere want.

sentences.zh: 袁氏之治也，使豪彊擅恣，親戚兼并；

translations.literal: Under the Yuan regime, they let powerful houses act as they pleased and kin annex neighbors;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuans the mighty seized what they wished and relatives swallowed neighbors' land;

sentences.zh: 下民貧弱，代出租賦，衒鬻家財，不足應命；

translations.literal: the lower people were poor and weak, substituted paying rent and tax, hawked family wealth, yet could not meet demands;
translations.idiomatic: the poor paid their lords' taxes, sold their goods, and still could not satisfy collectors;

sentences.zh: 審配宗族，至乃藏匿罪人，爲逋逃主。

translations.literal: Shen Pei's clan group went so far as to hide criminals and act as masters for fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pei's kin harbored fugitives and sheltered outlaws.

sentences.zh: 欲望百姓親附，甲兵彊盛，豈可得邪！

translations.literal: Desiring the hundred surnames to draw close and weapons to grow stronghow could that be obtained!"
translations.idiomatic: How could such a regime win the people or a strong army!"

sentences.zh: 其收田租畝四升，戶出絹二匹、緜二斤而已，他不得擅興發。

translations.literal: Collect field rent at four sheng per mu, per household only two bolts of silk and two jin of floss; beyond this none may on their own impose levies.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the rate at four sheng of grain per mu and two bolts of silk plus two jin of floss per household, forbidding any extra exactions.

sentences.zh: 郡國守相明檢察之，無令彊民有所隱藏，而弱民兼賦也。」〉

translations.literal: Commandery and state guardians shall clearly inspect; do not let strong people hide anything while weak people bear double taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Local magistrates must audit accounts so the rich cannot hide income and the poor cannot be double-taxed."

sentences.zh: 天子以公領冀州牧，公讓還兖州。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven appointed the duke to act as shepherd of Ji province; the duke declined and returned Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him inspector of Ji, but he yielded the title and kept Yan instead.

sentences.zh: 公之圍鄴也，譚略取甘陵、安平、勃海、河閒。

translations.literal: When the duke besieged Ye, Tan seized Ganling, Anping, Bohai, and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: While Ye was under siege Yuan Tan snapped up Ganling, Anping, Bohai, and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 尚敗，還中山。

translations.literal: Shang was defeated and returned to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang fell back to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 譚攻之，尚奔故安，遂并其衆。

translations.literal: Tan attacked him; Shang fled to Gu'an, thereupon annexed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan attacked; Yuan Shang fled to Gu'an and Yuan Tan absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 公遺譚書，責以負約，與之絕婚，女還，然後進軍。

translations.literal: The duke sent Tan a letter blaming him for breaking the covenant, broke off the marriage alliance, returned the daughter, and then advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote denouncing the broken pact, annulled the betrothal, sent the bride home, and marched.

sentences.zh: 譚懼，拔平原，走保南皮。

translations.literal: Tan was afraid, abandoned Pingyuan, fled to protect Nanpi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tan abandoned Pingyuan and bolted to Nanpi.

sentences.zh: 十二月，公入平原，略定諸縣。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the duke entered Pingyuan and pacified the various counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he occupied Pingyuan and secured its counties.

sentences.zh: 十年春正月，攻譚，破之，斬譚，誅其妻子，冀州平。

translations.literal: Tenth year spring first month, attacked Tan, broke him, beheaded Tan, executed his wife and children; Ji province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 205 CE, he stormed Nanpi, killed Yuan Tan, executed his family, and pacified Ji.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：公攻譚，旦及日中不決；

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: when the duke attacked Tan, from dawn to midday it was not decided;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says the assault stalled from dawn until noon;

sentences.zh: 公乃自執桴鼓，士卒咸奮，應時破陷。〉

translations.literal: the duke thereupon personally grasped the drum mallet; soldiers all roused and in the moment broke and took the city."
translations.idiomatic: then Cao Cao beat the war drums himself and the men carried the walls in one rush."

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「其與袁氏同惡者，與之更始。

translations.literal: He issued an order: "Those who shared evil with the Yuan clan shall be given a fresh start."
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed amnesty for everyone who had sided with the Yuans.

sentences.zh: 」令民不得復私讎，禁厚葬，皆一之於法。

translations.literal: He ordered the people not again to pursue private vengeance, prohibited lavish burials, and unified all under the law.
translations.idiomatic: Private feuds, extravagant funerals, and all other matters were brought under uniform law.

sentences.zh: 是月，袁熙大將焦觸、張南等叛攻熙、尚，熙、尚奔三郡烏丸。

translations.literal: That month, Yuan Xi's great generals Jiao Chu and Zhang Nan and others rebelled, attacked Xi and Shang; Xi and Shang fled to the three-commanderies Wuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Jiao Chu and Zhang Nan mutinied against Yuan Xi, who fled with Yuan Shang to the Wuhuan of the three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 觸等舉其縣降，封爲列侯。

translations.literal: Chu and the others raised their counties in surrender and were enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: They surrendered their districts and received full marquisates.

sentences.zh: 初討譚時，民亡椎冰，

translations.literal: At first when campaigning against Tan, the people fled pounding ice,
translations.idiomatic: During the Nanpi campaign peasants fled the corvée of ice-breaking,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲討譚時，川渠水凍，使民椎冰以通舩，民憚役而亡。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that when campaigning against Tan, the canals were frozen; they made the people pound ice to open passage for boats; the people feared the labor and fled."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi explains that frozen rivers forced laborers to break ice for supply boats, and many ran away."

sentences.zh: 令不得降。

translations.literal: The order was that they could not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade accepting those deserters.

sentences.zh: 頃之，亡民有詣門首者，公謂曰：「聽汝則違令，殺汝則誅首，歸深自藏，無爲吏所獲。

translations.literal: Before long, fugitive people came to the gate to turn themselves in; the duke said to them: "If I heed you I violate the order; if I kill you I punish those who surrender; go deep and hide yourselves, do not be caught by clerks."
translations.idiomatic: When runaways appeared at headquarters, Cao Cao told them, "If I spare you I break my decree; if I execute you I punish capitulation; slip away and hide where officials cannot find you."

sentences.zh: 」民垂泣而去；

translations.literal: The people wept hanging their heads and departed;
translations.idiomatic: They left in tears;

sentences.zh: 後竟捕得。

translations.literal: afterward they were indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: yet were caught afterward anyway.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，黑山賊張燕率其衆十餘萬降，封爲列侯。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, Black Mountain bandit Zhang Yan led his host of more than a hundred thousand to surrender and was enfeoffed as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Zhang Yan of the Black Mountains surrendered over a hundred thousand men and became a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 故安趙犢、霍奴等殺幽州刺史、涿郡太守。

translations.literal: Gu'an Zhao Du, Huo Nu, and others killed the Inspector of You and the grand administrator of Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Du and Huo Nu of Gu'an murdered the inspector of You and the governor of Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 三郡烏丸攻鮮于輔於獷平。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan of three commanderies attacked Xianyu Fu at Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuhuan of three commanderies besieged Xianyu Fu at Guangping.

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》郡國志曰：獷平，縣名，屬漁陽郡。〉

translations.literal: The Xu Han shu treatise on commanderies and states says: Guangping is a county name belonging to Yuyang commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The Later Han geography notes Guangping as a Yuyang county."

sentences.zh: 秋八月，公征之，斬犢等，乃渡潞河救獷平，烏丸奔走出塞。

translations.literal: Autumn eighth month, the duke campaigned against them, beheaded Du and others, then crossed the Lu River to relieve Guangping; the Wuhuan fled running out of the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he executed the rebels, crossed the Lu River, relieved Guangping, and drove the Wuhuan beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 九月，令曰：「阿黨比周，先聖所疾也。

translations.literal: Ninth month, he issued an order: "Faction and clique, former sages abhorred it."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he condemned clique politics.

sentences.zh: 聞冀州俗，父子異部，更相毀譽。

translations.literal: I have heard that in Ji custom, father and son serve in different departments and mutually slander and praise.
translations.idiomatic: He had heard that in Ji fathers and sons in rival offices traduce each other for factional gain.

sentences.zh: 昔直不疑無兄，世人謂之盜嫂；

translations.literal: Formerly Zhi Buyi had no elder brother, yet the world called him one who stole his sister-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Buyi had no brother yet rumor called him his sister-in-law's seducer;

sentences.zh: 弟五伯魚三娶孤女，謂之撾婦翁；

translations.literal: the fifth brother Yu thrice married an orphan girl, and people called it beating the father-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Fifth Brother Yu thrice wed an orphan and gossip mocked his fathers-in-law;

sentences.zh: 王鳳擅權，谷永比之申伯；

translations.literal: Wang Feng monopolized power, yet Gu Yong compared him to the Earl of Shen;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng's faction drew praise from Gu Yong like the Earl of Shen;

sentences.zh: 王商忠議，張匡謂之左道：此皆以白爲黑，欺天罔君者也。

translations.literal: Wang Shang offered loyal counsel, yet Zhang Kuang called it heterodox path: these all took white for black and deceived Heaven and beguiled the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: loyal Wang Shang was smeared as a sorcererall lies that invert truth and cheat the throne."

sentences.zh: 吾欲整齊風俗，四者不除，吾以爲羞。

translations.literal: I wish to set in order custom and wind; if these four are not removed, I take it as shame."
translations.idiomatic: "Until such slander stops I will be ashamed of my rule."

sentences.zh: 」冬十月，公還鄴。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the duke returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 初，袁紹以甥高幹領并州牧，公之拔鄴，幹降，遂以爲刺史。

translations.literal: At first Yuan Shao made his nephew Gao Gan act as shepherd of Bing province; when the duke took Ye, Gan surrendered, and he was thereupon made inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao had put his nephew Gao Gan over Bing; after Ye fell Gao Gan submitted and stayed on as inspector.

sentences.zh: 幹聞公討烏丸，乃以州叛，執上黨太守，舉兵守壺關口。

translations.literal: When Gan heard the duke was campaigning against the Wuhuan, then rebelled with the province, seized the Shangdang grand administrator, raised troops, and guarded Hukou pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao marched against the Wuhuan, Gao Gan revolted, seized the Shangdang governor, and blocked Hukou.

sentences.zh: 遣樂進、李典擊之，幹還守壺關城。

translations.literal: He dispatched Yue Jin and Li Dian to strike them; Gan returned to defend Hukou city.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Jin and Li Dian attacked until Gao Gan fell back inside Hukou city.

sentences.zh: 十一年春正月，公征幹。

translations.literal: Eleventh year spring first month, the duke campaigned against Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 206 CE, he marched against Gao Gan.

sentences.zh: 幹聞之，乃留其別將守城，走入匈奴，求救於單于，單于不受。

translations.literal: When Gan heard it, he left his lieutenant general to guard the city and fled into the Xiongnu, begging rescue from the Shanyu; the Shanyu did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan abandoned his deputy, fled to the Xiongnu for aid, and the shanyu refused him.

sentences.zh: 公圍壺關三月，拔之。

translations.literal: The duke besieged Hukou three months and took it.
translations.idiomatic: After a three-month siege he took Hukou pass.

sentences.zh: 幹遂走荊州，上洛都尉王琰捕斬之。

translations.literal: Gan thereupon fled to Jingzhou; Shangluo commandant Wang Yan captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan bolted toward Jingzhou; Shangluo commandant Wang Yan ran him down and executed him.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，公東征海賊管承，至淳于，遣樂進、李典擊破之，承走入海島。

translations.literal: Autumn eighth month, the duke east campaigned against sea bandit Guan Cheng, reached Chunyu, dispatched Yue Jin and Li Dian to break him; Cheng fled running into sea islands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn he marched east against the pirate Guan Cheng, reached Chunyu, sent Yue Jin and Li Dian to defeat him, and Guan Cheng fled to offshore islands.

sentences.zh: 割東海之襄賁、郯、戚以益琅邪，省昌慮郡。

translations.literal: He severed Donghai's Xiangben, Tan, and Qi to enlarge Langye, abolished Changlu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred Xiangben, Tan, and Qi from Donghai to Langye commandery and abolished Changlu.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載十月乙亥令曰：「夫治世御衆，建立輔弼，誡在面從，詩稱『聽用我謀，庶無大悔』，斯實君臣懇懇之求也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records an order of the tenth month yihai day: "For governing the age and controlling the multitude, establishing assistants and supports, the warning is against yes-men to the face; the Odes say 'hearken to my plans and you will have no great regret'this is truly what ruler and minister earnestly seek."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei preserves his yihai-day edict of the tenth month demanding frank counsel instead of flattery, quoting the Classic of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 吾充重任，每懼失中，頻年已來，不聞嘉謀，豈吾開延不勤之咎邪？

translations.literal: I fill a heavy charge and always fear missing the mean; for years now I have not heard good plansis it my fault for not opening the way diligently enough?"
translations.idiomatic: "I bear a heavy burden and fear misjudgment; for years I have heard too few good plansis that my fault for not inviting criticism?"

sentences.zh: 自今已後，諸掾屬治中、別駕，常以月旦各言其失，吾將覽焉。」〉

translations.literal: From now on, all clerks and aides, headquarters and chief clerks, on each new moon shall each speak of my faults; I will read them."
translations.idiomatic: "Henceforth every chief clerk shall on the first of each month report my faults for my review."

sentences.zh: 三郡烏丸承天下亂，破幽州，略有漢民合十餘萬戶。

translations.literal: The Wuhuan of three commanderies, riding the realm's chaos, broke You province and seized more than a hundred thousand households of Han people.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting civil war, the Wuhuan of three commanderies overran You and carried off a hundred thousand Han households.

sentences.zh: 袁紹皆立其酋豪爲單于，以家人子爲己女，妻焉。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao all established their chieftains as shanyu, taking servant girls as his own daughters and marrying them to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao recognized their chiefs as shanyus and sealed the alliances by marrying them to women he claimed as daughters.

sentences.zh: 遼西單于蹋頓尤彊，爲紹所厚，故尚兄弟歸之，數入塞爲害。

translations.literal: Liaoxi Shanyu Tadun was especially strong, was treated generously by Shao; therefore Shang and his younger brothers returned to him and repeatedly entered the passes to do harm.
translations.idiomatic: Tadun of Liaoxi was the strongest of these clients and had been favored by Yuan Shao, so the Yuan brothers fled to him and raided inside the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 公將征之，鑿渠，自呼沲入泒水，

translations.literal: The duke was about to campaign against them, dug a canal from Hutuo into the Gu River,
translations.idiomatic: To supply the northern expedition he cut a canal from the Hutuo River into the Gu River,

sentences.zh: 〈泒音孤。〉

translations.literal: (Gu is read like gu.)
translations.idiomatic: The commentary gives the reading of that place-name graph as gu.

sentences.zh: 名平虜渠；

translations.literal: named the Pacify-the-Barbarians Canal;
translations.idiomatic: He named it the Pacify-the-Barbarians Canal;

sentences.zh: 又從泃河口

translations.literal: again from the Ju River mouth
translations.idiomatic: then from the mouth of the Ju River

sentences.zh: 〈泃音句。〉

translations.literal: (Ju is read like ju.)
translations.idiomatic: The commentary reads the river name graph as ju.

sentences.zh: 鑿入潞河，名泉州渠，以通海。

translations.literal: dug into the Lu River, named the Quanzhou Canal, in order to reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He cut through to the Lu River in a channel called the Quanzhou Canal to link the interior with the sea.

sentences.zh: 十二月春二月，公自淳于還鄴。

translations.literal: Twelfth month spring second month, the duke returned from Chunyu to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring of the twelfth year of Jian'an he returned from Chunyu to Ye.

sentences.zh: 丁酋，令曰：「吾起義兵誅暴亂，於今十九年，所征必克，豈吾功哉？

translations.literal: On the day dingyou he issued an order: "I raised righteous troops to punish violence and chaos; down to now nineteen years; wherever I campaigned, there was sure victoryis it my merit?"
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day he proclaimed, "Nineteen years ago I took up arms against tyranny; every campaign has succeededbut the credit is not mine alone."

sentences.zh: 乃賢士大夫之力也。

translations.literal: It is the strength of worthy gentlemen and grandees.
translations.idiomatic: It belongs to the worthy men who have served with me.

sentences.zh: 天下雖未悉定，吾當要與賢士大夫共定之；

translations.literal: Though the realm is not yet fully settled, I must with worthy gentlemen and grandees settle it together;
translations.idiomatic: "The empire is not yet at peace, and I mean to finish the work with you;

sentences.zh: 而專饗其勞，吾何以安焉！

translations.literal: yet alone to enjoy their laborhow can I be at peace!"
translations.idiomatic: yet I alone would swallow the gloryhow could I rest easy!"

sentences.zh: 其促定功行封。

translations.literal: Hasten to fix merit and carry out enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Hurry to register merit and grant fiefs."

sentences.zh: 」於是大封功臣二十餘人，皆爲列侯，其餘各以次受封，及復死事之孤，輕重各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly enfeoffed more than twenty meritorious subjects, all as full marquises; the rest each in order received enfeoffment, and he restored orphans of those who died in service, heavy and light each having its gradation.
translations.idiomatic: He then ennobled over twenty chief followers as full marquises, ranked the rest in order, and pensioned the orphans of the fallen according to merit.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載公令曰：「昔趙奢、竇嬰之爲將也，受賜千金，一朝散之，故能濟成大功，永世流聲。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the duke's order: "Formerly when Zhao She and Dou Ying were generals, they received a thousand in gold and scattered it in one morning; therefore they could accomplish great merit and their fame flows forever."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei quotes him praising Zhao She and Dou Ying, who shared sudden wealth with their men and won lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 吾讀其文，未甞不慕其爲人也。

translations.literal: I read their texts and never do I not admire their persons.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I read their stories I admire them.

sentences.zh: 與諸將士大夫共從戎事，幸賴賢人不愛其謀，羣士不遺其力，是以夷險平亂，而吾得竊大賞，戶邑三萬。

translations.literal: Together with the various generals and gentlemen and grandees I have followed military affairs; fortunately relying on worthies not sparing their plans, the host of gentlemen not leaving their strength, thereby in danger and safety we have pacified rebellion, while I have stolen a great reward, households and towns thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: You have shared every campaign; thanks to your counsel and courage we have crushed rebels while I alone have amassed thirty thousand households of fief.

sentences.zh: 追思竇嬰散金之義，今分所受租與諸將掾屬及故戍於陳、蔡者，庶以疇荅衆勞，不擅大惠也。

translations.literal: Recalling Dou Ying's meaning in scattering gold, now I divide the rent I receive among the generals, clerks, and those formerly garrisoned at Chen and Cai, hoping thereby to answer the host's toil and not monopolize great favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Dou Ying's spirit I now share my rents with officers and with veterans of the Chen–Cai garrisons so the reward is not mine alone.

sentences.zh: 宜差死事之孤，以租穀及之。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to grade orphans of those who died in service and give them rent grain.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans of the fallen shall be graded for grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 若年殷用足，租奉畢入，將大與衆人悉共饗之。」〉

translations.literal: If in a year the use is ample and rent tribute is fully collected, I will greatly with the multitude all together feast on it."
translations.idiomatic: When the harvest is full and taxes are in, I will feast the whole host with you."

sentences.zh: 將北征三郡烏丸，諸將皆曰：「袁尚，亡虜耳，夷狄貪而無親，豈能爲尚用？

translations.literal: He was about to north campaign against the Wuhuan of three commanderies; the generals all said: "Yuan Shang is a defeated fugitive only; the barbarians are greedy and without kinship; how can they work for Shang?"
translations.idiomatic: Before the northern expedition his generals argued, "Yuan Shang is a beaten refugee; the tribes care nothing for kin; why would they fight for him?"

sentences.zh: 今深入征之，劉備必說劉表以襲許。

translations.literal: Now if we deeply enter to campaign against them, Liu Bei is sure to persuade Liu Biao to raid Xu.
translations.idiomatic: "If we march deep into the steppe, Liu Bei will talk Liu Biao into striking Xu."

sentences.zh: 萬一爲變，事不可悔。

translations.literal: If by chance there is change, the affair cannot be regretted back."
translations.idiomatic: "If the capital falls we cannot undo it."

sentences.zh: 」惟郭嘉策表必不能任備，勸公行。

translations.literal: Only Guo Jia calculated that Biao would surely not be able to employ Bei, and urged the duke to go.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guo Jia judged that Liu Biao would never give Liu Bei real authority and urged the march.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，至無終。

translations.literal: Summer fifth month, he reached Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he reached Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，大水，傍海道不通，田疇請爲鄉導，公從之。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, great flood; the coastal road was impassable; Tian Chou requested to be local guide; the duke followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn floods blocked the coast road; Tian Chou offered to guide a mountain detour and Cao Cao accepted.

sentences.zh: 引軍出盧龍塞，塞外道絕不通，乃壍山堙谷五百餘里，經白檀，歷平岡，涉鮮卑庭，東指柳城。
