translations.literal: He led the army out Lulong Pass; outside the pass the road was cut off and impassable; then for more than five hundred li he trenched mountains and filled valleys, passed through Baitan, crossed Pinggang, crossed the Xianbei court, and pointed east toward Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He threaded Lulong Pass, cut a five-hundred-li road through mountains and valleys past Baitan and Pinggang, crossed Xianbei territory, and aimed for Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 未至二百里，虜乃知之。

translations.literal: Not yet two hundred li, the barbarians then knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Within two hundred li the enemy learned of his approach.

sentences.zh: 尚、熙與蹋頓、遼西單于樓班、右北平單于能臣抵之等，將數萬騎逆軍。

translations.literal: Shang, Xi with Tadun, Liaoxi Shanyu Louban, Right Beiping Shanyu Nengchen Dizhi and others led several tens of thousands of riders to oppose the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shang, Yuan Xi, Tadun, Louban of Liaoxi, Nengchen Dizhi of Right Beiping, and others met him with tens of thousands of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 八月，登白狼山，卒與虜遇，衆甚盛。

translations.literal: Eighth month, he ascended White Wolf Mountain; suddenly met the barbarians; the host was very large.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he climbed White Wolf Mountain and stumbled into a huge enemy host.

sentences.zh: 公車重在後，被甲者少，左右皆懼。

translations.literal: The duke's baggage train was behind; those in armor were few; those at his left and right were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: His wagons lagged behind, few men wore armor, and his staff was terrified.

sentences.zh: 公登高，望虜陳不整，乃縱兵擊之，使張遼爲先鋒，虜衆大崩，斬蹋頓及名王已下，胡、漢降者二十餘萬口。

translations.literal: The duke ascended high, saw the barbarian formation was not orderly, then released troops to strike them, made Zhang Liao the vanguard; the barbarian host greatly collapsed; he beheaded Tadun and those below famous kings; Hu and Han who surrendered were more than two hundred thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: From the height he saw their ranks were loose, ordered a charge with Zhang Liao in the lead, shattered them, killed Tadun and other chieftains, and accepted over two hundred thousand Hu and Han capitulations.

sentences.zh: 遼東單于速僕丸及遼西、北平諸豪，棄其種人，與尚、熙奔遼東，衆尚有數千騎。

translations.literal: Liaodong Shanyu Supuyan and Liaoxi and Beiping notables abandoned their tribesmen and fled Liaodong with Shang and Xi; the host still had several thousand riders.
translations.idiomatic: Supuyan of Liaodong and western notables abandoned their people and fled to Liaodong with the Yuan brothers, still trailing a few thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 初，遼東太守公孫康恃遠不服。

translations.literal: At first Liaodong Grand Administrator Gongsun Kang relied on distance and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong governor Gongsun Kang had long defied the court from his remote seat.

sentences.zh: 及公破烏丸，或說公遂征之，尚兄弟可禽也。

translations.literal: When the duke had broken the Wuhuan, some urged the duke thereupon to campaign against him; Shang and his younger brother could be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged an immediate strike on Liaodong to bag the Yuan brothers.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「吾方使康斬送尚、熙首，不煩兵矣。

translations.literal: The duke said: "I am about to make Kang behead and send Shang and Xi's heads; it will not trouble the army."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao said, "I will let Gongsun Kang send me their heads; no need to march."

sentences.zh: 」九月，公引兵自柳城還，

translations.literal: Ninth month, the duke led troops returning from Liucheng,
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he withdrew his army from Liucheng,

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：時寒且旱，二百里無復水，軍又乏食，殺馬數千匹以爲糧，鑿地入三十餘丈乃得水。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: at the time it was cold and also drought; for two hundred li there was again no water; the army also lacked food; they killed several thousand horses to use as grain; dug the earth more than thirty zhang before obtaining water.
translations.idiomatic: the Cao Man Zhuan describes bitter cold and drought, two hundred li without water, forced slaughter of thousands of horses for meat, and wells sunk thirty zhang before water came.

sentences.zh: 旣還，利問前諫者，衆莫知其故，人人皆懼。

translations.literal: After returning, he sharply questioned those who had remonstrated earlier; the host none knew the reason; each man was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Back in camp he sharply questioned the officers who had opposed the expedition; no one knew why and everyone feared punishment.

sentences.zh: 公皆厚賞之，曰：「孤前行，乘危以徼倖，雖得之，天所佐也，顧不可以爲常。

translations.literal: He all generously rewarded them, saying: "I earlier went forward, riding danger to seek fortune; though I obtained it, it was Heaven's aiding, yet one cannot take that as constant.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he rewarded them richly: "I took a reckless gamble and won by heaven's help; that cannot be the rule.

sentences.zh: 諸君之諫，萬安之計，是以相賞，後勿難言之。」〉

translations.literal: Your gentlemen's remonstrance was the plan of perfect safety; therefore I reward you; afterward do not find it hard to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Your warnings were the safe course; take this reward and never fear to speak your minds again."

sentences.zh: 康即斬尚、熙及速僕丸等，傳其首。

translations.literal: Kang thereupon beheaded Shang, Xi, and Supuyan and others, and forwarded their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Kang executed Yuan Shang, Yuan Xi, Supuyan, and their party and sent the heads south.

sentences.zh: 諸將或問：「公還而康斬送尚、熙，何也？

translations.literal: Some generals asked: "The duke returned yet Kang beheaded and sent Shang and Xi; why?"
translations.idiomatic: Officers asked why Gongsun Kang killed the Yuans only after Cao Cao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「彼素畏尚等，吾急之則并力，緩之則自相圖，其勢然也。

translations.literal: The duke said: "They plain feared Shang and the rest; if I pressed them they would unite their strength; if I eased them they would plot against each other; such was the momentum."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered, "Kang feared the Yuans; pressure would unite them, slackness would set them at each other's throats."

sentences.zh: 」十一月至易水，代郡烏丸行單于普富盧、上郡烏丸行單于那樓將其名王來賀。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, reaching Yi River, acting Shanyu Pulu of Dai commandery Wuhuan and acting Shanyu Lou of Shang commandery Wuhuan led their famous kings to come congratulate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month at the Yi River, Wuhuan acting shanyus Pulu of Dai and Lou of Shang led their chiefs to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月，公還鄴，作玄武池以肄舟師。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year spring first month, the duke returned to Ye, made the Black Warrior Pool to drill the navy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 208 CE, he returned to Ye and dug the Black Warrior Pool to train the fleet.

sentences.zh: 〈肄，以四反。

translations.literal: (Yi is read with the fourth tone.)
translations.idiomatic: The gloss prescribes the fourth tone for the graph read yi.

sentences.zh: 三蒼曰：「肄，習也。」〉

translations.literal: The San Cang says: "Yi means practice."
translations.idiomatic: The San Cang lexicon glosses that graph (read yi) as "drill" or "practice."

sentences.zh: 漢罷三公官，置丞相、御史大夫。

translations.literal: Han abolished the three dukes' offices and established chancellor and imperial counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court abolished the three excellencies and created the posts of chancellor and imperial counselor.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，以公爲丞相。

translations.literal: Summer sixth month, appointed the duke chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer he was named chancellor.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：使太常徐璆即授印綬。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xian's Daily Notes says: he sent Minister of Ceremonies Xu Qiu immediately to confer the seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The court diary records Minister Xu Qiu presenting the seals of office.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫不領中丞，置長史一人。

translations.literal: The imperial counselor did not supervise the palace assistant secretary; one chief clerk was established.
translations.idiomatic: The new imperial counselor post came with a chief clerk and without the old censorate tie.

sentences.zh: 《先賢行狀》曰：璆字孟平，廣陵人。

translations.literal: The Xianxian xingzhuang says: Qiu's style name was Mengping; he was a man of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The Worthies' Conduct describes Xu Qiu (courtesy Mengping) of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 少履清爽，立朝正色。

translations.literal: In youth he trod pure clarity; standing at court he had correct color.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was known for integrity and stern dignity at court.

sentences.zh: 歷任城、汝南、東海三郡，所在化行。

translations.literal: He successively served Rencheng, Runan, and Donghai three commanderies; wherever he was, transformation was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Rencheng, Runan, and Donghai he left a record of good rule.

sentences.zh: 被徵當還，爲袁術所劫。

translations.literal: When summoned to return, he was seized by Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu intercepted him when he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 術僭號，欲授以上公之位，璆終不爲屈。

translations.literal: Shu usurped the title and wished to confer on him the exalted duke's rank; Qiu in the end would not bend.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu declared himself emperor he offered Xu Qiu exalted rank, but Xu Qiu refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 術死後，璆得術璽，致之漢朝，拜衞尉太常；

translations.literal: After Shu died, Qiu obtained Shu's seal and delivered it to the Han court; he was appointed Minister of the Guards and Minister of Ceremonies;
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Shu's death Xu Qiu brought the imperial seal to the Han court and was named minister of the guards and minister of ceremonies;

sentences.zh: 公爲丞相，以位讓璆焉。〉

translations.literal: when the duke became chancellor, he yielded the rank to Qiu."
translations.idiomatic: when Cao Cao became chancellor he tried to yield precedence to Xu Qiu."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，公南征劉表。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, the duke south campaigned against Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he marched south against Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 八月，表卒，其子琮代，屯襄陽，劉備屯樊。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Biao died; his son Cong succeeded, encamped at Xiangyang; Liu Bei encamped at Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao died in the eighth month; Liu Cong held Xiangyang while Liu Bei was at Fan.

sentences.zh: 九月，公到新野，琮遂降，備走夏口。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the duke reached Xinye; Cong thereupon surrendered; Bei fled to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Cao Cao reached Xinye; Liu Cong capitulated and Liu Bei fled toward Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 公進軍江陵，下令荊州吏民，與之更始。

translations.literal: The duke advanced the army to Jiangling and issued an order to Jingzhou clerks and people to give them a fresh start.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Jiangling and proclaimed amnesty and a new beginning for the people of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃論荊州服從之功，侯者十五人，以劉表大將文聘爲江夏太守，使統本兵，引用荊州名士韓嵩、鄧義等。

translations.literal: He then discussed the merit of Jingzhou's submission; fifteen were enfeoffed as marquises; he made Liu Biao's great general Wen Pin grand administrator of Jiangxia, had him command his original troops, and employed Jingzhou notables such as Han Song and Deng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He ennobled fifteen men for surrendering Jingzhou, named Wen Pin governor of Jiangxia with his old command, and enrolled Han Song, Deng Yi, and other local luminaries.

sentences.zh: 〈衞恒《四體書勢序》曰：上谷王次仲善隷書，始爲楷法。

translations.literal: Wei Heng's preface to the Four Styles of Calligraphy says: Wang Cizhong of Shanggu was skilled at clerical script and first set the model for regular script.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng's preface credits Wang Cizhong of Shanggu with the first regular-script forms of clerical hand.

sentences.zh: 至靈帝好書，世多能者。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ling's love of writing, the age had many who could do it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling's passion for calligraphy produced many masters.

sentences.zh: 而師宜官爲最，甚矜其能，每書，輙削焚其札。

translations.literal: Yet Shi Yiguan was the best; he greatly prided himself on his ability; each time he wrote, he always shaved and burned his slips.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yiguan was the finest but so vain that he burned every draft.

sentences.zh: 梁鵠乃益爲版而飲之酒，候其醉而竊其札，鵠卒以攻書至選部尚書。

translations.literal: Liang Hu then enlarged a board and fed him wine, waited until he was drunk and stole his slips; Hu in the end by attacking calligraphy reached Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu got him drunk, stole his drafts, and parlayed the hand into an appointment as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 於是公欲爲洛陽令，鵠以爲北部尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the duke wished to make him magistrate of Luoyang; Hu thought it better to be northern district captain.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao first offered him Luoyang magistrate; Liang Hu chose the northern district captaincy instead.

sentences.zh: 鵠後依劉表。

translations.literal: Hu afterward relied on Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu later served Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 及荊州平，公募求鵠，鵠懼，自縛詣門，署軍假司馬，使在祕書，以勤書自効。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was pacified, the duke publicly sought Hu; Hu was afraid, bound himself and came to the gate; he was appointed acting army marshal of the staff, was put in the secretariat, and by diligent writing expiated his merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest Liang Hu surrendered bound, was made acting army marshal on staff, and worked in the secretariat to redeem himself by brushwork.

sentences.zh: 公甞懸著帳中，及以釘壁玩之，謂勝宜官。

translations.literal: The duge once hung his writing in the tent and also nailed it to the wall to admire, saying it surpassed Yiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao hung Liang Hu's calligraphy in his tent and on his wall, judging it finer than Shi Yiguan's.

sentences.zh: 鵠字孟皇，安定人。

translations.literal: Hu's style name was Menghuang; he was a man of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hu (courtesy Menghuang) came from Anding.

sentences.zh: 魏宮殿題署，皆鵠書也。

translations.literal: Wei palace hall inscriptions were all Hu's writing.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the plaques for Wei palace halls.

sentences.zh: 皇甫謐逸士傳曰：汝南王儁，字子文，少爲范滂、許章所識，與南陽岑晊善。

translations.literal: Huangfu Mi's Biographies of Recluses says: Wang Jun of Runan, style Ziwen, in youth was recognized by Fan Pang and Xu Zhang, and was on good terms with Cen Zhi of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Mi's recluses text tells of Wang Jun (courtesy Ziwen) of Runan, noted by Fan Pang and Xu Zhang, friend of Cen Zhi of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 公之爲布衣，特愛儁；

translations.literal: When the duke was common cloth, he especially loved Jun;
translations.idiomatic: While still a commoner Cao Cao was especially close to Wang Jun;

sentences.zh: 儁亦稱公有治世之具。

translations.literal: Jun also praised the duke as having the tools to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun in turn said Cao Cao had what it takes to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 及袁紹與弟術喪母，歸葬汝南，儁與公會之，會者三萬人。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shao with his younger brother Shu buried their mother at Runan, Jun met the duke at the gathering; those assembled were thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuans' mother's funeral in Runan, thirty thousand mourners saw Cao Cao and Wang Jun meet.

sentences.zh: 公於外密語儁曰：「天下將亂，爲亂魁者必此二人也。

translations.literal: The duge outside secretly said to Jun: "The realm is about to be in chaos; those who will be chiefs of chaos are surely these two men."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao whispered to Wang Jun, "Chaos is coming, and those two will lead it."

sentences.zh: 欲濟天下，爲百姓請命，不先誅此二子，亂今作矣。

translations.literal: Desiring to save the realm and seek life for the hundred surnames, if we do not first execute these two sons, chaos will now arise."
translations.idiomatic: "If we mean to save the empire we must kill those two first or the storm will break."

sentences.zh: 」儁曰：「如卿之言，濟天下者，舍卿復誰？

translations.literal: Jun said: "As you speak, the one who saves the realm, leaving you, who again is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun replied, "If anyone can save the age after them, it is you."

sentences.zh: 」相對而笑。

translations.literal: They faced each other and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: They looked at each other and laughed.

sentences.zh: 儁爲人外靜而內明，不應州郡三府之命。

translations.literal: Jun as a man was outwardly quiet yet inwardly bright; he did not answer summons from provinces, commanderies, or the three offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was outwardly calm and inwardly shrewd and ignored every official summons.

sentences.zh: 公車徵，不到，避地居武陵，歸儁者一百餘家。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage summoned him; he did not arrive; he avoided trouble and dwelt in Wuling; those who joined Jun were more than a hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He ignored imperial summons, retired to Wuling, and drew more than a hundred families with him.

sentences.zh: 帝之都許，復徵爲尚書，又不就。

translations.literal: When the emperor established the capital at Xu, again summoned him as secretary; again he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to Xu he was summoned as secretary and again refused.

sentences.zh: 劉表見紹彊，陰與紹通，儁謂表曰：「曹公，天下之雄也，必能興霸道，繼桓、文之功者也。

translations.literal: Liu Biao saw Shao was strong and secretly communicated with Shao; Jun said to Biao: "Lord Cao is a hero of the realm; he is sure able to revive hegemonic rule and continue the labors of Huan and Wen."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao secretly favored Yuan Shao while strong; Wang Jun warned him that Cao Cao was the true hegemon who could revive Qi and Jin greatness.

sentences.zh: 今乃釋近而就遠，如有一朝之急，遙望漠北之救，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Now you cast aside what is near and cleave to what is far; if one morning there is urgent need, gazing afar for rescue on the northern desertis it not difficult!"
translations.idiomatic: "You snub your neighbor to court a distant ally; when crisis strikes, a plea across the desert will come too late!"

sentences.zh: 」表不從。

translations.literal: Biao did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 儁年六十四，以壽終于武陵，公聞而哀傷。

translations.literal: Jun at age sixty-four by old age ended at Wuling; the duke heard and mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun died at sixty-four in Wuling; Cao Cao grieved when he heard.

sentences.zh: 及平荊州，自臨江迎喪，改葬于江陵，表爲先賢也。〉

translations.literal: When he pacified Jingzhou, he personally came to the river to welcome the coffin, changed burial at Jiangling, and displayed him as a former worthy."
translations.idiomatic: After taking Jingzhou Cao Cao met the hearse at the river, reburied Wang Jun at Jiangling, and honored him as a sage of old."

sentences.zh: 益州牧劉璋始受徵役，遣兵給軍。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yi Liu Zhang for the first time accepted conscript duty and dispatched troops to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yi province governor Liu Zhang for the first time answered a levy and sent troops to reinforce Cao Cao's host.

sentences.zh: 十二月，孫權爲備攻合肥。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Sun Quan for Bei attacked Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: That December Sun Quan struck Hefei to relieve Liu Bei's pressure.

sentences.zh: 公自江陵征備，至巴丘，遣張憙救合肥。

translations.literal: The duke from Jiangling campaigned against Bei, reached Baqiu, dispatched Zhang Xi to relieve Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched from Jiangling against Liu Bei, reached Baqiu, and sent Zhang Xi to reinforce Hefei.

sentences.zh: 權聞憙至，乃走。

translations.literal: Quan heard Xi had arrived, then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan withdrew when Zhang Xi approached.

sentences.zh: 公至赤壁，與備戰，不利。

translations.literal: The duke reached Chibi, battled with Bei; it was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: At Chibi he fought Liu Bei and lost.

sentences.zh: 於是大疫，吏士多死者，乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Thereupon a great pestilence; clerks and soldiers many died; thereupon he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: A plague swept the army; he abandoned the campaign and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 備遂有荊州、江南諸郡。

translations.literal: Bei then possessed Jingzhou and the various commanderies south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei took Jingzhou and the Jiangnan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 〈《山陽公載記》曰：公船艦爲備所燒，引軍從華容道步歸，遇泥濘，道不通，天又大風，悉使羸兵負草填之，騎乃得過。

translations.literal: The Shan gong zai ji says: the duke's ships were burned by Bei; he led the army from the Huarong road to return on foot; met mud and mire, the road impassable; heaven again had great wind; he ordered all weak soldiers to carry grass to fill it; riders then could pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Shan gong zai ji describes Liu Bei's fireship attack, then Cao Cao's retreat down the Huarong trail through mud and a gale, packing the mire with straw so cavalry could cross.

sentences.zh: 羸兵爲人馬所蹈藉，陷泥中，死者甚衆。

translations.literal: Weak soldiers were trampled by men and horses, sank in the mud; dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: The straw-bearers were trampled into the morass and died in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 軍旣得出，公大喜，諸將問之，公曰：「劉備，吾儔也。

translations.literal: When the army had gotten out, the duke greatly rejoiced; the generals asked him; the duke said: "Liu Bei is my peer."
translations.idiomatic: Once clear of the trap he crowed to his generals, "Liu Bei is my match."

sentences.zh: 但得計少晚；

translations.literal: Only his plan was a little late;
translations.idiomatic: His plan was just a beat too slow;

sentences.zh: 向使早放火，吾徒無類矣。

translations.literal: if he had set fire earlier, we would have had no survivors.
translations.idiomatic: had he fired earlier, none of us would have escaped."

sentences.zh: 」備尋亦放火而無所及。

translations.literal: Bei soon after also set fire but could not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei did try to burn the retreat later, but too late to catch them.

sentences.zh: 孫盛異同評曰：案吳志，劉備先破公軍，然後權攻合肥，而此記云權先攻合肥，後有赤壁之事。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's Yitong ping says: According to the Wu zhi, Liu Bei first broke the duke's army, then Quan attacked Hefei; yet this record says Quan first attacked Hefei, afterward there was the Chibi affair.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng notes that the Wu zhi order of events differs from this account of Hefei before Chibi.

sentences.zh: 二者不同，吳志爲是。〉

translations.literal: The two differ; the Wu zhi is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu chronicle is the reliable sequence."

sentences.zh: 十四年春三月，軍至譙，作輕舟，治水軍。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year spring third month, the army reached Qiao, made light boats, trained the navy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of spring, 209 CE, he reached Qiao, built light craft, and drilled the fleet.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，自渦入淮，出肥水，軍合肥。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, from the Guo River entered the Huai, exited the Fei River, army at Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he moved from the Guo into the Huai, then up the Fei to camp at Hefei.

sentences.zh: 辛未，令曰：「自頃已來，軍數征行，或遇疫氣，吏士死亡不歸，家室怨曠，百姓流離，而仁者豈樂之哉？

translations.literal: On the day xinwei he issued an order: "Recently armies have repeatedly gone on campaign; sometimes they meet pestilence; clerks and soldiers die and do not return; families resent separation; the hundred surnames drift and scatteryet would the benevolent delight in this?"
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day he mourned how plague and war left widows and refugees, asking whether any humane ruler could relish such suffering.

sentences.zh: 不得已也。

translations.literal: It was not what they wished.
translations.idiomatic: It was necessity, not choice."

sentences.zh: 其令死者家無基業不能自存者，縣官勿絕廩，長吏存卹撫循，以稱吾意。

translations.literal: Let the dead whose families have no foundation or property and cannot support themselvesnot let the county office cut off rations; senior clerks shall care and comfort them, to match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered counties to keep rations flowing to destitute military families and sent officers to comfort them."

sentences.zh: 」置揚州郡縣長吏，開芍陂屯田。

translations.literal: He established Yangzhou commandery and county senior clerks, opened Shao Lake military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yangzhou local officials and opened military farms at Shao Lake.

sentences.zh: 十二月，軍還譙。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the army returned to Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: That December the army was back in Qiao.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，下令曰：「自古受命及中興之君，曷甞不得賢人君子與之共治天下者乎！

translations.literal: Fifteenth year spring, he issued an order: "From antiquity, those receiving the mandate and restoration rulershow have they ever governed the realm without worthy gentlemen!"
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 210 CE he proclaimed that every founder needs wise ministers.

sentences.zh: 及其得賢也，曾不出閭巷，豈幸相遇哉？

translations.literal: When they obtained worthies, they did not come from beyond lanes and alleys; was it a lucky meeting?"
translations.idiomatic: Worthies are found in every ward; luck has little to do with it.

sentences.zh: 上之人不求之耳。

translations.literal: Those above do not seek them.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers fail because they do not search them out.

sentences.zh: 今天下尚未定，此特求賢之急時也。

translations.literal: Now the realm is not yet settled; this is especially the urgent time to seek worthies.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire still unsettled, recruitment is urgent.

sentences.zh: 『孟公綽爲趙、魏老則優，不可以爲滕、薛大夫』。

translations.literal: "Meng Gongchuo as steward to Zhao or Wei would excel, but could not serve as grandee of Teng or Xue."
translations.idiomatic: He quoted the Analects: not every talent fits every post.

sentences.zh: 若必廉士而後可用，則齊桓其何以霸世！

translations.literal: If one must have pure gentlemen only then employ them, how did Duke Huan of Qi hegemon his age!"
translations.idiomatic: If only the spotless may serve, how did Duke Huan ever build a hegemony?"

sentences.zh: 今天下得無有被褐懷玉而釣於渭濵者乎？

translations.literal: Now in the realm can there be none wearing coarse cloth, hiding jade, fishing by the Wei bank?"
translations.idiomatic: Are there no Jiang Taigongs in coarse cloth along the Wei?"

sentences.zh: 又得無盜嫂受金而未遇無知者乎？

translations.literal: Again can there be none who stole a sister-in-law, received gold, yet has not met one who knows them?"
translations.idiomatic: Are there no Chen Pings, slandered for scandal, awaiting a discerning eye?"

sentences.zh: 二三子其佐我明揚仄陋，唯才是舉，吾得而用之。

translations.literal: You gentlemen shall assist me to brighten the humble places; only talent shall be raised; I will obtain and use them."
translations.idiomatic: Help me lift hidden talent wherever merit lies; I will use it."

sentences.zh: 」冬，作銅爵臺。

translations.literal: Winter, he made the Bronze Sparrow Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he raised the Bronze Sparrow Terrace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏武故事》載公十二月己亥令曰：「孤始舉孝廉，年少，自以本非巖穴知名之士，恐爲海內人之所見凡愚，欲爲一郡守，好作政教，以建立名譽，使世士明知之；

translations.literal: The Wei Wu gushi records the duke's order of the twelfth month jihai day: "When I first rose as filial and incorrupt, I was young; I myself thought I was not a famous scholar of cliff and cave; I feared being seen by people within the seas as ordinary foolish; I wished to be a grand administrator of one commandery, fond of making government and instruction, to establish reputation, so that gentlemen of the age clearly knew it;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Wu anecdotes preserve his jihai-day memoir of 210 CE: as a young filial-and-incorrupt graduate he had hoped only to govern one commandery well and build a name,

sentences.zh: 故在濟南，始除殘去穢，平心選舉，違迕諸常侍。

translations.literal: therefore at Jinan I began to remove cruelty and cast away filth, impartially chose in elections, and opposed the various regular attendants."
translations.idiomatic: so at Jinan he purged corruption, held fair selections, and defied the eunuchs,

sentences.zh: 以爲彊豪所忿，恐致家禍，故以病還。

translations.literal: Therefore powerful houses resented me; I feared bringing disaster on the family; therefore I returned citing illness."
translations.idiomatic: which earned the hatred of magnates and forced him home on sick leave,

sentences.zh: 去官之後，年紀尚少，顧視同歲中，年有五十，未名爲老，內自圖之，從此却去二十年，待天下清，乃與同歲中始舉者等耳。

translations.literal: After leaving office, my years were still few; looking at those of the same age, there were those fifty years old not yet called old; inwardly I plotted that from here I would withdraw twenty years, wait until the realm was clear, then be no different from those of the same age who had just been recommended."
translations.idiomatic: planning to sit out twenty years of chaos until he could re-enter office with peers his age,

sentences.zh: 故以四時歸鄉里，於譙東五十里築精舍，欲秋夏讀書，冬春射獵，求底下之地，欲以泥水自蔽，絕賔客往來之望，然不能得如意。

translations.literal: Therefore in the four seasons I returned to the village, east of Qiao fifty li built a refined lodge, wishing in autumn and summer to read books, in spring and winter to hunt, seeking low-lying land, wishing to hide myself in mud and water, cut off hope of guests coming and going, yet could not obtain as wished."
translations.idiomatic: building a study fifty li east of Qiao for reading, hunting, and obscuritythough peace eluded him,

sentences.zh: 後徵爲都尉，遷典軍校尉，意遂更欲爲國家討賊立功，欲望封侯作征西將軍，然後題墓道言『漢故征西將軍曹侯之墓』，此其志也。

translations.literal: Later I was summoned as commandant, promoted to colonel director of the army; my intent then changed to wishing for the state to campaign against bandits and establish merit, desiring to be enfeoffed marquis and become general who campaigns west, then inscribe on the tomb path saying "Han's former general who campaigns west, Marquis Cao's tomb"this was my ambition."
translations.idiomatic: until summons pulled him back with a new dream: to earn the title general who campaigns west and a modest epitaph for his tomb,

sentences.zh: 而遭值董卓之難，興舉義兵。

translations.literal: But I encountered Dong Zhuo's disaster and raised righteous troops."
translations.idiomatic: then Dong Zhuo's coup forced him to arms."

sentences.zh: 是時合兵能多得耳，然常自損，不欲多之；

translations.literal: At that time combined troops could have been obtained in great numbers, yet I always diminished myself, not wishing them to be many;
translations.idiomatic: He could have swollen his ranks but deliberately kept armies small,

sentences.zh: 所以然者，多兵意盛，與彊敵爭，儻更爲禍始。

translations.literal: the reason was: many troops make intentions swell; contending with strong enemies, perhaps would again become the beginning of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: fearing that swollen hosts provoke stronger foes and fresh catastrophe,

sentences.zh: 故汴水之戰數千，後還到揚州更募，亦復不過三千人，此其本志有限也。

translations.literal: Therefore at Bianshui battle only several thousand; later returning to Yangzhou to recruit again, again not more than three thousand menthis was my original intent's limit."
translations.idiomatic: so he fought at Bianshui with thousands and later raised barely three thousand in Yangzhouhis self-imposed ceiling,

sentences.zh: 後領兖州，破降黃巾三十萬衆。

translations.literal: Later I led Yan province, broke and surrendered the Yellow Turbans' three hundred thousand host."
translations.idiomatic: until Yan province and three hundred thousand surrendered Turbans changed the scale,

sentences.zh: 又袁術僭號於九江，下皆稱臣，名門曰建號門，衣被皆爲天子之制，兩婦預爭爲皇后。

translations.literal: Again Yuan Shu usurped the title at Jiujiang; those below all called him lord; he named a gate Establish-the-Era Gate; clothing and bedding were all in the Son of Heaven's system; two women beforehand vied to be empress."
translations.idiomatic: while Yuan Shu played emperor at Jiujiang with court dress and rival empresses,

sentences.zh: 志計已定，人有勸術使遂即帝位，露布天下，荅言『曹公尚在，未可也』。

translations.literal: His ambition and plan already fixed, men urged Shu immediately to take the imperial throne and expose it to the realm; he answered, "Lord Cao still lives; it is not yet possible."
translations.idiomatic: yet even Yuan Shu knew better than to proclaim the throne while Cao Cao lived,

sentences.zh: 後孤討禽其四將，獲其人衆，遂使術窮亡解沮，發病而死。

translations.literal: Later I campaigned and captured his four generals, seized his people and host, thereupon made Shu destitute, broken, and dispirited, ill and dead."
translations.idiomatic: until Cao Cao smashed his armies and watched him die broken,

sentences.zh: 及至袁紹據河北，兵勢彊盛，孤自度勢，實不敵之，但計投死爲國，以義滅身，足垂於後。

translations.literal: When it reached Yuan Shao holding Hebei, military momentum was strong and flourishing; I myself measured the situation, truly could not match him; but my plan was to cast life for the state, by righteousness destroy the body, enough to hang for posterity."
translations.idiomatic: then faced Yuan Shao in Hebei outmatched yet ready to die for the Han,

sentences.zh: 幸而破紹，梟其二子。

translations.literal: Fortunately I broke Shao and displayed his two sons."
translations.idiomatic: and by fortune broke him and his sons,

sentences.zh: 又劉表自以爲宗室，包藏姧心，乍前乍却，以觀世事，據有當州，孤復定之，遂平天下。

translations.literal: Again Liu Biao, thinking himself imperial kin, harbored treacherous intent, now forward now back, to observe the age's affairs; he held this province; I again settled it, thereupon pacified the realm."
translations.idiomatic: then unmasked Liu Biao's vacillating treason and took Jingzhou,

sentences.zh: 身爲宰相，人臣之貴已極，意望已過矣。

translations.literal: My person is chancellor; a minister's honor is already extreme; my hopes have already passed what is due."
translations.idiomatic: until he stood as chancellor at the summit of any subject's career,

sentences.zh: 今孤言此，若爲自大，欲人言盡，故無諱耳。

translations.literal: Now I speak this as if self-aggrandizing; I desire men's words to be exhausted; therefore I have no taboo."
translations.idiomatic: and tells this story not to boast but to leave nothing unsaid."

sentences.zh: 設使國家無有孤，不知當幾人稱帝，幾人稱王。

translations.literal: Supposing the state had not had me, I do not know how many would have styled themselves emperor, how many styled themselves king.
translations.idiomatic: Without me at the helm, countless warlords would have crowned themselves emperors or kings.

sentences.zh: 或者人見孤彊盛，又性不信天命之事，恐私心相評，言有不遜之志，妄相忖度，每用耿耿。

translations.literal: Perhaps men see me strong and flourishing, and moreover by nature I do not trust Heaven's mandate affairs; they fear private hearts will judge each other, saying I have intent not submissive to the throne, rashly conjecturing; therefore I am always uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Because I am powerful and skeptical of omens, people whisper that I aim at the throne; the suspicion gnaws at me.

sentences.zh: 齊桓、晉文所以垂稱至今日者，以其兵勢廣大，猶能奉事周室也。

translations.literal: The reason Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin are praised down to today is that though their military momentum was vast, they still were able to serve the house of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan and Duke Wen are praised because great power did not stop them from serving the Zhou king.

sentences.zh: 論語云『三分天下有其二，以服事殷，周之德可謂至德矣』，夫能以大事小也。

translations.literal: The Analects says "He held two parts in three of the realm yet served Yin; Zhou's virtue can be called utmost virtue"he could use the great to serve the small.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects praises King Wen for holding two-thirds of the realm yet serving Shangthe strong serving the weak.

sentences.zh: 昔樂毅走趙，趙王欲與之圖燕，樂毅伏而垂泣，對曰：『臣事昭王，猶事大王；

translations.literal: Formerly Yue Yi fled to Zhao; the King of Zhao wished with him to plot against Yan; Yue Yi bowed prostrate and wept tears, answering, "Your servant served King Zhao as he serves the great king;
translations.idiomatic: When King Zhao of Zhao asked the exile Yue Yi to plot against Yan, Yue Yi wept and said he served Zhao as he had served Yan;

sentences.zh: 臣若獲戾，放在他國，沒世然後已，不忍謀趙之徒隷，況燕後嗣乎！

translations.literal: if your servant incurs blame and is cast in another state, until the end of life then stops; I cannot bear to plot against Zhao's convict laborers, how much less Yan's later heirs!"
translations.idiomatic: "Even exiled I would not scheme against Zhao's meanest slave, let alone Yan's descendants."

sentences.zh: 』胡亥之殺蒙恬也，恬曰：『自吾先人及至子孫，積信於秦三世矣；

translations.literal: When Huhai killed Meng Tian, Tian said: "From my ancestors down to my sons and grandsons, accumulated trust in Qin has been three generations;
translations.idiomatic: When Huhai killed Meng Tian, the general said his family had served Qin faithfully for three generations;

sentences.zh: 今臣將兵三十餘萬，其勢足以背叛，然自知必死而守義者，不敢辱先人之教以忘先王也。

translations.literal: now your servant leads troops more than three hundred thousand; the momentum is enough to rebel, yet knowing I must die yet guarding righteousness is because I dare not shame my ancestors' instruction and forget the former king."
translations.idiomatic: "Though I commanded three hundred thousand men and could have revolted, I chose death from loyalty to Qin's old kings."

sentences.zh: 』孤每讀此二人書，未曾不愴然流涕也。

translations.literal: Whenever I read these two men's words, never do I not mournfully weep.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao says he weeps every time he reads those speeches.

sentences.zh: 孤祖父以至孤身，皆當親重之任，可謂見信者矣，以及子桓兄弟，過於三世矣。

translations.literal: From my grandfather and father down to my solitary person, all have held close and weighty trust; one can say I have been seen as trustworthy; reaching to my sons Pi and their brothers, it has passed three generations.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held the Han's highest trust for three generations down to Cao Pi and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 孤非徒對諸君說此，也常以語妻妾，皆令深知此意。

translations.literal: It is not only to you gentlemen that I speak this; I also always tell wives and concubines, ordering them deeply to know this meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated the same confession to his wives and concubines so they would understand.

sentences.zh: 孤謂之言：『顧我萬年之後，汝曹皆當出嫁，欲令傳道我心，使他人皆知之。

translations.literal: I tell them, saying: "Look to after my ten thousand years; you all ought to marry out, wishing to transmit my heart, making others all know it."
translations.idiomatic: He told them that after his death they should remarry so the world would know his loyalty was not feigned.

sentences.zh: 』孤此言皆肝鬲之要也。

translations.literal: These words of mine are all essentials of liver and diaphragm.
translations.idiomatic: These are words straight from the guts.

sentences.zh: 所以勤勤懇懇敘心腹者，見周公有金縢之書以自明，恐人不信之故。

translations.literal: The reason I earnestly narrate what is in the belly is that I see the Duke of Zhou had the metal-bound casket writing to clarify himself; I fear people will not believe.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Duke of Zhou's golden-coffer oath, he writes to be believed.

sentences.zh: 然欲孤便爾委捐所典兵衆以還執事，歸就武平侯國，實不可也。

translations.literal: Yet wishing me immediately thus to cast away the troops and hosts I administer and return them to the office, go back to the Marquis of Wuping state, is truly not possible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cannot simply disband his armies and retire to his Wuping marquisate.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why not?

sentences.zh: 誠恐己離兵爲人所禍也。

translations.literal: Truly I fear that once I leave the army I will be harmed by others.
translations.idiomatic: Because stripped of troops he would be murdered.

sentences.zh: 旣爲子孫計，又己敗則國家傾危，是以不得慕虛名而處實禍，此所不得爲也。

translations.literal: Both for the sake of sons and grandsons' plans, and because if I am defeated then the state will overturn and be imperiled; therefore I cannot admire empty fame while dwelling in real disaster; this is what cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: His fall would topple the state, so he refuses empty honor that invites real ruin.

sentences.zh: 前朝恩封三子爲侯，固辭不受，今更欲受之，非欲復以爲榮，欲以爲外援，爲萬安計。

translations.literal: Formerly the court in grace enfeoffed three sons as marquises; I firmly declined and did not accept; now I further wish to accept them; it is not that I again wish to take it as glory; I wish to take them as external aid, as a plan of perfect safety.
translations.idiomatic: He once refused three son's marquisates but now accepts them as political hostages for safety.

sentences.zh: 孤聞介推之避晉封。

translations.literal: I have heard of Jie Tui's avoiding Jin enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He cites Jie Tui refusing Jin rewards,

sentences.zh: 申胥之逃楚賞，未甞不捨書而歎，有以自省也。

translations.literal: Shen Xu's fleeing Chu reward, never do I not lay aside the book and sigh, having thereby to examine myself.
translations.idiomatic: and Shen Xu fleeing Chu honors, and sets the book aside to reflect.

sentences.zh: 奉國威靈，仗鉞征伐，推弱以克彊，處小而禽大，意之所圖，動無違事，心之所慮，何向不濟，遂蕩平天下，不辱主命，可謂天助漢室，非人力也。

translations.literal: Receiving the state's awesome spirit, leaning on the axe to campaign and punish, pushing weakness to overcome strength, dwelling small yet capturing great, where intent plotted, in movement nothing went against the plan, where the heart pondered, what direction did not succeed; thereupon I swept the realm flat, not shaming the lord's charge; one can say Heaven aided the house of Han, not human strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wielding Han authority he turned weakness to strength, small to great, and pacified the realm by heaven's favor, not his own might alone.

sentences.zh: 然封兼四縣，食戶三萬，何德堪之！

translations.literal: Yet enfeoffment spanning four counties, eating households thirty thousandwhat virtue can bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Four counties and thirty thousand households are more than his virtue deserves.

sentences.zh: 江湖未靜，不可讓位；

translations.literal: The rivers and lakes are not yet still; I cannot yield position;
translations.idiomatic: The south is still restless, so he cannot resign command;

sentences.zh: 至於邑土，可得而辭。

translations.literal: as for town and soil, that can be declined.
translations.idiomatic: but he can give back fief income.

sentences.zh: 今上還陽夏、柘、苦三縣戶二萬，但食武平萬戶，且以分損謗議，少減孤之責也。」〉

translations.literal: Now I return upward Yangxia, Zhe, and Ku three counties' twenty thousand households, only eating Wuping ten thousand households, and thereby divide and lessen slanderous talk, slightly reduce blame toward my solitary person."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore returns twenty thousand households from three counties and keeps only ten thousand at Wuping to silence critics."

sentences.zh: 十六年春正月，

translations.literal: Sixteenth year spring first month,
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 211 CE,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：庚辰，天子報：減戶五千，分所讓三縣萬五千封三子，植爲平原侯，據爲范陽侯，豹爲饒陽侯，食邑各五千戶。〉

translations.literal: the Wei Shu says: on gengchen the Son of Heaven replied: reduce households five thousand, divide the three counties' fifteen thousand you yielded to enfeoff three sonsZhi as marquis of Pingyuan, Ju as marquis of Fanyang, Bao as marquis of Raoyang, each eating territory five thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: the court answered on gengchen: accept the five-thousand-household cut and split the yielded fifteen thousand among Cao Zhi, Cao Ju, and Cao Bao as marquises of five thousand households each."

sentences.zh: 天子命公世子丕爲五官中郎將，置官屬，爲丞相副。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the duke's heir Pi as general of the household for the five offices, established subordinate offices, as the chancellor's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Cao Pi general of the household for the five offices with full staff as the chancellor's deputy.

sentences.zh: 太原商曜等以大陵叛，遣夏侯淵、徐晃圍破之。

translations.literal: Shang Yao and others of Taiyuan rebelled at Daling; he dispatched Xiahou Yuan and Xu Huang to besiege and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Yao of Taiyuan rebelled at Daling; Xiahou Yuan and Xu Huang crushed the revolt.

sentences.zh: 張魯據漢中，三月，遣鍾繇討之。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu held Hanzhong; third month, he dispatched Zhong Yao to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he sent Zhong Yao against Zhang Lu in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 公使淵等出河東與繇會。

translations.literal: The duke made Yuan and others exit Hedong to join with Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xiahou Yuan east from Hedong to join Zhong Yao.

sentences.zh: 是時關中諸將疑繇欲自襲，馬超遂與韓遂、楊秋、李堪、成宜等叛。

translations.literal: At this time the Guanzhong generals suspected Yao intended personally to raid them; Ma Chao thereupon with Han Sui, Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Cheng Yi, and others rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The western lords feared Zhong Yao meant to attack them, so Ma Chao, Han Sui, Yang Qiu, Li Kan, Cheng Yi, and others mutinied.

sentences.zh: 遣曹仁討之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Cao Ren to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Cao Ren against them.

sentences.zh: 超等屯潼關，公勑諸將：「關西兵精悍，堅壁勿與戰。

translations.literal: Chao and the others encamped at Tong Pass; the duke ordered the generals: "Guanxi troops are crack and fierce; hold firm walls and do not battle with them."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao sealed Tong Pass; Cao Cao ordered his men to stand on the defense against the fierce western levies.

sentences.zh: 」秋七月，公西征，

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, the duke west campaigned,
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he marched west,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：議者多言「關西兵彊，習長矛，非精選前鋒，則不可以當也」。

translations.literal: the Wei Shu says: debaters mostly said, "Guanxi troops are strong, practiced with long spears; unless the vanguard is finely selected, one cannot withstand them."
translations.idiomatic: while his staff warned that western lancers required picked vanguard troops,

sentences.zh: 公謂諸將曰：「戰在我，非在賊也。

translations.literal: The duke said to the generals: "The battle lies with me, not with the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao answered that the initiative was his, not the enemy's,

sentences.zh: 賊雖習長矛，將使不得以刺，諸君但觀之耳。」〉

translations.literal: Though the bandits practice long spears, I will make them unable to use the thrust; you gentlemen only watch."
translations.idiomatic: "They may drill long spears; I will keep them from thrustingwatch me."

sentences.zh: 與超等夾關而軍。

translations.literal: With Chao and the others he flanked the pass and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: He faced Ma Chao across Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 公急持之，而潛遣徐晃、朱靈等夜渡蒲阪津，據河西爲營。

translations.literal: The duke urgently pinned them while secretly dispatching Xu Huang, Zhu Ling, and others by night to cross the Puban ford and occupy the west of the river to make a camp.
translations.idiomatic: He pinned Ma Chao frontally while Xu Huang and Zhu Ling slipped across Puban at night to camp west of the river.

sentences.zh: 公自潼關北渡，未濟，超赴船急戰。

translations.literal: The duke from Tong Pass north crossed; not yet finished crossing, Chao rushed the boats in urgent battle.
translations.idiomatic: During his own northward crossing Ma Chao stormed the ferries before the army was over.

sentences.zh: 校尉丁斐因放牛馬以餌賊，賊亂取牛馬，公乃得渡，

translations.literal: Colonel Ding Fei thereupon released oxen and horses to bait the bandits; the bandits disorderly seized oxen and horses; the duke then was able to cross,
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Ding Fei stampeded draft animals as a decoy; the rebels scattered to round them up and Cao Cao got across,

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：公將過河，前隊適渡，超等奄至，公猶坐胡牀不起。

translations.literal: the Cao Man Zhuan says: when the duke was about to cross the river, the van had just crossed when Chao and the others suddenly arrived; the duke still sat on a folding couch and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: the Cao Man Zhuan adds that Ma Chao caught him still seated on a camp stool,

sentences.zh: 張郃等見事急，共引公入船。

translations.literal: Zhang He and others seeing the affair urgent, together pulled the duke into a boat.
translations.idiomatic: until Zhang He and others dragged him aboard,

sentences.zh: 河水急，北渡，流四五里，超等騎追射之，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The river water was swift; north crossing, drifted four or five li; Chao and others' riders pursued shooting; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: then the current swept the boat four or five li downstream under a rain of arrows,

sentences.zh: 諸將見軍敗，不知公所在，皆惶懼，至見，乃悲喜，或流涕。

translations.literal: The generals seeing the army defeated, not knowing where the duke was, all were frightened; when they saw him, then sorrow and joy, some shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: while officers who thought him lost wept with relief when he appeared,

sentences.zh: 公大笑曰：「今日幾爲小賊所困乎！」〉

translations.literal: The duke laughed greatly and said: "Today I was nearly trapped by petty bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: and he laughed, "Nearly done in by young bravos today!"

sentences.zh: 循河爲甬道而南。

translations.literal: He followed the river making a covered way south.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove a covered gallery south along the bank.

sentences.zh: 賊退，拒渭口，公乃多設疑兵，潛以舟載兵入渭，爲浮橋，夜，分兵結營於渭南。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated, guarded the Wei mouth; the duke then set many doubtful troops, secretly used boats to carry troops into the Wei, made a floating bridge; by night divided troops and tied camps south of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy fell back to the Wei estuary he feinted broadly, ferried troops across the Wei by night on pontoon bridges, and planted camps on the south bank.

sentences.zh: 賊夜攻營，伏兵擊破之。

translations.literal: The bandits by night attacked the camp; ambush troops struck and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: A night raid on Cao Cao's camp walked into an ambush and was shattered.

sentences.zh: 超等屯渭南，遣信求割河以西請和，公不許。

translations.literal: Chao and the others encamped south of the Wei; they sent a letter asking to cede the land west of the Yellow River and beg peace; the duke did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao's coalition camped south of the Wei and offered to trade the west bank for peace; Cao Cao refused.

sentences.zh: 九月，進軍渡渭。

translations.literal: Ninth month, advanced the army and crossed the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he forced the crossing of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：時公軍每渡渭，輒爲超騎所衝突，營不得立，地又多沙，不可築壘。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: at the time each time the duke's army crossed the Wei, they were always rushed by Chao's cavalry; the camp could not be established; the ground was also much sand, impossible to build ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says Ma Chao's horse kept disrupting each crossing and the sandy soil would not hold walls.

sentences.zh: 婁子伯說公曰：「今天寒，可起沙爲城，以水灌之，可一夜而成。

translations.literal: Lou Zibo persuaded the duke, saying: "Now the weather is cold; you can raise sand as a city, pour water on it, and in one night it will be completed."
translations.idiomatic: Lou Zibo advised packing sand ramparts and freezing them solid overnight with water.

sentences.zh: 」公從之，乃多作縑囊以運水，夜渡兵作城，比明，城立，由是公軍盡得渡渭。

translations.literal: The duke followed it; then made many silk bags to carry water, by night crossed troops to build a city; compared to dawn, the city stood; thereby the duke's army fully was able to cross the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao followed the plan, ferried water in silk sacks, raised frozen sand walls overnight, and got his whole army across the Wei.

sentences.zh: 或疑于時九月，水未應凍。

translations.literal: Some doubted that at that time in the ninth month water ought not yet to freeze.
translations.idiomatic: Skeptics noted that September seemed early for ice.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案《魏書》：公軍八月至潼關，閏月北渡河，則其年閏八月也，至此容可大寒邪！〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates the Wei Shu: the duke's army eighth month reached Tong Pass, intercalary month north crossed the river; then that year's intercalation was the eighth month; by here perhaps it could be severely cold!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi checks the Wei Shu: the army reached Tong in the eighth month and crossed north in an intercalary eighth month, so deep cold by the Wei crossing is plausible."

sentences.zh: 超等數挑戰，又不許；

translations.literal: Chao and the others repeatedly challenged battle; again he did not permit;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao baited him repeatedly; Cao Cao still refused battle;

sentences.zh: 固請割地，求送任子，公用賈詡計，偽許之。

translations.literal: they firmly asked to cede land, begged to send hostage sons; the duke used Jia Xu's plan and falsely consented.
translations.idiomatic: they begged for a territorial settlement and hostages; Cao Cao followed Jia Xu's advice and pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 韓遂請與公相見，公與遂父同歲孝廉，又與遂同時儕輩，於是交馬語移時，不及軍事，但說京都舊故，拊手歡笑。

translations.literal: Han Sui requested to meet the duke face to face; the duke with Sui's father was the same year filial and incorrupt, and with Sui was of the same generation of companions; therefore they crossed horses and talked for a long time, not reaching military affairs, only speaking of old matters in the capital, clapping hands and laughing happily.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui asked for a parley; he and Cao Cao had been recommended the same year as Sui's father had been, so they sat horse to horse reminiscing about Luoyang like old friends, never touching strategy.

sentences.zh: 旣罷，超等問遂：「公何言？

translations.literal: When finished, Chao and others asked Sui: "What did the duke say?"
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Ma Chao demanded, "What did Cao Cao say?"

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「無所言也。

translations.literal: Sui said: "He said nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui answered, "Nothing important."

sentences.zh: 」超等疑之。

translations.literal: Chao and the others suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: The western lords began to doubt Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：公後日復與遂等會語，諸將曰：「公與虜交語，不宜輕脫，可爲木行馬以爲防遏。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: the duke another day again met with Sui and others to talk; the generals said: "When the duke talks with the barbarians face to face, you ought not lightly expose yourself; you can make wooden cheval-de-frise to serve as defense."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei says his officers wanted a wooden palisade for the next meeting with Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 」公然之。

translations.literal: The duke approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 賊將見公，悉於馬上拜，秦、胡觀者，前後重沓，公笑謂賊曰：「爾欲觀曹公邪？

translations.literal: When the bandit generals saw the duke, all on horseback bowed; Qin and Hu onlookers, front and back piled layer on layer; the duke laughed and said to the bandits: "You wish to view Lord Cao?
translations.idiomatic: Enemy chiefs saluted from the saddle while crowds of Qiang and Hu pressed close; Cao Cao laughed, "So you want a look at Cao Cao?

sentences.zh: 亦猶人也，非有四目兩口，但多智耳！

translations.literal: He is also like other men; he does not have four eyes and two mouths, only much wisdom!"
translations.idiomatic: He has the same face as anyone elsejust a busier mind!"

sentences.zh: 」胡前後大觀。

translations.literal: The Hu in front and rear greatly viewed.
translations.idiomatic: The nomad spectators surged forward for a better view.

sentences.zh: 又列鐵騎五千爲十重陣，精光耀日，賊益震懼。〉

translations.literal: Again he arrayed iron cavalry five thousand in ten-layered formations; refined armor dazzled the sun; the bandits increased in shock and fear."
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand armored horse in ten ranks glittered in the sun until the rebels were paralyzed with fear."

sentences.zh: 他日，公又與遂書，多所點竄，如遂改定者；

translations.literal: Another day, the duke again wrote Sui a letter, with many dots and alterations as if Sui had revised it;
translations.idiomatic: Later Cao Cao sent Han Sui a letter visibly edited as if Han Sui had altered it himself;

sentences.zh: 超等愈疑遂。

translations.literal: Chao and the others increasingly suspected Sui.
translations.idiomatic: deepening Ma Chao's distrust of Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 公乃與克日會戰，先以輕兵挑之，戰良久，乃縱虎騎夾擊，大破之，斬成宜、李堪等。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon with them fixed a day for joined battle; first with light troops challenged them; battled a long time; then released tiger cavalry in a pincer strike, greatly defeated them, beheaded Cheng Yi, Li Kan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He then set a battle day, skirmished until the enemy tired, and unleashed his heavy cavalry to crush them, killing Cheng Yi, Li Kan, and others.

sentences.zh: 遂、超等走涼州，楊秋奔安定，關中平。

translations.literal: Sui, Chao, and others fled to Liangzhou; Yang Qiu fled to Anding; Guanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui and Ma Chao fled west, Yang Qiu to Anding, and the Guanzhong plain was his.

sentences.zh: 諸將或問公曰：「初，賊守潼關，渭北道缺，不從河東擊馮翊而反守潼關，引日而後北渡，何也？

translations.literal: Some generals asked the duke: "At first the bandits guarded Tong Pass; the north-of-the-Wei road was lacking; why did you not strike Fengyi from Hedong but instead guarded Tong Pass, drawing out days and afterward north crossingwhat was the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Officers asked why he had feinted at Tong Pass instead of driving straight through Hedong to Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 」公曰：「賊守潼關，若吾入河東，賊必引守諸津，則西河未可渡，吾故盛兵向潼關；

translations.literal: The duke said: "When the bandits guarded Tong Pass, if I entered Hedong, the bandits were sure to lead guards to all the fords, then the west of the river could not be crossed; therefore I displayed a strong host toward Tong Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao explained that a Hedong thrust would have sealed every ford; feinting at Tong drew the whole enemy south,

sentences.zh: 賊悉衆南守，西河之備虛，故二將得擅取西河；

translations.literal: the bandits used all their host to guard south; the west-of-the-river preparations were empty; therefore the two generals were able to seize the west of the river at will;
translations.idiomatic: emptying the west bank so Xu Huang and Zhu Ling could seize it,

sentences.zh: 然後引軍北渡，賊不能與吾爭西河者，以有二將之軍也。

translations.literal: then I led the army north across; the reason the bandits could not contend with me for the west of the river is that there were the two generals' armies."
translations.idiomatic: which let him cross north while Ma Chao could not contest the west bank."

sentences.zh: 連車樹柵，爲甬道而南，

translations.literal: Connected carts and planted palisades, making a covered way south,
translations.idiomatic: He then linked wagons and stakes into a gallery southward,

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：漢高祖二年，與楚戰滎陽京、索之間，築甬道屬河以取敖倉粟。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: Han Gaozu in the second year, battling Chu between Jingyang and Jingsuo, built a covered way connecting to the river to obtain Aocang grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi cites Gaozu's siege gallery to Aocang between Jingyang and Jingsuo,

sentences.zh: 應劭曰：「恐敵鈔輜重，故築垣牆如街巷也。

translations.literal: Ying Shao said: "Fearing the enemy would raid the baggage train, therefore they built wall-ways like lanes and alleys."
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao glossing the gallery as a walled lane to protect supplies,

sentences.zh: 」今魏武不築垣牆，但連車樹柵以扞兩面。〉

translations.literal: Now Wei Wu did not build wall-ways, only connected carts and planted palisades to shield two sides."
translations.idiomatic: while Cao Cao used only wagon lines and stakes for flank cover."

sentences.zh: 旣爲不可勝，且以示弱。

translations.literal: Having made himself unbeatable, and moreover to show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: He looked invulnerable yet acted weak on purpose.

sentences.zh: 渡渭爲堅壘，虜至不出，所以驕之也；

translations.literal: Crossing the Wei he made firm ramparts; when the bandits arrived he did not emerge; this was the means to make them arrogant;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Wei he dug in and refused sorties to lull the enemy into arrogance;

sentences.zh: 故賊不爲營壘而求割地。

translations.literal: therefore the bandits did not make camp ramparts but sought to cede land.
translations.idiomatic: so Ma Chao neglected fortifications and begged for a partition deal instead.

sentences.zh: 吾順言許之，所以從其意，使自安而不爲備，因畜士卒之力，一旦擊之，所謂疾雷不及掩耳，兵之變化，固非一道也。

translations.literal: I smoothly in words consented to them; this was the means to follow their intent, make them self-assured and not prepare; thereby storing the soldiers' strength, in one morning striking themwhat is called swift thunder not catching ear-covering; the army's transformations, solidly are not one path."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed to buy time, let them relax their guard, then hit them with stored fury like lightning before they could cover their earswar has many faces."

sentences.zh: 」始，賊每一部到，公輒有喜色。

translations.literal: At first, each time one bandit division arrived, the duke always had a joyful color.
translations.idiomatic: At first he smiled wider every time another rebel column arrived.

sentences.zh: 賊破之後，諸將問其故。

translations.literal: After the bandits were broken, the generals asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory they asked why he had looked pleased.

sentences.zh: 公荅曰：「關中長遠，若賊各依險阻，征之，不一二年不可定也。

translations.literal: The duke answered: "Guanzhong is long and far; if the bandits each relied on perilous barriers, to campaign against them would not be settled in one or two years.
translations.idiomatic: He said Guanzhong was vast; if each stronghold had held out, the war could have lasted years,

sentences.zh: 今皆來集，其衆雖多，莫相歸服，軍無適主，一舉可滅，爲功差易，吾是以喜。」

translations.literal: Now they all came and gathered; though their host is large, none mutually submits in allegiance; the army has no supreme commander; one stroke can extinguish them; the merit is rather easy; therefore I was glad."
translations.idiomatic: but they had massed in one place without unity or single command, so one blow could end themthat was cause for joy."

sentences.zh: 冬十月，軍自長安北征楊秋，圍安定。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the army from Chang'an north campaigned against Yang Qiu, besieged Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he marched from Chang'an against Yang Qiu and besieged Anding.

sentences.zh: 秋降，復其爵位，使留撫其民人。

translations.literal: Qiu surrendered, restored his rank and position, and made him remain to soothe his people.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiu surrendered, kept his titles, and was left to pacify his district.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：楊秋，黃初中遷討寇將軍，位特進，封臨涇侯，以壽終。〉

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Yang Qiu in Huangchu era was promoted general who attacks bandits, rank tejin, enfeoffed marquis of Linjing, and by old age ended."
translations.idiomatic: The Brief Account of Wei adds that Yang Qiu later rose to general who attacks bandits, tejin rank, marquis of Linjing, and died of old age."

sentences.zh: 十二月，自安定還，留夏侯淵屯長安。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, returning from Anding, he left Xiahou Yuan encamped at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In December he withdrew from Anding, leaving Xiahou Yuan in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 十七年春正月，公還鄴。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year spring first month, the duke returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 212 CE, he was back in Ye.

sentences.zh: 天子命公贊拜不名，入朝不趨，劔履上殿，如蕭何故事。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the duke in audience not to be named, entering court not to hasten, sword and shoes on the hall, according to Xiao He's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him Xiao He's honors: no name called in court, no need to trot in audience, sword and shoes in the hall.

sentences.zh: 馬超餘衆梁興等屯藍田，使夏侯淵擊平之。

translations.literal: Ma Chao's remaining host Liang Xing and others encamped at Lantian; he made Xiahou Yuan strike and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao's lieutenant Liang Xing held Lantian until Xiahou Yuan wiped him out.

sentences.zh: 割河內之蕩陰、朝歌、林慮，東郡之衞國、頓丘、東武陽、發干，鉅鹿之廮陶、曲周、南和，廣平之任城，趙之襄國、邯鄲、易陽以益魏郡。

translations.literal: He severed Henei's Tangyin, Zhaoqi, and Linlu, Dongjun's Weiguo, Dunqiu, Dongwuyang, and Fagan, Julu's Yingtao, Quzhou, and Nanhe, Guangping's Rencheng, Zhao's Xiangguo, Handan, and Yiyang to enlarge Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred a long list of counties from Henei, Dongjun, Julu, Guangping, and Zhao into the enlarged Wei commandery around Ye.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，公征孫權。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the duke campaigned against Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he marched against Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 十八年春正月，進軍濡須口，攻破權江西營，獲權都督公孫陽，乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year spring first month, advanced the army to Ruxu mouth, broke Sun Quan's west-of-the-river camp, captured Quan's area commander Gongsun Yang, thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 213 CE, he struck Ruxu, took Sun Quan's west-bank camp and commander Gongsun Yang, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔書并十四州，復爲九州。

translations.literal: An edict merged the fourteen provinces and again made nine provinces.
translations.idiomatic: An edict collapsed the fourteen provinces back into the nine ancient provinces.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，至鄴。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he arrived in Ye.

sentences.zh: 五月丙申，天子使御史大夫郗慮持節策命公爲魏公

translations.literal: Fifth month bingshen day, the Son of Heaven dispatched Imperial Counselor Xi Chu bearing the staff of office to invest the duke as Duke of Wei
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day of the fifth month the emperor sent Imperial Counselor Xi Chu with credentials to ennoble Cao Cao as duke of Wei

sentences.zh: 〈《續漢書》曰：慮字鴻豫，山陽高平人。

translations.literal: The Xu Han shu says: Chu's style name was Hongyu; he was a man of Gaoping in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Continuation of the Han History identifies Xi Chu (courtesy Hongyu) of Gaoping in Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 少受業於鄭玄，建安初爲侍中。

translations.literal: In youth he received instruction from Zheng Xuan; at the beginning of Jian'an he was palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under Zheng Xuan and became a palace attendant early in the Jian'an era.

sentences.zh: 虞溥《江表傳》曰：獻帝甞特見慮及少府孔融，問融曰：「鴻豫何所優長？

translations.literal: Yu Pu's Jiang biao zhuan says: the Emperor once specially received Chu and Minister of the Lesser Treasury Kong Rong, and asked Rong: "In what is Hongyu superior?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu's southern chronicle says the emperor once received Xi Chu and Kong Rong together and asked Kong Rong Xi Chu's strengths.

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「可與適道，未可與權。

translations.literal: Rong said: "One may travel the Way with him, not yet wield power with him."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong answered, "You can discuss the Way with him, not power politics."

sentences.zh: 」慮舉笏曰：「融昔宰北海，政散民流，其權安在也！

translations.literal: Chu raised his tablet and said: "Rong once governed Beihai; government scattered and people driftedwhere was his power then!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chu shot back, raising his hu tablet, "When Rong ruled Beihai the people fledwhere was his power?"

sentences.zh: 」遂與融互相長短，以至不睦。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Rong they exchanged long and short until not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: They traded barbs until they were enemies.

sentences.zh: 公以書和解之。

translations.literal: The duke with letters reconciled them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao wrote letters to patch things up.

sentences.zh: 慮從光祿勳遷爲大夫。〉

translations.literal: Chu moved from grand master of splendid carriage to imperial counselor."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chu was later promoted from grand master of splendid carriage to imperial counselor."

sentences.zh: 曰：

translations.literal: It said:
translations.idiomatic: The investiture text began:

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，少遭愍凶，越在西土，遷于唐、衞。

translations.literal: We, lacking virtue, in youth met with grievous misfortune, crossed to the western lands, moved to Tang and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor speaks: "We, unworthy, suffered exile in the west, shuttled between Tang and Wei,

sentences.zh: 當此之時，若綴旒然，

translations.literal: At this time it was as if hanging by the tassels;
translations.idiomatic: dangling like a king whose tassels are tugged by others;

sentences.zh: 〈《公羊傳》曰：「君若贅旒然。

translations.literal: The Gongyang zhuan says: "The lord is like excess tassels on a banner."
translations.idiomatic: the Gongyang Commentary compares the ruler to excess banner tassels,

sentences.zh: 贅猶綴也。

translations.literal: Excess is like hanging.
translations.idiomatic: meaning "excess" like something hung,

sentences.zh: 」何休云：「旒，旂旒也。

translations.literal: He Xiu said: "The tassel is the banner tassel."
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu glosses the tassel as the silk fringe of the standard,

sentences.zh: 以旒譬者，言爲下所執持東西也。」〉

translations.literal: Using the tassel as comparison means being grasped and pulled east and west by those below."
translations.idiomatic: pulled this way and that by inferiors."

sentences.zh: 宗廟乏祀，社稷無位；

translations.literal: The ancestral temple lacked sacrifice; the altars of soil and grain had no lord;
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral rites ceased and the state altars stood empty;

sentences.zh: 羣凶覬覦，分裂諸夏，率土之民，朕無獲焉，即我高祖之命將墜于地。

translations.literal: the host of villains eyed greedily, split apart the various Xia; within the realm's lands, We have none to obtain; then Our high ancestor's mandate was about to fall to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: rebels carved up China while We held no true realm and Gaozu's mandate nearly fell to earth.

sentences.zh: 朕用夙興假寐，震悼于厥心，曰「惟祖惟父，股肱先正，

translations.literal: We therefore rise at dawn and sleep with clothes on, tremble in Our heart, saying "Only grandfathers and fathers, arms and legs of former upright ministers,"
translations.idiomatic: We rise before dawn in dread, crying for the old ministers who were the arms and legs of the state,

sentences.zh: 〈文侯之命曰：「亦惟先正。

translations.literal: The charge to the Marquis of Wen says: "Also only the former upright."
translations.idiomatic: quoting the "Charge to Wen" on "the former upright,"

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「先正，先臣。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Former upright means former ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glossing that as former ministers,

sentences.zh: 謂公卿大夫也。」〉

translations.literal: Meaning the dukes and grandees."
translations.idiomatic: meaning the high ministers of the court."

sentences.zh: 其孰能恤朕躬」？

translations.literal: Who then can pity Our person?"
translations.idiomatic: Who then will pity Us?

sentences.zh: 乃誘天衷，誕育丞相，保乂我皇家，弘濟于艱難，朕實賴之。

translations.literal: Then Heaven moved in Our breast and bore the chancellor, who protects and stabilizes Our royal house, broadly saves Us in hardship and peril; We truly rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven then sent the chancellor to steady the throne and carry Us through peril; We lean entirely on him.

sentences.zh: 今將授君典禮，其敬聽朕命。

translations.literal: Now We will confer on you the canonical rites; respectfully hearken to Our command.
translations.idiomatic: Now We confer the ducal rites; listen with care to Our charge."

sentences.zh: 昔者董卓初興國難，羣后釋位以謀王室，

translations.literal: Formerly when Dong Zhuo first raised the state's calamity, the regional lords relinquished office to plot for the royal house,
translations.idiomatic: The text turns to Cao Cao's merit list: when Dong Zhuo first struck, lords left their posts to rescue the dynasty,

sentences.zh: 〈《左氏傳》曰：「諸侯釋位以間王政。

translations.literal: The Zuo zhuan says: "The feudal lords relinquished office to intervene in royal government."
translations.idiomatic: citing the Zuo Commentary on lords who set aside private rule to aid the king,

sentences.zh: 」服虔曰：「言諸侯釋其私政而佐王室。」〉

translations.literal: Fu Qian said: "It means the feudal lords set aside their private government to assist the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian explaining that they gave up local power to serve Zhou."

sentences.zh: 君則攝進，首啟戎行，此君之忠于本朝也。

translations.literal: You then advanced and took the lead, opening the first ranks of war; this is your loyalty to this court.
translations.idiomatic: While you, Duke, marched first in the vanguard—that was loyalty to the Han.

sentences.zh: 後及黃巾反易天常，侵我三州，延及平民，君又翦之，以寧東夏，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Later when the Yellow Turbans rebelled and overturned Heaven's constant, invading Our three provinces and extending to the common people, you again extirpated them, thereby quieting the eastern Xia; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow Turbans ravaged three provinces you exterminated them and calmed the east.

sentences.zh: 韓暹、楊奉專用威命，君則致討，克黜其難，遂遷許都，造我京畿，設官兆祀，不失舊物，天地鬼神於是獲乂，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Han Xian and Yang Feng monopolized awesome commands; you then inflicted punishment, deposed their disaster, then moved the capital to Xu, built Our capital region, set up offices and began sacrifice, not losing the former heritage; Heaven and earth and the ghosts thereby obtained peace; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You purged Han Xian and Yang Feng, moved the court to Xu, restored offices and rites, and brought peace to heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 袁術僭逆，肆於淮南，懾憚君靈，用丕顯謀，蘄陽之役，橋蕤授首，稜威南邁，術以隕潰，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu usurped and rebelled, acted wildly in Huainan; he feared your awesomeness, used a great manifest plan; at the battle of Qiyang, Qiao Rui lost his head; your majesty marched south and Shu thereby collapsed; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You broke Yuan Shu at Qiyang, beheaded Qiao Rui, and drove Shu to ruin.

sentences.zh: 迴戈東征，呂布就戮，乘轅將返，張楊殂斃，眭固伏罪，張繡稽服，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Turning the halberd eastward, Lü Bu met execution; turning the chariot to return, Zhang Yang died violently; Sui Gu submitted his crime; Zhang Xiu kowtowed in submission; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You executed Lü Bu, destroyed Zhang Yang, forced Sui Gu and Zhang Xiu to yield.

sentences.zh: 袁紹逆亂天常，謀危社稷，憑恃其衆，稱兵內侮，當此之時，王師寡弱，天下寒心，莫有固志，君執大節，精貫白日，奮其武怒，運其神策，致屆官渡，大殲醜類，

translations.literal: Yuan Shao rebelled against Heaven's constant, plotted danger to the altars of soil and grain, relied on his multitude, raised arms to insult within; at that time royal armies were weak and few; all under Heaven chilled at heart; none had firm resolve; you grasped the great norm, essence pierced the bright sun, roused your martial wrath, exercised your divine stratagem, brought the expedition to Guandu, greatly annihilated the vile host,
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shao menaced the throne with superior numbers you held fast to duty, struck at Guandu, and annihilated his army,

sentences.zh: 〈詩曰：「致天之屆，于牧之野。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Bring Heaven's punishment to the limit, at Mu's wilds."
translations.idiomatic: as the Odes say of bringing Heaven's wrath to the foe,

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「屆，極也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Limit means utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glossing "limit" as utmost,

sentences.zh: 」鴻範曰：「鯀則殛死。」〉

translations.literal: The Hong fan says: "Gun then was put to death."
translations.idiomatic: and the Hong fan on executing the wicked."

sentences.zh: 俾我國家拯於危墜，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Causing Our state to be lifted from peril and fall; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You snatched the dynasty from the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 濟師洪河，拓定四州，袁譚、高幹，咸梟其首，海盜奔迸，黑山順軌，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: You ferried the army across the great Yellow River, expanded and settled four provinces; Yuan Tan and Gao Gan, both displayed their heads; sea bandits fled in panic; Black Mountains submitted to the track; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You crossed the Yellow River, secured four provinces, took the heads of Yuan Tan and Gao Gan, scattered pirates, and pacified the Black Mountains.

sentences.zh: 烏丸三種，崇亂二世，袁尚因之，逼據塞北，束馬縣車，一征而滅，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: The three kinds of Wuhuan, through two reigns causing chaos, Yuan Shang relying on them, forced occupation north of the passes; binding horses and suspending carts, one expedition extinguished them; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You crushed the Wuhuan whom Yuan Shang had sheltered beyond the passes in one winter campaign.

sentences.zh: 劉表背誕，不供貢職，王師首路，威風先逝，百城八郡，交臂屈膝，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Liu Biao betrayed and resisted, did not supply tribute duties; royal armies set out on the road, your awesome wind went first; a hundred cities and eight commanderies, crossed arms and bent knees; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Biao withheld tribute your host made every city in Jingzhou kneel.

sentences.zh: 馬超、成宜，同惡相濟，濵據河、潼，求逞所欲，殄之渭南，獻馘萬計，遂定邊境，撫和戎狄，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Ma Chao and Cheng Yi, same evil aiding each other, banked on the Yellow River and Tong Pass, seeking to indulge their desires; you exterminated them south of the Wei, presented ten thousand counted ears, then settled the borderlands and soothed Rong and Di; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: You destroyed Ma Chao and Cheng Yi at the Wei, counted ten thousand ears of the slain, and pacified the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑、丁零，重譯而至，箄于、白屋，請吏率職，此又君之功也。

translations.literal: Xianbei and Dingling, through repeated translation arrived; Bi and Baiwu, requested clerks and led duty; this again is your merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbei, Dingling, Bi, and Baiwu tribes sent envoys and accepted Han officials.

sentences.zh: 君有定天下之功，重之以明德，班敘海內，宣美風俗，旁施勤教，恤慎刑獄，吏無苛政，民無懷慝；

translations.literal: You have the merit of settling the realm, heavy with bright virtue, ordering within the seas, spreading beautiful customs, broadly applying diligent instruction, careful in punishments and prisons; clerks have no harsh government; the people harbor no hidden malice;
translations.idiomatic: You ordered the realm, spread humane rule, taught diligently, judged fairly, and left officials and commoners without grievance;

sentences.zh: 敦崇帝族，表繼絕世，舊德前功，罔不咸秩；

translations.literal: You honor the imperial clan, display those whose line was cut off; former virtue and prior merit, none not given rank;
translations.idiomatic: you honored the Liu clan, restored ruined houses, and ennobled every past worthy;

sentences.zh: 雖伊尹格于皇天，周公光于四海，方之蔑如也。

translations.literal: though Yi Yin matched Heaven's grid, the Duke of Zhou shone within the four seas, compared to you they are as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: yet beside you even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou shrink to nothing."

sentences.zh: 朕聞先王並建明德，胙之以土，分之以民，崇其寵章，備其禮物，所以藩衞王室，左右厥世也。

translations.literal: We have heard that former kings together established bright virtue, enfeoffed them with land, divided among them the people, raised their splendid insignia, prepared their ritual goods, thereby to screen and guard the royal house and assist the generations.
translations.idiomatic: The edict continues: ancient kings enfeoffed the worthy with land, people, and full rites to guard the Zhou line,

sentences.zh: 其在周成，管、蔡不靜，懲難念功，乃使邵康公賜齊太公履，東至于海，西至于河，南至于穆陵，北至于無棣，五侯九伯，實得征之，世祚太師，以表東海；

translations.literal: In the case of Zhou's completion, Guan and Cai were not tranquil; remembering the hardship and recalling the merit, then he sent the Duke of Shao to confer on the Grand Duke of Qi the treading of his realm, east reaching the sea, west reaching the river, south reaching Muleng, north reaching Wudi; the five marquises and nine chiefs, in truth could be campaigned against; generation after generation feasted as grand preceptor, to display east of the sea;
translations.idiomatic: as when Duke of Zhou, troubled by Guan and Cai, sent Duke of Shao to invest Jiang Taigong with authority from sea to river, Muleng to Wudi, with right to chastise any feudal lord, making Qi the eastern bulwark of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 爰及襄王，亦有楚人不供王職，又命晉文登爲侯伯，錫以二輅、虎賁、鈇鉞、秬鬯、弓矢，大啟南陽，世作盟主。

translations.literal: Reaching King Xiang, again there were Chu people not supplying royal duty; again he ordered Jin Wen to ascend as marquis-overlord, granted him the two chariots, tiger guards, axe and halberd, black-millet ale, bow and arrows; greatly opened Nanyang; generation after generation acted as covenant chief.
