translations.idiomatic: Under King Xiang of Zhou, when Chu withheld tribute, Jin Wend of Jin was named hegemon with the paired chariots, royal guard, ritual axes, sacrificial ale, and bows; he opened Nanyang and his line chaired the feudal alliances for generations.

sentences.zh: 故周室之不壞，繄二國是賴。

translations.literal: Therefore the Zhou house's not being ruined depended on these two states.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Zhou owed its survival to Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 今君稱丕顯德，明保朕躬，奉荅天命，導揚弘烈，緩爰九域，莫不率俾，

translations.literal: Now you are called to display bright virtue, clearly protect Our person, reverently answer Heaven's mandate, guide and raise grand achievements, pacify the nine regions, none not leading and serving,
translations.idiomatic: You now shine with virtue, shelter the throne, answer Heaven, spread order, and pacify the nine domains so that all submit,

sentences.zh: 〈盤庚曰：「綏爰有衆。

translations.literal: The Pan Geng says: "Pacify thereby the multitudes."
translations.idiomatic: as Pan Geng says of "bringing peace to the people,"

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄曰：「爰，於也，安隱於其衆也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Yuan means in; peacefully settle among their multitudes."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glossing yuan as "thereby" and the sense as settling the people,

sentences.zh: 」君奭曰：「海隅出日，罔不率俾。

translations.literal: The Lord Shi says: "At the sea's corner where the sun emerges, none do not lead and serve."
translations.idiomatic: and the Lord Shi on every shore under the sun obeying the king,

sentences.zh: 」率，循也。

translations.literal: Lead means follow.
translations.idiomatic: shu meaning "to follow,"

sentences.zh: 俾，使也。

translations.literal: Bi means make.
translations.idiomatic: bi meaning "to employ,"

sentences.zh: 四海之隅，日出所照，無不循度而可使也。〉

translations.literal: Within the four seas' corners, wherever the sun shines, none do not follow the measure and can be employed."
translations.idiomatic: so that all within the sun's reach follows law and serves the throne."

sentences.zh: 功高于伊、周，而賞卑於齊、晉，朕甚恧焉。

translations.literal: Merit is higher than Yi and Zhou, yet reward is lower than Qi and Jin; We are greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Your deeds outshine Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, yet your fief is smaller than Qi or Jin ever received; We blush at the mismatch.

sentences.zh: 朕以眇眇之身，託于兆民之上，永思厥艱，若涉淵冰，非君攸濟，朕無任焉。

translations.literal: We, on Our tiny person, entrusted above the myriad people, forever ponder its hardship, as if treading deep water on ice; were it not for you, lord, to ford, We would have nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: We stand a frail child on the people's shoulders, dreading every step like thin ice over a pit; without you to bridge it We are lost.

sentences.zh: 今以冀州之河東、河內、魏郡、趙國、中山、常山、鉅鹿、安平、甘陵、平原凡十郡，封君爲魏公。

translations.literal: Now with Ji province's Hedong, Henei, Wei commandery, Zhao state, Zhongshan, Changshan, Julu, Anping, Ganling, Pingyuan, in all ten commanderies, We enfeoff you as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore enfeoff you as duke of Wei over Hedong, Henei, Wei, Zhao, Zhongshan, Changshan, Julu, Anping, Ganling, and Pingyuanten commanderies of Ji.

sentences.zh: 錫君玄土，苴以白茅；

translations.literal: We grant you black soil wrapped in white reeds;
translations.idiomatic: You receive the black earth and white reed bundle of a true vassal;

sentences.zh: 爰契爾龜，用建冢社。

translations.literal: thereby mark your tortoise, thereby establish the grand and soil altars.
translations.idiomatic: divine the tortoise and raise altars to Heaven and Earth for Wei.

sentences.zh: 昔在周室，畢公、毛公入爲卿佐，周、邵師保出爲二伯，外內之任，君實宜之，其以丞相領冀州牧如故。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Zhou house Duke Bi and Duke Mao entered as minister assistants; Zhou and Shao as tutor and guardian went out as the two bols; inner and outer tasks you truly fit; let you as chancellor also lead Ji shepherd as before.
translations.idiomatic: As Bi and Mao served inside court while Zhou and Shao held the two bols outside, you shall match both rolesremain chancellor and inspector of Ji as before.

sentences.zh: 又加君九錫，其敬聽朕命。

translations.literal: Further We add you the nine bestowals; respectfully hearken to Our command.
translations.idiomatic: We now add the nine ritual gifts; hear each charge with care.

sentences.zh: 以君經緯禮律，爲民軌儀，使安職業，無或遷志，是用錫君大輅、戎輅各一，玄牡二駟。

translations.literal: Because you weave warp and weft of ritual and law, are the people's track and measure, make them secure in occupation, none daring to shift intent, therefore We grant you the great chariot and war chariot, one each, black male teams two four-horse teams.
translations.idiomatic: First gift: for ordering law and livelihood so none stray from duty, the paired state chariots with black four-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 君勸分務本，穡人昏作，

translations.literal: You encourage sharing and attend to the root; the grain men toil at dusk;
translations.idiomatic: Second: for urging harvest and husbandry, for the farmers' tireless labor,

sentences.zh: 〈盤庚曰：「墮農自安，不昏作勞。

translations.literal: The Pan Geng says: "If farmers indulge ease and do not toil at dusk in labor."
translations.idiomatic: citing Pan Geng's warning against lazy farmers,

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄云：「昏，勉也。」〉

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said: "Dusk means exert oneself."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glossing "dusk toil" as striving without cease."

sentences.zh: 粟帛滯積，大業惟興，是用錫君衮冕之服，赤舄副焉。

translations.literal: Millet and silk stagnate in accumulation; the great enterprise only then rises; therefore We grant you the robe and cap of nine emblems, with red shoes accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Third: for overflowing granaries and silks, the nine-symbol court robes and crimson shoes.

sentences.zh: 君敦尚謙讓，俾民興行，少長有禮，上下咸和，是用錫君軒縣之樂，六佾之舞。

translations.literal: You honor and esteem modest yielding, causing the people to rise in conduct; young and old have ritual, high and low all harmonious; therefore We grant you the suspended music of a marquis, the dance of six rows.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: for teaching humility and harmony, the hall music and six-row dance of a lord.

sentences.zh: 君翼宣風化，爰發四方，遠人革面，華夏充實，是用錫君朱戶以居。

translations.literal: You wing-spread and proclaim transforming influence, thereby issuing to the four quarters; far people change face; Hua and Xia are filled; therefore We grant you vermilion doors to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: for civilizing frontier and heartland alike, vermilion-lacquered palace gates.

sentences.zh: 君研其明哲，思帝所難，官才任賢，羣善必舉，是用錫君納陛以登。

translations.literal: You grind your clear wisdom, pondering what the emperor finds hard; matching office to talent, all good is surely raised; therefore We grant you the ascending dais.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: for wise appointments, the raised inner steps to the hall.

sentences.zh: 君秉國之鈞，正色處中，纖豪之惡，靡不抑退，是用錫君虎賁之士三百人。

translations.literal: You grasp the state's steelyard, correct color standing in the center; the slightest evil, none not suppressed and removed; therefore We grant you three hundred tiger-guard knights.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: for crushing corruption from the center, three hundred royal guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 君糾虔天刑，章厥有罪，

translations.literal: You inspect and revere Heaven's punishments, manifest those who have guilt,
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: for enforcing justice and exposing guilt,

sentences.zh: 〈「糾虔天刑」語出《國語》，韋昭注曰：「糾，察也。

translations.literal: The phrase "inspect and revere Heaven's punishments" comes from the Guo yu; Wei Zhao's commentary says: "Inspect means examine."
translations.idiomatic: from the Guo yu, Wei Zhao glossing jiu as "examine,"

sentences.zh: 虔，敬也。

translations.literal: Qian means reverent.
translations.idiomatic: qian as "reverent,"

sentences.zh: 刑，法也。」〉

translations.literal: Xing means law."
translations.idiomatic: xing as "law."

sentences.zh: 犯關干紀，莫不誅殛，是用錫君鈇鉞各一。

translations.literal: Those who violate the passes and defy the norms, none are not executed and destroyed; therefore We grant you axe and halberd, one each.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore We grant you axe and halberd, one each—the regalia of execution.

sentences.zh: 君龍驤虎視，旁眺八維，掩討逆節，折衝四海，是用錫君彤弓一，彤矢百，玈弓十，玈矢千。

translations.literal: You dragon-soar and tiger-gaze, look askance at the eight directions, smother and punish rebellious nodes, repel foes within the four seas; therefore We grant you one red bow, one hundred red arrows, ten black bows, one thousand black arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: for commanding campaigns in every quarter, the crimson and black bows with their full quivers.

sentences.zh: 君以溫恭爲基，孝友爲德，明允篤誠，感于朕思，是用錫君秬鬯一卣，珪瓚副焉。

translations.literal: You take mild respect as foundation, filial friendship as virtue, clear trust and deep sincerity, moving Our thoughts; therefore We grant you one jar of black-millet ale, with jade ladle accompanying.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: for filial loyalty that touched the throne, the black-millet sacrificial ale with jade dipper.

sentences.zh: 魏國置丞相已下羣卿百寮，皆如漢初諸侯王之制。

translations.literal: The Wei state shall establish from the chancellor down the host of ministers and hundred officials, all according to the Han founding feudal kings' system.
translations.idiomatic: Wei may copy the full Han royal bureaucracy under its duke.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉，敬服朕命！

translations.literal: Go reverently; respectfully serve Our command!
translations.idiomatic: Accept these honors and serve Our mandate faithfully.

sentences.zh: 簡恤爾衆，時亮庶功，用終爾顯德，對揚我高祖之休命！

translations.literal: Discipline and pity your multitudes, always brighten common tasks, thereby complete your manifest virtue, answering and raising Our high ancestor's fine command!
translations.idiomatic: Rule your people with care, fulfill every duty, and bring glory to the Han house your ancestors served.

sentences.zh: 〈後漢尚書左丞潘勗之辭也。

translations.literal: (This was the diction of Later Han secretariat left vice director Pan Xu.)
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Songzhi credits the edict to Pan Xu of the Han secretariat.)

sentences.zh: 勗字元茂，陳留中牟人。

translations.literal: Xu's style name was Yuanmao; he was a man of Zhongmou in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xu (courtesy Yuanmao) came from Zhongmou in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》載公令曰：「夫受九錫，廣開土宇，周公其人也。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the duke's order: "To receive the nine bestowals and broadly open territory was Duke Zhou's person."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's modest reply in the Wei Shu says only the Duke of Zhou deserved nine tins and a great domain.

sentences.zh: 漢之異姓八王者，與高祖俱起布衣，刱定王業，其功至大，吾何可比之？

translations.literal: The Han's eight non-surname kings, together with Gaozu rose from common cloth, founded the royal enterprise; their merit was the greatest; how could I compare to them?"
translations.idiomatic: Han's eight non-Liu kings who rose with Gaozu built an empire; he could not rank beside them."

sentences.zh: 」前後三讓。

translations.literal: Before and after he declined three times.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the bundle three separate times.

sentences.zh: 於是中軍師王凌、謝亭侯荀攸、前軍師東武亭侯鍾繇、左軍師涼茂、右軍師毛玠、平虜將軍華鄉侯劉勳、建武將軍清苑亭侯劉若、伏波將軍高安侯夏侯惇、揚武將軍都亭侯王忠、奮威將軍樂鄉侯劉展、建忠將軍昌鄉亭侯鮮于輔、奮武將軍安國亭侯程昱、太中大夫都鄉侯賈詡、軍師祭酒千秋亭侯董昭、都亭侯薛洪、南鄉亭侯董蒙、關內侯王粲、傅巽、祭酒王選、袁奐、王朗、張承、任藩、杜襲、中護軍國明亭侯曹洪、中領軍萬歲亭侯韓浩、行驍騎將軍安平亭侯曹仁、領護軍將軍王圖、長史萬潛、謝奐、袁霸等勸進曰：「自古三代，胙臣以土，受命中興，封秩輔佐，皆所以襃功賞德，爲國藩衞也。

translations.literal: Thereupon central army director Wang Ling, Xieting marquis Xun You, front army director Dongwuting marquis Zhong Yao, left army director Liang Mao, right army director Mao Jie, general who pacifies barbarians Hua township marquis Liu Xun, general who establishes martial Qingyuan pavilion marquis Liu Ruo, general who calms waves Gaoan marquis Xiahou Dun, general who raises martial Duting marquis Wang Zhong, general who rouses might Lexiang marquis Liu Zhan, general who establishes loyalty Changxiangting marquis Xianyu Fu, general who rouses martial Anguo pavilion marquis Cheng Yu, grand counsellor of the palace Duxiang marquis Jia Xu, military counsellor libationer Qianqiu pavilion marquis Dong Zhao, Duting marquis Xue Hong, Nanxiangting marquis Dong Meng, guannei marquises Wang Can, Fu Sun, libationers Wang Xuan, Yuan Huan, Wang Lang, Zhang Cheng, Ren Fan, Du Xi, central protector Guoming pavilion marquis Cao Hong, central command Wansui pavilion marquis Han Hao, acting general who rouses cavalry Anping pavilion marquis Cao Ren, leading protector general Wang Tu, chief clerks Wan Qian, Xie Huan, Yuan Ba and others urged advancement, saying: "From antiquity the three dynasties, enfeoffing ministers with land, receiving the mandate's restoration, sealing ranks to assistants, all thereby praise merit and reward virtue, to be the state's screen and guard."
translations.idiomatic: A coalition led by Wang Ling, Xun You, Zhong Yao, Xiahou Dun, Cao Hong, Cao Ren, Jia Xu, Dong Zhao, Wang Can, and dozens of others then submitted a joint memorial urging him to accept the duchy, arguing that since high antiquity founders have always enfeoffed helpers to guard the throne.

sentences.zh: 徃者天下崩亂，羣凶豪起，顛越跋扈之險，不可忍言。

translations.literal: Formerly the realm collapsed in chaos; the host of villains and braves rose; the peril of overturning and domineering cannot be endured in words.
translations.idiomatic: They recalled the warlords' chaos when the realm nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 明公奮身出命以徇其難，誅二袁篡盜之逆，滅黃巾賊亂之類，殄夷首逆，芟撥荒穢，沐浴霜露二十餘年，書契已來，未有若此功者。

translations.literal: The enlightened duke risked body and gave life to follow their hardship, punished the two Yuans' usurpation and theft's rebellion, extinguished the Yellow Turbans' bandit chaos's kind, wiped out chief rebels, cleared away waste and filth, bathed in frost and dew more than twenty years; since writing began, none has had merit like this.
translations.idiomatic: They praised Cao Cao's twenty years of campaigns that crushed the Yuans, Yellow Turbans, and every rebel without parallel in recorded history.

sentences.zh: 昔周公承文、武之迹，受已成之業，高枕墨筆，拱揖羣后，商、奄之勤，不過二年，呂望因三分有二之形，據八百諸侯之勢，暫把旄鉞，一時指麾，然皆大啟土宇，跨州兼國。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou inherited Wen and Wu's traces, received already completed enterprise, high pillow and ink brush, bowed hands and yielded to the regional lords; Shang and Yan's toil was not more than two years; Lü Wang relying on two-thirds of the realm's shape, occupying eight hundred feudal lords' momentum, temporarily grasped staff and axe, for a time directed them; yet all greatly opened soil and territory, spanning provinces and combining states.
translations.idiomatic: They compared him to the Duke of Zhou and Lü Wang, who despite easier inheritances still carved out vast domains.

sentences.zh: 周公八子，並爲侯伯，白牡騂剛，郊祀天地，典策備物，擬則王室，榮章寵盛如此之弘也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou's eight sons all became marquises and earls, white bull and red bull, suburban sacrifice to Heaven and earth, canonical slips and full ritual goods, modeled on the royal house; glory and favor were thus vast.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's eight sons all became lords with full royal-style sacrifices and honors.

sentences.zh: 逮至漢興，佐命之臣，張耳、吳芮，其功至薄，亦連城開地，南面稱孤。

translations.literal: Down to Han's rise, ministers who aided the mandate, Zhang Er and Wu Rui, their merit was the thinnest, yet linked cities and opened territory, southward called themselves solitary.
translations.idiomatic: Even minor helpers at Han's founding like Zhang Er and Wu Rui became kings of wide domains.

sentences.zh: 此皆明君達主行之於上，賢臣聖宰受之於下，三代令典，漢帝明制。

translations.literal: These all are enlightened lords and penetrating masters practicing them above, worthy ministers and sage stewards receiving them below; the three dynasties' fine canons, Han emperor's clear system.
translations.idiomatic: Such rewards were always how wise emperors treated founding ministers.

sentences.zh: 今比勞則周、呂逸，計功則張、吳微，論制則齊、魯重，言地則長沙多；

translations.literal: Now comparing labor then Zhou and Lü are leisurely; counting merit then Zhang and Wu are slight; discussing institutions then Qi and Lu are weighty; speaking of land then Changsha is more;
translations.idiomatic: By labor Zhou and Lü Wang had it easier; by merit Zhang and Wu were smaller men; Qi and Lu held heavier titles; Changsha held more land;

sentences.zh: 然則魏國之封，九錫之榮，況於舊賞，猶懷玉而被褐也。

translations.literal: then as for Wei state's enfeoffment and nine bestowals' glory, compared to old rewards, it is still like hiding jade while wearing coarse cloth.
translations.idiomatic: yet your Wei fief and nine tins are still modest beside those old precedentslike pearls hidden under a beggar's cloak.

sentences.zh: 且列侯諸將，幸攀龍驥，得竊微勞，佩紫懷黃，蓋以百數，亦將因此傳之萬世，而明公獨辭賞於上，將使其下懷不自安，上違聖朝歡心，下失冠帶至望，忘輔弼之大業，信匹夫之細行，攸等所大懼也。

translations.literal: Moreover the full marquises and various generals, fortunately climbing the dragon's scales, were able to steal slight merit, wearing purple and hugging gold, perhaps numbering a hundred; they also will thereby transmit to ten thousand generations; yet the enlightened duke alone declines reward above, making those below harbor unease in themselves; above it violates the sage court's joy, below it loses the gentry's utmost hope; forgetting the great enterprise of assistance and support, trusting petty conduct of common menthis is what You and the others greatly fear."
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of officers owe their purple sashes to your rise; if you alone refuse the throne's thanks, you unsettle your men, disappoint the emperor, and betray the cause for false modestythey beg you not to do it."

sentences.zh: 」於是公勑外爲章，但受魏郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the duke ordered outwardly to memorialize, but only accept Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then filed a memorial saying he would accept only Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 攸等復曰：「伏見魏國初封，聖朝發慮，稽謀羣寮，然後策命；

translations.literal: You and the others again said: "We have seen that when Wei state was first enfeoffed, the sage court issued plans, examined counsel among the host of ministers, then issued the mandate;
translations.idiomatic: They replied that the court had already deliberated the full Wei enfeoffment,

sentences.zh: 而明公久違上指，不即大禮。

translations.literal: yet the enlightened duke for long has disobeyed superior intent, not immediately performing the great rites.
translations.idiomatic: while he kept defying the emperor's will by delaying the full acceptance.

sentences.zh: 今旣虔奉詔命，副順衆望，又欲辭多當少，讓九受一，是猶漢朝之賞不行，而攸等之請未許也。

translations.literal: Now having reverently received the edict's command, matching the multitude's hope, again wishing to decline much and take little, yielding nine and receiving one, is still as if Han court's rewards were not carried out and You and the others' requests were not permitted."
translations.idiomatic: Now that he had bowed to the edict, taking only one part of nine would still nullify the court's intent and their petition."

sentences.zh: 昔齊、魯之封，奄有東海，疆域井賦，四百萬家，基隆業廣，易以立功，故能成翼戴之勳，立一匡之績。

translations.literal: Formerly Qi and Lu's enfeoffments embraced the eastern sea; territory and well-field levies, four million households; foundation lofty and enterprise broad, easy thereby to accomplish merit; therefore they could complete the wing-supporting merit, establish the one-correction's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Lu once held the eastern sea with four million households, making hegemony easy.

sentences.zh: 今魏國雖有十郡之名，猶減於曲阜，計其戶數，不能參半，以藩衞王室，立垣樹屏，猶未足也。

translations.literal: Now though Wei state has the name of ten commanderies, it is still less than Qufu; counting its household numbers, it cannot reach half; to screen and guard the royal house, raise ramparts and plant screens, is still not enough."
translations.idiomatic: Wei's ten commanderies are smaller than Qufu alone by household countinsufficient even as a bulwark for the Han."

sentences.zh: 且聖上覽亡秦無輔之禍，懲曩日震蕩之艱，託建忠賢，廢墜是爲，願明公恭承帝命，無或拒違。

translations.literal: Moreover the sage above surveys the misfortune of fallen Qin lacking support, takes warning from the recent days' shaking hardship, entrusts and establishes loyal worthies, what is fallen is thereby raised; We wish the enlightened duke respectfully to receive the imperial command, none or refuse and oppose."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven, mindful of Qin's fall without allies, leans on you to shore up the dynasty; accept fully and do not resist."

sentences.zh: 」公乃受命。

translations.literal: The duke thereupon received the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then accepted the ducal investiture.

sentences.zh: 《魏略》載公上書謝曰：「臣蒙先帝厚恩，致位郎署，受性疲怠，意望畢足，非敢希望高位，庶幾顯達。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe records the duke's upward memorial thanking, saying: "Your servant received former emperors' thick grace, reached office in the gentleman's suite; received nature tired and slack; intent and hope were fully satisfied, not daring to hope for high position, perhaps to shine and rise."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe preserves his thank-you memorial: he had only wished for a modest court career until Dong Zhuo forced him to arms.

sentences.zh: 會董卓作亂，義當死難，故敢奮身出命，摧鋒率衆，遂值千載之運，奉役目下。

translations.literal: It happened that Dong Zhuo made chaos; righteousness required dying in hardship; therefore I dared risk body and give life, broke the vanguard and led the host, then encountered a thousand years' fortune, serving under Your eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Then fortune raised him to serve the emperor.

sentences.zh: 當二袁炎沸侵侮之際，陛下與臣寒心同憂，顧瞻京師，進受猛敵，常恐君臣俱陷虎口，誠不自意能全首領。

translations.literal: When the two Yuans boiled and invaded and insulted, Your Majesty with your servant shared cold heart and same worry, gazing toward the capital, advancing to receive fierce enemies; always feared ruler and minister together would fall into the tiger's mouth; truly did not expect in myself to be able to preserve head and neck."
translations.idiomatic: At the height of the Yuan war he and the emperor had expected to die together.

sentences.zh: 賴祖宗靈祐，醜類夷滅，得使微臣竊名其間。

translations.literal: Relying on ancestors' and spirits' blessing, the vile host was leveled, enabling your slight servant to steal a name among them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven allowed him to survive and earn a name.

sentences.zh: 陛下加恩，授以上相，封爵寵祿，豐大弘厚，生平之願，實不望也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty added grace, conferring the highest minister, enfeoffing rank and favoring salary, vast, great, broad, and thick; the wish of a lifetime, truly I did not hope for it.
translations.idiomatic: Each promotion exceeded his wildest hopes.

sentences.zh: 口與心計，幸且待罪，保持列侯，遺付子孫，自託聖世，永無憂責。

translations.literal: Mouth and heart together calculated, fortunately for the time bearing blame, preserving full marquis rank, handing down to sons and grandsons, self-entrusting to the sage age, forever without worry or responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: He had hoped only to keep a marquisate for his heirs in peace.

sentences.zh: 不意陛下乃發盛意，開國備錫，以貺愚臣，地比齊、魯，禮同藩王，非臣無功所宜膺據。

translations.literal: I did not expect Your Majesty then to issue abundant intent, opening a state and preparing tins, thereby to reward your foolish servant; land comparable to Qi and Lu, ritual the same as a feudal king; it is not what your servant without merit ought to shoulder."
translations.idiomatic: The new duchy rivaled Qi and Lu in ritual rank beyond his deserts.

sentences.zh: 歸情上聞，不蒙聽許，嚴詔切至，誠使臣心俯仰偪迫。

translations.literal: My feelings reported upward were not granted hearing; stern edicts arrived urgently, truly making your servant's heart bow and rise under pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated refusals met only sterner edicts.

sentences.zh: 伏自惟省，列在大臣，命制王室，身非己有，豈敢自私，遂其愚意，亦將黜退，令就初服。

translations.literal: Bowing and examining myself, arrayed among great ministers, fate controlling the royal house, my body not belonging to myself, how dare I be selfish and follow my foolish intent; I also would be dismissed and retired, ordered to take up original dress."
translations.idiomatic: He knew his life belonged to the state and could not indulge private modesty without being removed.

sentences.zh: 今奉疆土，備數藩翰，非敢遠期，慮有後世；

translations.literal: Now receiving territory and filling the number of screen and fence, I do not dare far-reaching expectation, considering later generations;
translations.idiomatic: Accepting the fief he thinks not of dynastic ambition but of duty,

sentences.zh: 至於父子相誓終身，灰軀盡命，報塞厚恩。

translations.literal: as for father and son swearing to the end of life, reducing body to ash and exhausting life, repaying and blocking thick grace."
translations.idiomatic: and swears father and son will spend life and ash repaying the Han."

sentences.zh: 天威在顏，悚懼受詔。」〉

translations.literal: Heaven's awesomeness is on the face; I tremble and receive the edict."
translations.idiomatic: He ends trembling before Heaven's command."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，始建魏社稷宗廟。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, first established Wei altars of soil and grain and ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Wei raised its own altars of soil and grain and ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 天子娉公三女爲貴人，少者待年於國。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven betrothed three of the duke's daughters as honorable ladies; the youngest waited years in the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took three of Cao Cao's daughters as imperial consorts, the youngest to come of age in Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：使使持節行太常大司農安陽亭侯王邑，齎璧、帛、玄纁、絹五萬匹之鄴納娉，介者五人，皆以議郎行大夫事，副介一人。〉

translations.literal: The Emperor Xian's Daily Notes says: he sent credential-bearer acting Minister of Ceremonies grand minister of agriculture Anyangting marquis Wang Yi, carrying jade, silks, black and red silks, fifty thousand bolts of plain silk to Ye to complete the betrothal; five intermediaries all acting as grandees with grandee affairs, one vice-intermediary."
translations.idiomatic: The diary lists the embassy of Wang Yi with silks and five matchmakers sent to Ye for the betrothal.

sentences.zh: 九月，作金虎臺，鑿渠引漳水入白溝以通河。

translations.literal: Ninth month, made the Golden Tiger Terrace, dug a canal leading Zhang River into Baigou to connect the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he built the Golden Tiger Terrace and linked the Zhang to Baigou toward the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，分魏郡爲東西部，置都尉。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, divided Wei commandery into east and west parts, established commandants.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he split Wei commandery into east and west with commandants.

sentences.zh: 十一月，初置尚書、侍中、六卿。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first established secretariat, palace attendant, six ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he created the secretariat, palace attendants, and six ministers for Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：以荀攸爲尚書令，涼茂爲僕射，毛玠、崔琰、常林、徐奕、何夔爲尚書，王粲、杜襲、衞覬、和洽爲侍中。〉

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu says: he made Xun You secretariat director, Liang Mao vice director, Mao Jie, Cui Yan, Chang Lin, Xu Yi, He Kui as secretaries, Wang Can, Du Xi, Wei Ji, He Qia as palace attendants."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Annals names Xun You, Liang Mao, Mao Jie, Cui Yan, Wang Can, Du Xi, and others for the new posts."

sentences.zh: 馬超在漢陽，復因羌、胡爲害，氐王千萬叛應超，屯興國。

translations.literal: Ma Chao was in Hanyang, again by means of Qiang and Hu did harm; Di king Qianwan rebelled answering Chao, encamped at Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chao stirred Qiang and Hu in Hanyang; Di chief Qianwan joined him at Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 使夏侯淵討之。

translations.literal: He made Xiahou Yuan campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiahou Yuan against them.

sentences.zh: 十九年春正月，始耕籍田。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year spring first month, first plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 214 CE, he first performed the royal plowing rite.

sentences.zh: 南安趙衢、漢陽尹奉等討超，梟其妻子，超奔漢中。

translations.literal: Nan'an Zhao Qu, Hanyang Yin Feng and others campaigned against Chao, displayed his wife and children's heads; Chao fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qu and Yin Feng of Nan'an turned on Ma Chao, killed his family, and drove him to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 韓遂徙金城，入氐王千萬部，率羌、胡萬餘騎與夏侯淵戰，擊，大破之，遂走西平。

translations.literal: Han Sui moved to Jincheng, entered Di king Qianwan's division, led more than ten thousand Qiang and Hu riders to battle Xiahou Yuan; Yuan attacked and greatly defeated them; Sui fled to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui joined Qianwan with ten thousand allied horse to fight Xiahou Yuan; Xiahou Yuan smashed the coalition and Han Sui fled to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 淵與諸將攻興國，屠之。

translations.literal: Yuan with the various generals attacked Xingguo and slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan stormed Xingguo and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 省安東、永陽郡。

translations.literal: Abolished Andong and Yongyang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished Andong and Yongyang commanderies.

sentences.zh: 安定太守毌丘興將之官，公戒之曰：「羌，胡欲與中國通，自當遣人來，慎勿遣人徃。

translations.literal: Anding Grand Administrator Muqiu Xing was about to take office; the duke warned him, saying: "Qiang and Hu, if they wish to communicate with the Central States, themselves ought to send people; be careful not to send people thither."
translations.idiomatic: As Muqiu Xing left for Anding, Cao Cao warned him never to send Han envoys into Qiang country first.

sentences.zh: 善人難得，必將教羌、胡妄有所請求，因欲以自利；

translations.literal: Good men are hard to obtain; they are sure to teach Qiang and Hu recklessly to have requests, thereby wishing to profit themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Meddling Han clerks would teach the tribes to make impossible demands for private gain;

sentences.zh: 不從便爲失異俗意，從之則無益事。

translations.literal: if you do not follow, then it becomes losing the different customs' intent; if you follow, then it is without benefit to affairs."
translations.idiomatic: refusing offends them; granting harms the stateno win."

sentences.zh: 」興至，遣校尉范陵至羌中，陵果教羌，使自請爲屬國都尉。

translations.literal: When Xing arrived, he dispatched Colonel Fan Ling to the Qiang; Ling indeed taught the Qiang, making them self-request to be dependent-state commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Muqiu Xing ignored the warning: his colonel Fan Ling coached the Qiang to petition for a dependent-state commandantcy.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「吾預知當爾，非聖也，但更事多耳。」

translations.literal: The duke said: "I foreknew it would be thus; it is not sagehood, only that I have passed through more affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao remarked, "I foresaw thatnot prophecy, just experience."

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：使行太常事大司農安陽亭侯王邑與宗正劉艾，皆持節，介者五人，齎束帛駟馬，及給事黃門侍郎、掖庭丞、中常侍二人，迎二貴人于魏公國。

translations.literal: The Emperor Xian's Daily Notes says: he sent acting Minister of Ceremonies grand minister of agriculture Anyangting marquis Wang Yi with Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ai, both bearing staffs, five intermediaries, carrying silk bundles and four-horse teams, and supplying-attendant yellow-gate gentleman, palace internment aide, two regular attendants, to welcome two honorable ladies in the duke of Wei's state."
translations.idiomatic: The diary describes the second embassy escorting the two elder consorts from Wei toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 二月癸亥，又於魏公宗廟授二貴人印綬。

translations.literal: Second month guihai, again in the duke of Wei's ancestral temple conferred on the two honorable ladies seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the second month the two consorts received seals in the Wei ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詣魏公宮延秋門，迎貴人升車。

translations.literal: Jiazi, went to the duke of Wei palace's Yanqiu Gate, welcomed the honorable ladies ascending carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi they were escorted through Yanqiu Gate into the carriages.

sentences.zh: 魏遣郎中令、少府、博士、御府乘黃廄令、丞相掾屬侍送貴人。

translations.literal: Wei dispatched chamberlain commandant, minister of the lesser treasury, erudite, imperial stable yellow-stable commandant, chancellor's aides to accompany and send off the honorable ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei officials accompanied the escort.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，二貴人至洧倉中，遣侍中丹將宂從虎賁前後駱驛往迎之。

translations.literal: Guiyou, the two honorable ladies reached Weicang center; he dispatched palace attendant Dan general Mi with tiger guards front and rear in relays to go welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou they reached Weicang; palace attendants and tiger guards relayed them onward.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，二貴人入宮，御史大夫、中二千石將大夫、議郎會殿中，魏國二卿及侍中、中郎二人，與漢公卿並升殿宴。〉

translations.literal: Yihai, the two honorable ladies entered the palace; the imperial counselor, two-thousand-shi leading grandees and counsellors assembled in the hall; Wei state's two ministers and two palace attendants and two gentlemen consultants, together with Han dukes and ministers, jointly ascended the hall to feast."
translations.idiomatic: On yihai they entered the Luoyang palace for a joint Han–Wei banquet.

sentences.zh: 三月，天子使魏公位在諸侯王上，改授金璽，赤紱、遠遊冠。

translations.literal: Third month, the Son of Heaven made the duke of Wei's rank above the feudal kings, changed to confer the gold seal, crimson ribbon, and far-roaming cap.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor ranked the duke of Wei above all kings and reissued the gold seal, crimson ribbons, and far-roaming crown.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝起居注》曰：使左中郎將楊宣、亭侯裴茂持節、印授之。〉

translations.literal: The Emperor Xian's Daily Notes says: he sent left gentleman of the household Yang Xuan and Ting marquis Pei Mao bearing staff and seal to confer them."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan and Pei Mao delivered the new regalia."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，公征孫權。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, the duke campaigned against Sun Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he marched again against Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：參軍傅幹諫曰：「治天下之大具有二，文與武也；

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou chunqiu says: staff adviser Fu Gan remonstrated, saying: "The great tools for ordering the realm are two, pattern and martial;"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan's Jiuzhou chunqiu memorial urged him to balance wen and wu,

sentences.zh: 用武則先威，用文則先德，威德足以相濟，而後王道備矣。

translations.literal: using martial, first awe; using pattern, first virtue; awe and virtue enough to aid each other, then the kingly way is complete."
translations.idiomatic: Using force, establish awe first; using civil rule, establish virtue first; when awe and virtue reinforce each other, the kingly way is complete."

sentences.zh: 往者天下大亂，上下失序，明公用武攘之，十平其九。

translations.literal: Formerly the realm was greatly in chaos; high and low lost order; the enlightened duke used martial power to repel it, nine tenths of it he pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan continued: when the empire collapsed you restored order by force nine-tenths of the way.

sentences.zh: 今未承王命者，吳與蜀也，吳有長江之險，蜀有崇山之阻，難以威服，易以德懷。

translations.literal: Now those not yet receiving royal command are Wu and Shu; Wu has the Yangzi's peril; Shu has towering mountains' block; difficult thereby to awe into submission, easy thereby to cherish with virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wu and Shu remain; the Yangzi and Shu passes yield to virtue more readily than to terror.

sentences.zh: 愚以爲可且按甲寢兵，息軍養士，分土定封，論功行賞，若此則內外之心固，有功者勸，而天下知制矣。

translations.literal: I foolishly think you can for the time sheath armor and rest weapons, rest the army and nourish gentlemen, divide land and fix enfeoffments, discuss merit and carry out rewards; if so then inner and outer hearts are firm, those with merit are encouraged, and all under Heaven knows regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He urged demobilization, rewards for merit, and consolidation so the realm sees stable rule.

sentences.zh: 然後漸興學校，以導其善性而長其義節。

translations.literal: Then gradually raise schools, thereby guiding their good nature and lengthening their righteous integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Then build schools to shape character and ritual.

sentences.zh: 公神武震於四海，若修文以濟之，則普天之下，無思不服矣。

translations.literal: The duke's divine martial awes within the four seas; if you cultivate pattern thereby to aid it, then under all Heaven none will think of not submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Your military fame already fills the seas; add civil arts and the world will submit willingly.

sentences.zh: 今舉十萬之衆，頓之長江之濵，若賊負固深藏，則士馬不能逞其能，奇變無所用其權，則大威有屈而敵心未能服矣。

translations.literal: Now raising a hundred thousand host, halting it on the Yangzi's shore; if the bandits rely on fortifications and hide deep, then soldiers and horses cannot display their ability, strange shifts have nowhere to use their power; then great awe is bent yet enemy hearts are not yet able to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Parking an army on the Long River while Sun Quan digs in wastes men and gains nothing.

sentences.zh: 唯明公思虞舜舞干戚之義，全威養德，以道制勝。

translations.literal: Only let the enlightened duke ponder Shun of Yu's meaning in dancing shield and axe, preserve awe and nourish virtue, thereby use the Way to overcome victory.
translations.idiomatic: Think of Shun winning enemies with ritual dance: conserve strength and win by moral ascendancy.

sentences.zh: 」公不從，軍遂無功。

translations.literal: The duke did not follow; the army then had no success.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao ignored him and the campaign failed.

sentences.zh: 幹字彥材，北地人，終於丞相倉曹屬。

translations.literal: Gan's style name was Yancai; he was a man of Beidi; he ended as a clerk in the chancellor's granary bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gan (courtesy Yancai) of Beidi died in office as a chancellor's granary clerk.

sentences.zh: 有子曰玄。〉

translations.literal: He had a son named Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: His son was named Fu Xuan."

sentences.zh: 初，隴西宋建自稱河首平漢王，聚衆枹罕，改元，置百官，三十餘年。

translations.literal: At first, Longxi Song Jian styled himself King Who Pacifies the Han at the River's Head, gathered a host at Fuhan, changed the era title, established the hundred officials, more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Song Jian of Longxi had ruled Fuhan as a self-styled king for over thirty years.

sentences.zh: 遣夏侯淵自興國討之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Xiahou Yuan from Xingguo to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan marched from Xingguo against him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，屠枹罕，斬建，涼州平。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, slaughtered Fuhan, beheaded Jian; Liang province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Cao Cao took Fuhan, executed Song Jian, and pacified Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 公自合肥還。

translations.literal: The duke returned from Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: He returned from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，漢皇后伏氏坐昔與父故屯騎校尉完書，云帝以董承被誅怨恨公，辭甚醜惡，發聞，后廢黜死，兄弟皆伏法。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Han Empress nee Fu sat crime because formerly with her father former colonel of agile cavalry Wan she wrote letters, saying the emperor because Dong Cheng was executed resented the duke; the language was very ugly; when it was exposed, the empress was deposed and died; brothers all suffered the law.
translations.idiomatic: In November Empress Fu fell because letters to her father Fu Wan showed she and the emperor resented Cao Cao after Dong Cheng's death; she was deposed and killed with her kin.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：公遣華歆勒兵入宮收后，后閉戶匿壁中。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: the duke dispatched Hua Xin leading troops into the palace to seize the empress; the empress closed the door and hid in a wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says Hua Xin stormed the palace while the empress hid in a wall cavity.

sentences.zh: 歆壞戶發壁，牽后出。

translations.literal: Xin broke the door and opened the wall, dragged the empress out.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin broke in and dragged her out.

sentences.zh: 帝時與御史大夫郗慮坐，后被髮徒跣過，執帝手曰：「不能復相活邪？

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was sitting with Imperial Counselor Xi Chu; the empress, hair unbound and barefoot, passed, grasped the emperor's hand saying: "Can we not again preserve each other alive?"
translations.idiomatic: She clutched the emperor's hand barefoot, begging for life.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我亦不自知命在何時也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I also do not myself know when fate rests."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor whispered that he did not know his own fate.

sentences.zh: 」帝謂慮曰：「郗公，天下寧有是乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Chu: "Lord Xi, can there be such a thing under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Xi Chu, "Can the world hold such cruelty?"

sentences.zh: 」遂將后殺之，完及宗族死者數百人。〉

translations.literal: Thereupon they led the empress away and killed her; Wan and the clan group dead numbered several hundred persons."
translations.idiomatic: They took her away to die; Fu Wan's clan lost hundreds."

sentences.zh: 十二月，公至孟津。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the duke reached Meng Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In December he reached Meng Ford.

sentences.zh: 天子命公置旄頭，宮殿設鍾虡。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the duke to establish plumed spearsmen and set bell-stands in the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him plumed guard and palace bell-stands.

sentences.zh: 乙未，令曰：「夫有行之士未必能進取，進取之士未必能有行也。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei he issued an order: "Men of conduct are not necessarily able to advance; advancing men are not necessarily able to have conduct."
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day he proclaimed that virtue and ambition need not coincide in the same man.

sentences.zh: 陳平豈篤行，蘇秦豈守信邪？

translations.literal: Was Chen Ping surely of steadfast conduct? Was Su Qin surely trustworthy?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping was hardly a saint; Su Qin was hardly loyal.

sentences.zh: 而陳平定漢業，蘇秦濟弱燕。

translations.literal: Yet Chen Ping settled Han's enterprise; Su Qin aided weak Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they saved Han and Yan.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，士有偏短，庸可廢乎！

translations.literal: Speaking from this, gentlemen have partial shortcomings; how can they be cast aside!
translations.idiomatic: Therefore never discard a man for a single flaw.

sentences.zh: 有司明思此義，則士無遺滯，官無廢業矣。

translations.literal: If those in charge clearly ponder this meaning, then gentlemen will not be left stranded and offices will not lack work.
translations.idiomatic: Let personnel officers heed this and talent will not stall.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「夫刑，百姓之命也，而軍中典獄者或非其人，而任以三軍死生之事，吾甚懼之。

translations.literal: " Again he said: "As for punishments, they are the hundred surnames' life; yet those in the army who manage prisons may not be the right men, yet are entrusted with the three armies' life and death affairs; I greatly fear this."
translations.idiomatic: He added that military jailers hold lives and must be legally trained.

sentences.zh: 其選明達法理者，使持典刑。

translations.literal: Select those clear and penetrating in law and principle, make them hold canonical punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint only clear-minded jurists to run military justice."

sentences.zh: 」於是置理曹掾屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established law-bureau clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He created the law bureau staff.

sentences.zh: 二十年春正月，天子立公中女爲皇后。

translations.literal: Twentieth year spring first month, the Son of Heaven established the duke's middle daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 215 CE, his middle daughter became empress.

sentences.zh: 省雲中、定襄、五原、朔方郡，郡置一縣領其民，合以爲新興郡。

translations.literal: Abolished Yunzhong, Dingxiang, Wuyuan, and Shuofang commanderies, each commandery establishing one county to lead its people, combining them to make Xinxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He merged northern border commanderies into Xinxing with one county seat each.

sentences.zh: 三月，公西征張魯，至陳倉，將自武都入氐；

translations.literal: Third month, the duke west campaigned against Zhang Lu, reached Chencang, was about to enter Di from Wudu;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he marched on Hanzhong via Chencang toward Wudu and the Di country;

sentences.zh: 氐人塞道，先遣張郃、朱靈等攻破之。

translations.literal: Di people blocked the road; first he dispatched Zhang He, Zhu Ling, and others to break them.
translations.idiomatic: the Di blocked the road until Zhang He and Zhu Ling cleared it.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，公自陳倉以出散關，至河池。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, the duke from Chencang exited San Pass, reached Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he passed San Pass from Chencang to Hechi.

sentences.zh: 氐王竇茂衆萬餘人，恃險不服，五月，公攻屠之。

translations.literal: Di king Dou Mao's host more than ten thousand men, relying on peril did not submit; fifth month, the duke attacked and slaughtered them.
translations.idiomatic: Di king Dou Mao held defiles with ten thousand men until Cao Cao stormed and slaughtered them in May.

sentences.zh: 西平、金城諸將麴演、蔣石等共斬送韓遂首。

translations.literal: Xiping and Jincheng various generals Qu Yan, Jiang Shi, and others jointly beheaded and sent Han Sui's head.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yan and Jiang Shi of Xiping and Jincheng sent in Han Sui's head.

sentences.zh: 〈《典略》曰：遂字文約，始與同郡邊章俱著名西州。

translations.literal: The Dian lüe says: Sui's style name was Wenyue; at first with same commandery Bian Zhang both were famed in the western province.
translations.idiomatic: The Dian lüe gives Han Sui (courtesy Wenyue) and his early fame with Bian Zhang.

sentences.zh: 章爲督軍從事。

translations.literal: Zhang was supervising army clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Zhang was an army supervisor clerk.

sentences.zh: 遂奉計詣京師，何進宿聞其名，特與相見，遂說進使誅諸閹人，進不從，乃求歸。

translations.literal: Sui carried documents to the capital; He Jin long had heard his name and specially met him; Sui persuaded Jin to execute the various eunuchs; Jin did not follow; then he sought to return.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sui once urged He Jin to purge the eunuchs, failed, and went home.

sentences.zh: 會涼州宋揚、北宮玉等反，舉章、遂爲主，章尋病卒，遂爲揚等所劫，不得已，遂阻兵爲亂，積三十二年，至是乃死，年七十餘矣。

translations.literal: It happened that Liangzhou Song Yang, Beigong Yu, and others rebelled, raising Zhang and Sui as lords; Zhang soon died of illness; Sui was coerced by Yang and the others, had no choice, then blocked arms and made chaos, accumulating thirty-two years; down to here then died, age more than seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Later mutineers forced Han Sui and Bian Zhang to lead; Zhang died; Han Sui rebelled for thirty-two years until his seventies when his own men killed him.

sentences.zh: 劉艾《靈帝紀》曰：章，一名元。〉

translations.literal: Liu Ai's Annals of Emperor Ling says: Zhang, another name was Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ai notes Bian Zhang was also called Yuan."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，公至陽平。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, the duke reached Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he reached Yangping.

sentences.zh: 張魯使弟衞與將楊昂等據陽平關，橫山築城十餘里，攻之不能拔，乃引軍還。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu made younger brother Wei and generals Yang Ang and others hold Yangping Pass, spanning the mountain building a city more than ten li; attacking could not take it; then he led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei and Yang Ang held a ten-li wall at Yangping until Cao Cao withdrew, seemingly beaten.

sentences.zh: 賊見大軍退，其守備解散。

translations.literal: The bandits saw the great army retreat; their guard preparations dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing retreat, the defenders relaxed.

sentences.zh: 公乃密遣解𢢼、高祚等乘險夜襲，大破之，斬其將楊任，進攻衞，衞等夜遁，魯潰奔巴中。

translations.literal: The duke then secretly dispatched Xie Xiao, Gao Zuo, and others to exploit the peril and raid by night, greatly defeated them, beheaded their general Yang Ren, advanced to attack Wei; Wei and others fled by night; Lu broke and fled to Bazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xie Xiao and Gao Zuo on a night climb, routed them, killed Yang Ren, and drove Zhang Wei away so Zhang Lu fled toward Ba.

sentences.zh: 公軍入南鄭，盡得魯府庫珍寶。

translations.literal: The duke's army entered Nanzheng, fully obtained Lu's treasury treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Nanzheng, the Hanzhong administrative seat, he seized Zhang Lu's hoard.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：軍自武都山行千里，升降險阻，軍人勞苦；

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: the army from Wudu mountain marched a thousand li, ascending and descending peril and obstruction; soldiers and army were toiling and bitter;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei notes the brutal march through Wudu mountains,

sentences.zh: 公於是大饗，莫不忘其勞。〉

translations.literal: the duke thereupon greatly feasted, none not forgetting their labor."
translations.idiomatic: then feasted the army in gratitude for their ordeal."

sentences.zh: 巴、漢皆降。

translations.literal: Ba and Han all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ba commandery and Hanzhong submitted.

sentences.zh: 復漢寧郡爲漢中；

translations.literal: Restored Hanning commandery as Hanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: He restored Hanning as Hanzhong commandery;

sentences.zh: 分漢中之安陽、西城爲西城郡，置太守；

translations.literal: divided Hanzhong's Anyang and Xicheng to make Xicheng commandery, established grand administrator;
translations.idiomatic: split Anyang and Xicheng from Hanzhong into a new Xicheng commandery with a governor;

sentences.zh: 分錫、上庸郡，置都尉。

translations.literal: divided Xi and Shangyong commanderies, established commandants.
translations.idiomatic: and carved Xi and Shangyong with commandants.

sentences.zh: 八月，孫權圍合肥，張遼、李典擊破之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Sun Quan besieged Hefei; Zhang Liao and Li Dian broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sun Quan besieged Hefei until Zhang Liao and Li Dian broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 九月，巴七姓夷王朴胡、賨邑侯杜濩舉巴夷、賨民來附，

translations.literal: Ninth month, the seven-surname Yi king of Ba Pu Hu and Cong district marquis Du Hu raised Ba Yi and Cong people to come attach,
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Pu Hu, Yi king of the seven Ba clans, and Du Hu, lord of the Cong district, led Ba and Cong tribes to surrender,

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：朴音浮。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Pu is read like fu.
translations.idiomatic: (Sun Sheng notes 朴 is read like fu.)

sentences.zh: 濩音戶。〉

translations.literal: Hu is read like hu."
translations.idiomatic: The gloss reads the graph as hu.

sentences.zh: 於是分巴郡，以胡爲巴東太守，濩爲巴西太守，皆封列侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon divided Ba commandery, made Hu grand administrator of Badong, Hu grand administrator of Baxi, both enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was split; Pu Hu became governor of Badong and Du Hu of Baxi, both full marquises.

sentences.zh: 天子命公承制封拜諸侯守相。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the duke by received authority to enfeoff and appoint feudal lords, guardians, and chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor authorized Cao Cao to appoint regional lords and governors on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 〈孔衍《漢魏春秋》曰：天子以公典任于外，臨事之賞，或宜速疾，乃命公得承制封拜諸侯守相，詔曰：「夫軍之大事，在茲賞罰，勸善懲惡，宜不旋時，故《司馬法》曰『賞不逾日』者，欲民速覩爲善之利也。

translations.literal: Kong Yan's Han Wei chunqiu says: the Son of Heaven because the duke's canonical charge was outside, rewards for affairs on the spot sometimes ought to be swift; therefore ordered the duke able by received authority to enfeoff and appoint feudal lords, guardians, and chancellors; the edict said: "As for the army's great matters, in these rewards and punishments, encouraging good and punishing evil, ought not to turn on the moment; therefore the Sima fa says 'reward does not pass the day' is wishing the people quickly to see the profit of doing good."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yan records an edict citing the Sima fa on prompt military rewards so soldiers see virtue rewarded at once,

sentences.zh: 昔在中興，鄧禹入關，承制拜軍祭酒李文爲河東太守，來歙又承制拜高峻爲通路將軍，察其本傳，皆非先請，明臨事刻印也，斯則世祖神明，權達損益，蓋所用速示威懷而著鴻勳也。

translations.literal: Formerly at restoration, Deng Yu entered the passes, by received authority appointed army libationer Li Wen as Hedong grand administrator; Lai Xi again by received authority appointed Gao Jun as general who opens the road; examining their basic biographies, all were not first requested, showing on-the-spot sealing of seals; this then was Shizu's divine clarity, weighing expedient gain and loss, because what was used was swift in displaying awe and cherishing and manifesting great merit."
translations.idiomatic: likening this to Guangwu's letting Deng Yu and Lai Xi commission officers in the field without prior imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 其春秋之義，大夫出疆，有專命之事，苟所以利社稷安國家而已。

translations.literal: As for the Spring and Autumn's meaning, when grandees leave the frontier, they have matters of sole command, if thereby it profits the altars of soil and grain and settles the state only."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn allows ministers abroad sole discretion for the state's good.

sentences.zh: 況君秉任二伯，師尹九有，實征夷夏，軍行蕃甸之外，失得在於斯須之間，停賞俟詔以滯世務，固非朕之所圖也。

translations.literal: Moreover you grasp the two bols' charge, are master of the nine domains, truly campaign against Yi and Xia; the army moves beyond the royal domain; failure and success lie between moments; stopping rewards to await edicts would clog worldly affairs; solidly is not what We intend."
translations.idiomatic: You command like the ancient two bols beyond the capital; waiting for Luoyang on every promotion would cripple the war effort.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，臨事所甄，當加寵號者，其便刻印章假授，咸使忠義得相獎勵，勿有疑焉。」〉

translations.literal: From now on, in affairs you discern, when you should add favor titles, then conveniently carve seals and grant by proxy, all causing loyalty and righteousness to be able mutually to encourage; have no doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth carve seals and commission on your own judgment to keep loyalty rewarded without delay."

sentences.zh: 冬十月，始置名號侯至五大夫，與舊列侯、關內侯凡六等，以賞軍功。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, first established title-rank marquis down to grandee fifth rank, together with old full marquis and guannei marquis in all six grades, thereby to reward military merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he created six grades of military nobility from title marquis down to grandee fifth class.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：置名號侯爵十八級，關中侯爵十七級，皆金印紫綬；

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: established title-rank marquis rank eighteen grades, Guanzhong marquis rank seventeen grades, both gold seal purple ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei lists eighteen ranks of title marquis and seventeen of Guanzhong marquis with gold and purple,

sentences.zh: 又置關內外侯十六級，銅印龜紐墨綬；

translations.literal: again established inside-outside Guanzhong marquis sixteen grades, copper seal turtle knob black ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: sixteen ranks of inner/outer Guanzhong marquis with copper turtle seals,

sentences.zh: 五大夫十五級，銅印環紐，亦墨綬，皆不食租，與舊列侯關內侯凡六等。

translations.literal: grandee fifth rank fifteen grades, copper seal ring knob, also black ribbon, all not eating rent lands; together with old full marquis and guannei marquis in all six grades.
translations.idiomatic: and fifteen ranks of grandee fifth class with ring-knob copper sealsnone with rent fiefs, six grades in all beside old marquises.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以爲今之虛封蓋自此始。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that today's hollow enfeoffment probably began from this."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi marks this as the start of purely nominal nobility."

sentences.zh: 十一月，魯自巴中將其餘衆降。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Lu from Bazhong led his remaining host to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In November Zhang Lu surrendered from Ba with his remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 封魯及五子皆爲列侯。

translations.literal: Lu and five sons were all enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu and his five sons all received full marquisates.

sentences.zh: 劉備襲劉璋，取益州，遂據巴中；

translations.literal: Liu Bei raided Liu Zhang, took Yizhou, then occupied Bazhong;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei seized Yizhou from Liu Zhang and pushed into Ba;

sentences.zh: 遣張郃擊之。

translations.literal: he dispatched Zhang He to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Zhang He against him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，公自南鄭還，留夏侯淵屯漢中。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the duke returned from Nanzheng, left Xiahou Yuan encamped in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In December he left Nanzheng for Ye, leaving Xiahou Yuan in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 〈是行也，侍中王粲作五言詩以美其事，曰：「從軍有苦樂，但問所從誰。

translations.literal: On this march, palace attendant Wang Can made a five-character poem to praise the affair, saying: "Following the army has bitterness and joy, only ask whom you follow."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can's poem on the campaign begins, "War brings joy and woeit depends whom you serve."

sentences.zh: 所從神且武，安得久勞師？

translations.literal: Whom you follow is divine and martial; how can the army long labor?"
translations.idiomatic: "Follow a divine commander and the march feels short."

sentences.zh: 相公征關右，赫怒振天威，一舉滅獯虜，再舉服羌夷，西牧邊地賊，忽若俯拾遺。

translations.literal: The minister duke campaigns west of the pass; fierce anger shakes Heaven's might; one stroke extinguishes the savage Hu; second stroke submits Qiang and Yi; west he herds borderland bandits, sudden as stooping to pick lost things."
translations.idiomatic: It praises the western campaign smashing Hu and Qiang like picking up pebbles.

sentences.zh: 陳賞越山嶽，酒肉踰川坻，軍中多饒飫，人馬皆溢肥，徒行兼乘還，空出有餘資。

translations.literal: Spread rewards cross mountain ranges; wine and meat overflow river islets; in the army much surfeit; men and horses all overflow fat; foot marchers also ride back; going out empty they have surplus goods.
translations.idiomatic: It boasts rich feasts, fat horses, and soldiers returning laden with booty.

sentences.zh: 拓土三千里，往反速如飛，歌舞入鄴城，所願獲無違。」〉

translations.literal: Expanded territory three thousand li; round trip swift as flying; song and dance enter Ye city; what was wished was obtained without opposition."
translations.idiomatic: It ends with a triumphal entry into Ye after three thousand li gained."

sentences.zh: 二十一年春二月，公還鄴。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year spring second month, the duke returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, 216 CE, he was back in Ye.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：辛未，有司以太牢告至，策勳于廟，甲午始春祠，令曰：「議者以爲祠廟上殿當解履。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: on xinwei the officials with grand sacrifice announced arrival, recorded merit in the temple; on jiawu he began spring temple sacrifice; he issued an order saying: "Debaters think that in ancestral temple ascending the hall one ought to remove shoes."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Shu records his spring sacrifice order rejecting the rule that one must remove shoes in the temple,

sentences.zh: 吾受錫命，帶劔不解履上殿。

translations.literal: I received the tin mandate, gird sword and do not remove shoes ascending the hall."
translations.idiomatic: because his nine-tins privilege allowed sword and shoes in the Han hall,

sentences.zh: 今有事于廟而解履，是尊先公而替王命，敬父祖而簡君主，故吾不敢解履上殿也。

translations.literal: Now having affairs in the temple yet removing shoes is honoring former dukes while diminishing royal mandate, revering father and grandfather while slighting the ruler; therefore I dare not remove shoes ascending the hall."
translations.idiomatic: so removing shoes only for ancestors would slight the emperor's grant.

sentences.zh: 又臨祭就洗，以手擬水而不盥。

translations.literal: Again at the sacrifice approaching the wash, with hand he touches water but does not wash.
translations.idiomatic: He also refused the empty hand-wetting ritual at the lavabo,

sentences.zh: 夫盥以絜爲敬，未聞擬向不盥之禮，且『祭神如神在』，故吾親受水而盥也。

translations.literal: Washing takes purity as reverence; I have not heard of the rite of touching toward but not washing; moreover "sacrificing to the spirits as if the spirits were present"; therefore I personally receive water and wash."
translations.idiomatic: insisting on a real ablution because the spirits are present.

sentences.zh: 又降神禮訖，下階就幕而立，須奏樂畢竟，似若不愆，烈祖遲祭，不速訖也。

translations.literal: Again after the descending-the-spirit rite finished, descending the steps he stood under the canopy and waited until the music entirely finished, as if not hasty; blazing ancestors' delayed sacrifice does not hurry to finish.
translations.idiomatic: He waited under the canopy until the music ended rather than rushing the spirits away,

sentences.zh: 故吾坐俟樂闋送神乃起也。

translations.literal: Therefore I sit waiting for the music to end and the spirit to be sent off then rise."
translations.idiomatic: so he sat through the final cadence before rising.

sentences.zh: 受胙納神以授侍中，此爲敬恭不終實也，古者親執祭事，故吾親納于神，終抱而歸也。

translations.literal: Receiving the sacrificial flesh, accepting the spirit, thereby handing to palace attendant, this is respect not carried to the end in substance; in antiquity one personally held the sacrifice; therefore I personally hand in to the spirit, at the end embrace and return."
translations.idiomatic: He personally carried the offering to the spirit instead of delegating to attendants.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰『雖違衆，吾從下』，誠哉斯言也。」〉

translations.literal: Zhongni said "though against the multitude, I follow the lower"; truly this saying is apt."
translations.idiomatic: He quotes Confucius on following the lower ritual path when the crowd is wrong."

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅，公親耕籍田。

translations.literal: Third month renyin, the duke personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the third month he plowed the sacred field again.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：有司奏：「四時講武於農隙。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: the officials memorialized: "In the four seasons drill troops in the farming gaps."
translations.idiomatic: Officials cited classical seasonal drills in agricultural off-seasons,

sentences.zh: 漢承秦制，三時不講，唯十月都試車馬，幸長水南門，會五營士爲八陣進退，名曰乘之。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin's system, the three seasons did not drill; only in the tenth month capital review of chariots and horses, favoring Changshui south gate, assembling five-camp soldiers for eight formations advance and retreat, named riding them."
translations.idiomatic: while Han had dropped to a single October review at Changshui with five camps in eight formations,

sentences.zh: 今金革未偃，士民素習，自今已後，可無四時講武，但以立秋擇吉日大朝車騎，號曰治兵，上合禮名，下承漢制。

translations.literal: Now metal and leather have not been laid aside; officers and people are habituated; from now afterward, there need be no four-seasons drill troops, but only on Start of Autumn select an auspicious day for a great assembly of chariots and cavalry, named ordering troops, above matching ritual names, below inheriting Han system."
translations.idiomatic: They proposed scrapping quarterly drills in wartime and holding one grand review each Start of Autumn, called "ordering troops," to match classical language and Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 」奏可。〉

translations.literal: The memorial was approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the memorial."

sentences.zh: 夏五月，天子進公爵爲魏王。

translations.literal: Summer fifth month, the Son of Heaven advanced the duke's rank to King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer the emperor raised him to king of Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《獻帝傳》載詔曰：「自古帝王，雖號稱相變，爵等不同，至乎襃崇元勳，建立功德，光啟氏姓，延于子孫，庶姓之與親，豈有殊焉。

translations.literal: The Xian di zhuan records the edict saying: "From antiquity emperors, though titles and phases changed, ranks were not the same; down to praising and honoring the first achievement, establishing merit and virtue, brightening the clan surname, extending to sons and grandsons, commoner surname and kin, how could there be difference."
translations.idiomatic: The Xian di zhuan preserves the king-making edict opening with the universality of rewarding merit for kin and stranger alike,

sentences.zh: 昔我聖祖受命，刱業肇基，造我區夏，鑒古今之制，通爵等之差，盡封山川以立藩屏，使異姓親戚，並列土地，據國而王，所以保乂天命，安固萬嗣。

translations.literal: Formerly Our sage ancestor received the mandate, founded enterprise and began the base, made Our central Xia, mirrored ancient and modern's systems, penetrated rank grades' differences, fully enfeoffed mountains and rivers to establish screens and fences, causing different-surname kin together to array land, occupy states and be kings, thereby to protect the received mandate and secure the myriad heirs."
translations.idiomatic: praising Han founders for enfeoffing all worthy lines to guard the mandate,

sentences.zh: 歷世承平，臣主無事。

translations.literal: Generation after generation inherited peace; lord and minister had no affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and long eras of peace between ruler and ministers,

sentences.zh: 世祖中興而時有難易，是以曠年數百，無異姓諸侯王之位。

translations.literal: Shizu restored the middle but the times had difficulty and ease; therefore empty years several hundred, without different-surname feudal king positions."
translations.idiomatic: until Guangwu's restoration left centuries without non-Liu kings until your rise."

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，繼序弘業，遭率土分崩，羣兇縱毒，自西徂東，辛苦卑約。

translations.literal: We, lacking virtue, continued the sequence and enlarged the enterprise, encountered the realm splitting apart, the host of villains unleashing poison, from west to east, toiling in hardship and lowly constraint.
translations.idiomatic: The edict continues: the emperor claims unworthiness while chaos ran from west to east.

sentences.zh: 當此之際，唯恐溺入于難，以羞先帝之聖德。

translations.literal: At this juncture We only feared drowning into hardship, thereby shaming the former emperors' sage virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He feared disgracing the Han ancestors.

sentences.zh: 賴皇天之靈，俾君秉義奮身，震迅神武，捍朕于艱難，獲保宗廟，華夏遺民，含氣之倫，莫不蒙焉。

translations.literal: Relying on August Heaven's spirit, We made you grasp righteousness and rouse body, shake and speed divine martial prowess, shield Us in hardship and peril, obtained to preserve the ancestral temple; Hua Xia's surviving people, all who breathe, none did not receive grace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent Cao Cao to save the altars and every living Han subject.

sentences.zh: 君勤過稷、禹，忠侔伊、周，而掩之以謙讓，守之以彌恭，是以往者初開魏國，錫君土宇，懼君之違命，慮君之固辭，故且懷志屈意，封君爲上公，欲以欽順高義，須俟勳績。

translations.literal: You toiled past Ji and Yu, loyalty matched Yi and Zhou, yet covered it with modest yielding, guarded it with ever greater reverence; therefore formerly when first opening the Wei state, We granted you land and territory; fearing you would disobey the command, worrying you would firmly decline, therefore for the time We cherished intent and bent will, enfeoffed you as supreme duke, wishing thereby to honor and follow high righteousness, awaiting your accumulated merit.
translations.idiomatic: Your labors exceed ancient worthies yet you stayed humble, so the court first made you duke of Wei only, waiting to reward true merit.

sentences.zh: 韓遂、宋建，南結巴、蜀，羣逆合從，圖危社稷，君復命將，龍驤虎奮，梟其元首，屠其窟栖。

translations.literal: Han Sui, Song Jian, south linked Ba and Shu, the host of rebels joined in vertical alliance, plotting danger to the altars of soil and grain; you again ordered generals, dragon-soaring tiger-leaping, displayed their chiefs' heads, slaughtered their den nests.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Sui and Song Jian allied with Shu you sent generals who took their heads.

sentences.zh: 曁至西征，陽平之役，親擐甲冑，深入險阻，芟夷蝥賊，殄其兇醜，盪定西陲，懸旌萬里，聲教遠振，寧我區宇。

translations.literal: Down to the western expedition, the Yangping campaign, personally donning armor and helmet, deeply entering peril and obstruction, mowing mantis bandits, wiping out their fierce ugliness, sweeping and settling the western frontier, hanging banners ten thousand li, sound and instruction far quivering, quieting Our region and domain.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangping you wore armor yourself and cleared the west to the horizon.

sentences.zh: 蓋唐、虞之盛，三后樹功，文、武之興，旦、奭作輔，二祖成業，英豪佐命；

translations.literal: Covering Tang and Yu's flourishing, the three queens established merit; Wen and Wu's rise, Dan and Shi were assistants; the two ancestors completed enterprise, heroes aided the mandate;
translations.idiomatic: He compares the achievement to Tang, Yu, Wen, Wu, and their ministers.

sentences.zh: 夫以聖哲之君，事爲己任，猶錫士班瑞以報功臣，豈有如朕寡德，仗君以濟，而賞典不豐，將何以荅神祇慰萬方哉？

translations.literal: As for sage and wise lords, taking affairs as their own task, still granted soil and distributed jade to repay meritorious subjects; how can it be like Us, scant in virtue, leaning on you to save us, yet the reward canon is not rich; how shall We answer the spirits and console the myriad regions?
translations.idiomatic: Even sage kings rewarded helpers richly; how can a weak emperor repay you so poorly?

sentences.zh: 今進君爵爲魏王，使使持節行御史大夫、宗正劉艾奉策璽玄土之社，苴以白茅，金虎符第一至第五，竹使符第一至十。

translations.literal: Now We advance your rank to King of Wei, dispatch credential-bearer acting imperial counselor and director of the imperial clan Liu Ai to bear the document, seal, black-soil altar, wrapped in white reeds, gold tiger tallies first to fifth, bamboo mission tallies first to ten.
translations.idiomatic: He advances Cao Cao to king of Wei with Liu Ai bearing seals, soil bundle, and tallies one through five and one through ten.

sentences.zh: 君其正王位，以丞相領冀州牧如故。

translations.literal: You shall rectify the kingly rank, as chancellor also leading Ji shepherd as before.
translations.idiomatic: Assume kingship while remaining chancellor and inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 其上魏公璽綬符冊。

translations.literal: Present upward the Wei duke's seal, ribbon, tallies, and document.
translations.idiomatic: Return the old duke of Wei insignia.

sentences.zh: 敬服朕命，簡恤爾衆，克綏庶績，以揚我祖宗之休命。

translations.literal: Respectfully serve Our command; discipline and pity your multitudes; be able to pacify common tasks; thereby raise Our ancestors' fine command.
translations.idiomatic: Rule Wei with care for the people and the Han ancestors' honor.

sentences.zh: 」魏王上書三辭，詔三報不許。

translations.literal: The King of Wei upward memorialized declining three times; the edict three times replied not permitting.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao declined three times; the court refused three times.

sentences.zh: 又手詔曰：「大聖以功德爲高美，以忠和爲典訓，故刱業垂名，使百世可希，行道制義，使力行可效，是以勳烈無窮，休光茂著。

translations.literal: Again a handwritten edict said: "Great sages take merit and virtue as highest beauty, take loyalty and harmony as canonical instruction; therefore founding enterprise hangs a name so a hundred generations may aspire, walking the Way and fixing righteousness so exertion may be emulated; therefore meritorious blaze is inexhaustible, glorious blessing flourishes and shows."
translations.idiomatic: A personal edict praises sage kings as models of merit and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 稷、契載元首之聦明，周、邵因文、武之智用，雖經營庶官，仰歎俯思，其對豈有若君者哉？

translations.literal: Ji and Qi bore the chief's brightness; Zhou and Shao relied on Wen and Wu's wisdom and use; though they managed the hundred offices, looking up sighing looking down pondering, could their answers be like you, lord?"
translations.idiomatic: It asks whether even Ji, Qi, Zhou, and Shao matched Cao Cao's burden.

sentences.zh: 朕惟古人之功，美之如彼，思君忠勤之績，茂之如此，是以每將鏤符析瑞，陳禮命冊，寤寐慨然，自忘守文之不德焉。

translations.literal: We ponder ancient men's achievements, praising them so; pondering your loyal and diligent traces, flourishing them so; therefore each time about to carve tally and split auspicious jade, array ritual and command document, waking and sleeping We sigh, forgetting Ourselves that guarding the pattern lacks virtue."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor says he loses sleep over how to honor such service.

sentences.zh: 今君重違朕命，固辭懇切，非所以稱朕心，而訓後世也。

translations.literal: Now you heavily disobey Our command, firmly decline with earnest cutting; this is not the means to declare Our heart and instruct later generations."
translations.idiomatic: Further refusal would frustrate the court and mislead posterity.

sentences.zh: 其抑志撙節，勿復固辭。

translations.literal: Suppress intent and restrain integrity; do not again firmly decline."
translations.idiomatic: Accept the crown and stop refusing."

sentences.zh: 」《四體書勢序》曰：梁鵠以公爲北部尉。

translations.literal: The preface to the Four Styles of Calligraphy says: Liang Hu made the duke northern district captain.
translations.idiomatic: The calligraphy preface notes Liang Hu once made Cao Cao northern district captain.

sentences.zh: 《曹瞞傳》曰：爲尚書右丞司馬建公所舉。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: he was recommended by right aide of the secretariat Sima Jian-gong.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says Sima Fang recommended him.

sentences.zh: 及公爲王，召建公到鄴，與歡飲，謂建公曰：「孤今日可復作尉否？

translations.literal: When the duke became king, he summoned Jian-gong to Ye, drank merrily with him, said to Jian-gong: "Can I today again be a captain?"
translations.idiomatic: As king he feasted Sima Fang in Ye and joked whether he could be a captain again.

sentences.zh: 」建公曰：「昔舉大王時，適可作尉耳。

translations.literal: Jian-gong said: "Formerly when I recommended the great king, you were fit only to be a captain."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fang answered that when he recommended Cao Cao, a captain was all he deserved.

sentences.zh: 」王大笑。

translations.literal: The king laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 建公名防，司馬宣王之父。

translations.literal: Jian-gong's name was Fang; he was Sima Yi's father.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fang was the father of Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案《司馬彪序傳》，建公不爲右丞，疑此不然，而王隱《晉書》云趙王篡位，欲尊祖爲帝，博士馬平議稱京兆府君昔舉魏武帝爲北部尉，賊不犯界，如此則爲有徵。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates Sima Biao's preface to tradition: Jian-gong was not right aide; I suspect this is not so, yet Wang Yin's Jin shu says when the prince of Zhao usurped, doctors debated honoring his grandfather as emperor; doctor Ma Ping cited the capital governor who once recommended Wei Wudi as northern district captain, saying bandits did not violate his districtthus there is some confirmation."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi doubts Sima Fang was right aide but cites a Jin source linking the recommendation to Cao Cao's early police post.

sentences.zh: 代郡烏丸行單于普富盧與其侯王來朝。

translations.literal: Acting Shanyu Pulu of Dai commandery Wuhuan with his marquises and kings came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuan acting shanyu Pulu of Dai brought his chiefs to audience.

sentences.zh: 天子命王女爲公主，食湯沐邑。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the king's daughter to be princess, eating tang-mu fief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Cao Cao's daughter a princess with bath-town revenue.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，匈奴南單于呼廚泉將其名王來朝，待以客禮，遂留魏，使右賢王去卑監其國。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, the Xiongnu southern Shanyu Huchuquan led his famous kings to come to court; he was treated with guest ritual, then was detained in Wei, making right Shanyu Qubei supervise his state.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xiongnu shanyu Huchuquan came to court, was honored as a guest, then kept in Wei while Qubei ruled the steppe for him.

sentences.zh: 八月，以大理鍾繇爲相國。

translations.literal: Eighth month, made grand judge Zhong Yao prime minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhong Yao became prime minister.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：始置奉常宗正官。〉

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: first established minister of ceremonies and director of the imperial clan offices."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei records new minister of ceremonies and imperial clan posts."

sentences.zh: 冬十月，治兵，

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, ordering troops,
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he held the troop review,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：王親執金鼔以令進退。〉

translations.literal: the Wei Shu says: the king personally grasped the metal drum to command advance and retreat."
translations.idiomatic: beating the signal drum himself."

sentences.zh: 遂征孫權，十一月至譙。

translations.literal: Thereupon campaigned against Sun Quan; eleventh month reached Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Then he marched on Wu and reached Qiao in November.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春正月，王軍居巢，二月，進軍屯江西郝谿。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year spring first month, the king's army was at Juchao; second month, advanced the army and encamped at Haoxi west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 217 his host camped at Juchao, then moved to Haoxi west of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 權在濡須口築城拒守，遂逼攻之，權退走。

translations.literal: Quan at Ruxu mouth built a city to resist and guard; thereupon pressed and attacked him; Quan retreated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan walled Ruxu until Cao Cao pressed him and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，王引軍還，留夏侯惇、曹仁、張遼等屯居巢。

translations.literal: Third month, the king led the army back, left Xiahou Dun, Cao Ren, Zhang Liao, and others encamped at Juchao.
translations.idiomatic: In March he withdrew, leaving Xiahou Dun, Cao Ren, and Zhang Liao at Juchao.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，天子命王設天子旌旗，出入稱警蹕。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, the Son of Heaven ordered the king to set up Son of Heaven plumed banners, entering and exiting called clearing the way.
translations.idiomatic: In April the emperor granted imperial banners and cleared-road ceremony.

sentences.zh: 五月，作泮宮。

translations.literal: Fifth month, made the Pan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In May he built the Pan Palace at Ye.

sentences.zh: 六月，以軍師華歆爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: Sixth month, made military counsellor Hua Xin imperial counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In June Hua Xin became imperial counselor.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：初置衞尉官。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu says: first established minister of the guards office."
translations.idiomatic: First minister of the guards was appointed."

sentences.zh: 秋八月，令曰：「昔伊摯、傅說出於賤人，管仲，桓公賊也，皆用之以興。

translations.literal: Autumn eighth month, he issued an order: "Formerly Yi Zhi and Fu Yue came from mean men; Guan Zhong was Duke Huan's enemy; all were used thereby to rise."
translations.idiomatic: His famous talent edict cites Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and Guan Zhong risen from low or hostile origins.

sentences.zh: 蕭何、曹參，縣吏也，韓信、陳平負汙辱之名，有見笑之恥，卒能成就王業，聲著千載。

translations.literal: Xiao He and Cao Shen were county clerks; Han Xin and Chen Ping bore names of filth and insult, had shame of being laughed at; in the end they were able to complete the kingly enterprise, sound renowned a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He, Cao Shen, Han Xin, and Chen Ping had humble or scandalous pasts yet built the Han.

sentences.zh: 吳起貪將，殺妻自信，散金求官，母死不歸，然在魏，奏人不敢東向，在楚則三晉不敢南謀。

translations.literal: Wu Qi was a grasping general, killed his wife to prove trust, scattered gold seeking office, mother died yet did not return; yet in Wei Qin people did not dare face east; in Chu then the three Jin did not dare plot southward."
translations.idiomatic: Even ruthless Wu Qi froze Qin and Jin when he served Wei and Chu.

sentences.zh: 今天下得無有至德之人放在民間，及果勇不顧，臨敵力戰；

translations.literal: Now in the realm can there be none of utmost virtue hidden among the people, and of fruit-like courage not looking back, facing the enemy fighting with strength;
translations.idiomatic: There may be hidden sages and fearless warriors;

sentences.zh: 若文俗之吏，高才異質，或堪爲將守；

translations.literal: if pattern-minded clerks, high talent and unusual substance, perhaps can serve as generals or guardians;
translations.idiomatic: civil officials of unusual ability fit for command;

sentences.zh: 負汙辱之名，見笑之行，或不仁不孝而有治國用兵之術：其各舉所知，勿有所遺。」〉

translations.literal: bearing names of filth and insult, conduct that invites laughter, or lacking humaneness and filial piety yet having the arts of ordering a state and using troops: each recommend what you know, do not leave anything out."
translations.idiomatic: recommend scoundrels with statecraft anyway."

sentences.zh: 冬十月，天子命王冕十有二旒，乘金根車，駕六馬，設五時副車，以五官中郎將丕爲魏太子。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the Son of Heaven ordered the king's crown twelve tassels, to ride the metal-root chariot, six horses harnessed, to set up five-seasons attendant chariots, to make general of the household for the five offices Pi Wei heir of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In October the emperor gave twelve-tassel crown, six-horse imperial chariot, five-seasons escort, and named Cao Pi heir.
