sentences.zh: 劉備遣張飛、馬超、吳蘭等屯下辯；

translations.literal: Liu Bei dispatched Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, Wu Lan, and others to encamp at Xiabian;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei posted Zhang Fei, Ma Chao, and Wu Lan at Xiabian;

sentences.zh: 遣曹洪拒之。

translations.literal: he dispatched Cao Hong to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Cao Hong to hold them.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春正月，漢太醫令吉本與少府耿紀、司直韋晃等反，攻許，燒丞相長史王必營，

translations.literal: Twenty-third year spring first month, Han grand physician director Ji Ben with minister of the lesser treasury Geng Ji, upright clerk Wei Huang, and others rebelled, attacked Xu, burned chief clerk Wang Bi's camp,
translations.idiomatic: In spring 218 Ji Ben, Geng Ji, and Wei Huang rose in Xu, torched Wang Bi's yamen,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏武故事》載令曰：「領長史王必，是吾披荊棘時吏也。

translations.literal: The Wei Wu gushi records an order saying: "Chief clerk Wang Bi was a clerk when I cut through brambles."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's order praises Wang Bi as an old comrade from the first campaigns.

sentences.zh: 忠能勤事，心如鐵石，國之良吏也。

translations.literal: Loyal and able, diligent in affairs, heart like iron and stone, the state's fine clerk."
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, tireless, iron-willed—a model clerk."

sentences.zh: 蹉跌久未辟之，捨騏驥而弗乘，焉遑遑而更求哉？

translations.literal: Stumbling long I did not summon him; abandoning a swift steed yet not riding, how anxiously yet further seek?"
translations.idiomatic: He regrets having delayed promoting him.

sentences.zh: 故教辟之，已署所宜，便以領長史統事如故。」〉

translations.literal: Therefore I instructed to summon him; already signed what was fitting; then let him as chief clerk direct affairs as before."
translations.idiomatic: He had just appointed Wang Bi chief clerk of Xu."

sentences.zh: 必與潁川典農中郎將嚴匡討斬之。

translations.literal: Bi with Yingchuan agrarian colonel general Yan Kuang campaigned and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi and Yan Kuang crushed the coup and executed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 〈《三輔決錄注》曰：時有京兆金禕字德禕，自以世爲漢臣，自日磾討莽何羅，忠誠顯著，名節累葉。

translations.literal: The Sanfu jue lu commentary says: at the time there was Jingzhao Jin Yi, style Deyi, who thought his family for generations Han ministers, from Jin Midi's campaign against Wang He Luo, loyalty manifest, name and integrity piled generations.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary names Jin Yi of Jingzhao, who boasted a Han-loyalist pedigree from Jin Midi.

sentences.zh: 覩漢祚將移，謂可季興，乃喟然發憤，遂與耿紀、韋晃、吉本、本子邈、邈弟穆等結謀。

translations.literal: Seeing Han's mandate about to shift, said one could assist the revival; therefore sighed and roused anger, then with Geng Ji, Wei Huang, Ji Ben, Ben's son Ji Miao, Miao's younger brother Ji Mu, and others knotted a plot.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Han failing, he plotted with Geng Ji, Wei Huang, the Ji family, and others.

sentences.zh: 紀字季行，少有美名，爲丞相掾，王甚敬異之，遷侍中，守少府。

translations.literal: Ji's style name was Jixing; in youth he had a fair name, was chancellor's aide; the king greatly respected and treated him as unusual, promoted palace attendant, guarding minister of the lesser treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Ji (courtesy Jixing) had been a trusted chancellor aide promoted to palace attendant and minister of the lesser treasury.

sentences.zh: 邈字文然，穆字思然，以禕慷慨有日磾之風，又與王必善，因以閒之，若殺必，欲挾天子以攻魏，南援劉備。

translations.literal: Miao's style name was Wenran; Mu's style name was Siran; because Yi was generous with Midi's style, and also was on good terms with Wang Bi, thereby used the interval between them; if they killed Bi, they wished to seize the Son of Heaven to attack Wei, south aiding Liu Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Miao and Ji Mu worked through Jin Yi, who was close to Wang Bi, hoping to kill Wang Bi, seize the emperor, and join Liu Bei.

sentences.zh: 時關羽彊盛，而王在鄴，留必典兵督許中事。

translations.literal: At the time Guan Yu was strong flourishing while the king was at Ye, leaving Bi to model troops and supervise Xu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: With Guan Yu ascendant and Cao Cao in Ye, Wang Bi held Xu.

sentences.zh: 文然等率雜人及家僮千餘人夜燒門攻必，禕遣人爲內應，射必中肩。

translations.literal: Wenran and others led miscellaneous people and household retainers more than a thousand men by night burning the gate attacking Bi; Yi sent men as inner response, shot Bi in the shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the gate at night, Jin Yi's men inside shot Wang Bi in the shoulder.

sentences.zh: 必不知攻者爲誰，以素與禕善，走投禕，夜喚德禕，禕家不知是必，謂爲文然等，錯應曰：「王長史已死乎？

translations.literal: Bi did not know who the attackers were; because ordinarily on good terms with Yi, fled to throw himself on Yi, by night called Deyi; Yi's household did not know it was Bi, thought it was Wenran and others, wrongly answered saying: "Has Chief Clerk Wang already died?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi fled to Jin Yi's house; Jin Yi's people mistook him for a conspirator and shouted that the chief clerk must be dead,

sentences.zh: 卿曹事立矣！

translations.literal: Your band's affair is established!"
translations.idiomatic: so your plot has succeeded!"

sentences.zh: 」必乃更他路奔。

translations.literal: Bi then changed to another road and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing the trap, Wang Bi ran another way.

sentences.zh: 一曰：必欲投禕，其帳下督謂必曰：「今日事竟知誰門而投入乎？

translations.literal: One version says: Bi wished to throw himself on Yi; his tent adjutant said to Bi: "Tonight's affair finished, do you know whose gate to throw yourself into?"
translations.idiomatic: Another version says his adjutant warned him not to trust Jin Yi.

sentences.zh: 」扶必奔南城。

translations.literal: He supported Bi to flee to the south city.
translations.idiomatic: The adjutant helped him reach the south city.

sentences.zh: 會天明，必猶在，文然等衆散，故敗。

translations.literal: It happened that dawn brightened; Bi still lived; Wenran and others' host scattered; therefore they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Wang Bi still lived and the rebels melted away.

sentences.zh: 後十餘日，必竟以創死。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, Bi in the end because of wounds died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bi died of his wounds days later.

sentences.zh: 《獻帝春秋》曰：收紀、晃等，將斬之，紀呼魏王名曰：「恨吾不自生意，竟爲羣兒所誤耳！

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian says: arresting Ji, Huang, and others, about to behead them, Ji called the King of Wei's name saying: "I hate that I did not take my own counsel, in the end was misled by a pack of boys!"
translations.idiomatic: At execution Geng Ji cursed Cao Cao by title for trusting fools.

sentences.zh: 」晃頓首搏頰，以至於死。

translations.literal: Huang kowtowed and beat cheeks, until death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Huang wept and beat his face until the blade fell.

sentences.zh: 《山陽公載記》曰：王聞王必死，盛怒，召漢百官詣鄴，令救火者左，不救火者右。

translations.literal: The Shan gong zai ji says: the king heard Wang Bi died, greatly angry, summoned Han hundred officials to Ye, ordered those who fought the fire stand left, those who did not fight the fire stand right.
translations.idiomatic: Furious at Wang Bi's death, Cao Cao summoned Luoyang officials to Ye and ordered fire-fighters left, non-fighters right.

sentences.zh: 衆人以爲救火者必無罪，皆附左；

translations.literal: The host thought those who fought the fire surely were without guilt, all attached to the left;
translations.idiomatic: Everyone crowded left thinking fire-fighters were safe,

sentences.zh: 王以爲「不救火者非助亂，救火乃實賊也」。

translations.literal: the king thought "those who did not fight fire were not aiding rebellion; fighting fire was truly the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: but Cao Cao called the fire-fighters the real rebels and the idle bystanders innocent,

sentences.zh: 皆殺之。〉

translations.literal: all killed them."
translations.idiomatic: and executed everyone who had fought the blaze."

sentences.zh: 曹洪破吳蘭，斬其將任夔等。

translations.literal: Cao Hong broke Wu Lan, beheaded their general Ren Kui and others.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hong defeated Wu Lan and killed Ren Kui.

sentences.zh: 三月，張飛、馬超走漢中，陰平氐強端斬吳蘭，傳其首。

translations.literal: Third month, Zhang Fei and Ma Chao fled to Hanzhong; Yinping Di chief Qiang Duan beheaded Wu Lan and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: In March Zhang Fei and Ma Chao withdrew; Qiang Duan of Yinping Di killed Wu Lan and sent the head.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，代郡、上谷烏丸無臣氐等叛，遣鄢陵侯彰討破之。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, Wuhuan Wuchenshi and others of Dai commandery and Shanggu rebelled; dispatched Yanling marquis Zhang to campaign and break them.
translations.idiomatic: In April Wuhuan Wuchenshi rebelled in Dai and Shanggu; Cao Zhang crushed them.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載王令曰：「去冬天降疫癘，民有凋傷，軍興于外，墾田損少，吾甚憂之。

translations.literal: The Wei Shu records the king's order saying: "Last winter Heaven sent pestilence; the people had withering harm; the army rose outside; reclaimed fields were few; I greatly worry for this."
translations.idiomatic: An edict mourns plague, war, and poor harvests.

sentences.zh: 其令吏民男女：女年七十已上無夫子，若年十二已下無父母兄弟，及目無所見，手不能作，足不能行，而無妻子父兄產業者，廩食終身。

translations.literal: Let clerks and people, male and female: women age seventy and above without husband or sons, or age twelve and below without parents or brothers, and eyes unable to see, hands unable to work, feet unable to walk, yet without wives or sons or fathers or brothers or property, grant food for life.
translations.idiomatic: It orders lifelong grain for the blind, crippled, childless elderly, and orphans under twelve.

sentences.zh: 幼者至十二止，貧窮不能自贍者，隨口給貸。

translations.literal: Young ones stop at twelve; poor unable to support themselves, follow mouth and grant loans.
translations.idiomatic: Aid for minors ends at twelve; other poor get ration loans.

sentences.zh: 老耄須待養者，年九十已上，復不事，家一人。」〉

translations.literal: Old and aged needing support, age ninety and above, again not serving corvée, one person per household."
translations.idiomatic: Households with dependents over ninety get one corvée exemption."

sentences.zh: 六月，令曰：「古之葬者，必居瘠薄之地。

translations.literal: Sixth month, he issued an order: "Burials of antiquity must occupy lean and thin lands."
translations.idiomatic: In June he ordered his tomb on poor soil per ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 其規西門豹祠西原上爲壽陵，因高爲基，不封不樹。

translations.literal: He marked west of Lord Ximen Bao's shrine on the western plateau for Shouling, relying on height for the base, no mound no trees.
translations.idiomatic: He chose the plateau west of Ximen Bao's shrine for a low unmarked tumulus.

sentences.zh: 周禮冢人掌公墓之地，凡諸侯居左右以前，卿大夫居後，漢制亦謂之陪陵。

translations.literal: The Zhou li tomb man controls the land of the ducal cemetery; all feudal lords dwell left and right in front, grandees dwell behind; Han system also calls it accompanying tomb.
translations.idiomatic: He cites Zhou and Han rules on clustering tombs around the royal mound.

sentences.zh: 其公卿大臣列將有功者，宜陪壽陵，其廣爲兆域，使足相容。」

translations.literal: Those dukes, ministers, great ministers, and ranked generals with merit should accompany Shouling; broadly make grave space enough to contain each other."
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious officers may be buried beside him in ample ground."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，治兵，遂西征劉備，九月，至長安。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, ordering troops, thereupon west campaigned against Liu Bei; ninth month, reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In July he reviewed troops and marched to Chang'an in September.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，宛守將侯音等反，執南陽太守，劫略吏民，保宛。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, Wan defending general Hou Yin and others rebelled, seized Nanyang grand administrator, plundered clerks and people, guarded Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In October Hou Yin seized Wan, took the governor hostage, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 初，曹仁討關羽，屯樊城，是月使仁圍宛。

translations.literal: At first, Cao Ren campaigned against Guan Yu, encamped at Fancheng; this month he made Ren besiege Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren had been facing Guan Yu at Fan; he was now ordered to invest Wan.

sentences.zh: 二十四年春正月，仁屠宛，斬音。

translations.literal: Twenty-fourth year spring first month, Ren slaughtered Wan, beheaded Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 219 Cao Ren took Wan and executed Hou Yin.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：是時南陽間苦繇役，音於是執太守東里襃，與吏民共反，與關羽連和。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: at that time Nanyang bitterly suffered corvée labor; Yin therefore seized grand administrator Dongli Bao, together with clerks and people jointly rebelled, joining with Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan blames harsh corvée for Hou Yin's revolt with Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 南陽功曹宗子卿往說音曰：「足下順民心，舉大事，遠近莫不望風；

translations.literal: Nanyang merit officer Zong Ziqing went to persuade Yin saying: "You follow the people's heart, raise a great affair; far and near none do not look to the wind;
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ziqing urged Hou Yin that seizing the governor hurt the cause,

sentences.zh: 然執郡將，逆而無益，何不遣之。

translations.literal: yet seizing the commandery general, is contrary and without benefit; why not release him."
translations.idiomatic: and he should free the governor.

sentences.zh: 吾與子共戮力，比曹公軍來，關羽兵亦至矣。

translations.literal: I with you together will exert strength; by the time Lord Cao's army arrives, Guan Yu's troops also will have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Together they could hold until Cao Cao and Guan Yu arrived.

sentences.zh: 」音從之，即釋遣太守。

translations.literal: Yin followed it, immediately released and sent off the grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yin freed the governor.

sentences.zh: 子卿因夜踰城亡出，遂與太守收餘民圍音，會曹仁軍至，共滅之。〉

translations.literal: Ziqing then by night climbed over the wall and fled out, then with the grand administrator gathered remaining people besieging Yin; it happened that Cao Ren's army arrived, together extinguished them."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ziqing escaped, rallied loyalists, and joined Cao Ren to end the siege."

sentences.zh: 夏侯淵與劉備戰於陽平，爲備所殺。

translations.literal: Xiahou Yuan battled Liu Bei at Yangping, was killed by Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Yuan fell to Liu Bei at Yangping.

sentences.zh: 三月，王自長安出斜谷，軍遮要以臨漢中，遂至陽平。

translations.literal: Third month, the king from Chang'an exited Xie Valley, army blocking key points to press Hanzhong, then reached Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: In March Cao Cao took Xie Valley toward Hanzhong and Yangping.

sentences.zh: 備因險拒守。

translations.literal: Yi relied on peril to resist and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei held the defiles.

sentences.zh: 〈《九州春秋》曰：時王欲還，出令曰「雞肋」，官屬不知所謂。

translations.literal: The Jiuzhou chunqiu says: at the time the king wished to return, issued an order saying "chicken ribs"; subordinates did not know what it meant.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiuzhou chunqiu says he muttered "chicken ribs" when debating retreat;

sentences.zh: 主簿楊脩便自嚴裝，人驚問脩：「何以知之？

translations.literal: Chief clerk Yang Xiu then by himself tightened baggage; people startled asked Xiu: "How did you know?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu packed to leave, astonishing the staff.

sentences.zh: 」脩曰：「夫雞肋，棄之如可惜，食之無所得，以比漢中，知王欲還也。」〉

translations.literal: Xiu said: "As for chicken ribs, to cast them away seems a pity; eating them obtains nothing; comparing this to Hanzhong, I know the king wishes to return."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiu said, "Chicken ribs: throwing them away feels wasteful, yet eating them yields nothing. Hanzhong is the same; the king intends to pull back."

sentences.zh: 夏五月，引軍還長安。

translations.literal: Summer fifth month, led the army back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer he withdrew to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，以夫人卞氏爲王后。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, made Lady Bian the queen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Lady Bian became queen.

sentences.zh: 遣于禁助曹仁擊關羽。

translations.literal: He dispatched Yu Jin to assist Cao Ren in striking Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yu Jin to reinforce Cao Ren against Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 八月，漢水溢，灌禁軍，軍沒，羽獲禁，遂圍仁。

translations.literal: Eighth month, the Han River overflowed, flooded Jin's army, the army drowned; Yu captured Jin, thereupon besieged Ren.
translations.idiomatic: In August the Han River rose, drowned Yu Jin's corps, Guan Yu captured Yu Jin, and tightened the siege of Cao Ren.

sentences.zh: 使徐晃救之。

translations.literal: He made Xu Huang rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xu Huang to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 九月，相國鍾繇坐西曹掾魏諷反免。

translations.literal: Ninth month, prime minister Zhong Yao was stripped of office because western bureau clerk Wei Feng rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In September Zhong Yao lost his post as prime minister when his western-bureau clerk Wei Feng plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：諷字子京，沛人，有惑衆才，傾動鄴都，鍾繇由是辟焉。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Feng's style name was Zijing; he was a man of Pei; he had talent to delude the multitude, swaying Ye capital; Zhong Yao therefore summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu describes Wei Feng (Zijing) of Pei as a charismatic schemer whom Zhong Yao had employed.

sentences.zh: 大軍未反，諷潛結徒黨，又與長樂衞尉陳禕謀襲鄴。

translations.literal: The great army had not returned; Feng secretly knotted a faction, again with Changle guard captain Chen Wei plotted to raid Ye.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army was away Wei Feng conspired with Chen Wei to seize Ye.

sentences.zh: 未及期，禕懼，告之太子，誅諷，坐死者數十人。

translations.literal: Before the date arrived, Wei was afraid, reported it to the heir apparent, executed Feng; those who sat death were several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wei panicked, informed the crown prince, and Wei Feng was executed along with dozens of accomplices.

sentences.zh: 王昶家誡曰「濟陰魏諷」，而此云沛人，未詳。〉

translations.literal: Wang Chang's Family Admonition calls him "Wei Feng of Jiyin," yet here he is said to be from Pei; it is not clear which is right.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chang's text places Wei Feng in Jiyin; this passage calls him a man of Pei, and the discrepancy is unresolved.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，軍還洛陽。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, the army returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the army reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：王更脩治北部尉廨，令過於舊。〉

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: the king again renovated the northern-district captain's compound and ordered it to outdo its former state.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan says he rebuilt the compound of his old northern-district captaincy and made it grander than before.

sentences.zh: 孫權遣使上書，以討關羽自效。

translations.literal: Sun Quan dispatched envoys upward with a memorial, offering to attack Guan Yu to prove loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wrote offering to strike Guan Yu to show loyalty.

sentences.zh: 王自洛陽南征羽，未至，晃攻羽，破之，羽走，仁圍解。

translations.literal: The king from Luoyang south campaigned against Yu; before reaching, Xu Huang attacked Yu, broke him; Yu fled; Ren's siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao marched south for Guan Yu but Xu Huang defeated him first, lifting the siege of Fan.

sentences.zh: 王軍摩陂。

translations.literal: The king's army was at Mopo.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Mopo.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：孫權上書稱臣，稱說天命。

translations.literal: The Wei lüe says: Sun Quan upward memorial called himself subject, proclaimed and expounded Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei lüe says Sun Quan submitted as vassal and flattered the Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 王以權書示外曰：「是兒欲踞吾著爐火上邪！

translations.literal: The king showed Quan's letter outside saying: "This brat wants to seat me on the stove fire, does he!"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sneered that Sun Quan wanted to roast him with flattery about abdication.

sentences.zh: 」侍中陳羣、尚書桓階奏曰：「漢自安帝已來，政去公室，國統數絕，至於今者，唯有名號，尺土一民，皆非漢有，期運久已盡，歷數久已終，非適今日也。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Chen Qun and secretariat director Huan Jie memorialized saying: "Han from Emperor An onward, government left the ducal house, the state's line several times cut off; down to the present only the name remains; a foot of soil or one commoner is not Han's; the allotted span long finished, the numeration long ended; it is not only today."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun and Huan Jie argued that Han had been hollow for generations and the mandate was spent.

sentences.zh: 是以桓、靈之閒，諸明圖緯者，皆言『漢行氣盡，黃家當興』。

translations.literal: Therefore between Huan and Ling, those who understood charts and weft all said 'Han's line of qi is exhausted, the Yellow House ought to rise.'"
translations.idiomatic: They cited omens that the Yellow Heaven would replace Han.

sentences.zh: 殿下應期，十分天下而有其九，以服事漢，羣生注望，遐邇怨歎，是故孫權在遠稱臣，此天人之應，異氣齊聲。

translations.literal: Your Highness answered the period, nine tenths of all under Heaven are yours, yet you serve Han; the hundred kinds all fix hope; far and near resent and sigh; therefore Sun Quan from afar calls himself subject; this is Heaven and men's response, different vapors with one voice."
translations.idiomatic: They urged him to take the throne since he held nine-tenths of the realm and even Sun Quan acknowledged it.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲虞、夏不以謙辭，殷、周不吝誅放，畏天知命，無所與讓也。

translations.literal: Your servants foolishly think Yu and Xia did not use modest phrases, Yin and Zhou did not grudge execution and banishment; fearing Heaven and knowing the mandate, there is nothing to yield to."
translations.idiomatic: They compared him to dynastic founders who seized power without false modesty.

sentences.zh: 」《魏氏春秋》曰：夏侯惇謂王曰：「天下咸知漢祚已盡，異代方起。

translations.literal: The Wei shi chunqiu says: Xiahou Dun said to the king: "All under Heaven know Han's mandate is ended; a different generation is about to rise."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Annals records Xiahou Dun urging abdication.

sentences.zh: 自古已來，能除民害爲百姓所歸者，即民主也。

translations.literal: From antiquity down, whoever could remove harm for the people and be whom the hundred surnames turned to was then the people's lord."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever saves the people is their true ruler.

sentences.zh: 今殿下即戎三十餘年，功德著於黎庶，爲天下所依歸，應天順民，復何疑哉！

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has borne arms more than thirty years; merit and virtue show on the black-haired; you are what the realm relies on; answer Heaven and follow the people—what more doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: After more than thirty years at war your merit is plain to the common people; you are the pillar they lean on. Heaven and the multitude are aligned—why hesitate further?"

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「『施於有政，是亦爲政』。

translations.literal: The king said: "'Apply it in government, and that too is government.'"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao quoted the Analects on governing without the title.

sentences.zh: 若天命在吾，吾爲周文王矣。

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate is on me, I will be King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven chose him, he would be another King Wen and leave the actual takeover to his heir.

sentences.zh: 」《曹瞞傳》及《世語》並云桓階勸王正位，夏侯惇以爲宜先滅蜀，蜀亡則吳服，二方旣定，然後遵舜、禹之軌，王從之。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan and Shi Yu together say Huan Jie urged the king to rectify the position, Xiahou Dun thought one ought first to extinguish Shu; when Shu perished then Wu would submit; when both sides were settled, then follow Shun and Yu's tracks; the king followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Other sources say Huan Jie urged enthronement while Xiahou Dun wanted Shu conquered first; the king agreed with the latter.

sentences.zh: 及至王薨，惇追恨前言，發病卒。

translations.literal: By the time the king died, Dun looked back on his earlier words with remorse, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao died, Xiahou Dun brooded over what he had said before, sickened, and passed away.

sentences.zh: 孫盛評曰：夏侯惇恥爲漢官，求受魏印，桓階方惇，有義直之節；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng's appraisal: Xiahou Dun was ashamed to serve as a Han official yet asked to receive Wei seals; Huan Jie stood up to Dun and kept an upright integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng argues that Xiahou Dun was eager for Wei titles while posing as a Han servant, whereas Huan Jie confronted him and kept his integrity;

sentences.zh: 考其傳記，《世語》爲妄矣。〉

translations.literal: examining the transmitted accounts, the Shi Yu version is false.
translations.idiomatic: and when the sources are compared, the Shi Yu story does not hold up.

sentences.zh: 二十五年春正月，至洛陽。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year spring first month, reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, 220 CE, he reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 權擊斬羽，傳其首。

translations.literal: Quan struck and beheaded Yu, forwarded his head.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan killed Guan Yu and sent the head north.

sentences.zh: 庚子，王崩于洛陽，年六十六。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, the king collapsed at Luoyang, age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day he died in Luoyang at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 〈《世語》曰：太祖自漢中至洛陽，起建始殿，伐濯龍祠而樹血出。

translations.literal: The Shi Yu says: Taizu, coming from Hanzhong to Luoyang, raised Jianshi Hall; he cut a tree at the Zhuolong Shrine and sap like blood flowed out.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi Yu records an omen: while building Jianshi Hall he had a tree felled at the Zhuolong Shrine and it bled like a wound.

sentences.zh: 《曹瞞傳》曰：王使工蘇越徙美棃，掘之，根傷盡出血。

translations.literal: The Cao Man Zhuan says: the king made workman Su Yue transplant a fine pear; digging it, the roots were wounded and all bled.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man Zhuan adds a bleeding pear root when transplanting.

sentences.zh: 越白狀，王躬自視而惡之，以爲不祥，還遂寑疾。〉

translations.literal: Yue reported the condition; the king personally inspected it, detested what he saw, deemed it ill-omened, and after returning then took to his bed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yue reported it; Cao Cao went to look, hated the sign, took it as a bad omen, and soon afterward fell ill.

sentences.zh: 遺令曰：「天下尚未安定，未得遵古也。

translations.literal: His final order said: "All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed instructions forbid a lavish Han-style funeral until the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，皆除服。

translations.literal: When burial is finished, all remove mourning garb.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning should end with the burial.

sentences.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，皆不得離屯部。

translations.literal: Those who lead troops garrisoning shall none leave their encampment posts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison troops must stay at their posts.

sentences.zh: 有司各率乃職。

translations.literal: Let each office perform its duties.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should keep working.

sentences.zh: 斂以時服，無藏金玉珍寶。

translations.literal: Dress the corpse in seasonal garments; do not bury gold or jade or precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Let the shroud be everyday clothes; do not inter gold, jade, or costly grave goods.

sentences.zh: 」謚曰武王。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title King Wu.

sentences.zh: 二月丁卯，葬高陵。

translations.literal: Second month dingmao, buried at Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the second month he was buried at Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：太祖自統御海內，芟夷羣醜，其行軍用師，大較依孫、吳之法，而因事設奇，譎敵制勝，變化如神。

translations.literal: The Wei shu says: From the time Taizu took command within the seas, he mowed down the host of villains; in marching armies and using troops he largely followed the methods of Sunzi and Wuzi, yet according to events devised surprises, outwitted foes to seize victory, and shifted like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shu praises Cao Cao for clearing the realm: his campaigns followed Sunzi and Wuzi, yet he improvised stratagems and outthought every opponent.

sentences.zh: 自作兵書十萬餘言，諸將征伐，皆以新書從事。

translations.literal: He personally composed a military treatise of more than one hundred thousand characters; on all the generals' expeditions they acted according to the new book.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote over one hundred thousand characters of military doctrine, and his commanders fought by that new manual.

sentences.zh: 臨事又手爲節度，從令者克捷，違教者負敗。

translations.literal: When matters arose he again personally issued directions; those who obeyed his orders won, those who defied his teaching were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the field he micromanaged orders: obedience brought victory, disobedience brought rout.

sentences.zh: 與虜對陣，意思安閑，如不欲戰，然及至決機乘勝，氣勢盈溢，故每戰必克，軍無幸勝。

translations.literal: Facing enemies across a battle line his bearing was calm, as if he did not wish to fight; yet when the moment came to decide the issue and press an advantage, his momentum brimmed over, so in every fight he prevailed and his army knew no lucky wins.
translations.idiomatic: Against an enemy line he looked almost indifferent to battle, yet at the decisive stroke his fury surged, and he won every engagement by skill, not fortune.

sentences.zh: 知人善察，難眩以偽，拔于禁、樂進於行陣之間，取張遼、徐晃於亡虜之內，皆佐命立功，列爲名將；

translations.literal: He knew men and observed keenly, and was hard to dazzle with pretense; he raised Yu Jin and Le Jin from the ranks, took Zhang Liao and Xu Huang from among vanquished captives, and all aided the mandate, achieved merit, and were enrolled as famous generals;
translations.idiomatic: He read people shrewdly: Yu Jin and Le Jin rose from the ranks, Zhang Liao and Xu Huang from defeated enemies, yet each became a pillar general.

sentences.zh: 其餘拔出細微，登爲牧守者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: The rest whom he lifted from low obscurity to become shepherds and prefects cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others he pulled from obscurity into governorships and magistracies.

sentences.zh: 是以刱造大業，文武並施，御軍三十餘年，手不捨書，晝則講武策，夜則思經傳，登高必賦，及造新詩，被之管絃，皆成樂章。

translations.literal: Therefore he founded a great enterprise, applying both civil and martial arts; for more than thirty years he commanded armies yet never put down his books—by day he lectured on war and policy, by night he pondered the classics and commentaries; whenever he climbed high he would compose verse, and the new poems he set to pipes and strings all became musical pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He built a state with both pen and sword: thirty years of command without neglecting study—days for strategy, nights for the classics, and every climb inspired a poem that became court music.

sentences.zh: 才力絕人，手射飛鳥，躬禽猛獸，甞於南皮一日射雉獲六十三頭。

translations.literal: His strength surpassed other men; with his own hands he shot birds on the wing and seized fierce beasts; once at Nanpi in a single day he shot pheasants and took sixty-three heads.
translations.idiomatic: His physical power was legendary—hawking on the wing, wrestling beasts—and at Nanpi he bagged sixty-three pheasants in one day.

sentences.zh: 及造作宮室，繕治器械，無不爲之法則，皆盡其意。

translations.literal: When it came to building palaces and repairing weapons, there was nothing for which he did not supply models and rules, and in every case he exhausted his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Palace works and armory refits all bore his personal standards, worked out down to the last detail.

sentences.zh: 雅性節儉，不好華麗，後宮衣不錦繡，侍御履不二采，帷帳屏風，壞則補納，茵蓐取溫，無有緣飾。

translations.literal: By disposition he was frugal and disliked splendor; in the rear palace garments were not brocade, attendants' shoes did not use two colors; curtains, screens, and hangings, when damaged, were patched; mats and bedding sought warmth alone and bore no ornamental borders.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly: no brocade in the harem, single-color footwear for servants, patched drapes instead of new silks, and bedding chosen for warmth, not display.

sentences.zh: 攻城拔邑，得靡麗之物，則悉以賜有功，勳勞宜賞，不吝千金，無功望施，分豪不與，四方獻御，與羣下共之。

translations.literal: When attacking cities and seizing towns, if he obtained luxurious goods he gave them all to the meritorious; for labor deserving reward he was not stingy with a thousand in gold; for those without merit who hoped for largesse he gave not the smallest fraction; tribute offered from the four quarters he shared with his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Spoils of conquest went to the deserving; he paid fortunes for real merit and refused a copper to favor-seekers, while sharing regional gifts with his staff.

sentences.zh: 常以送終之制，襲稱之數，繁而無益，俗又過之，故預自制終亡衣服，四篋而已。〉

translations.literal: He often held that the rites for seeing off the dead and the reckoning of mourning grades were elaborate without benefit, and custom went even beyond that; therefore he beforehand made his own shroud for death—only four chests of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He despised wasteful funeral pomp and pre-made his own winding-sheet—four small boxes of clothes, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：太祖愍嫁娶之奢僭，公女適人，皆以皁帳，從婢不過十人。〉

translations.literal: The Fu zi says: Taizu pitied the extravagance of weddings; when a ducal daughter married, black curtains were used all around, and following maids did not exceed ten persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu zi adds that he curbed bridal excess: ducal brides had plain black hangings and no more than ten attendants.

sentences.zh: 〈張華《博物志》曰：漢世，安平崔瑗、瑗子寔、弘農張芝、芝弟昶並善草書，而太祖亞之。

translations.literal: Zhang Hua's Bowu zhi says: In Han times Anping Cui Yuan, Yuan's son Shi, Hongnong Zhang Zhi, and Zhi's younger brother Chang were all skilled at cursive script, while Taizu ranked next to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua lists the great Han calligraphers—Cui Yuan and Cui Shi, Zhang Zhi and Zhang Chang—and places Cao Cao a close second.

sentences.zh: 桓譚、蔡邕善音樂，馮翊山子道、王九真、郭凱等善圍棊，太祖皆與埒能。

translations.literal: Huan Tan and Cai Yong were skilled at music; Fengyi Shan Zidao, Wang Jiuzhen, Guo Kai, and others were skilled at weiqi; Taizu matched their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: He could hold his own with Huan Tan and Cai Yong in music and with noted weiqi masters of the day.

sentences.zh: 又好養性法，亦解方藥，招引方術之士，廬江左慈、譙郡華他、甘陵甘始、陽城郄儉無不畢至，又習啖野葛至一尺，亦得少多飲鴆酒。〉

translations.literal: He also loved longevity arts and understood prescriptions and drugs; he summoned masters of esoteric techniques—Lujiang Zuo Ci, Qiao commandery Hua Tuo, Ganling Gan Shi, Yangcheng Qie Jian—and none failed to arrive; he also practiced eating wild kudzu up to a foot at a sitting and could likewise drink a measure of zhen wine.
translations.idiomatic: He dabbled in longevity lore and pharmacology, inviting Zuo Ci, Hua Tuo, Gan Shi, Qie Jian, and others; he even trained himself to swallow wild kudzu by the foot and to tolerate poison wine in quantity.

sentences.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：漢末王公，多委王服，以幅巾爲雅，是以袁紹、崔豹之徒，雖爲將帥，皆著縑巾。

translations.literal: The Fu zi says: At the end of Han many kings and dukes cast aside kingly robes and took plain headcloth as refined, so Yuan Shao, Cui Bao, and their like, though they were commanders, all wore silk headwraps.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han magnates affected scholar's headcloths instead of court dress—even generals like Yuan Shao and Cui Bao wrapped their heads in silk.

sentences.zh: 魏太祖以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，擬古皮弁，裁縑帛以爲帢，合于簡易隨時之義，以色別其貴賤，于今施行，可謂軍容，非國容也。〉

translations.literal: Wei Taizu, because the realm was stricken with famine and goods were exhausted, modelled the ancient leather cap, cut plain silk to make a qia, in accord with the meaning of simplicity suited to the times, and used color to distinguish noble from base; down to the present it is practiced—this may be called military dress, not court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao introduced the plain silk qia as wartime headgear—color-coded for rank—a practical field style rather than full court regalia.

sentences.zh: 〈《曹瞞傳》曰：太祖爲人佻易無威重，好音樂，倡優在側，常以日達夕。

translations.literal: The Cao Man zhuan says: Taizu was by nature flighty and easy, without dignified gravity; he loved music, and with performers at his side he would pass from dawn to dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The Cao Man zhuan paints him as irreverent and music-mad, keeping entertainers with him from morning till night.

sentences.zh: 被服輕綃，身自佩小鞶囊，以盛手巾細物，時或冠帢帽以見賔客。

translations.literal: He wore light gauze and personally carried a small belt-pouch to hold a handkerchief and small things; at times he would don a qia cap to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: He dressed lightly, tucked a kerchief in a belt pouch, and sometimes received visitors in a casual qia cap.

sentences.zh: 每與人談論，戲弄言誦，盡無所隱，及歡恱大笑，至以頭沒柸案中，肴膳皆沾洿巾幘，其輕易如此。

translations.literal: Whenever he talked with people he jested and bantered with complete openness; when pleased he would laugh until his head sank into the cup-tray, and meats and sauces smeared turban and cap—such was his levity.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation he joked without reserve, and in mirth he might bury his face in the dishes until sauce stained his headgear.

sentences.zh: 然持法峻刻，諸將有計畫勝出己者，隨以法誅之，及故人舊怨，亦皆無餘。

translations.literal: Yet he held the law harshly; if generals had plans that surpassed his own, he would promptly execute them by law; old friends and past grudges likewise left no survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the law was ruthless: any general who outshone him could die for it, and old scores were settled in blood.

sentences.zh: 其所刑殺，輒對之垂涕嗟痛之，終無所活。

translations.literal: Those he punished and killed he would face while shedding tears and sighing in pain for them, yet in the end they were not spared.
translations.idiomatic: He wept theatrically over men he executed, but never spared them.

sentences.zh: 初，袁忠爲沛相，甞欲以法治太祖，沛國桓邵亦輕之，及在兖州，陳留邊讓言議頗侵太祖，太祖殺讓，族其家。

translations.literal: In the beginning Yuan Zhong was chancellor of Pei and once wished to use the law to control Taizu; Huan Shao of the Pei kingdom also despised him; when he was in Yanzhou, Bian Rang of Chenliu in discourse greatly offended Taizu, and Taizu killed Rang and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhong and Huan Shao had once slighted him; later, when Bian Rang mocked him in Yanzhou, Cao Cao had Bian killed and his kin wiped out.

sentences.zh: 忠、邵俱避難交州，太祖遣使就太守止燮盡族之。

translations.literal: Zhong and Shao both fled to refuge in Jiaozhou; Taizu sent a messenger to the grand warden to have them exterminated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhong and Huan Shao fled to Jiaozhou, he sent orders through the local governor to extirpate both families.

sentences.zh: 桓邵得出首，拜謝於庭中，太祖謂曰：「跪可解死邪！

translations.literal: Huan Shao was able to come forward and surrender; he bowed in apology in the courtyard, and Taizu said to him, "Can kneeling explain away death, villain!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shao came out to beg pardon on his knees; Cao Cao sneered, "Think kneeling saves you?"

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had him executed.

sentences.zh: 甞出軍，行經麥中，令「士卒無敗麥，犯者死」。

translations.literal: Once when he led the army and passed through standing wheat, he ordered, "Soldiers shall not ruin the wheat; violators die."
translations.idiomatic: On a march through wheat he decreed death for anyone who trampled the crop.

sentences.zh: 騎士皆下馬，付麥以相付，於是太祖馬騰入麥中，勑主簿議罪；

translations.literal: The horsemen all dismounted and passed the standing grain from hand to hand to clear a path; nevertheless Taizu's horse bolted into the wheat field, and he ordered the chief clerk to deliberate on the crime;
translations.idiomatic: The troopers dismounted and shifted the crop aside by hand—yet his own mount broke into the field, and he told his chief clerk to rule on the breach.

sentences.zh: 主簿對以春秋之義，罰不加於尊。

translations.literal: The chief clerk answered with the Spring and Autumn meaning that punishment is not applied to the exalted.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk cited the Chunqiu principle that law does not bind the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「制法而自犯之，何以帥下？

translations.literal: Taizu said, "If I establish a law yet break it myself, how shall I lead those below?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao replied, "How can I legislate a rule and break it before the ranks?"

sentences.zh: 然孤爲軍帥，不可自殺，請自刑。

translations.literal: Yet I alone am commander of the army and cannot kill myself; I ask to impose punishment on myself.
translations.idiomatic: As commander-in-chief he could not execute himself, so he proposed a substitute punishment.

sentences.zh: 」因援劔割髮以置地。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew his sword, cut off his hair, and cast it on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword, sheared off his hair, and threw it down as symbolic execution.

sentences.zh: 又有幸姬常從晝寢，枕之卧，告之曰：「須臾覺我。

translations.literal: There was also a favored concubine who often attended his daytime nap; he pillowed on her as he lay and told her, "Wake me in a little while."
translations.idiomatic: A favorite concubine shared his daylight nap; he told her to rouse him shortly.

sentences.zh: 」姬見太祖卧安，未即寤，及自覺，棒殺之。

translations.literal: The concubine saw that Taizu lay peacefully and did not wake him at once; when he woke on his own, he clubbed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: She let him sleep on; when he woke on his own, he beat her to death for disobeying.

sentences.zh: 常討賊，廩穀不足，私謂主者曰：「如何？

translations.literal: Often when campaigning against bandits the granary grain was insufficient; he privately said to the steward, "What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, short of army grain, he quietly asked the quartermaster what to do.

sentences.zh: 」主者曰：「可以小斛以足之。

translations.literal: The steward said, "You may use a small measure to make it sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: The man suggested short-measuring the ration scoops.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「善。

translations.literal: Taizu said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao agreed.

sentences.zh: 」後軍中言太祖欺衆，太祖謂主者曰：「特當借君死以猒衆，不然事不解。

translations.literal: Later the army said Taizu had deceived the multitude; Taizu said to the steward, "For the moment I must borrow your death to quiet the multitude, or the affair will not be resolved."
translations.idiomatic: When the troops cried fraud, he told the steward he needed his head to calm the camp.

sentences.zh: 」乃斬之，取首題徇曰：「行小斛，盜官穀，斬之軍門。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beheaded him, took the head, and posted an inscription: "Used a small measure, stole official grain—beheaded at the camp gate."
translations.idiomatic: He executed the man and displayed the head with a placard blaming short measure and theft of public grain.

sentences.zh: 」其酷虐變詐，皆此之類也。〉

translations.literal: His cruelty and shifting deceit were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such episodes typify his cruelty and cunning.

sentences.zh: 評曰：漢末，天下大亂，雄豪並起，而袁紹虎眎四州，彊盛莫敵。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: At the end of Han the realm was in great chaos and bold heroes rose together, yet Yuan Shao tiger-gazed over four provinces and his might had no rival.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's verdict: in the late Han collapse Yuan Shao dominated four provinces and seemed unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 太祖運籌演謀，鞭撻宇內，擥申、商之法術，該韓、白之奇策，官方授材，各因其器，矯情任筭，不念舊惡，終能總御皇機，克成洪業者，惟其明略最優也。

translations.literal: That Taizu could plan strategies and extend schemes, lash the realm within, embrace the legal arts of Shen and Shang and encompass the stratagems of Han and Bai, confer office and assign talents each according to their capacity, curb emotion and trust calculation, and not brood on old wrongs, and in the end grasp the imperial mechanism and complete a great enterprise—this was because his enlightened strategy was supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao matched Legalist rigor with Han Xin–style stratagem, matched men to posts, mastered his passions, forgave old slights when useful, and seized the mandate—above all because his political vision was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 抑可謂非常之人，超世之傑矣。

translations.literal: Indeed he may be called an extraordinary man and a hero who transcended his age.
translations.idiomatic: He ranks among the rare figures who tower above their times.
